entries.summary: Distorts a layer over texture seams using adjacency.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See [Border types|/copernicus/glossary#border] for more information.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: The world space direction in which you want to distort. This parameter doesn't apply when you wire in a `dir` input, which instead distorts the layer in a texture space direction.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: The strength of distortion. Negative values follow the directions backwards when tracing. This parameter distorts along the __Direction__ parameter's values. When you wire in a `dir` input, this parameter then distorts in that texture space direction.

parameters.label: Pixels per Step
parameters.description: Controls the tracing quality to increase the accuracy of tracing curved trajectories. Higher values let the node take larger steps, which runs faster, but can miss intermediate variations in the distortion directions and texture island transitions. When off, the node takes a single step for each pixel to determine the source location. This is fast, but causes inconsistencies at texture seams and inaccuracies when the direction or scale vary.

entries.title: Bake Geometry Textures
entries.summary: Generates textures by baking between a low-resolution and high-resolution mesh at interactive speeds.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware.

parameters.label: Tracing Mode
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracing mode that the baker utilizes.

parameters.label: UDIM Override
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: Select a UDIM to bake, which overrides the UDIM context option.

parameters.label: Sample Multiplier
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The amount to multiply against the Sample parameters, such as __Occlusion Samples__ and __Thickness Samples__. This acts as a general quality scale. For example, a __Sample Multiplier__ of `0.5` and __Occlusion Samples__ of `256` bakes occlusion at `128`.

parameters.label: Face Culling
parameters.heading: Ray Setup
parameters.description: Specifies which polygons to ignore when Ray Tracing primary rays.

parameters.label: Visibility Culling
parameters.heading: Ray Setup
parameters.description: The method used to handle secondary rays that interact with the geometry. This can allow floaters on the geometry to be projected onto the low-resolution map without casting a shadow.

parameters.label: Ray Start (Point)
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the `cage` input, which stores the Ray Start Positions.

parameters.label: Ray Direction (Vertex)
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes
parameters.description: The vertex attribute that lives on the `cage` input, which stores the Ray Directions.

parameters.label: Ray Length (Point)
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes
parameters.description: The point attribute that lives on the `cage` input, which stores the Ray Lengths. If Ray Length Missing:: How to handle the ray lengths when the ray length attribute doesn't exist, such as when a Bake Pre-Process node is not used in the workflow. For example, use this parameter when a custom cage already exists.

parameters.label: Custom Ray Length
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes
parameters.description: The length of the rays in world units.

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.heading: Cage Attributes
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-resolution mesh when rays are sent from the low-resolution mesh to the scene. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-resolution mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.

parameters.label: Normals
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals.

parameters.label: Tangents
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing tangent attributes. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have tangent attributes.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup
parameters.description: The attribute to use for UV unwrapping and rasterization. This can be a vertex or point.

parameters.label: Remove UV Z values
parameters.heading: Geometry Setup
parameters.description: Flattens the Z component of float3 UV attributes to 0. Some UV nodes output float3 values by default, which can lead to unexpected results when rasterizing in UV mode.

parameters.label: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: Lets you control which primitives are visible when computing ray tracing effects like occlusion and curvature. This matches primitives between the low-resolution and high-resolution geometry and isolates them in their own pocket dimension, which can be used to prevent intersection errors. If a ray hits an object that doesn't belong to the current matched piece, it's ignored. This causes a rebake and changes the bake results.

parameters.label: Piece Attribute
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: The primitive piece attribute to use to identify the different pieces across the low-resolution, high-resolution, and cage.

parameters.label: Include Pieces
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: The sets to always include in the bake. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching.

parameters.label: Exclude Pieces
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: The sets to always exclude from the bake. This happens after the include pieces are gathered. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching. For example, if your include is `*` but your exclude is `hat`, the baker bakes every set available except `hat`.

parameters.label: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Fills empty areas of the image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas. This is a post-process that fixes darker pixel values at the edges of UV seams, and can produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures.

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding.

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack and read clean values for extrapolation.

parameters.label: Exclude Alpha from UV Fill
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Turns off UV filling on the `alpha` map. Adding UV filling to `alpha` often results in a fully white output.

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.heading: Alignment
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.

parameters.label: Tangent Normal
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Tangent Normal__ map. When off, the `normal` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Normal Space
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from `-1` to `1`. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from `0` to `1`.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Rounded Edge Normal__ map. When off, the `edgenormal` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Space
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from `-1` to `1`. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from `0` to `1`.

parameters.label: Rounded Samples
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Rounded Edge Normal__. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Rounded Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold are assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.heading: Alignment
parameters.description: Whether to record the world space position in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.

parameters.label: World Normal
parameters.heading: World Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __World Normal__ map. When off, the `worldnormal` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: World Normal Space
parameters.heading: World Normal
parameters.description: How to represent the normal map.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Position__ map. When off, the `position` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Position Space

parameters.label: Bounding Box

parameters.label: Curvature Samples

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Smaller values (which create smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (which represent greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.

parameters.label: Bias

parameters.label: Edge

parameters.label: Radius

parameters.label: Cusp Angle

parameters.label: Cavity

parameters.label: Cavity Samples

entries.title: Blend
entries.summary: Blends two layers, VDBs, or attributes together.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The method used to determine which pixels in the foreground and background match. See [/copernicus/spaces] for more information.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See [Border types|/copernicus/glossary#border] for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See [Filters|/copernicus/glossary#filter] for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA [channels|Wp:Channel_(digital_image)] to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is `1`, which means this node uses only the new value. See [Mask|/copernicus/glossary#mask] for more information.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Specifies the global compositing operation.

parameters.label: Alpha Compositing
parameters.description: For RGBA layers, you can process the blending operation per-component or by using Alpha Compositing rules. When on, this extends monochrome layers with `1` in the alpha so they act like opaque layers. When off, each component (including alpha) is processed independently. This allows a multiply with mono layer to multiply all channels the same.

parameters.label: Swap FG and BG
parameters.description: Swaps the values of the foreground and background. This is useful for non-commutative operators. This has no effect with commutative operators, as this does not affect the masking operation.

parameters.label: Compare Lengths
parameters.description: In maximum and minimum mode, choose the output based on the length of the two values; rather than working component-wise.  This allows one to mix vector fields where the highest or lowest magnitude vector is kept.

parameters.label: Clip by Data Window
parameters.description: Adds an implied mask that matches the [data window|/copernicus/transition#data_display] of the `fg` input. This prevents the image from extending into the destination.

parameters.label: Crop to Content
parameters.description: Crop the new layer to the union of the foreground layer's transformed data window and the background layer's data window.

entries.title: Block End
entries.summary: End of a block, declaring its outputs.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Turns on simulation so block outputs feed directly back into the inputs, which creates a feedback loop. This is useful for complex motion and simulations.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is the amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of `1` maintains the normal speed, a value greater than `1` speeds up the simulation, and a value less than `1` slows down the simulation.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this enables the caching of the simulation.  If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to `24` to cache frames `24`, `48`, `72`, and such.  This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to `0` to disable checkpointing.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: When __Live Simulation__ is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.description: When __Live Simulation__ is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: How many iterations of the block to run per frame. For example, if you set this to `40` it runs the internals of the block 40 times for each generated frame. This means that by frame 10 it's run 400 iterations but only produced 10 frames.

parameters.label: Iteration Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that stores the current iteration, which starts at `0` and counts up to one less than the __Iterations__ amount. Use the [Exp:contextoption] expression function to access this value inside the block.

parameters.label: Total Iterations Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that stores the total number of iterations this block is set to run for, which is equal to the __Iterations__ amount. Use the [Exp:contextoption] expression function to access this value inside the block.

parameters.label: First Pass Variable
parameters.description: The name of the context option that identifies the first pass in the block. This is equal to `1` on the first iteration of a simple loop or the first substep of a simulation, otherwise it evaluates to `0`. Use the [Exp:contextoption] expression function to read this variable's value.

parameters.label: Enable Compiling
parameters.description: Compiles the block when its outputs need to be cooked. This is more efficient, but doesn't save out any of the intermediate results within the block.

parameters.label: Register as Slap Comp Block
parameters.description: Makes this block available to use for slap comp in the Solaris viewport.

parameters.label: Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs
parameters.label_norm: import cameras with slap comp inputs
parameters.description: When __Register as Slap Comp Block__ is on, this controls where the incoming layers are placed. When __Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs__ is on, the layers come in with the view transform of the camera. When __Import Cameras with Slap Comp Inputs__ is off, this places all layers at the origin, facing the Z axis. Turn this parameter on if you plan to combine the render results with other objects in 3D space.

parameters.label: Add AOVs from Last Render
parameters.description: When __Register as Slap Comp Block__ is on, this populates the block's output list with AOVs from the last Solaris viewport render. The [Slap Comp Import COP|Node:cop/slapcompimport] also has this parameter to fill that node with the render's AOVs and any Block Begin nodes plugged into it.

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.

parameters.label: Block Outputs
parameters.description: The number of outputs for this block.

parameters.label: Output Name
parameters.description: The name of the output. This string identifies the output when using the Invoke Block COP to execute the block, or when the block is used for slap comp.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: The type of the output and the corresponding ports on the node. See [Data types|/copernicus/glossary#data_type] for more information.

entries.title: Bubble Noise
entries.summary: Generates bubble noise.

parameters.label: Type Info
parameters.description: The type information for the resulting layer. See [Type info|/copernicus/glossary#type_info] for more information.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: The amount by which to multiply the noise, which the node applies before the __Center__ adjustment. For example, a value of `0.5` makes a pixel value of `0.5` become `0.25`.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: The center of the output noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of `0.5` makes a pixel value of `0.5` become `1`.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: The size (in [image coordinates|/copernicus/spaces]) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ button to adjust this further using the __Element Scale__ parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: When the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.

parameters.label: Phase
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: The location of the noise in four-dimensional space, which lets you smoothly pick different seeds. Torus noise works by sampling a flat torus in a four-dimensional space.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.heading: Bubble Noise
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the fractal noise.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the noise.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration, which is rounded to an integer value for periodic noise.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.

parameters.label: Distortion
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: The amount to distort the noise in the direction of decreasing noise values (when greater than `1`) or increasing noise values (when less than `1`).

parameters.label: Stretch
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: The amount to stretch the noise in each direction in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Droop
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: The amount to warp the generated noise pattern so it bends or hangs towards the __Droop Direction__.

parameters.label: Droop Direction
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: When __Droop__ is on, this is the direction in image coordinates in which to warp the noise.

parameters.label: Fold each Octave
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: Remaps the values between `-1` and `1` and flips values below `0` to the positive range. For example, a pixel value of `-2` becomes `2`. This makes all valleys become peaks.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of `-2` becomes `2`.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value `x` to `1 - x`.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) towards zero (if __Bias__ is less than `1`) or one (if __Bias__ is greater than `1`). A bias value of `0.5` doesn't affect the values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg]

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) together, while values around `0` and `1` are pulled apart. A gain value of `0.5` doesn't affect the noise values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg]

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than `1` increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than `1` stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if __Contrast__ is less than `1`) or away from (if __Contrast__ is greater than `1`) medium grey values (around `0.5`).

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

entries.title: Camera Properties
entries.summary: Adjusts the camera properties of a layer.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.description: The basic projection type.

parameters.label: Imaging Distance
parameters.description: The layer is placed a certain distance away from the eye of the layer's camera.  This controls how far this is.  The distance can be set explicitly or adjusted from the current distance.  It can also be set to automatically set the distance at which the layer will go through a particular point.

parameters.label: Imaging Point
parameters.description: The point in worldspace the imaging layer should go through.  The imaging distance will be adjusted so the imaging plane will intersect this point.  This makes it straightforward to stick the imaging layers on a focus object despite camera motion.

parameters.label: Near/Far
parameters.description: The near and far clipping of the camera, measured from the distance from the camera origin (rather than from the layer's origin).

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.description: The distance, in the same units as Aperture, to set the camera's origin back from the layer's origin.

parameters.label: Aperture (mm)
parameters.description: The width of the camera's aperture. This can be viewed as the width of the layer. The ratio of focal length and aperture is what determines the offset of the camera. The absolute values are not relevant, so they can be in any unit as long as they're consistent.

parameters.label: Aperture Offset
parameters.description: The horizontal adjustment of the aperture, allowing offseting of the imaging point.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.description: The metadata that controls when the camera should start receiving light and stop receiving light. This is relative to the frame rate. When you have a `source` layer this parameter isn't used.

parameters.label: Focus Distance
parameters.description: The distance that should be in focus, relative to the layer's origin. By default the layer is at the focus plane. When you have a `source` layer this parameter isn't used.

parameters.label: F-Stop

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When you turn on the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ option, this parameter scales the element size per axis to create anisotropic noise.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points. parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When you turn on [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ option, this is the per-axis scaling of the jitter.

parameters.label: Density
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: Values above this threshold randomly cull the cells.

parameters.label: Density Seed
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The seed used to randomly cull the cells.

parameters.label: Lattice Type
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The grid to define Worley noise on and determine the cell shape.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The metric for computing the distance to a point.

parameters.label: Smooth Edge
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Metric__ is set to __Euclidean__, you can control the roundness of the cells.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: Shifts the entire noise function in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default covers the entire standard image space ("canonical image"). If you have a non-square image, the values should match the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: Determines whether the shape parameters work as absolute values in [image Space|/copernicus/spaces], or as relative values in the 0 to 1 range.

parameters.label: Gap
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The amount of space between each cell. Higher values increase the spacing between cells, and the cells will shrink until they're not visible.

parameters.label: Random Height
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The scale factor for an additional random noise value that is added to each cell.

parameters.label: Height Seed
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The random seed used to control the __Random Height__.

parameters.label: Bevel
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The amount of bevel to add to the outer edges of each cell. Higher values taper the cells inwards to create a pointy top. Lower values decrease the slope to create a flat top with hard edges.

parameters.label: Bevel Ramp
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: A ramp to adjust the shape of the bevel. The left side of the ramp corresponds to each cell's border, and the right side corresponds to the inset length given by the __Bevel__ parameter.

parameters.label: Orient
parameters.heading: Orient
parameters.description: Tilt cell's noise value by a fixed amount of __Steepness__.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Orient
parameters.description: Rotates the tilt direction of all cells. Higher values rotate the cells in a counterclockwise direction.

parameters.label: Steepness
parameters.heading: Orient
parameters.description: The slope of each cell's noise value. Higher values create inclined cells. Lower values create flat cells.

parameters.label: Random Rotation
parameters.heading: Orient
parameters.description: The maximum amount to randomly vary the tilt direction of each cell.

parameters.label: Tilt Seed
parameters.heading: Orient
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the tilt direction of each cell.

parameters.label: Distort
parameters.heading: Distort
parameters.description: Applies distortion to the footprint of the cells.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.heading: Distort
parameters.description: The amplitude of noise to drive the distortion.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.heading: Distort
parameters.description: The size (in [image coordinates|/copernicus/spaces]) of the basic element noise that drives the distortion.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Distort
parameters.description: The strength of distortion.

parameters.label: Global Seed
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: The global seed used to randomize the cells.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of `-2` becomes `2`.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value `x` to `1 - x`.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) towards zero (if __Bias__ is less than `1`) or one (if __Bias__ is greater than `1`). A bias value of `0.5` doesn't affect the values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg]

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) together, while values around `0` and `1` are pulled apart. A gain value of `0.5` doesn't affect the noise values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg]

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than `1` increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than `1` stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if __Contrast__ is less than `1`) or away from (if __Contrast__ is greater than `1`) medium grey values (around `0.5`).

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Green

parameters.label: Blue
parameters.heading: Distortion

parameters.label: Global Distortion Scale
parameters.heading: Distortion
parameters.description: The amount (in image space) to scale all three channels. This applies a zoom-like effect to the image based on the __Distortion Scale Mask__ parameter and the `effect` input. The default value is `0.15`.

parameters.label: Distortion Scale Mask
parameters.heading: Distortion
parameters.description: Scales the distortion based on the pixel's coordinates. By default, the ramp is set up so that the corners of the image are distorted while the center stays the same. For more information about using ramps, see [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps].

parameters.label: Red
parameters.heading: Rotation
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the red channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction. The default value is `0`.

parameters.label: Green
parameters.heading: Rotation
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to rotate the green channel by this angle. Higher values rotate the channel in a counterclockwise direction, which makes the offset between the channels more apparent. Lower values rotate the channel in a clockwise direction. The default value is `0`.

parameters.label: Blue

parameters.heading: Cloud Noise

parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.heading: Fractal

parameters.label: Distortion

parameters.label: Stretch
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: The amount to stretch the noise in each direction in world coordinates.

parameters.label: Droop
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: The amount to warp the generated noise pattern so it bends or hangs towards the __Droop Direction__.

parameters.label: Droop Direction
parameters.heading: Warping
parameters.description: When __Droop__ is on, this is the direction in world coordinates in which to warp the noise.

parameters.label: Fold Each Octave
parameters.heading: Warping

parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Fold

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value `x` to `1 - x`.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) together, while values around `0` and `1` are pulled apart. A gain value of `0.5` doesn't affect the noise values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg]

parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.heading: Post Processing

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum

entries.title: Convolve Filter
entries.summary: Convolves an image with an arbitrary kernel image using an FFT.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that this node convolves. The `input` and `kernel` images are both interpreted with this type. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Normalize Kernel
parameters.description: Divides the kernel by the sum of all its values before convolving, so the values total `1`. This keeps the operation from brightening or darkening the image. Turn this off when the kernel is already normalized or when you want the kernel's absolute magnitude to scale the result.

parameters.label: Centered Kernel
parameters.description: Treats the center of the kernel image as its origin, so the convolution does not shift the result. When off, the origin is taken at the corner of the kernel image, which translates the output by half the kernel's size (the raw behavior of a frequency-space convolution).

parameters.label: Padding
parameters.heading: Padding
parameters.description: When on, extends the image with a border of extra pixels before the transform and crops it back afterward; the value sets the fraction of the image size to add on each side. Because the [FFT|Node:cop/fft] convolution is cyclic, the kernel otherwise wraps from one edge of the image to the opposite edge, and padding pushes those wrap-around artifacts outside the cropped region. Larger values suppress more wrap-around at the cost of a larger transform.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.heading: Padding
parameters.description: How the padded region added around the image is filled. See [Border types|/copernicus/glossary#border] for more information.

entries.summary: Crops a layer to a new size.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Cropping can be seen as cutting out part of an image, throwing out the extra, but leaving it in the same location of your work space. But it can also be seen as a pan & zoom to reframe the desired region to now fit the center of your workspace.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: Override the border values used when un-cropping an image.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.description: Controls how to specify the crop.  This controls the range of the values and if they are in respect to the input's display or data window.

parameters.label: Geometry Units
parameters.description: If a geometry input is used to drive the crop, this controls what the units of the geometry are.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: The method used to specify the crop region.

parameters.label: Lower Left
parameters.description: The lower-left of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the __Units__ parameter determines.

parameters.label: Upper Right
parameters.description: The upper-right of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the __Units__ parameter determines.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The size of the crop in image, texture, or pixel space, which the __Units__ parameter determines.

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: Adjust the final crop values to have this aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Extract Tile
parameters.description: Divide the cropped region into equal sized tiles, and crop to one of the tiles.  Pixel padding is done after the tile determination, so can be used to ensure there is a buffer around the tiles.

parameters.label: Tile Counts
parameters.description: Number of tiles to divide the image into in each axis.

parameters.label: Tile Number
parameters.description: The tile number to extract, starting with `0` at the bottom left and increasing to the right.

parameters.label: Minimum Resolution
parameters.description: The cropped region will be increased to include at least this number of pixels.

parameters.label: Limit Resolution
parameters.description: Lets you set a __Maximum Resolution__ to limit the size.

parameters.label: Maximum Resolution
parameters.description: The cropped region will be clamped to at most this size.  This is useful for dynamic cropping to avoid unexpected input from creating overly large textures.

parameters.label: Reset Pixel Origin
parameters.description: Adjusts the pixel coordinates to match the display window. This is useful when reframing the display window, because the location of the (0, 0) pixel may no longer refer to the corner of the display window. This makes pixel coordinates appear to be offset, which can cause confusion if this was unintended.

parameters.label: Left/Right

parameters.description: Additional pixels to pad the cropped image on the left and right.

parameters.label: Top/Bottom

parameters.description: Additional pixels to pad the cropped image on the top and bottom.

parameters.description: The distance (in [buffer elements|/copernicus/spaces]) to compute the derivatives used for the curl. parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range. Turning this parameter on is useful when building seamless textures with a wrap [border type|/copernicus/glossary#border]. Turn this off if you want to avoid artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in a clamp border type, as it acts like an extrapolation.

entries.summary: Computes the derivative of the source layer along its width (x-axis) and height (y-axis).

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.description: The [space|/copernicus/spaces] in which to compute the derivative.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Rotates the position at which the pixels are sampled by this angle. An angle of 90 degrees would mean that the x derivative would be equal to the y derivative of an angle 0.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the output value by this amount.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: Adds this amount to the output value.

parameters.label: Read Pixels outside Image
parameters.description: Determines if derivatives at the boundary should read outside the image or restrict to the image range.  Reading outside is useful for building seamless textures with wrap-mode.  But restricting to the image range avoids artificial flattening of the derivative at the boundary in clamp modes, as it acts more like an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.description: Usually a derivative is computed with adjacent pixels, but if the values are slowly varying there may not be enough bit-depth to get smooth derivatives.  This will expand the distance (in buffer elements) to compute the derivative, possibly removing stepping artifacts from the derivative.

parameters.label: Difference Mode
parameters.description: The [finite difference|Wp:Finite_difference] used to compute the derivatives. See [What are screen space derivatives|https://gamedev.stackexchange.com/questions/130888/what-are-screen-space-derivatives-and-when-would-i-use-them] for more information and an image example.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See [Border types|/copernicus/glossary#border] for more information.

parameters.label: Units

parameters.label: Output Drop Shadow Only
parameters.description: Outputs only the drop shadow effect, which displays a preview of the effect. Turn this on if you want to make the shadow a separate AOV or configure the shadow further before you composite it on top of the source layer.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow
parameters.description: The direction in which to offset the shadow.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow
parameters.description: The amount (based on the __Units__ parameter) to offset the shadow to give the effect of directional lighting.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow
parameters.description: The angle by which to offset the shadow.

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow
parameters.description: The distance (based on the __Units__ parameter) along the angle by which to offset the shadow from the original input.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow
parameters.description: The color of the drop shadow.

parameters.label: Multiply with Original
parameters.heading: Drop Shadow
parameters.description: Multiplies the drop shadow's __Color__ with the original input's color before offsetting. When off, the drop shadow's __Color__ replaces the original input's color.

parameters.label: Expansion
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: The amount (based on the __Units__ parameter) to expand the shadow. Higher values spread the shadow outwards while lower values contract the shadow inwards. Adding some expansion can ensure a strong shadow that blurring would otherwise wash out, especially for thin text.

parameters.description: When __Streak__ is on, this ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For more information about using ramps, see [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps].

entries.title: Fast Fourier Transform
entries.summary: Computes the Fourier transform of an image.

parameters.label: FFT Direction
parameters.description: Selects whether to perform the forward or the inverse transform. __Forward FFT__ converts an image into frequency space, while __Inverse FFT__ reconstructs an image from its frequencies. To perform the __Forward FFT__ of an image, you can plug it into the `real` input.

parameters.label: Center DC
parameters.description: When enabled, the low-frequency components of the spectrum are shifted to be at the center of the image. If __Center DC__ is disabled, center of the image contains the high frequencies, and the low frequencies are at the corners.

parameters.label: Normalize on Forward Pass
parameters.description: When this checkbox is turned on, normalization is applied during the forward transform. When disabled, normalization happens during the inverse pass. Turning this option on allows for easier visualization of the power in the spectrum. Value of this parameter must match on nodes that perform forward and inverse passes for faithful reconsturction.

parameters.label: Target Sum
parameters.description: When enabled, rescales the spectrum such that the sum of all pixel values after the inverse pass will work out to __Target Sum__.

entries.title: File
entries.summary: Loads an image or video from disk.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.description: The method used to load your image or video.

parameters.label: File Name
parameters.description: When __Source__ is `File`, this is the path to the image, image sequence, or video file to load. You can load individual images by providing the path to the image on disk. For image sequences, you can use either `$F` as a placeholder for the frame number or `<F>` to use the __Video Timing__ parameter. Use the `<UDIM>` token to load a specific UDIM. The context option UDIM is used unless you override it with the __UDIM__ parameter. Use the `<LAYER>` token to load from multiple files at once. Instead of the AOV names referring to specific AOVs in one input file, the AOV name replaces the `<LAYER>` token in the filename and the loaded `C` AOV (or the first AOV if `C` isn't present).

parameters.label: Clone Name
parameters.description: When __Source__ is `Clone`, this is the name of the clone to load in the [Clone Control Panel|/ref/panes/clonecontrol].

parameters.label: Live Render LOP
parameters.description: When __Source__ is `Live Render`, this is the path to the [Live Render LOP|Node:/lop/liverender] you want to grab data from. The File COP is dirtied whenever the live render updates, so recook when you view something dependent on it. See [Live rendering in Solaris|/solaris/support/liverender#copernicus] for information about how to start and stop a live render session.

parameters.label: Reload Image
parameters.description: Reloads the image.

parameters.label: Video Timing
parameters.description: Defines how to generate the frame number for either image sequences that use the `<F>` notation or video files.

parameters.label: Video Start Frame
parameters.description: When __Video Timing__ is `Start Frame`, this is the frame when the image sequence or video starts playing back.

parameters.label: Video Frame
parameters.description: When __Video Timing__ is `Frame Number`, this is the frame when the image sequence or video displays. You can use this parameter to write custom frame number expressions.

parameters.label: UDIM
parameters.description: Overrides the current UDIM with a specific one. This is the value that replaces any `<UDIM>` token in the filename. Otherwise, the current context UDIM value is used.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The method used to handle the border of the raster when the __Tile Visualization__ parameter is on in the enclosing [COP Network node|Node:/manager/copnet] or [COP Network SOP|Node:/sop/copnet]. See [Border types|/copernicus/glossary#border] for more information.

parameters.label: Missing Data
parameters.description: The method used to handle missing data, such as missing AOVs and missing frames in a sequence.

parameters.label: Missing Color
parameters.description: When __Missing Data__ is `Use Color`, this is the constant color that replaces the missing data.

parameters.label: Incoming Colorspace
parameters.description: The method used to interpret AOV color data.

parameters.label: Pre-Multiply if Necessary
parameters.description: Pre-multiplies color with alpha for formats that store data un-premultiplied (PNG, TGA). This doesn't effect other formats.

parameters.label: Load Camera
parameters.description: Loads the camera information from the file metadata and appropriately sets the transform and camera of the layers. This looks for the worldToCamera and worldToNDC metadata, and prefers the `_d` suffixed versions because those are usually double versions.

parameters.label: Display Window from Input
parameters.description: Makes the file use the input's display window. When unwired, this uses the default context option for Copernicus and causes all files to have equal-sized pixels. Turn this on when you want pixel-to-pixel correspondences. For example, this makes a 2k texture twice the size of a 1k texture. When off, files normally generate a new display window from the file's own data. This frames all files to the same size in [image space|/copernicus/spaces] regardless of the resolution of the file, which is useful for switching between 1k and 2k textures without changing locations.

parameters.label: Add AOVs from File
parameters.description: Imports each AOV from the specified file or video and sets their properties in the __Number of AOVs__ parameters. If the file has a `<LAYER>` token, this finds all files that match that pattern and creates an AOV for each. ((Ctrl + LMB)) to reset the AOV list, otherwise this adds only newly detected AOVs.

parameters.label: Number of AOVs
parameters.description: The AOVs to load from the __Source__ image or video.

parameters.label: File AOV
parameters.description: The name of the AOV to load from the specified file or video. For images, if `C` is specified and it doesn't exist in the file, the first AOV in the file is loaded instead. Video files only support `C`.

parameters.label: Channel Type
parameters.description: The channel type to use for this AOV. See [Data types|/copernicus/glossary#data_type] for more information.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.description: The precision to use for this AOV, which controls how many bits the channel uses.

parameters.label: Raw
parameters.description: Converts pixel values into the working scene linear color space (from the file's color space based on the OCIO settings of the loaded file's type). When off, pixel values are loaded from the file without modifications.

entries.title: Filter Frequencies
entries.summary: Boosts or suppresses spatial frequencies in an image.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type this node filters. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Multiplies the filtered result. Use values above `1` to boost the kept band or below `1` to attenuate it. The default of `1` passes the band through unchanged.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.heading: Frequency
parameters.description: The center of the kept band, as a normalized radial frequency from `0` to `1`. A value of `0` is the lowest frequency (the broad, slowly varying content at the center of the transform) and `1` is the highest frequency the image can represent (the finest detail). parameters.label: Width

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.heading: Frequency

parameters.label: Angle

parameters.label: Width
parameters.heading: Anisotropy

parameters.label: Smooth
parameters.heading: Anisotropy
parameters.description: Gives the wedge a soft falloff at its angular edges instead of a hard cutoff.

parameters.label: Reflect
parameters.heading: Anisotropy
parameters.description: Mirrors the wedge to the opposite direction, so a wedge at __Angle__ also covers `Angle + 180`. Because the frequency spectrum of a real image is symmetric about its center, you usually want this on so the filter treats a direction and its opposite alike.

parameters.label: Per Component
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: Computes a separate noise for each channel of the output. If off, the output is grayscale for mono and non-mono layers.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Noise Type__ is `Worley Cellular F1` or `Worley Cellular F2-F1`, this is how to define different metrics for computing the distance to a point.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Noise Type__ is `Worley Cellular F1` or `Worley Cellular F2-F1`, this is the amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The size (in [image coordinates|/copernicus/spaces]) of the basic element of the noise. You can turn on the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ button to adjust this further using the __Element Scale__ parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anistropic noise.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The amount to offset the entire noise function in image coordinates.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The size of a single tile of noise. The noise periodically repeats in this size. The size is in image coordinates, so the default is for the entire default canoncial image. If you have a non-square image, this should match the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: 3D Noise
parameters.heading: 3D Noise
parameters.description: Evaluates the noise in a 3D space. Use these parameters to control the third dimension, while the first two dimensions are the location in the image.

parameters.label: Animate
parameters.heading: 3D Noise
parameters.description: Implicitly adds time to the third coordinate.

parameters.label: Pulse Length
parameters.heading: 3D Noise
parameters.description: The interval length (in seconds) of the noise's pulse in the third dimension. Lower values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while higher values decrease this rate.

parameters.label: Time Offset
parameters.heading: 3D Noise
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) that's added to the start frame.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: 3D Noise
parameters.description: The amount of time (in seconds) by which to multiply the start frame. Higher values increase the rate at which the noise switches its appearance, while lower values decrease this rate.

parameters.label: Loop Length (sec)
parameters.heading: 3D Noise
parameters.description: This is the time (in seconds) at which to repeat the noise. This clamps other options to enforce periodic behavior. Turn this on to generate animations that seamlessly loop. When off, the animation generally doesn't repeat after any amount of time.

parameters.label: Fractal Type
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: How to add successive layers of noise to create finer-scale details.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount of times to scale add together the noise.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration, which is rounded to an integer value for periodic noise.

parameters.label: Octave Offset
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to offset the noise for each iteration.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of `-2` becomes `2`.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value `x` to `1 - x`.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) towards zero (if __Bias__ is less than `1`) or one (if __Bias__ is greater than `1`). A bias value of `0.5` doesn't affect the values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg]

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) together, while values around `0` and `1` are pulled apart. A gain value of `0.5` doesn't affect the noise values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg]

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than `1` increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than `1` stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if __Contrast__ is less than `1`) or away from (if __Contrast__ is greater than `1`) medium grey values (around `0.5`).

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

entries.title: Height to Ambient Occlusion
entries.summary: Imagines a sphere for each pixel and determines how occluded that sphere is based on its surroundings.

parameters.label: Space
parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The distance (in the given __Space__) to send rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. Higher values increase the distance you send the rays and provide more accurate measurements, but may slow cooking. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: How many steps (in [buffer space|/copernicus/spaces]) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel's occluded. parameters.heading: Quality

parameters.label: Remap Ramp

entries.title: Knit
entries.summary: Generates a grid of knitted fabric stitches.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Loads a predefined collection of settings for a particular style of knit. Choosing a preset overwrites the parameters below. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/knit_presets.jpg]

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.description: The initial seed for all of the node's randomization, including __Jitter__ and the `Variance` and `Min/Max` modes of __Scale__, __Stretch__, and __Angle__. Changing it produces a new random arrangement.

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.heading: Point Generation
parameters.description: The number of rows of stitches in the grid.

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.heading: Point Generation
parameters.description: The number of columns of stitches in the grid.

parameters.label: Row Offset
parameters.heading: Point Generation
parameters.description: Staggers each successive row sideways by this amount, in [image space|/copernicus/spaces]. Use a small offset to break up the regular grid.

parameters.label: Column Offset
parameters.heading: Point Generation
parameters.description: Staggers each successive column by this amount, in [image space|/copernicus/spaces].

parameters.label: Jitter Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Jitter
parameters.description: Scales how much the `jitter` input layer affects the result. Disabled when nothing is connected to the `jitter` input.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.heading: Jitter
parameters.description: The amount of random positional offset added to each stitch, in [image space|/copernicus/spaces]. Higher values scatter the stitches off their grid positions.

parameters.label: Jitter Type
parameters.heading: Jitter
parameters.description: Toggles per-component jitter controls.

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Jitter
parameters.description: Per-axis multipliers for the __Jitter__ amount, biasing the random offset more along X or Y. Visible when __Jitter Type__ has per-component controls enabled.

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: Controls how much the `scale` input layer affects each stitch's size. Disabled when nothing is connected to the `scale` input.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The base size of each stitch, in [image space|/copernicus/spaces]. Lower values leave gaps between stitches; higher values pack them closer together.

parameters.label: Scale Mode
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: How each stitch's scale is chosen.

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The maximum random deviation from __Scale__ when __Scale Mode__ is `Variance`.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The smallest random scale when __Scale Mode__ is `Min/Max`.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The largest random scale when __Scale Mode__ is `Min/Max`.

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: Scales how much the `stretch` input layer affects the per-stitch stretch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the `stretch` input.

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: How each stitch's stretch is chosen.

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The horizontal stretch factor for each stitch. Values above `1` widen stitches; below `1` narrow them.

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The vertical stretch factor for each stitch. Values above `1` lengthen stitches; below `1` shorten them.

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The maximum random X and Y deviation from __Stretch X__/__Stretch Y__ when __Stretch Mode__ is `Variance`.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The smallest random X and Y stretch when __Stretch Mode__ is `Min/Max`.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The largest random X and Y stretch when __Stretch Mode__ is `Min/Max`.

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: Scales how much the `angle` input layer rotates each stitch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the `angle` input.

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: Scales how much the `direction` input layer orients each stitch. Disabled when nothing is connected to the `direction` input.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The base rotation applied to every stitch, in degrees.

parameters.label: Angle Mode
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: How each stitch's rotation is chosen.

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The maximum random deviation, in degrees, from __Angle__ when __Angle Mode__ is `Variance`.

parameters.label: Min Value
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The smallest random angle, in degrees, when __Angle Mode__ is `Min/Max`.

parameters.label: Max Value
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The largest random angle, in degrees, when __Angle Mode__ is `Min/Max`.

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: When the toggle is on, snaps each stitch's final angle to the nearest multiple of this value, in degrees. Applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Knit Shape Type
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: The style of stitch the node generates.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: The width of each purl stitch. Larger values round out the shape, while smaller values make it more compact and pinched at the ends.

parameters.label: Bulge Scale
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: How far the purl stitch bulges outward in height.

parameters.label: Softness
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: Softens the edges of the stitch, blurring the transition between the stitch and the gaps around it.

parameters.label: Wrinkles
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: The strength of the fine wrinkles added across the stitch surface.

parameters.label: Wrinkle Size
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: The size of the wrinkle detail. Smaller values produce finer wrinkles.

parameters.label: Edge Bend
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: How much the stitch bends along its edges. Negative values bend it the opposite way.

parameters.label: Edge Bend Bias
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: Shifts the balance of the __Edge Bend__ across the stitch, weighting the bend more toward one end than the other. At `0` the bend stays concentrated on one side; higher values push it toward the opposite side, distributing the curvature more evenly.

parameters.label: Bulge Ramp
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: Remaps the cross-sectional bulge profile of the stitch, controlling how its height falls off from the center toward the edges.

parameters.label: Height Ramp
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: Remaps the height profile of the stitch along its length.

parameters.label: Double Knit
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Invert Knit

parameters.label: Weave Width
parameters.heading: Knit Shape

parameters.label: Weave Height

parameters.label: Weave Radius

parameters.label: Fiber Strength

parameters.label: Fiber Cycles
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: The number of fiber twist cycles along each strand.

parameters.label: Fiber Twist
parameters.heading: Knit Shape
parameters.description: The direction and amount of twist in the fiber detail. Negative values twist the opposite way.

parameters.label: Pixel Padding
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: The provided resolution fits the display window. This further expands or erodes the data window to allow overscanning or cropping effects.

parameters.label: Left/Right

parameters.description: The amount to adjust the left and right of the data window.

parameters.label: Top/Bottom
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the top and bottom of the data window.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: The precision of the layer.

parameters.label: Use Fixed Point Storage
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: Stores 8-bit unsigned and 16-bit signed floating point values as fixed point values. This clamps 8-bit fixed point values to the `0` to `1` range and 16-bit fixed point values to the `-1` to `1` range. This parameter applies to only non-ID layers. Storage types are propagated through the network, so nodes often use the same storage type as their inputs. Fixed point storage offers more consistent precision for the same amount of storage compared to floating point, but can only represent values in a limited range.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding

parameters.label: Type Info

parameters.description: The layer's type information. This controls the visualization of the layer in the 3D viewport. See [Type info|/copernicus/glossary#type_info] for more information.

parameters.label: Pixel Scale
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: The number of pixels that fit across one buffer element. This allows for fast proxy cooking without changing measurements specified in pixels. For example, a value of `2` means a `640`x`480` image has only `320`x`240` buffer elements to store the data.

parameters.label: Identity Transform
parameters.heading: Pixel Padding
parameters.description: Resets the layer to the canonical space. This moves the layer to the origin, aligns it with the XY plane, and resets its camera properties to the canonical orthographic projection.

entries.title: Light
entries.summary: Lights a layer given a light direction and normals.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA [channels|Wp:Channel_(digital_image)] to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is `1`, which means this node uses only the new value. See [Mask|/copernicus/glossary#mask] for more information.

parameters.label: Normal Type
parameters.description: The type of the input normal.

parameters.label: Directional
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Directional lights are considered at infinity.  All the light rays will be parallel.  When points are used as a source, the direction from the points to the origin is the direction of the light. Non-directional lights are point lights emanating from the 3d location.

parameters.label: Light Direction
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, this is the direction pointing to the source light. The magnitude doesn't matter. The default value is `0, 0, 1`.

parameters.label: Light Position
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: When no point geometry is provided, this is the center of the light when not directional.

parameters.label: Light Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Point lights have a singularity at their location, so if a point light is inside a volume it will become infinitely bright at that location.  This regularizes the falloff by treating the light to be approximately a sphere of this radius. This will be multiplied by the `pscale` attribute on points.

parameters.label: Light Color
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: The color of the light. The default value is `1, 1, 1`.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: The linear brightness of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: An exponential brightness of the light. Each `1` value higher is `2` times the brightness.

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Angle to rotate the environment map around the Y-axis.

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.heading: Material
parameters.description: A tint for the diffuse colour of the material.  The incoming `source` layer will be multiplied by this to determine the diffuse contribution.  Setting to zero can allow the extraction of the pure reflective or specular components.

parameters.label: Specular
parameters.heading: Material
parameters.description: A specular color for the material.  This will be multiplied by the light color to form the specular color in light models that have specular, such as Phong.

parameters.label: Metallic
parameters.heading: Material
parameters.description: The amount of metallicity of the material.  Increasing metallicity will lower the diffuse value and replace it with a reflected color.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.heading: Material
parameters.description: The lighting model to shade with.

parameters.label: Terminator
parameters.heading: Material
parameters.description: Where the terminator of the Wrapped Diffuse should lie.  `-1` will make it entirely black, `0` will be at the half way part and so match Lambertian shading, and `1` will wrap all the way to the far side of the object.

parameters.label: Exponent
parameters.heading: Material
