parameters.label: Stretch Shape
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: Stretches the shape according to the tile ratio. Turn this off to not stretch the shape.

parameters.label: Basic Shapes
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The list of available elementary algebraic shapes when __Shape Class__ is set to `Basic`. See [Basic Shapes|#basic] for more information.

parameters.label: Markers
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The list of available marker shapes when __Shape Class__ is set to `Marker`. See [Markers|#markers] for more information.

parameters.label: Compound Shapes
parameters.heading: Shape
parameters.description: The list of available complex shapes when __Shape Class__ is set to `Compound`. See [Compound Shapes|#compound] for more information.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The radius of the circle. Use this parameter to control the size of the circle.

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than `1`, the circle becomes an open arc, which can be used to create shapes of a sliced pie.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, and the value is less than `1`, the circle becomes hollowed, which can be used to create ring-like shapes.

parameters.label: Round Ends
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When both Arc and Thickness are turned on, use this to make the end of the ring shape rounded.

parameters.label: Quadratic Circle
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, the circle changes into a quadratic circle shape.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the diamond shape.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the length of the line, which is oriented horizontally at the center. Turn on __Use Points__ next to this parameter if you need to control the exact positions for the start and end points of the line.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the line.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the line.

parameters.label: Add Thickness
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, the start and end thickness of the lines can be controlled by __Start Thickness__ and __End Thickness__.

parameters.label: Start Thickness
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the start point.

parameters.label: End Thickness
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The thickness of the line at the end point.

parameters.label: Bulge
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the thickness at the center of the line. A value of `0` means no bulging. In this mode, only __Start Thickness__ is on to control the same thickness at both ends of the line.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal and vertical size of the rectangle shape.

parameters.label: Round Corners
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, controls the roundness of the corners. With a value of `1` and both horizontal and vertical size is equal, the shape becomes a circle. When this is set to `0`, the rectangle is not rounded. Use __Separate Controls__ next to this parameter to control the roundness for each corner separately.

parameters.label: Separate Controls
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When turned on, the roundness of each corner can be controlled separately.

parameters.label: Top Left
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top left corner of the rectangle. Value of `1` means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of `0` means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Top Right
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the top right corner of the rectangle. Value of `1` means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of `0` means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Bottom Left
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom left corner of the rectangle. Value of `1` means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of `0` means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Bottom Right
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the roundness for the bottom right corner of the rectangle. Value of `1` means the corner is rounded to the maximum, and the value of `0` means that the corner is not rounded.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the polygon shape.

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the polygon. The larger the number the more the shape will resemble a circle.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the spiral shape.

parameters.label: Arc Bend
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls how much each arc length segment should bend towards the center. When this value is set to `0` and the __Number of Arcs__ is set to 4, the arc is a perfect circle.

parameters.label: Number of Arcs
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the number of components the spiral is made of. When __Arc Bend__ is set to `0`, a value of `4` creates a perfect circle.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The size of the radius for a squircle, which is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the shape of the squircle. The value of `2` creates a perfect circle. Values above this will blend the shape more into a square. A value of `1` creates a diamond shape.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the star shape.

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the number of sides for the star. The larger the number, the more the shape will resemble a circle.

parameters.label: Angle Factor
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls how much the center of the sides push towards the center of the shape. The angle factor of `2` will create a regular polygon shape instead of a star.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the trapezoid.

parameters.label: Bottom Length
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the trapezoid.

parameters.label: Top Length
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the top of the trapezoid.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal length at the bottom of the triangle.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the triangle.

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the three corners of the triangle are controlled by __Point0__, __Point1__ and __Point2__ parameters.

parameters.label: Point 0
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the bottom left corner position of the triangle.

parameters.label: Point 1
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the top corner position of the triangle.

parameters.label: Point 2
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the bottom right corner position of the triangle.

parameters.label: Arc
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the amount of distortion applied to the wave. Values closer to `0` will make the wave look like a flat line. The value of `0.5` closer resembles a sine wave, while a value of `1` will fold the wave pattern onto each other.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.heading: Basic Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the size of the wave pattern. Lower values will make smaller patterns.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.id: marker_asterisk_size, marker_check_size, marker_chevron_size, marker_clobber_size, marker_cross_size, marker_infinity_size, marker_ring_size, marker_tag_size, marker_t_size
internal_names: marker_asterisk_size, marker_check_size, marker_chevron_size, marker_clobber_size, marker_cross_size, marker_infinity_size, marker_ring_size, marker_tag_size, marker_t_size
parameters.heading: Markers
parameters.description: The radius of the marker. Use this parameter to control the size of the shape.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the horizontal width of the arch. Increase this value to make the shape wider.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the vertical height of the arch. The value of `0` creates a half-circle.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the overall length of the arrow, both shaft and head. After adjusting the length, use the __Head Ratio__ to control the size of the head relative to the new arrow length.

parameters.label: Use Points
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: When this is turned on, the start and end points of the arrow can be controlled by __Start Point__ and __End Point__ parameters.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the start point of the arrow.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal and vertical position for the end point of the arrow.

parameters.label: Shaft Thickness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the vertical thickness of the shaft of the arrow. Increase this parameter to make the shaft thicker.

parameters.label: Head Thickness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the vertical thickness of the head of the arrow. Increase this parameter to make the head thicker.

parameters.label: Head Ratio
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal ratio between the head and the shaft of the arrow.

parameters.label: Cross Size
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the overall size of the cross shape.

parameters.label: Cross Inset
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the amount to chip away from the corners of a square. When this value is set to `0`, the result is a perfect square. Increasing this value will chip away the shape starting from the corners of the square.

parameters.label: Cross Bevel
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the amount of rounding at the inner corner of the cross.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the egg.

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the roundness of the top edge of the egg. A value of `0` creates an egg shape with a sharp top edge, and increasing this value smooths the top edge. The value of `1` will create a perfect circle shape.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the fishscale shape. This shape is generally used for fishscale-like tile patterns.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The overall size of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Separation
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the arc length of the horseshoe. The value of `0` creates a perfect round shape, closing both ends of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the extent of each end of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the horseshoe.

parameters.label: Outter Radius
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the overall radius of the moon. For a generic moon shape, this parameter should be larger than __Inner Radius__.

parameters.label: Inner Radius
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the radius of the shape that will be cut out from the body of the moon given by __Outter Radius__.

parameters.label: Inner Offset
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The horizontal position of the inner shape given by __Inner Radius__ to control where to cut into the moon.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the octagon-dot shape. This shape is generally used for octagon-dot-like tile patterns.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the overall size of the cross. The value of `0` creates a perfect circle.

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the cross.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: The size of the radius for the vesica.

parameters.label: Roundness
parameters.heading: Compound Shapes
parameters.description: Controls the vertical thickness of the vesica shape. Increasing this value makes the shape more rounded.

parameters.label: Draw As
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: Controls how to draw the shape into the tile.

parameters.label: Shape Edge Filter
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: A filter-scale to apply for filtering the edge of the cutout of a stamped shape.  Zero will make it all or nothing but result in aliasing, `1` will do the expected level of aliasing for the current resolution.

parameters.label: Anti-Aliasing
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: When turned on, it reduces the jagged edges by smoothing the drawn shapes and outlines.

parameters.label: Fade Distance
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: When __Draw As__ is set to __Distance__, this controls the distance from the edge, from which the zero edge value fades into the __Tile Value__ towards the center.

parameters.label: Ramp Type
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: The type of ramp to generate.

parameters.label: Gradient Ramp
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: Draws the shape as a gradient ramp. For more information about using ramps, see [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps].

parameters.label: Outline Width
parameters.heading: Drawing
parameters.description: Controls the thickness of the outline. Increase this value to create a thicker outline.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.heading: Stamping
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. The default value is `Box`. See [Filters|/copernicus/glossary#filter] for more information.

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.heading: Stamping
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together.

parameters.label: Randomize Stamp Order
parameters.heading: Stamping
parameters.description: Randomly varies the point order by which the points are stamped into the image. Change the value if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Tile Value
parameters.heading: Value
parameters.description: Controls the value of the shape inside the tile.  Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to randomize the value per tile.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Value
parameters.description: The maximum allowed variation for the tiles. The value of `0` means no variation from __Tile Value__.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Value
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the __Seed__ if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Background Value
parameters.heading: Value
parameters.description: Controls the value outside of the shape.

parameters.label: Row Offset
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Offsets the horizontal position of each tile with this amount.

parameters.label: Column Offset
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Offsets the vertical position of each tile with this amount.

parameters.label: Row Slide Offset
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Offsets each row horizontally with increasing amount based on the row number. This is used to create brick wall like patterns. To add further offset randomness to each row, change the menu on the right side of this parameter from __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed row offset variation.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the __Seed__ if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Uniform Jitter
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Controls the offset to move the points along the plane of grid. This is used to create positional randomness both horizontally and vertically for each tile.

parameters.label: Horizontal Jitter
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Controls the offset to move the points horizontally along the plane of grid.

parameters.label: Vertical Jitter
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Controls the offset to move the points vertically along the plane of grid.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation for __Uniform Jitter__, __Horizontal Jitter__ and __Vertical Jitter__.

parameters.label: Rotate Pattern
parameters.heading: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the pattern based on the value in degrees.

parameters.label: Rotate Tile
parameters.heading: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates each tile from its center in degrees.

parameters.label: Rotate Variation
parameters.heading: Rotate
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation in degrees. Rotated angles will be between `Rotate Tile - Rotate Variation` and `Rotate Tile + Rotate Variation`.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Rotate
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the __Seed__ if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Checkerboard Rotate
parameters.heading: Rotate
parameters.description: Rotates the tiles that the rotation alternates between `0` and `90` degrees.

parameters.label: Orient Tiles
parameters.heading: Rotate
parameters.description: Sets the orientation attribute for the tiles. This ensures that using __Horizontal Scale__ and __Vertical Scale__ always scale the right edge of the tiles. Especially when the pattern consists of tiles that are both longer than wider and wider than longer.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the scale for the tiles. Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to randomize the scale per tile. The amount of scale depends on the size of each tile. If you need to dilate the tiles with equal amounts use __Inset__ instead.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of `0` means that there is no variation from __Uniform Scale__.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the __Seed__ if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Horizontal Scale
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the horizontal scale for the tiles. Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to randomize the scale per tile.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of `0` means that there is no variation from __Horizontal Scale__.

parameters.label: Vertical Scale
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the vertical scale for the tiles. Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to randomize the scale per tile.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of `0` means that there is no variation from __Vertical Scale__.

parameters.label: Inset
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Dilates the edges of the tiles regardless of the height or width of each tile. Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to randomize the inset per tile.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Size
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of `0` means that there is no variation from __Inset__.

parameters.label: By Tile Order
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: This menu controls the order by which the tiles are removed. If you turned on __Row Offset__ or __Column Offset__ or if you use a custom pattern, the first tile might not be the tile at the bottom left position.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: Controls the number of tiles to be removed. This is a normalized value, `0` does not remove any tiles, while the value of `1` removes all tiles in the pattern. Turn on __Negate Selection__ on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.

parameters.label: Negate Selection
parameters.id: reversethresholdselection, reverseidselection, reverserowidselection, reversecolumnidselection, reversecheckerboard, negate
internal_names: reversethresholdselection, reverseidselection, reverserowidselection, reversecolumnidselection, reversecheckerboard, negate
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: When turned on, instead of deleting anything selected, it will delete anything not selected.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: When __Random__ tile order is selected, controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the __Seed__ if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: When __Shift__ tile order is selected, offsets the tiles that are removed.

parameters.label: Every Nth Tile
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: When this is turned on, deletes every (number of the parameter) tile. Turn on __Negate Selection__ on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.

parameters.label: Every Nth Row
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: When this is turned on, deletes every (number of the parameter) row. Turn on __Negate Selection__ on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.

parameters.label: Every Nth Column
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: When this is turned on, deletes every (number of the parameter) column. Turn on __Negate Selection__ on the right side of this parameter to reverse the selection.

parameters.label: Checkerboard
parameters.heading: Tile Selection
parameters.description: The removal alternates across the pattern.

parameters.label: Split Tiles
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: When this is turned on, tiles can be split according to various rules.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: When this is turned on, tiles that already split have a chance to split again iteratively. This number controls the maximum number of times a tile can be split.

parameters.label: Area Threshold
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: When this is turned on, any tile that has an area smaller than this value will not be split. Use this parameter to limit splitting small tiles.

parameters.label: Split Treshold
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: Controls the number of tiles to be split. This is a normalized value, `0` does not split any tiles, while the value of `1` splits all tiles in the pattern.

parameters.label: Number of Splits
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: When a tile is selected for split, this controls the number of splits for a tile. Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to randomize the number of splits per tile.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of `0` means that there is no variation from __Number of Splits__. While the value of `1` means that a tile can split `1` or __Number of Splits__`-1` times.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: Controls random selection for variation. Change the value of the __Seed__ if the current variation is undesirable.

parameters.label: Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: Controls the split position of the tiles. Set __Uniform__ to __Set Varying__ on the right side of this parameter to further randomize the number of splits per tile.

parameters.label: Variation
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: Sets the maximum allowed variation. The value of `0` means that there is no variation from __Jitter Scale__.

parameters.label: Orient Ratio
parameters.heading: Split Tiles
parameters.description: Controls whenever the tiles should be split horizontally or vertically. The value of `0` means that all tiles are split horizontally, and the value of `1` means that all tiles are split 'vertically'. The value of `0.5` will split tiles both horizontally and vertically in equal ratio.

parameters.label: Hold Last Frame

entries.title: Time Loop
entries.summary: Repeats input frame range to form a looping animation.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Frame Start

Ie, if the loop starts at frame `10`, then the output frame `10` will match the input frame `10`; if you want the output sequence to start at frame `1` use a Time Shift COP.

parameters.label: Frame Length
parameters.description: The length of the sequence to loop, in frames.

parameters.label: Loop Type
parameters.description: How to loop the sequence.

parameters.label: Blend Shape
parameters.description: How to blend in the offset sequence.

entries.title: Time Pack
entries.summary: Combines its input at multiple times into a cable.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Relative: Uses a window that is relative to the requested frame (for example, you can bundle the previous, current, and next frames together). Absolute: Specify a start and end directly.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: When __Method__ is set to __By Frame__, this is the frame number to cook the input on.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, relative, and specified in frames.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, absolute, and specified in frames.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, relative, and specified in seconds.

parameters.label: Range
parameters.description: The range to obtain from the input, absolute, and specified in seconds.

parameters.label: Step
parameters.description: The increment between samples, in frames.

parameters.label: Step
parameters.description: The increment between samples, in seconds.

parameters.label: Add Time As
parameters.description: Whether to add an indication of the sample number to the name as a __Prefix__ or a __Suffix__.

entries.title: Time Shift
entries.summary: Cooks its input at a different time.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: Determines if the input should be cooked at a given frame number or time. Time is measured in seconds.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Determines what mode the shift should operate in. In Absolute Shift you specify an 'origin' and a 'destination' frame (or time); in Relative Shift, you provide an offset in frames (or seconds), and in Custom you provide a value in frames (or seconds) that is designed to be driven directly by an expression.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Custom__, specifies the frame to pull from the input.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Relative Shift__, specifies the offset to apply to the clip. This offset is added to the requested frame to get the frame pulled from the input, so a negative offset will make the input be moved forward in time.

parameters.label: Shift from
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Absolute Shift__, specifies an anchor for a frame that will be moved.

parameters.label: to
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Absolute Shift__, specifies a new frame that the anchored frame will be moved to.

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.description: Whether to round frame numbers back down to integers after other calculations are done.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Custom__, specifies the time to pull from the input.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Relative Shift__, specifies the offset to apply to the clip. This offset is added to the requested frame to get the frame pulled from the input, so a negative offset will make the input be moved forward in time.

parameters.label: Shift from
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Absolute Shift__, specifies an anchor for a time that will be moved.

parameters.label: to
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Absolute Shift__, specifies a new time that the anchored time will be moved to.

parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.description: Optional clamping of the __Frame__/__Time__ value to retrieve. The choices are: __None__, __Clamp to First__ (uses only the start frame/time value), __Clamp to Last__ (uses only the end frame/time value),  or __Clamp to Both__.

parameters.label: Start/End Frame
parameters.description: The frame values used to perform clamping. This parameter is available when __Method__ is set to __By Frame__, and __Clamp__ is not __None__.

parameters.label: Start/End Time
parameters.description: The time values used to perform clamping. This parameter is available when __Method__ is set to __By Time__, and __Clamp__ is not __None__.

entries.title: Triplanar
entries.summary: Generates a texture by projecting X, Y, and Z textures onto the position layer.

entries.title: Wrangle
entries.summary: Runs a VEX snippet to modify layer values.

parameters.label: Volumes to Write to
parameters.description: Only modify layers if their names match this pattern. The default pattern allows any layer to be modified. You can speed up the node by only listing layers that are _actually_ modified by the snippet. For example, in the following snippet, only the `density` layer is modified. The `temperature` layer is not modified, only read. {{{ #!vex @density = @temperature; }}} However, for obscure reasons, the node will both modify `density` and _copy_ `temperature`. This uses time and memory. To prevent this, you could set this parameter to `density` to prevent the node from copying `temperature`. Of course, this requires that you explicitly manage the list of writable layers.

parameters.label: Evaluation Node Path
parameters.description: VEX functions like `ch()` usually evaluate with respect to this node. Providing a path here can override where the path search starts from.  This is useful for embedding in a digital asset where you would like the top level digital asset to be the search root.

parameters.label: Export Parameters
parameters.description: This pattern can be used to override the export option on the VEX shader to avoid writing to certain volumes.  The pattern matches the VEX parameter, not the bound volume.  The volume will still be bound for reading.

parameters.label: Rename Wires Using Output Labels
parameters.description: When this toggle is enabled, name of each output wire is set based on its respective port label. Otherwise, wire names are propagated from inputs. Turn this option on if you'd like to discard incoming wire names and harden new ones for the downstream network to use.

parameters.label: Type

parameters.label: Input Index

parameters.description: Geometry inputs can be referred to by this index.  For example, if it is `2`, then to read the number of points `npoints(2)` would be used.  `0` is reserved for the implicit layer input.

entries.title: Bake Geometry Textures
entries.summary: Generates textures by baking between a low-resolution and high-resolution mesh at interactive speeds.

parameters.label: Tracer
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracer to use. This is an automatic menu that shows only available options based on your hardware.

parameters.label: Tracing Mode
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The tracing mode that the baker utilizes.

parameters.label: UDIM Override
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: Select a UDIM to bake, which overrides the UDIM context option.

parameters.label: Face Visibility Culling
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The method used to handle secondary rays that interact with the geometry. This can allow floaters on the geometry to be projected onto the low-resolution map without casting a shadow.

parameters.label: Sample Multiplier
parameters.heading: Tracer
parameters.description: The amount to multiply against the Sample parameters, such as __Occlusion Samples__ and __Thickness Samples__. This acts as a general quality scale. For example, a __Sample Multiplier__ of `0.5` and __Occlusion Samples__ of `256` bakes occlusion at `128`.

parameters.label: Auto Generate Cage
parameters.heading: Auto Generate Cage
parameters.description: Creates a duplicate mesh of the low-resolution mesh. This automatically generates a cage mesh internally instead of requiring a `cage` input.

parameters.label: Cage Offset
parameters.heading: Auto Generate Cage
parameters.description: How far the duplicate mesh peaks out from the normals of the original low-resolution mesh.

parameters.label: Soften Cage
parameters.heading: Auto Generate Cage
parameters.description: Facets the geometry before applying the __Cage Offset__. A soft cage isn't faceted and ensures a seamless result across sharp edges, but can cause projection errors and skewed detail as the normals are averaged. An unsoftened cage (which is faceted) can fix this projection skewing, but can cause missing detail capture on sharp edges.

parameters.label: Normals
parameters.heading: Setup
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing normals. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have normals.

parameters.label: Tangents
parameters.heading: Setup
parameters.description: How the node deals with low-resolution geometry that's missing tangent attributes. For texture baking to work, the low-resolution mesh should have tangent attributes.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: The attribute to use for UV unwrapping and rasterization. This can be a vertex or point.

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: The amount to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-resolution mesh when rays are sent from the low-resolution mesh to the scene. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-resolution mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.

parameters.label: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: Lets you control which primitives are visible when computing ray tracing effects like occlusion and curvature. This matches primitives between the low-resolution and high-resolution geometry and isolates them in their own pocket dimension, which can be used to prevent intersection errors. If a ray hits an object that doesn't belong to the current matched piece, it's ignored. This causes a rebake and changes the bake results.

parameters.label: Piece Attribute
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: The primitive piece attribute to use to identify the different pieces across the low-resolution, high-resolution, and cage.

parameters.label: Include Pieces
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: The sets to always include in the bake. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching.

parameters.label: Exclude Pieces
parameters.heading: Match Pieces by Name
parameters.description: The sets to always exclude from the bake. This happens after the include pieces are gathered. This uses standard Houdini pattern matching. For example, if your include is `*` but your exclude is `hat`, the baker bakes every set available except `hat`.

parameters.label: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Fills empty areas of the image using colors at the edges of non-empty areas. This is a post-process that fixes darker pixel values at the edges of UV seams, and can produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures.

parameters.label: Exterior
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: The method used to set the pixels beyond the edge padding.

parameters.label: Edge Padding
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: The distance (in image coordinates) to directly copy pixel values into the exterior.

parameters.label: Edge Offset
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: When reading the original value to copy outwards for edge padding, the value exactly at the edge padding may already have exterior color incorporated. This is the distance (in image coordinates) to backtrack and read clean values for extrapolation.

parameters.label: Exclude Alpha from UV Fill
parameters.heading: Enable UV Boundary Filling
parameters.description: Turns off UV filling on the `alpha` map. Adding UV filling to `alpha` often results in a fully white output.

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.heading: Alignment
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.

parameters.label: Tangent Normal
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Tangent Normal__ map. When off, the `normal` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Normal Space
parameters.heading: Tangent Normal
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from `-1` to `1`. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from `0` to `1`.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Rounded Edge Normal__ map. When off, the `edgenormal` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal Space
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: The normal type the layer outputs as. The natural way to represent normals and how they're represented in geometry is to use signed normals. The red, green, and blue channel can store the x, y, and z components of the normal and range from `-1` to `1`. However, historically GPUs and photoediting software don't support negative ranges, so normal maps in image files are usually stored in an offset format where they have values from `0` to `1`.

parameters.label: Rounded Samples
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Rounded Edge Normal__. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Rounded Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.heading: Rounded Edge Normal
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold are assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.heading: Alignment
parameters.description: Whether to record the world space position in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.

parameters.label: World Normal
parameters.heading: World Normal
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __World Normal__ map. When off, the `worldnormal` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: World Normal Space
parameters.heading: World Normal
parameters.description: How to represent the normal map.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Position__ map. When off, the `position` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Position Space
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: How to represent the position map.

parameters.label: Bounding Box
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: When the __Position__ is stored, this is how the position is represented.

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Ambient Occlusion__ map. When off, the `occlusion` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Occlusion__. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Occlusion Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing __Occlusion__. A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Curvature__ map. When off, the `curvature` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Curvature__. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Curvature Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Smaller values (which create smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (which represent greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Edge__ map. When off, the `edge` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Edge__.  If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Edge Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: The types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.

parameters.label: Cusp Angle
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and don't appear in the __Edge__ map.

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Cavity__ map. When off, the `cavity` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Cavity__. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Cavity Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: Blends between a full cavity contrast (`0`) and a flat result (`1`).

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Thickness
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Thickness__ map. When off, the `thickness` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.heading: Thickness
parameters.description: The number of indirect rays used when computing __Thickness__. If the resulting AOV is noisy, increase __Thickness Samples__ to reduce noise.

parameters.label: Invert Thickness Map
parameters.heading: Thickness
parameters.description: Inverts the __Thickness__ map so that thinner areas create darker values and thicker areas create brighter values.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Height__ map. When off, the `height` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Height Space
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Height bakes the true displacement between the low-resolution and high-resolution. This distance may be miniscule so the output image can appear nearly entirely black, which may not be useful when used in masking or shaders so may require manual remapping later. Set this to `Custom` to remap the height map.

parameters.label: Inner Distance
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the inner distance to `0.0`.

parameters.label: Outer Distance
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Remaps the data within the height map from the outer distance to `1.0`.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.heading: Alpha
parameters.description: Turns on baking of the __Alpha__ map. When off, the `alpha` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Mask Out High Resolution Mesh
parameters.heading: Alpha
parameters.description: Checks for any valid hits on the high-resolution mesh and creates an alpha mask from this, rather than the low-resolution UV map.

parameters.label: Quick Setups
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: Add a geometry attribute to bake.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: Turns on the Position map's baking, which bakes the world position values to the RGB components of the layer. When off, the `position` output is a [Null|Node:cop/null] layer.

parameters.label: Attribute Name
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to rasterize. This must match the attribute present on the geometry. This can be a Point, Vertex, or Primitive.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Custom Attributes
parameters.description: The [output type|/copernicus/glossary#data_type] for the rasterized attribute. To be rasterized, an attribute must either be an integer or a float of four or less components.

parameters.label: Normalize Gathered Light

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.description: The vertical frequency of the `a` wave and the horizontal frequency of the `b` wave. Higher values zoom outward to increase how often the `a` wave repeats vertically and the `b` wave repeats horizontally. Lower values zoom inward to decrease how often these waves repeat vertically and horizontally. This is the primary frequency.

parameters.label: Frequency Anisotropy
parameters.description: The horizontal frequency of the `a` wave and the vertical frequency of the `b` wave. Higher values increase how often the `a` wave repeats horizontally and the `b` wave repeats vertically. Lower values decrease how often these waves repeat horizontally and vertically. This is the secondary frequency scale for the waves and a logarithmic adjustment. Each unit difference doubles or halves the actual frequency.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.description: The size (in [image space|/copernicus/spaces]) of the waves to create. This controls the distance over which the __Frequency__ is measured, which determines the wave size that repeats over the image space. parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

parameters.heading: Master
parameters.description: Applies the master adjustments to the combined image after the __Shadow__, __Midtone__, and __Highlight__ color corrections.

parameters.label: Master Add
parameters.heading: Master
parameters.description: The amount to offset the incoming values. Positive values brighten the image and negative values darken the image. This affects the pixels of all values.

parameters.label: Master Mult
parameters.heading: Master
parameters.description: The amount to scale the incoming values. Values greater than `1` brighten the image, while values between `0` and `1` darken the image. This also affects pixels at the white point (value of `1`).

parameters.label: Master Gamma
parameters.heading: Master
parameters.description: Take the incoming values to the specified power. Values greater than `1` often darken the image, while values between `0` and `1` brighten the image. This doesn't change pixels at the white or black points (values of `1` and `0`, respectively).

parameters.label: Master Contrast
parameters.heading: Master
parameters.description: Adjust the pixels depending on how they compare to the middle gray value, which boosts the distance of each pixel from `0.5`. Larger values increase this boosting effect. A value of `1` results in no adjustment and a value of `0` destroys any contrast in the image, producing `0.5` for every pixel.

parameters.label: Shadow
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: Adds the shadow component of the image to the final result. This component's weight is calculated as `exp(-7*t^2)`, where `t` is the original color.

parameters.label: Midtone
parameters.heading: Midtone
parameters.description: Adds the midtone component of the image to the final result. This component's weight is calculated as `exp(-7*(1-t)^2)`, where `t` is the original color.

parameters.label: Highlight
parameters.heading: Highlight
parameters.description: Adds the highlight component of the image to the final result. This component's weight is equal to `1-exp(-7*t^2)-exp(-7*(1-t)^2)`, where `t` is the original color.

parameters.description: White areas can be pushed beyond one, which is reasonable for HDR images, but if applying contrast to a mask it may be desireable to limit the growth to 1.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: RGBA layers are often premultiplied, so using a fixed pivot that doesn't take the alpha into consideration will cause low coverage areas to be considered dark.  This option will implicitly un-premultiply, contrast, and then pre-multiply, so the pivot works as expected.

entries.title: Convolve 3x3
entries.summary: Convolves a layer by a 3x3 kernel.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA [channels|Wp:Channel_(digital_image)] to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is `1`, which means this node uses only the new value. See [Mask|/copernicus/glossary#mask] for more information.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Multiplicative
parameters.description: The amount to scale all coefficients of the kernel. Use this value to set the normalization constant to make the kernel values integral. This value doesn't apply if __Normalize Kernel__ is on. Use the following dimensions to additionally scale the coefficients by the distance between samples used for the convolution. The samples are the buffer elements in a 3x3 neighborhood around the currently processed buffer element. See [/copernicus/spaces] for more information about buffer space.

parameters.label: Top
parameters.heading: Multiplicative
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the `(x-1, y+1)`, `(x, y+1)`, and `(x+1, y+1)` pixels.

parameters.label: Middle
parameters.heading: Multiplicative
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the `(x-1, y)`, `(x, y)`, and `(x+1, y)` pixels.

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.heading: Multiplicative
parameters.description: The three coefficients to multiply with the `(x-1, y-1)`, `(x, y-1)`, and `(x+1, y-1)` pixels.

parameters.label: Normalize Kernel
parameters.heading: Multiplicative
parameters.description: Normalizes the kernel by the sum of all coefficients. This prevents the application of the kernel from brightening or darkening the image. The node doesn't normalize the kernel if the kernel sums to zero (for example, as it does when you use the `Outline` [recipe|/network/recipes]).

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: The amount to scale all additive values. Use the following dimensions to additionally scale the additive values by the distance between samples used for the convolution. The samples are the buffer elements in a 3x3 neighborhood around the currently processed buffer element. See [/copernicus/spaces] for more information about buffer space.

parameters.label: Top
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: The three values to add to the `(x-1, y+1)`, `(x, y+1)`, and `(x+1, y+1)` pixels.

parameters.label: Middle
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: The three values to add to the `(x-1, y)`, `(x, y)`, and `(x+1, y)` pixels.

parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: The three values to add to the `(x-1, y-1)`, `(x, y-1)`, and `(x+1, y-1)` pixels.

parameters.label: Combine Operation
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: Mixes each active pixel in the 3x3 neighborhood together to create the output. This combination occurs after each pixel is scaled by the coefficent and has added additional values. This parameter considers only the __Active Terms__ that are on.

parameters.label: Active Terms
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: Controls which pixels in the 3x3 neighborhood are active and contribute to the final result. Terms you turn off aren't read from the input layer, which slightly increases performance. Off terms also don't contribute to the __Combine Operation__ or have their weights included in the normalization.

parameters.label: Clamp Below Zero
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: Clamps final resulting values below zero to zero before mixing these pixel values into the original image.

parameters.label: Clamp Above One
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: Clamps final resulting values above one to one before mixing these pixel values into the original image.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.heading: Additive
parameters.description: Un-premultiplies the RGBA layers before applying the kernel, and then premultiplies the RGBA layers after applying the kernel. Turn this off when you blur the alpha and color (RGB) layers, because blur operations require premultiplied space.

parameters.label: Center Pivot on Shape

parameters.label: Blend Method

parameters.label: Filter

parameters.label: Wrap Mode

parameters.label: Tile Size

parameters.label: Stamp Color

parameters.label: Color Ramp
parameters.heading: Stamping

parameters.label: Uniform Alpha
parameters.heading: Stamping
parameters.description: The amount of black (`0`) and white (`1`) by which to multiply the stamp's __Background Alpha__.

parameters.label: Change per Copy
parameters.heading: Stamping
parameters.description: A variable scale for the stamp, which can create an alpha change for each copy. This is an additive, not a multiplier.

parameters.label: Alpha Ramp
parameters.heading: Stamping
parameters.description: Applies a ramp over all copies and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's alpha. When on, this turns __Change per Copy__ off. See [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps] for more information.

parameters.label: Background Color

entries.title: Curve 3D
entries.summary: Lets you interactively draw Bézier curves using tools similar to 2D illustration programs, as well as polylines and NURBS.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.description: Type of curve primitives to create.

parameters.label: Order
parameters.description: The order of the NURBS or Bézier curve. Higher order curves give more control vertices and smoother curve interpolation between on-curve knots. However, you should generally use the default order (4) unless you have a reason for needing higher-order curves. Note that changing the __Order__ changes the interpretation of all existing curves to use the new order value. The drawing mode is optimized for cubic Bézier curves (__Order__ set to 4, the default). For higher-order Bézier curves, the drawing interface is the same as for cubic Bézier curves, but after you drag out the tangent handles, the node creates _more than one_ tangent handle on the trailing side of the point. It creates the extra control points in line, so they have the same shape as a cubic Bézier would, but after you're finished drawing you can use the Edit mode to move the extra control points independently. For NURBS, the drawing interface is always the same: placing points by clicking.

parameters.label: Reinterpret Curves as Current Type and Order
parameters.label_norm: reinterpret curves as current type and order
parameters.description: When on, all existing curves are converted by reinterpretting the curve points as the current __Primitive Type__ and __Order__. When converting curves to NURBs or Bezier, the last point on the curve may be repeated to fully define the curve. When off, only newly created curves are given the current __Primitive Type__ and __Order__.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: The mode that the tool is currently in.

parameters.label: Delete Selected Points
parameters.description: Removes the selected point(s), if any.

parameters.label: Join Selected Points
parameters.description: Joins two selected vertices together into a single vertex. If the two selected vertices are on the same curve, the result is one closed curve. If the vertices are from different curves, the result is one curve instead of two.

parameters.label: Cut Curves at Selected Points
parameters.description: Cuts the curve at each selected point. After the cut, each selected point becomes an end point. Any branches are also split prior to cutting curve vertices.

parameters.label: Add Segment Between Selected Endpoints
parameters.description: Joins the two selected vertices with a straight line. If the two selected vertices are on the same curve, the result is one closed curve. If the vertices are from different curves, the result is one curve instead of two, with a segment added between the end vertices.

parameters.label: Delete Segments Between Selected Points
parameters.description: Removes any selected segments, possibly splitting curves around selected segments.

parameters.label: Fuse Branch
parameters.description: Fuse all selected points into a single branch point containing all the vertices from the selected points.

parameters.label: Split Branch
parameters.description: Split the selected branch points to create separate points for each vertex of the branched point.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Corner
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a corner point.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Smooth
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a smooth point, possibly snapping handles to be aligned.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Balanced
parameters.description: Turns an anchor point into a balanced point, possibly snapping handles to be aligned.

parameters.label: Retract Tangents at Selected Points
parameters.description: Collapses the bezier handles down into a sharp bezier corner point.

parameters.label: Expand Tangents at Selected Points
parameters.description: Expands out the bezier handles to be intractable, if the selected point is collapsed.

parameters.label: Make Segments Between Selected Points Straight
parameters.label_norm: make segments between selected points straight
parameters.description: Collapses the handles on the ends of the selected segments, converting the segment into a straight line.

parameters.label: Close Selected Curves
parameters.description: Closes all curves with at least one point selected.

parameters.label: Create Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Turns the selected corner points into rounded corners.

parameters.label: Remove Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Turns the selected rounded corners into ordinary corners.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Auto
parameters.description: Makes selected points into auto points. Bezier curves are automatically computed to interpolate any auto points.

parameters.label: Make Selected Points Manual
parameters.description: Makes selected auto points into non-auto points and freezes the local interpolated curve so that it can be manually edited.

parameters.label: Reverse
parameters.description: Reverse selected curves.

parameters.label: Reset Operations
parameters.description: Resets all modeling operations that have been done. Resets the output geometry to the input geometry.

parameters.label: Snap Tangents when Fusing Ends in Draw Mode
parameters.label_norm: snap tangents when fusing ends in draw mode
parameters.description: Whether to snap the final tangent when fusing curves together or closing curves by clicking on the end point of another curve or the opposite end point of the same curve. Dragging out the tangent while fusing doesn't snap the tangents.

parameters.label: Approximate Shape on Delete
parameters.description: Approximates the previous curve shape on a point delete.

parameters.label: Approximate End Tangents
parameters.description: Prioritizes keeping the end derivatives of a segment when approximating the previous curve shape on a point delete.

parameters.label: Soft Transform Radius
parameters.description: The soft transform radius when soft transforms are on. Soft transforms are used when doing operations that manually move anchor points, including dragging points in edit and draw mode, dragging segments in polygons or NURBs curves, or bezier segments adjacent to rounded corners or auto points. This radius is relative to the distance along the backbone polygon of the given curve. For Polygons this is equivalent to the surface distance along the curve. For NURBS Curves this is equivalent to the distance along the control polygon of the curve. And for Bezier Curves, this is equivalent to the distance along the polygon that results from reinterpreting the curve as a polygon. In particular, in this polygon, auto points and rounded corners are collapsed to a single point, which can result in distances along the curve being slightly different than expected when looking at a curve.

parameters.label: Corner Points Group
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the corner points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the corner points from this node.

parameters.label: Smooth Points Group
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the smooth points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the smooth points from this node.

parameters.label: Auto Points Group
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the group to create that contains the auto points. When chaining curve nodes, this can be used to ensure later curve nodes pick up the auto points from this node.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name to place in the name attribute on all created geometry. Defaults to the name of the SOP ($OS).

parameters.label: X Axis
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the __X Axis__ of the orientations created on points in the __Orient Mode__. When active, geometry showing the x axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.

parameters.label: Y Axis
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the __Y Axis__ of the orientations created on points in the __Orient Mode__. When active, geometry showing the y axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.

parameters.label: Z Axis
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the attribute to create to store the __Z Axis__ of the orientations created on points in the __Orient Mode__. When active, geometry showing the x axis is present in the viewport. The density and scale of guide gnomons showing the axes can be controlled in the state parameters.

parameters.label: Orient
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The name of the orient attribute to create. The orient attribute created in the __Orient Mode__ is stored in this attribute. When active, guide geometry showing the orient attribute is present in the viewport. In the state parameters, you can toggle drawing the orient guide geometry, as well as control the density and scale of guide gnomons.

parameters.label: Tangent Type
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The method used to determine the implicit curve tangent. This tangent is used to parallel transport the orient attributes from the target points along the curves.

parameters.label: Align with Curve Tangent
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: When on, aligns orient attribute values with the curve tangent. When off, orient attribute values on target points are aligned with the value in __Tangent__.

parameters.label: Target Orientations
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The target orientations specified on points along curves. When determining the orient attribute, these target orientations are placed on curves, and a parallel transport is used between target points to create an orient attribute that smoothly blends between target orientations. For any curves that do not have any target orientations, a default orient is placed on the first point of the curve, achieved by rotating the vector (0,0,1) onto the curve tangent.

parameters.label: Enable Target Orientation
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: Toggles this target orientation.

parameters.label: Point
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The point to place the target orientation on.

parameters.label: Up
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The target up vector. Target up vectors are made perpendicular to the curve tangent if __Align with Curve Tangent__ is on, and are otherwise made perpendicular to the specified __Tangent__ vector.

parameters.label: Tangent
parameters.heading: Output
parameters.description: The target tangent vector. When __Align with Curve Tangent__ is off, this parameter is available to set alongside the __Up__ vector, allowing you to fully specify the orientation of this target __Point__, without being constrained by the curve tangent.

parameters.label: Active Points
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: Points used in the current operation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: The amount to translate the selected points or the selected handle end point by.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: The amount to rotate (in degrees) the selected points with respect to the pivot.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: The amount to scale the selected points with respect to the pivot.

parameters.label: Corner Points
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the corner points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through __Corner Points Group__, to pick up the corner points from previous nodes.

parameters.label: Smooth Points
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the smooth points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through __Smooth Points Group__, to pick up the smooth points from previous nodes.

parameters.label: Auto Points
parameters.heading: Current Operation
parameters.description: A group parameter specifying the auto points. When chaining multiple curve nodes, this can be set with an input group, such as that created through __Auto Points Group__, to pick up the auto points from previous nodes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: The position of the pivot, before any further translations.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Specifies the axis to align the transform handle with. Upon finishing any operation with the transform handle, it snaps back to this rotation to begin a new edit. Is specified as three angles in degrees representing the amount to rotate around each axis.

parameters.label: Fixed Pivot
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Whether to keep the pivot position the same when selecting new points. If off, the pivot resets to the center of the bounding box of the selected points on a selection change.

parameters.label: View Rounded Corners
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Whether to view rounded corners. When off, rounded corners are all shown with a radius of 0.0. The topology of created curves is not changed when this toggle is off.

parameters.label: Round Corner Points
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners
parameters.description: A string parameter encoding the rounded corners and their radii.

parameters.label: Round Corner Radius
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Sets the radius of the selected rounded corners.

parameters.label: Bake Selected Rounded Corners
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Convert selected rounded corners into regular bezier segments.

parameters.label: Show Rounded Corner Widget
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Whether to show a widget to modify rounded corner radii.

parameters.label: Show Rounded Corner Labels
parameters.heading: Rounded Corners
parameters.description: Whether to show labels for the radii on the rounded corner widgets. These labels are off if __Show Rounded Corner Widget__ is off.
