entries.title: Scatter on Curves
entries.summary: Scatters input stamps along an input curve using randomization controls.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the node outputs. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: The distribution mode for how to scatter the stamps along the curve.

parameters.label: Segment Length
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: When __Distribution__ is `Distance`, this is the maximum segment length of resulting edges.

parameters.label: Maximum Segments
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: When __Distribution__ is `Distance`, this is the maximum number of edges.

parameters.label: Treat Input Curve As
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: How to inteprolate the input curves.

parameters.label: Density Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: When __Distribution__ is `Scatter`, this is the amount of the `density` input's mono value to mix in with the __Density__ value. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: When __Distribution__ is `Scatter`, this is the amount to scale the density of the points. This parameter doesn't apply when __Max Count__ is on.

parameters.label: Max Count
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: When __Distribution__ is `Scatter` or `By Count`, this is the amount of points to generate.

parameters.label: Relaxation
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: When __Distribution__ is `Scatter` or `By Count`, this relaxes points by pushing them away from each other to avoid clumping. More relaxation iterations result in further separation between the points. Relaxation is done gradually to avoid chaotic behavior and allow control over how much relaxation takes place.

parameters.label: Scatter Seed
parameters.heading: Scattering
parameters.description: The seed value for all randomization that deals with stamp placement. This includes jitter, density, angle and direction, scale, and stretch.

parameters.label: Scale Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The amount of the `scale` input's mono value to mix in with the __Scale__ value, which impacts the stamps' scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps in image space. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the scale of the stamps.

parameters.label: Scale Variance
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale. This is applied as a post-process. If __Scale__ is `1` and __Scale Variance__ `1` for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from `0.5 * Scale` to `2.0 * Scale`.

parameters.label: Min Scale
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original __Scale__. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Scale
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original __Scale__. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Apply Scale along Curve
parameters.heading: Scale
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps] for more information.

parameters.label: Cut Curves by Relative Arc Length
parameters.label_norm: cut curves by relative arc length
parameters.heading: Curve
parameters.description: Solves for the actual location halfway along the curve as measured by distance. This is useful since curves have a parameterization that doesn't match the actual distance along the curve. For example, a curve of `0.5` isn't halfway along the curve but halfway along its parameterization.

parameters.label: Start Point
parameters.heading: Curve
parameters.description: The start point in [image space|/copernicus/spaces] of the curve.

parameters.label: End Point
parameters.heading: Curve
parameters.description: The end point in image space of the curve.

parameters.label: Smoothing
parameters.heading: Curve
parameters.description: The amount of smoothing to apply to the curve.

parameters.label: Mirror Stamps
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset
parameters.description: Creates a mirrored version of the stamps on the other side of the curve. Use the dropdown menu to set the mirror's behavior.

parameters.label: From Curve
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset
parameters.description: The amount to perpendicularly offset the stamps from the tangent of the curve.

parameters.label: Mirrored From Curve
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset
parameters.description: The amount to perpendicularly offset the mirrored stamps from the tangent of the curve.

parameters.label: Jitter
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset
parameters.description: The amount of random position offset to add to each stamp's position on the grid.

parameters.label: Offset along Curve
parameters.heading: Mirror and Offset
parameters.description: The amount to offset the stamp placement along the curve.

parameters.label: Angle Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The amount of the `angle` input's mono value to mix in with the __Angle__ value, which impacts the degree of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Direction Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The amount of the `direction` input's UV value to mix in with the __Angle__ value, which impacts the direction of the stamps' angles. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Angles Relative to Curve Direction
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: Accounts for the curve's usual direction when calculating the angle.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The angle in degrees to rotate each stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set the method of post-processing that applies to the angle of the stamps.

parameters.label: Angle Variance
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the angles. This is applied as a post-process. For example, a value of `30` makes each stamp have a random offset between `-30` degrees and `30` degrees.

parameters.label: Min Angle
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The minimum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original __Angle__. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Angle
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The maximum degree that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original __Angle__. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Increment per Stamp
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: The amount of angle increase for each stamp along the curve. For example, if __Increment per Stamp__ is `10` and your curve has 36 points, each stamp progressively rotates more and the end stamp makes a full rotation.

parameters.label: Round to Multiples
parameters.heading: Angle
parameters.description: Snaps all stamps to a specified angle. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Stretch Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The amount of the `stretch` input's UV value to mix in with the __Stretch X__ and __Stretch Y__ values, which impacts the XY scale. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stretch Mode
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The method of post-processing that applies to the non-uniform scale (stretch) of the stamps.

parameters.label: Stretch X
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the X-axis in image space.

parameters.label: Stretch Y
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The scale of the stamps along the Y-axis in image space.

parameters.label: Stretch Variance
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the scale of the X and Y-axes. This is applied as a post-process. If __Stretch X__ is `1`, __Stretch Y__ is ` 0`, and __Stretch Variance__ is `1, 0` for example, this represents a 100% range in sizes. This means the output stamps have a random scale from `0.5 * Stretch x` to `2.0 * Stretch x`.

parameters.label: Min Stretch
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The minimum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original __Stretch X__ and __Stretch Y__. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Max Stretch
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: The maximum value that the stamps can randomly select, and then multiply against the original __Stretch X__ and __Stretch Y__. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Stretch along Curve
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: Applies two ramps along the curve to scale stamps along the X and Y-axes.

parameters.label: Stretch X along Curve
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale along the X-axis. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps] for more information.

parameters.label: Stretch Y along Curve
parameters.heading: Stretch
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve and multiplies the ramp by the stamp's scale along the Y-axis. The curve of the ramp determines which stamps to scale. See [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps] for more information.

parameters.label: Blend Method
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: When mulitple stamps overlap, this controls how they blend together.

parameters.label: Use Sort Layer
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: Multiply the __Depth-Sorted Over__ or __Unsorted Depth-Weighted Over__ sort values by the `sort` input's value.

parameters.label: Apply Sort along Curve
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: Applies a ramp along the curve to sort the stamps. See [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps] for more information.

parameters.label: Color Seed
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp color and alpha.

parameters.label: Color Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The amount of the `color` input's RGB value to mix in with the __Stamp Color__ value, which impacts the stamps' tint. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stamp Color
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: A tint for the stamp. Use the dropdown menu to set how the color applies to the stamps.

parameters.label: Hue
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the hue. This is applied as a post-process. If set to `30` for example, the stamps randomly pick a hue offset from the range of `0` to `30`.

parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the saturation. This is applied as a post-process. If set to `0.5` for example, the stamps randomly pick a saturation from the range of `0` to `0.5`.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the value. This is applied as a post-process. If set to `0.5` for example, the stamps randomly pick a value from the range of `0` to `0.5`.

parameters.label: Alpha Layer Mask
parameters.heading: Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of the `alpha` input's mono value to mix in with the __Stamp Alpha__ value, which impacts the stamps' alpha. Higher values mix in more of the input's value. Lower values mix in less of the input's value.

parameters.label: Stamp Alpha
parameters.heading: Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of black (`0`) and white (`1`) by which to multiply the stamp's alpha. Use the dropdown menu to set how the alpha applies to the stamps.

parameters.label: Alpha Variance
parameters.heading: Alpha
parameters.description: The amount of random variance to apply to the alpha. This is applied as a post-process.

parameters.label: Background Color
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: The initial background color of the space around the stamps.

parameters.label: Background Alpha
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: The initial background alpha of the space around the stamps.

parameters.label: Selection Mode
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection
parameters.description: The stamps to place in the image. When no `stamps` input is wired in, this parameter applies to the default star pattern.

parameters.label: Limit Selection
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection
parameters.description: Limits the maximum number of stamps that the node uses.

parameters.label: Select Seed
parameters.heading: Stamp Selection
parameters.description: The seed value for randomization that deals with stamp selection.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: The method used to sample the image. See [Filters|/copernicus/glossary#filter] for more information.

parameters.label: Wrap Mode
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: The wrapping behavior of the stamps.

parameters.label: Tile Size
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: When __Wrap Mode__ is `Auto` or `On`, this is the size (in image space) of the region to wrap into. The resultant image periodically repeats in this size.

parameters.label: Focus Plane Blur

parameters.label: Focus Ramp

parameters.label: Radius

parameters.label: Gain

parameters.label: Resolution

parameters.label: Resample Input

parameters.label: Color Correct
parameters.heading: Color Correct

parameters.label: Brightness threshold
parameters.heading: Color Correct
parameters.description: The threshold that a pixel's luminance value must be above for the pixel to brighten.

parameters.label: Brightness Blur
parameters.heading: Color Correct
parameters.description: The amount to blur the brightness mask, which smooths the transition between pixels in and out of the threshold.

parameters.label: Brightness

parameters.label: Saturation Threshold

parameters.label: Saturation Blur

parameters.label: Gamma

parameters.label: Depth Blend

parameters.description: Applies depth to blend the original layer with the out of focus layer.

parameters.label: Min

parameters.label: Max

entries.summary: Denoises an input layer.

parameters.description: The library to use to denoise the image.

parameters.label: Auxiliary Planes Are Clean
parameters.description: Sets the _cleanAux_ filter parameter for further improving quality when the auxilary feature (albedo, normal) planes are noise-free, as described in the OIDN documentation.

parameters.label: Prefilter Auxiliary Planes
parameters.description: Whether to prefilter the albedo and normal auxiliary planes before denoising the image planes. While prefiltering generates better results and should be used for final frames, it will hurt performance and thus should be turned off when doing previews or interactive rendering.

You can use this option to minimize GPU memory requirements, for example when denoising large images or rendering on GPU-enabled farm machines.

parameters.label: Signature

entries.title: Distort
entries.summary: Distorts an input layer.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures |/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Border
parameters.description: The sampling behavior outside of the incoming layer's boundaries. Automatically uses the layer's border property. See [Border types|/copernicus/glossary#border] for more information.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.description: The filtering method used for sampling the source layer. Consider using one of the area filters (__Box__ and later) if the distortion shrinks large regions and you notice noise. See [Filters |/copernicus/glossary#filters] for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. A value of `1` means this node uses only the new value. The default value is `1`. See [Mask|/copernicus/glossary#mask] for more information.

parameters.label: Direction Type
parameters.description: Specifies the direction in which to distort the layer. This can be an angle in degrees (`Angle`) or a two-component vector representing the X and Y directions in image space (`Coordinates`).

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.description: Specifies the X and Y directions in image space when __Direction Type__ is set to `Coordinates`.

parameters.label: Normalize Direction
parameters.description: Normalizes __Direction__ when turned on.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.description: Specifies the angle of distortion when __Direction Type__ is set to `Angle`. Value of 0 corresponds to the positive X direction in image space.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: Overall strength of distortion. Negative values follow the directions backwards when tracing.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Adjusts the distortion's overall strength by the current timestep. The timestep is usually `1/$FPS`, but in a sub-stepped simulation it represents the current step size.

parameters.label: Streak
parameters.description: The method used to combine the pixel values along the direction of distortion.

parameters.label: Use Streak Weight Ramp
parameters.description: When __Streak__ is `Blur`, `Min`, or `Max` , weight the samples encountered along the path. Use __Streak Weight__ to weaken the values over the trajectory.

parameters.label: Streak Weight
parameters.description: When __Use Streak Weight Ramp__ is on, this ramp acts as a multiplier on the pixel values when streaking. The left side of the ramp corresponds to the start of the trajectory. For example, when the __Streak__ is `Blur`, the default linear ramp fades the pixels over their path. This makes the pixels more faint near the start. For more information about using ramps, see [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps].

parameters.label: Pixels per Step
parameters.description: When off, a single step is taken for each pixel to figure out the source location. Although this is fast, it produces inaccurate results when the directions or scales vary. Turning on this parameter uses a more accurate algorithm to trace curved trajectories. The provided value controls the tracing quality. More pixels per step allows the node to take larger steps (this runs faster, but may miss intermediate variations in the distortion directions).

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.description: Clamps the number of steps taken when __Pixels per Step__ is on. You can raise this parameter (and lower __Pixels per Step__) if the distortion doesn't faithfully follow the directions. This can be especially noticeable when __Streak__ is turned on.

parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.description: When __Live Simulation__ is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this enables the caching of the simulation.  If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is how many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is the rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to `24` to cache frames `24`, `48`, `72`, etc.  This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to `0` to disable checkpointing.

parameters.label: Collision Iterations
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection

parameters.label: Multigrid Iterations

parameters.heading: Glow
parameters.description: The amount of saturation to apply to the glow effect. Higher values increase the saturation to make the hue of the glow effect more intense. entries.title: HeightField Erode
entries.summary: Simulates hydraulic and thermal erosion at a specific scale to create more realistic terrain.

parameters.label: Simulate
parameters.description: Turns on simulation, so the node updates with the [Playbar|/anim/playbar]. When turned off, the node simulates a fixed number of erosion iterations.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is off, the number of erosion timesteps to simulate. This controls the duration of the erosion process.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, clears the entire simulation cache. ((Ctrl))-click to also reset to the start frame.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is the frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, how many iterations of the simulation to run per frame. Higher values create stronger erosion effects, but also take longer to simulate.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Turns on caching of the simulation. If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: How many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: The rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to `5` to cache frames 5, 10, 15, and such.  This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to `0` to turn off checkpointing.

parameters.label: Feature Size
parameters.heading: Erosion Model
parameters.description: The width of erosion features, in meters. Higher values will create wider channels, slopes, and deposits. Lower values will create sharper features. The smallest possible feature size is 3x the input terrain's pixel size. Features will be clamped to this size.

parameters.label: Spread Iterations
parameters.heading: Erosion Model
parameters.description: How many iterations of material transport to simulate in each frame. The number of iterations, together with the __Feature Size__, control the distance that eroded material can be transported within a single frame.

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.heading: Erosion Model
parameters.description: The seed used to randomize the erosion process. With each new value, the distribution of erosion features changes.

parameters.label: Erodability
parameters.heading: Erosion Model
parameters.description: How prone the terrain is to hydro and thermal erosion. You can use the `erodability` input to vary the softness of the terrain.

parameters.label: Flow Force
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: The force of hydro erosion. With `0` you turn off hydro erosion.

parameters.label: Bank Angle
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: Controls the angle of channel walls. Higher values will create steeper channels that appear to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a jagged appearance.

parameters.label: Rainfall Coverage
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: The amount of rainfall to simulate each frame as a proportion of the terrain's surface. This controls the intensity of hydro erosion in each frame. You can use the `rainfall` input to vary the rainfall across the terrain.

parameters.label: Slope Influence
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: Controls how closely streams will follow the slope of the terrain. Higher values will result in winding channels. Lower values will result in straighter channels.

parameters.label: Erosion Rate
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream erodes and accumulates material from the terrain.

parameters.label: Deposition Rate
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: Controls how quickly sediment is deposited once the stream's transport capacity is exceeded.

parameters.label: Removal Rate
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream's accumulated sediment decays. Higher values will _reduce_ the amount of deposited sediment, allowing hydro erosion to cut deeper into the terrain, creating a rocky appearance.

parameters.label: Evaporation Rate
parameters.heading: Hydro
parameters.description: The rate at which a stream's sediment capacity decays. Lower values will create more prominent channels that persist across longer distances with a rocky appearance. Higher values will create smaller local depressions with a soil-like or sandy appearance.

parameters.label: Weathering Force
parameters.heading: Thermal
parameters.description: The force of thermal erosion. With `0` you can turn off thermal erosion.

parameters.label: Cut Angle
parameters.heading: Thermal
parameters.description: The angle that thermal erosion will cut until. A lower angle will make the cuts flatter, and allow for more thermal erosion to take place.

parameters.label: Repose Angle
parameters.heading: Thermal
parameters.description: The angle at which the thermal erosion debris will remain in place without sliding.

entries.title: HeightField Mask by Feature
entries.summary: Creates a mask based on different features of the heightfield.

parameters.label: Smooth Radius
parameters.description: The blur radius in [local space|/copernicus/spaces] used to smooth the input heightfield before the features are measured.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: When more than one feature is being measured, you can choose a compositing operation to combine each feature's mask.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: When enabled, inverts the resulting mask values.

parameters.label: Mask by Slope
parameters.heading: Slope
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the slope of the heightfield.

parameters.label: Min Slope Angle
parameters.heading: Slope
parameters.description: Mask areas with slope greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Max Slope Angle
parameters.heading: Slope
parameters.description: Mask areas with slope less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Slope Ramp
parameters.heading: Slope
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the __Min Slope Angle__ to the __Max Slope Angle__.

parameters.label: Mask by Height
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the height.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Click to fill in the __Min Height__ and __Max Height__ parameters with the minimum and maximum values of the input `height` layer.

parameters.label: Min Height
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Mask areas with height greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Max Height
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Mask areas with height less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Height Ramp
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the __Min Height__ to the __Max Height__.

parameters.label: Mask by Curvature
parameters.heading: Peaks and Valleys
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the maximum curvature.

parameters.label: Max Curvature
parameters.heading: Peaks and Valleys
parameters.description: Mask areas with absolute curvature less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Curvature Ramp
parameters.heading: Peaks and Valleys
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from negative __Max Curvature__ to the positive __Max Curvature__.

parameters.label: Mask by Direction
parameters.heading: Direction
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the heightfield's slope direction.

parameters.label: Goal Angle
parameters.heading: Direction
parameters.description: Define an angle and all surfaces facing that direction get masked. `0` degrees is in the direction of increasing pixels along the `height` layer's width.

parameters.label: Angle Spread
parameters.heading: Direction
parameters.description: Mask areas with this amount of variance from the __Goal Angle__. The range of directions is the __Goal Angle__ minus/plus the __Angle Spread__.

parameters.label: Direction Ramp
parameters.heading: Direction
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range, from the __Goal Angle__ minus the __Angle Spread__, to the __Goal Angle__ plus the __Angle Spread__.

parameters.label: Mask by Occlusion
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Generate a mask based on the heightfield's ambient occlusion.

parameters.label: Compute Range
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Click to fill in the __Minimum Occlusion__ and __Maximum Occlusion__ parameters with the minimum and maximum ambient occlusion of the input `height` layer.

parameters.label: Minimum Occlusion
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Mask areas with ambient occlusion greater than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Maximum Occlusion
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Mask areas with ambient occlusion less than or equal to this value.

parameters.label: Height Scale
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: The scale applied to input height values before computing ambient occlusion. Higher values exaggerate the amount of occlusion and small variations in height appear more pronounced.

parameters.label: Occlusion Ramp
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Controls the value of the mask over the range from the __Minimum Occlusion__ to the __Maximum Occlusion__.

parameters.label: View Radius
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The distance in [local space|/copernicus/spaces] to send rays to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values extend the reach of the rays, producing more precise results, but at the cost of longer calculation times. Lower values decrease the distance you send the rays.

parameters.label: Step Scale
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: How many steps (in [buffer space|/copernicus/spaces]) to take along the rays to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values create less steps and therefore calculate faster, but may miss thin features since the steps are more spread out. Lower values create more steps, which are closer together.

parameters.label: Sample Count
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The amount of rays to send to determine if a pixel is occluded. Higher values increase the number of rays sent and provide more accurate measurements, but at the cost of longer calculation times. Lower values decrease the number of rays sent.

parameters.label: Sample from Hemisphere
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Divides the point's calculated angle by 90 degrees instead of 180 degrees.

parameters.label: Erosion Rate

parameters.label: Deposition Rate

entries.title: HeightField Strata
entries.summary: Adds sedimentary layering patterns to a HeightField.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of strata noise to mix into the input `height` layer.

parameters.label: Blend Mode
parameters.description: Specifies how the strata layer is combined with the input `height` layer.

parameters.label: Output Strata Only
parameters.description: When enabled, outputs only the `strata` layer, instead of blending the strata with the input `height` layer.

parameters.label: Amplitude
parameters.heading: Range
parameters.description: The multiplication factor for the strata noise applied by the node before the __Center__ adjustment. For example, a value of `0.5` makes a pixel value of `0.5` become `0.25`.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.heading: Range
parameters.description: The center of the output strata noise range, which offsets the pixel values. For example, a value of `0.5` makes a pixel value of `0.5` become `1`.

parameters.label: Noise Contrast
parameters.heading: Range
parameters.description: The amount of contrast to apply to the noise before the __Amplitude__ and __Center__ parameters. You can use this parameter to make the strata noise more extreme.

parameters.label: Noise Type
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The underlying noise function that's iteratively sampled to generate the strata noise.

parameters.label: Metric
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Noise Type__ is `Worley Cellular F1` or `Worley Cellular F2-F1`, you can define different metrics for computing the distance to a point.

parameters.label: Worley Jitter
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Noise Type__ is `Worley Cellular F1` or `Worley Cellular F2-F1`, this is the amount of random noise to add to each point's position on a grid. The random noise is added before the Worley noise measures the distance to the points.

parameters.label: Units
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The unit of measurement to control the strata noise pattern. See [/copernicus/spaces] for more information.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The size of the basic element of the strata noise in image or local coordinates (determined by the __Space__). You can turn on the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ button to adjust this further using the __Element Scale__ parameter.

parameters.label: Element Scale
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/decompose_transforms] __Per-Component Controls__ button is on, this is the per-axis scaling of the element size for anisotropic noise.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: An offset for the entire noise function in image or local coordinates (determined by the __Space__ parameter).

parameters.label: Strata Size
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The thickness of the strata.

parameters.label: Strata Offset
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The offset of the strata.

parameters.label: Tilt
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The angle of the strata in degrees. When set to zero, the layers are perpendicular to the height. If increased, the layers cut across the height.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The rotation of the strata about the __Origin__.

parameters.label: Origin
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: The center of rotation of the strata in image or local coordinates (defined by the __Space__ parameter).

parameters.label: Add Layers
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When enabled, adds numerous additional __Layers__ of strata noise, with randomly varying orientations.

parameters.label: Layers
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Add Layers__ is enabled, the number of additional layers of strata noise to add.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Add Layers__ is enabled, the amount to scale the amplitude of each successive strata noise.

parameters.label: Tilt Variance
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Add Layers__ is enabled, the maximum amount in degrees to vary each additional strata from the set __Tilt__.

parameters.label: Rotate Variance
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Add Layers__ is enabled, the maximum amount in degrees to vary each additional strata from the set __Rotate__.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: When __Add Layers__ is enabled, the random seed used to vary the orientation of the additional strata layers.

parameters.label: Base Height Influence
parameters.heading: Pattern
parameters.description: Controls how much the `baseheight` input affects the pattern of the strata.

parameters.label: Fractal Type
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: How to accumulate successive layers of noise to create finer-scale details.

parameters.label: Max Octaves
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The number of times the noise is scaled and layered on top of itself.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to scale the noise for each iteration.

parameters.label: Octave Offset
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to offset the noise for each iteration.

parameters.label: Roughness
parameters.heading: Fractal
parameters.description: The amount to scale the amplitude of each successive noise.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The node applies the post-processing operations in the order they're listed.

parameters.label: Fold
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the noise values to the absolute value. For example, a pixel value of `-2` becomes `2`.

parameters.label: Complement
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Sets the pixel value `x` to `1 - x`.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) towards zero (if __Bias__ is less than `1`) or one (if __Bias__ is greater than `1`). A bias value of `0.5` doesn't affect the values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_bias.jpg]

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to pull the medium grey values (around `0.5`) together, while values around `0` and `1` are pulled apart. A gain value of `0.5` doesn't affect the noise values. [Image:/images/nodes/cop/postprocessing_gain.jpg]

parameters.label: Gamma
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The overall gamma of the generated noise. Values greater than `1` increase the range of values in originally bright areas, which darkens the noise. Values less than `1` stretch out the range of values for originally dark areas, which increases the overall brightness of the noise.

parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: The amount to expand or shrink the overall range of tonal values. Each noise value is pushed towards (if __Contrast__ is less than `1`) or away from (if __Contrast__ is greater than `1`) medium grey values (around `0.5`).

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values below the specified threshold.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.heading: Post Processing
parameters.description: Clamps values exceeding the specified threshold.

entries.title: HSV Adjust
entries.summary: Converts between RGB and HSV color spaces, or modifies HSV.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. The default value is `1`, which means this node uses only the new value. See [Mask|/copernicus/glossary#mask] for more information.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The operation that this node performs.

parameters.label: Hue Shift
parameters.description: The amount (in degrees) to shift the hue around the HSV cone. This changes all colors to different hues. Gray pixels aren't affected.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Mode
parameters.description: When a `hueshift` input is wired in, this is how to shift the source layer's hue values.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Min
parameters.description: When __Hue Shift Mode__ is `Min/Max`, this is the degree to remap `0` to on the hue wheel.  A value of `0` represents no shift. For example, when set to `-60` the hue is shifted by `-60` degrees where the input equals `0`. The node interpolates for values between this setting and the __Hue Shift Max__.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Max
parameters.description: When __Hue Shift Mode__ is `Min/Max`, this is the degree to remap `1` to on the hue wheel. A value of `0` represents no shift. For example, when set to `88` the hue is shifted by `88` degrees where the input equals `1`. The node interpolates for values between this setting and the __Hue Shift Min__.

parameters.label: Hue Shift Width
parameters.description: When __Hue Shift Mode__ is `Width`, this is the distance in degrees to remap the width between `0` and `1` to on the hue wheel. A value of `0` represents no shift. For example, when set to `40` this remaps `0` to `-20` and `1` to `20`.

parameters.label: Keep Luminance
parameters.description: Maintains the perceptual luminance of the pixel when hues shift since some hues appear brighter than others.

parameters.label: Saturation Scale
parameters.description: The amount to increase (>1) or decrease (<1) the color saturation of the image. This multiplies the saturation.

parameters.label: Saturation Shift
parameters.description: The amount to shift the color saturation of the pixels. Higher values add to the saturation while lower values subtract from the saturation. Shifting is normally used only to reduce the saturation, otherwise grayscale elements suddenly take on a random color.

parameters.label: Value Scale
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the value (brightness) of the pixel. This multiplies the brightness.

parameters.label: Value Shift
parameters.description: The value (brightness) to add to all pixels. Higher values add to the brightness while lower values subtract from the brightness.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

entries.title: Hyperbolic Tile
entries.summary: Generates hyperbolic polygon tiles for texture patterns.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: The number of times that the base regular polygon's pattern repeats within the boundary of the Poincaré disk. Each copy reflects and inverts the previous copy's pattern.

parameters.label: Polygons
parameters.description: The amount of sides to give the base regular polygon.

parameters.label: Rectanglize
parameters.description: Changes the Poincaré disk's boundary to the [image space|/copernicus/spaces] square instead of a circle. Choose a mapping type from the dropdown menu to set how the pattern within the Poincaré disk's boundary maps outwards to occupy the entire image space square.

parameters.label: Stretch to Fit
parameters.description: When __Rectanglize__ is on and the `size_ref` has a rectangle input, this option stretches the square to fill the given rectangular region.

parameters.label: Flattening
parameters.description: The amount to flatten circular arcs in the base polygon. When set to `0`, the base polygon fits within the Poincaré disk. Higher values expand the circular arcs in the base regular polygon out towards the image's border to flatten them. They can't be entirely flat because straight lines must pass the center of the Poincaré disk to define the hyperbolic regular polygons.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: The length of straight lines in the base polygon. This parameter corresponds to the radius of the Poincaré disk when __Flattening__ is `0`.

parameters.label: Tile Fitting
parameters.description: Fills the image to tiles when the __uv__ output is used. A value of `0` makes the image appear as a square within each tile. Increasing the value to `1` stretches the image to fill the entire tile area.

parameters.label: Poincaré Disk Mask
parameters.description: Displays only the pattern that's within the boundary of the Poincaré disk. This parameter doesn't apply if __Rectanglize__ is on.

parameters.description: The [group syntax|/model/groups#manual] to use to filter IDs. If this is blank, the node filters all IDs.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask that the node generates.

parameters.label: Keep by Range
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: Filters IDs based on a range.

parameters.label: Range Type
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: Specifies the range that determines how to filter the IDs.

parameters.label: Start ID
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: When this parameter is on and the __Range Type__ is `Start and End`, this is the ID at the start of the range. For example, a value of `0` means the range includes IDs greater than and equal to `0`. The default value is `0`. When this parameter is off, there is no limit for the start of the range.

parameters.label: End ID
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: When this parameter is on and the __Range Type__ is `Start and End`, this is the ID at the end of the range. For example, a value of `100` means the range includes IDs less than and equal to `100`. The default value is `100`. When this parameter is off, there is no limit for the end of the range.

parameters.label: Range Offset
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: When __Range Type__ is `Start and End`, this is the value to add to the __Start ID__ and __End ID__ parameters. The default value is `0`.

parameters.label: Start ID
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: When __Range Type__ is `Start and Length`, this is the ID at the start of the range. For example, a value of `0` means the range includes IDs greater than and equal to `0`. The default value is `0`.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.heading: Keep by Range
parameters.description: When __Range Type__ is `Start and Length`, this is how many IDs to include in the range. The default value is `5`.

parameters.label: Select/of
parameters.heading: Range Filter
parameters.description: The number of IDs to select out of every block of IDs. For example, set __Select__ to `1` and __of__ to `2` so the filter selects half of the integer values. The __Offset__ parameter impacts whether the selected values are odd or even. The default values are `1` of `2`.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Range Filter
parameters.description: The start of the range filter, which is measured relative to the start of the range. The default value is `0`.

parameters.label: Keep by Chance
parameters.heading: Keep by Chance
parameters.description: Filters by selecting a subset of IDs by random chance.

parameters.label: Probability
parameters.heading: Keep by Chance
parameters.description: The chance (percentage) that the group includes the ID. For example, a value of `0.1` means that the group includes about 10% of the IDs. The default value is `0.5`.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Keep by Chance
parameters.description: The initial [seed|Wp:Random_seed] that determines which elements to include. Changing this value causes each ID to generate a new random value, which results in a new pattern. The default value is `30`.

parameters.label: Keep within Mask
parameters.heading: Keep within Mask
parameters.description: When you have a mask input, this filters by keeping a subset of IDs within a mask layer.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.heading: Keep within Mask
parameters.description: When you have a mask input, pixels in the mask layer that have a value greater than this threshold are considered when masking. The default value is `0.5`.

entries.title: Integrate Volume
entries.summary: Integrates a VDB along camera rays.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. The output is mono when the input's a `Float VDB`. The output is RGB when the input's a `Vector VDB`, accumulating each channel separately along the view ray. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Move to Origin
parameters.description: Moves the output layer to the origin.

parameters.label: Depth Conversion
parameters.description: Convert the `mindepth` and `maxdepth` inputs to distances from the camera from this kind of input.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: The value to compute along each view ray.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.heading: Density
parameters.description: The amount by which to scale the density. The node applies this scale after it linearly maps and applies the ramp to the density.

parameters.label: Min
parameters.heading: Density
parameters.description: The lower bound of the interval to linearly map to (`0, 1`). For each sample of the VDB, the node linearly maps the Density interval to (`0, 1`).

parameters.label: Max
parameters.heading: Density
parameters.description: The upper bound of the interval to linearly map to (`0, 1`). For each sample of the VDB, the node linearly maps the Density interval to (`0, 1`).

parameters.label: Ramp Mode
parameters.heading: Density
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp.

parameters.label: Density Ramp
parameters.heading: Density
parameters.description: The map to apply to the density after it's linearly remapped to (`0, 1`). See [Ramp parameters|/network/ramps] for more information.

parameters.label: Seed Jitter with Time
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Makes the sample location jittering depend on time.

parameters.label: Sample Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter sample locations. When `0`, sample locations are always at the centre of ray slices. When `1`, sample locations can be drawn from anywhere along their respective ray slice. There is never more than one sample drawn per ray slice.

parameters.label: Stratification Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter ray slice locations. This is a single offset applied to each view ray, not per sample. When `0`, the start of ray slice #0 coincides with the ray origin. When `1`, the start of ray slice #0 varies from backward and forward along the ray by half the step length.

parameters.label: Integration Step Size
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The length of ray slices. This is the expected distance between samples when samples are jittered.

parameters.label: Max Step Count
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Used to prevent the OpenCL kernel from running forever or timing out. You shouldn't need to change the `4096` value unless rastering a very deep volume.

parameters.label: Transmittance Cutoff
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: When __Operation__ is `Integral` or `Transmittance`, this is the transmittance of the accumulated portion of the ray after which to stop raymarching. A value of `-1` turns this off, which may be necessary to calculate the integral of a field that doesn't represent an optical density. This is an optimization for when a very dense region of the volume is encountered, where almost none of the light from behind this region reaches the camera so you can stop raymarching early to save time. Due to rounding error, it's possible for the accumulated transmittance to reach 0 despite this not being physically possible, and this is seen when rasterizing very dense volumes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Advection

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.heading: Advection

parameters.label: Trace Method
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: Controls the integration scheme used for a single trace step through the velocity field. This setting determines how closely the smoke follows turbulent flows and how well the simulation preserves detail over time. Options in this menu are listed in order of increasing accuracy and computational cost.

parameters.label: Path Tracing
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: A single trace step is often not enough to preserve sharp details, wispy tendrils, and small vortices through turbulent or fast-moving velocity flows. When this is turned on, multiple trace steps (given by __Trace Method__) are taken to better predict the curved path through the velocity field. The number of steps depends on the __Maximum Steps__ and the __CFL Condition__.

parameters.label: Maximum Steps
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: Global clamp on how many path tracing steps can be performed. For extremely fast motion this may need to be increased, but it might be better to raise the CFL condition instead.

parameters.label: CFL Condition
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: Controls how large a step should be used when tracing through the velocity field. This is approximately how many voxels will be stepped during a single trace step. Lower values mean better stability, but lower performance. Higher values force the tracing to take larger steps, allowing it to finish faster.

parameters.label: Adaptive Step Size
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: When turned on, this dynamically changes the given step size through each tracing step, based on the number of maximum steps.

parameters.label: Enable Velocity Advection

entries.title: Pyro Axis Force
entries.summary: Applies a force around an axis to a velocity VDB.

parameters.label: Start
parameters.description: Starting point of the line segment. This line segment is the axis for the force.

parameters.label: End
parameters.description: End point of the line segment. This line segment is the axis for the force.

parameters.label: Influence Distance
parameters.description: The forces are applied in a cylindrical region around the line segment. This parameter controls the radius of this cylinder. Increasing this value will extend the active region of this force.

parameters.label: Global Strength
parameters.description: A global strength multiplier for the force. _Suction_, _axis_, and _orbit_ components are affected by this strength. Increase this parameter to  uniformly amplify the effect of this node.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: Controls how the _axis_ and _orbit_ forces are applied to the velocity field. __Directional Drag__ splits the incoming velocity vector into components that point in the axial and orbital directions, then modifies these parts independently. If one of the forces has `0` strength, this mode leaves the respective velocity component unchanged (this includes the part of the velocity vectors that point at the line segment). __Full Drag__ first assembles the full goal velocity, then drives the incoming vectors toward the goal. When set to __Force__, the goal velocities instead act like an additive force. That is, the goal velocities are multiplied by the applicable strength, then scaled by the timestep, and added to the destination field.

parameters.label: Scale by Timestep
parameters.description: Scale the effect of the force by the timestep.  This ensures that the amount of force stays the same when substepping occurs, but if the instantaneous value needs to be computed, it can be turned off.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.heading: Suction Force
parameters.description: Strength of the suction force that pulls toward the line segment. Positive values pull toward the axis, whereas negative values blow outward (away from the axis). Set this parameter to `0` to turn off the suction force.

parameters.label: Pump Thickness
parameters.heading: Suction Force
parameters.description: Specifies the thickness of the tube around the line where divergence values are set. This value should be larger than the voxel size of the simulation fields to avoid aliasing. Increasing this parameter will also amplify the strength of the suction force.

parameters.label: Suction Along Axis
parameters.heading: Suction Force
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the amount of induced divergence (or strength of suction) along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to the __Start Point__ and __End Point__, and the vertical axis spans from `0` to the __Strength__ value.

parameters.label: Speed Range
parameters.heading: Speed
parameters.description: The range of goal speeds in the direction of the line segment. Negative speed signals that the goal velocity points in the opposite direction (from the __End Point__ toward the __Start Point__).

parameters.label: Speed Along Axis
parameters.heading: Speed
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the goal axis speed along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to __Start Point__ and __End Point__, and the vertical axis covers the given __Speed Range__.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.heading: Strength
parameters.description: Strength of the axis force that generates motion in the direction of the line segment. When applied as drag, larger values of this parameter will align the incoming velocities more closely with the goal. When applied as force, increasing strength will increase the magnitude of the additive force. Set this parameter to `0` to turn off the axis force.

parameters.label: Strength Along Axis
parameters.heading: Strength
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the axis force along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to __Start Point__ and __End Point__, respectively. The vertical axis spans `0` to `1`, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for __Strength__.

parameters.label: Strength Away from Axis
parameters.heading: Strength
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the axis force based on the distance to the line segment. The left side of this ramp represents the center of the active cylinder (distance of `0` to the axis), while the right side corresponds to its outer edge (at a separation of __Influence Distance__). The vertical axis spans `0` to `1`, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for __Strength__.

parameters.label: Speed Range
parameters.heading: Speed
parameters.description: The range of goal speeds around the line segment. With the axis directed from __Start Point__ to __End Point__, positive speeds correspond to right-handed rotation around the line. Negative speeds generate rotation in the opposite direction.

parameters.label: Speed Falloff
parameters.heading: Speed
parameters.description: Controls the relationship between orbital speed and orbital distance. When set to __Constant__, the speed is independent of distance. Orbital speed is directly proportional to distance in __Scale by Distance__ mode (similar to a rotating rigid body). When __Scale by Inverse Distance__ is selected, orbits are fastest at the line segment and gradually become slower as they get further away from the center of the active cylinder.

parameters.label: Speed Along Axis
parameters.heading: Speed
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the goal orbit speed along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to __Start Point__ and  __End Point__, and this ramp's vertical axis covers the given __Speed Range__.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.heading: Strength
parameters.description: Strength of the orbit force that generates rotational motion around the line segment. When applied as drag, larger values of this parameter will align the incoming velocities more closely with the goal. When applied as force, increasing strength will increase the magnitude of the additive force. Set this parameter to `0` to turn off the orbit force.

parameters.label: Strength Along Axis
parameters.heading: Strength
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the orbit force along the line segment. The left and right sides of this ramp correspond to __Start Point__ and __End Point__, respectively. The vertical axis spans `0` to `1`, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for __Strength__.

parameters.label: Strength Away from Axis
parameters.heading: Strength
parameters.description: Allows you to vary the strength of the orbit force based on the distance to the line segment. The left side of this ramp represents the center of the active cylinder (distance of `0` to the axis), while the right side corresponds to its outer edge (at a separation of __Influence Distance__). The vertical axis spans `0` to `1`, and the evaluated value of this ramp acts as a multiplier for __Strength__.

parameters.label: Mask Range
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Values in the __Mask Field__ are remapped from this range to `0-1`.

parameters.label: Remap Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: When this checkbox is turned on, the remapped mask values (from __Mask Range__) are additionally passed through the __Mask Ramp__.

parameters.label: Mask Ramp
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: This ramp's vertical axis is the strength modifier and the horizontal axis is the remapped mask value.

parameters.label: Reset Simulation
parameters.description: Clears the entire simulation cache.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The frame on the Houdini playbar where the simulation starts.

parameters.label: Correct Collisions
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: Zero out the density and temperature that are inside the collision SDF, avoiding any leaking of smoke.

parameters.label: Output Velocity Corrected by Timescale
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: The output velocity VDB `v` will be scaled by timescale, ensuring it will motion blur correctly.  However, if this is to be used by another simulation, you may want the raw velocity values.

parameters.label: Output Velocity Corrected by Ambient
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: The output velocity VDB `v` will be adjusted by ambient velocity, ensuring it will motion blur correctly.  However, if this is to be used by another simulation, you may want the raw velocity values.

parameters.label: Ambient Velocity
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: A global ambient velocity that the simulation operates within. All the fields will advect with this velocity, allowing it to provide a global wind effect that can be directly keyframed.  However, the actual velocity VDB doesn't contain this.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: The amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of `1` maintains the normal speed, a value greater than `1` speeds up the simulation, and a value less than `1` slows down the simulation.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: Each frame is broken into a series of substeps.  This can give more accurate results for fast moving simulations, but at the cost of increased time.

parameters.label: Live Simulation
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: Turns on live simulation to provide an interactive, non-deterministic simulation mode. It simulates independent of the playbar and isn't associated with any keyframes or caching. This parameter (and its associated parameters) is intended as a sandbox mode where you don't have to rely on the playbar.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: When __Simulate__ is on, this is the amount to scale the time inside the block. A value of `1` maintains the normal speed, a value greater than `1` speeds up the simulation, and a value less than `1` slows down the simulation.

parameters.label: Toggle Live Simulation
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: When __Live Simulation__ is on, this lets you pause and resume the live simulation.

parameters.label: Live Tick
parameters.heading: Simulation
parameters.description: When __Live Simulation__ is on, this is the current tick (frame) within the live simulation.

parameters.label: Cache Simulation
parameters.heading: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: Enables the caching of the simulation.  If the simulation is uncached, it will always have to cook from the start frame on any new frame.

parameters.label: Cached Frames
parameters.heading: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: How many frames behind the current frame to keep cached.

parameters.label: Checkpoint Rate
parameters.heading: Cache Simulation
parameters.description: The rate at which the node continually caches a single frame. For example, set this to `24` to cache frames `24`, `48`, `72`, and such.  This allows random-scrubbing to be faster as it only has to re-cook from the checkpoint frame. Set to `0` to turn off checkpointing.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: The projection process is repeated this number of times. Increased iterations takes longer, but will produce a more accurate result.  It will also increase the faithfulness of the collision operation.

parameters.label: Voxel Kernel Size
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: Size of the kernel to apply at the voxel size.  Larger will be higher quality but at a rapidly increasing cost in time.

parameters.label: Double Voxel Pass
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: Apply two voxel kernel passes before performing a block pass.

parameters.label: Block Pass
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: Enable the block pass.  In this pass, divergence is reduced to dipoles in large blocks, allowing action at distance without having to increase the voxel kernel size.

parameters.label: Block Kernel Size
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: The size, in blocks, to accumulate the surrounding block's dipoles when updating a voxel. Larger will be higher quality but at a rapidly increasing cost in time.

parameters.label: Feather Blocks
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: Reduce the strength of the block correction over the farthest blocks.  This avoids sharp transitions in the corrected velocity if there are strong impulses, but will require more iterations or time to correct divergence fully.

parameters.label: Point Pass
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: Combine the block dipoles into an even coarser set of points. These are then applied to every voxel.  This ensures global effect of divergence in a single pass.

parameters.label: Hourglass Filter
parameters.heading: Pressure Projection
parameters.description: Projecting using corner-sampled divergences can miss certain modes of the velocity.   The hourglass filter applies a smoothing operation to ensure these are correctly filtered; this can reduce jaggy artifacts.

parameters.label: Path Tracing
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: A single trace step is often not enough to preserve sharp details, wispy tendrils, and small vortices through turbulent or fast-moving velocity flows. When this is turned on, multiple trace steps (given by __Trace Method__) are taken to better predict the curved path through the velocity field. The number of steps depends on the __Maximum Steps__ and the __CFL Condition__.

parameters.label: CFL Condition
parameters.heading: Tracing
parameters.description: Controls how large a step should be used when tracing through the velocity field. This is approximately how many voxels will be stepped during a single trace step. parameters.label: Maximum Steps

parameters.label: Feather Blocks

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Operation

parameters.label: Buoyancy Scale
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: A global scale on the amount of buoyancy to apply. Hot gas expands, causing it to rise due to lowered density. Acceleration due to buoyancy is calculated using the values of the ambient and reference temperatures, as well as the __Gravity Acceleration__ scale.

parameters.label: Ambient Temp (K)
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Temperature corresponding to value of `0` in the `temperature` field (in Kelvin). This represents the ambient temperature of the environment.

parameters.label: Reference Temp (K)
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Temperature corresponding to a value of `1` in the `temperature` field (in Kelvin). The temperature range is used to calculate the strength of the buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Equilibrium Temp
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Hot gas rises in the buoyancy direction where temperature values are above this ambient temperature, and falls where they are below it. Since newly activated areas have zero temperature, this usually needs to be zero to leave dead-space unaffected. This is useful for simulating cloud formation where gases can rise and fall.

parameters.label: Gravity Acceleration
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Acceleration due to gravity. Stronger gravity results in a stronger buoyancy force.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: The direction in which temperatures hotter than the ambient temperature will be forced.

parameters.label: Threshold Volume
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the threshold field. Threshold fields are intended to provide harsh on/off effects, but the range can be used to soften the transition.

parameters.label: Threshold Range
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask
parameters.description: The value of the threshold field is mapped from this range to `0-1` and applied as a multiplier on top of __Scale__. The default `0.01` to `0` range is designed to concentrate the effect on the edges and empty regions of the threshold field, but not inside it. When the threshold field is a `Vector VDB`, this value represents the length of the given vector field.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask
parameters.description: Turns on the __Threshold Ramp__, to change how the threshold field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of __Threshold Range__.

parameters.label: Threshold Ramp
parameters.heading: Threshold Mask
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the threshold field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of  __Threshold Range__.

parameters.label: Control Volume
parameters.heading: Control Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect using the control field. Control fields are usually used the same way as masks, and represent a smooth engagement of the effect.

parameters.label: Control Range
parameters.heading: Control Mask
parameters.description: The value of the control field is mapped from this range to `0-1` and applied as a multiplier on top of __Scale__. The default `0` to `1` range is designed to concentrate the effect on regions with higher control field values. When the control field is a `Vector VDB`, this value represents the length of the given vector field.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.heading: Control Mask
parameters.description: Turns on the __Control Ramp__, to change how the control field should scale the effect between the minimum and maximum values of __Control Range__.

parameters.label: Control Ramp
parameters.heading: Control Mask
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the control field values are mapped between the minimum and maximum values of  __Control Range__.

parameters.label: Angle Mask
parameters.heading: Angle Mask
parameters.description: Mask out the effect by the angle between the velocity field values and a direction vector.

parameters.label: Angle Direction

parameters.description: The reference vector used to calculate the angle deviation against the velocity field.

parameters.label: Spread Angle
parameters.heading: Angle Mask
parameters.description: The value of the calculated angle is mapped until this angle range to `1-0` and applied as a multiplier on top of __Scale__. At the default 90 degrees, the effect is strongest where the vectors align, and gradually diminishes to zero as the angle reaches this value.

parameters.label: Use Ramp
parameters.heading: Angle Mask
parameters.description: Turns on the __Angle Control Ramp__, to change how the angle deviation should scale the effect between the aligned vectors and the given __Spread Angle__.

parameters.label: Angle Control Ramp
parameters.heading: Angle Mask
parameters.description: This ramp controls how the angle deviation is mapped between the aligned vectors and the given __Spread Angle__.

parameters.label: Axis Mask
parameters.heading: Axis Mask

parameters.label: Axis Range

parameters.label: Use Ramp

parameters.label: Axis Control Ramp

parameters.description: This ramp controls how the position is mapped between the minimum and maximum values of __Axis Range__.

entries.title: Pyro Light Ambient
entries.summary: Builds a light field of ambient illumination of a VDB.

parameters.label: Exposed Color
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: The color of light that is exposed to the ambient surroundings. This is normally white, but can be used to tint the effective environment map.

parameters.label: Occluded Color
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: The color of light where the voxel is exposed to the ambient surroundings. Normally this is black, but setting this to white and the __Exposed Color__ to a dark color will result in a self-lit look which works well for clouds.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Controls the linear brightness of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Controls the exponential brightness of the light. Each increase of `1` doubles the brightness.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Scales the density VDB values, causing it to occlude light more quickly.

parameters.label: Environment Map Offset
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Controls the angle used to rotate the environment map around the Y-axis

parameters.label: Steps Per MipMap
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Controls how many tracing steps are performed before dropping to the next MipMap level when tracing occlusion rays. Lower values make the rays effectively thicker, causing them to become more like cones than rays.

parameters.label: Max Steps
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Controls the maximum number of samples taken while tracing an occlusion ray. Since higher MipMap levels have larger step sizes, the distance covered will be larger than just the voxelsize times the maxsteps.

parameters.label: Environment Map Resolution
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Because only a few rays are used to sample the ambient light, the environment map must be downsampled to avoid aliasing. This parameter controls the resolution to which it is resampled.

parameters.label: MipMap Level
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Controls the starting mipmap level. Starting at MipMap level 1 computes the light in a half-resolution VDB and interpolates the result back to full resolution, making the operation more than eight times faster.

parameters.label: Max Steps
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Controls the maximum number of samples taken while tracing an occlusion ray. Since higher MipMap levels have larger step sizes, the distance covered will be larger than just the voxelsize times the maxsteps.

entries.summary: Builds a light field of internal glow of a VDB.

parameters.label: Density Scale
parameters.description: Scales the density VDB values, causing it to occlude light more quickly.

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.description: Controls how quickly emitted light is absorbed by the smoke particles instead of being scattered further through the volume.

parameters.label: Emission Scale
parameters.description: Applies a global scale to the incoming emission VDB.

parameters.description: The emission VDB is sent through this ramp to generate an emission color.

parameters.description: Controls how many diffusion iterations are performed when scattering light through the volume. The emission is treated as a source term during diffusion. Although the process eventually converges, it is typically stopped early to keep it fast and to adjust the look.

parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Controls the MipMap level used for the light scattering computation. A mipmap level of `1` computes at half the original resolution and halves the number of iterations, making the process approximately sixteen times faster. The final scatter values are the interpolated back to the original resolution.
