entries.title: Pyro Project Non-Divergent Electro Static
entries.summary: Removes divergence from a velocity VDB.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Controls how many times the projection process is repeated. Higher values increase computation time but produce more accurate results and improve the reliability of collision handling.

parameters.label: Ambient Velocity
parameters.description: Specifies the global implied velocity. The input velocity is assumed not to include this value. When using `v`, the ambient velocity is implicitly added to obtain the world-space velocity. Collision velocities are specified in world-space, not wind-space, and are adjusted accordingly.

parameters.label: Voxel Kernel Size
parameters.description: Controls the size of the voxel kernel. Larger values improve quality but significantly increase computation time.

parameters.label: Double Voxel Pass
parameters.description: Applies two voxel kernel passes before performing a block pass.

parameters.label: Block Pass
parameters.description: Turn on the block pass.  During the block pass, divergence is reduced to dipoles over large blocks, allowing action at distance without having to increase the voxel kernel size.

parameters.label: Block Kernel Size
parameters.description: The size, in blocks, to accumulate the surrounding block's dipoles when updating a voxel. Larger values improve quality but significantly increase computation time.

parameters.label: Feather Blocks
parameters.description: Reduce the strength of the block correction over the farthest blocks.  This helps avoid sharp transitions in the corrected velocity when strong impulses are present, but may require more iterations or computation time to fully remove divergence.

parameters.label: Point Pass
parameters.description: Combines the block dipoles into an even coarser set of points. These points are then applied to every voxel, allowing divergence to have a global effect in a single pass.

parameters.label: Hourglass Filter
parameters.description: Applies a smoothing operation to remove velocity modes that can be missed when projecting using corner-sampled divergence. This can reduce jagged artifacts.

parameters.label: Control Ramp

parameters.label: Angle Direction

parameters.label: Spread Angle

entries.title: Pyro Vortex Confinement Force

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The VDB type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.description: Turns this the effect of this node on and off. This node is only active when this value is `1`.

parameters.label: Operation
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Controls how the force is combined with the incoming velocity field.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Controls the method used to recover detail lost through diffusion. The first-order method uses first derivatives to approximate the local vorticity gradient. This method is fast and stable, but tends to introduce more numerical diffusion, resulting in greater loss of fine-scale detail. The second-order method uses a higher-order approximation that better preserves energy and small-scale features. This method can produce more detailed results, but is slower and may introduce instabilities. These can be mitigated using the __Positive Diffusion Scale__ and __Negative Diffusion Scale__ parameters.

parameters.label: Confinement Scale
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the vortex confinement force.

parameters.label: Positive Diffusion Scale
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Controls the amount of positive diffusion applied. Positive diffusion improves stability by smoothing high-frequency noise and sharp numerical spikes in the vorticity field.

parameters.label: Negative Diffusion Scale
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Controls the amount of negative diffusion applied. Negative diffusion acts as an anti-diffusion process, concentrating energy toward the centers of vortex structures instead of spreading it outward.

parameters.label: Kernel Size
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Controls the size of the neighborhood stencil used to compute curvature at each pixel. Larger values generally produce smoother curvature results. This parameter has a similar effect to __Frequency Separation__, as it removes high-frequency detail that can cause unnatural jittering.

parameters.label: Target Energy
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Applies smooth clamping based on the energy of the band. The target energy determines the maximum energy level at which curl can be amplified. This can help reduce unstable or noisy behavior.

parameters.label: Adaptive Confinement
parameters.heading: Force
parameters.description: Restricts vortex confinement to areas where vorticles are more likely to develop. This can help reduce the unnatural jittering that vortex confinement can introduce throughout the simulation.

parameters.label: Use Frequency Separation
parameters.heading: Frequency Separation
parameters.description: Enables frequency separation, allowing you to control which swirl sizes are affected by this node.

parameters.label: Min Swirl Size
parameters.heading: Frequency Separation
parameters.description: Defines the smallest swirl size to include. Swirls with a width equal to this value define the starting frequency of the band. When turned off, all swirl sizes up to __Max Swirl Size__ are included. Increase this value together with __Max Swirl Size__, or set it close to __Max Swirl Size__, to affect only larger swirls.

parameters.heading: Emission

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.heading: Emission
parameters.description: The minimum and maximum interval to use instead of the Density interval (__Min__ and __Max__).

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Emission
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp.

parameters.label: Emission Tint
parameters.heading: Emission Color
parameters.description: The RGB values by which to multiply the remapped value. The node applies this scale after the ramp.

parameters.label: Input Range
parameters.heading: Emission Color
parameters.description: The minimum and maximum interval to use instead of the Density interval (__Min__ and __Max__).

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Emission Color
parameters.description: The transformation to perform before the node applies the ramp.

parameters.label: Bake Light Fields
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Bakes the light fields together before raymarching through them. This remaps the values in the VDBs before starting to raymarch. The node iterates over the density field and light field VDBs (the combination of Diffuse Color and Emission Color). Quality decreases and the output can appear more blocky when the VDB contains tiles. Turn this off if you want higher quality output.

parameters.label: Multiply Diffuse with Density before Interpolation
parameters.label_norm: multiply diffuse with density before interpolation
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Determines the amount of diffuse light at any point. The node finds the eight voxels that surround the sample locations in the Density field and multiply these by the corresponding voxels in the Diffuse field. The node linearly interpolates the eight voxel values at the sample location. This has higher accuracy but can be slow since the node remaps each field eight times. This can cause a difference near the boundaries of the active region of the density field since you might expect regions with zero density to not contribute any color to the final raster. When off, the node samples the two fields at the given sample location and multiplies the interpolated values together. This is faster but has lower accuracy. Turn this on when there are visual artifacts in the output or the density changes very quickly from inactive (`0`) to a high density. This option may not make a difference for rasterizing pyro simulations because density often varies smoothly, so turn this off for better performance. For example, consider sampling halfway between a voxel with nonzero density and an inactive density voxel. In the color field there may be some non-black color where the density field is nonzero and a black background color. If you sample halfway between these two voxels, the interpolated density is nonzero but the interpolated color is darker because it's halfway between black and the active voxel's color. This results in the boundary of the active region looking darker than it should. When this option is turned on, the node first multiplies the density and diffuse fields and the inactive voxels with a black color don't contribute to the final output because they have zero density.

parameters.label: Integration Step Size
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The length of ray slices. This is the expected distance between samples when samples are jittered.

parameters.label: Max Step Count
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Used to prevent the OpenCL kernel from running forever or timing out. You shouldn't need to change the `4096` value unless rastering a very deep volume.

parameters.label: Transmittance Cutoff
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The transmittance of the accumulated portion of the ray after which to stop raymarching. A value of `-1` turns this off and forces raymarching to continue until the ray exits the volume's bounding box, though there should be no difference in the output between `0` and `-1`. This is an optimization for when a very dense region of the volume is encountered, where almost none of the light from behind this region reaches the camera so you can stop raymarching early to save time. Due to rounding error, it's possible for the accumulated transmittance to reach 0 despite this not being physically possible, and this is seen when rasterizing very dense volumes.

parameters.label: Seed Jitter with Time
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: Makes the sample location jittering depend on time.

parameters.label: Sample Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter sample locations. When `0`, sample locations are always at the centre of ray slices. When `1`, sample locations can be drawn from anywhere along their respective ray slice. There is never more than one sample drawn per ray slice.

parameters.label: Stratification Jitter Scale
parameters.heading: Quality
parameters.description: The amount by which to jitter ray slice locations. This is a single offset applied to each view ray, not per sample. When `0`, the start of ray slice #0 coincides with the ray origin. When `1`, the start of ray slice #0 varies from backward and forward along the ray by half the step length.

entries.title: Reaction-Diffusion Block End
entries.summary: Creates unique patterns by solving the reaction and diffusion of multiple chemicals as described by its inputs and parameters.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: Signature which controls the output of the node.

parameters.label: Model
parameters.description: The model to use to describe how the chemicals interact, which includes presets.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Sets parameters to create Gray-Scott preset patterns.

parameters.label: Preset
parameters.description: Sets parameters to create Kenjiro Maginu preset patterns.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.heading: Time
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to run in non-simulation mode.

parameters.label: Iterations per Step
parameters.heading: Time
parameters.description: Amount of iterations to take per step within non-simulation, simulation, or Live Simulation.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.heading: Time
parameters.description: Sets the amount of substeps for each simulated frame.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: When __Live Simulation__ is on, the __Start Frame__, __Cached Frames__, and __Checkpoint Rate__ parameters no longer apply.

parameters.label: Caching
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Turns on caching of frames.

parameters.label: Switch to Raw Values
parameters.heading: Reaction Parameters
parameters.description: Interprets the parameters and input layers as raw.

parameters.label: Scale Multiplier
parameters.heading: Reaction Parameters
parameters.description: Changes the size of the patterns by altering the reaction rate relative to the diffusion rate. This leads to the reaction happening slower at extreme scales, and tiny scales freeze the reaction altogether. Therefore, having a larger scale may require letting the reaction run for more iterations/ticks to fully grow into the requested scale.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Reaction Parameters
parameters.description: Input layers for `alpha`, `beta`, and `gamma` on the [Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP|Node:cop/reactiondiffusion_block_begin] override these parameters. Input layers for `scale` and `coefficient` on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP multiply these parameters.

parameters.label: Alpha α (Feed)
parameters.heading: Gray-Scott Model
parameters.description: Chemical A is added into the simulation at a given "feed" rate. This is scaled with `(1.0f - A)` so that A does not exceed 1.0.

parameters.label: Beta β (Kill)
parameters.heading: Gray-Scott Model
parameters.description: Chemical B is removed from the simulation at a given "kill" rate. This is scaled with `(kill + feed) * B` so that it does not go below 0.0.

parameters.label: Alpha α
parameters.heading: Kenjiro Maginu Model
parameters.description: Controls the nonlinear self-activation of A. Essentially the reaction strength of A.

parameters.label: Beta β
parameters.heading: Kenjiro Maginu Model
parameters.description: Determines how strongly Chemical B reacts to the presence of Chemical A.

parameters.label: Gamma γ
parameters.heading: Kenjiro Maginu Model
parameters.description: Controls how strongly B is pulled back towards A. Essenially a damping or decay coefficient that prevents B from growing indefinitely.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Diffusion Coefficients
parameters.description: The `coefficient` input on the Reaction-Diffusion Block Begin COP multiplies these parameters.

parameters.label: Diffusion A
parameters.heading: Diffusion Coefficients
parameters.description: Controls how fast chemical A diffuses. Generally, the __Gray-Scott__ model sits at `1.0` and the __Kenjiro Maginu__ model sits at `1.0`.

parameters.label: Diffusion B
parameters.heading: Diffusion Coefficients
parameters.description: Controls how fast chemical B diffuses. Generally, the __Gray-Scott__ model sits at `0.5` and the __Kenjiro Maginu__ model sits at `1.0`.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Boundary
parameters.description: The `activation` mask must have an activation area within a valid area of the boundary otherwise the reaction can't grow.

parameters.label: Invert Boundary
parameters.heading: Boundary
parameters.description: Inverts the input boundary shape.

parameters.label: Boundary Threshold
parameters.heading: Boundary
parameters.description: The offset of the boundary shape. Higher values grow the shape and lower values shrink the shape.

parameters.label: Boundary Smoothing
parameters.heading: Boundary
parameters.description: The amount to blur the boundary shape, which causes the reaction to contract away from the border of the boundary. At lower Reaction Scales, high values of smoothing can sometimes cause instability.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.heading: Output Correction
parameters.description: Inverts the values of the output pattern.

parameters.label: Normalize Model
parameters.heading: Output Correction
parameters.description: Remaps the range of the output to keep the values consistent across models. This is useful since some models and modes have 'weaker' values.

parameters.label: Clamp Minimum
parameters.heading: Output Correction
parameters.description: The minimum pixel value of the image.

parameters.label: Clamp Maximum
parameters.heading: Output Correction
parameters.description: The maximum pixel value of the image.

entries.title: Solve Poisson Multigrid
entries.summary: Solves Poisson's equation in a rectangular region using geometric multigrid.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: Number of V-cycle iterations to perform. The solution will be more accurate with a higher number of iterations, but will also take longer to produce.

parameters.label: Smoothing Method
parameters.description: The method used for relaxation on up- and down-strokes. Gauss-Seidel offers better asymptotic convergence; it also requires less memory, as the red-black partitioning of cells allows for in-place smoothing. The Jacobi method, on the other hand, works on all pixels at once. This avoids systemic checkerboard patterns in the residuals, but requires an extra copy of the image.

parameters.label: Up Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations to perform on the up-stroke (after prolongation of the coarse solution). Higher values will increase cost, but also improve the solution.

parameters.label: Down Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations to perform on the down-stroke (before restriction of the fine residual). Higher values will increase cost, but also improve the solution.

parameters.label: Coarsest Smoothing Iterations
parameters.description: Number of smoothing iterations to perform at the final coarsest level (in lieu of an exact solution). Higher values will increase cost, but also improve the solution. Value of this parameter should be on the same order as square of __Target Coarse Dimensions__.

parameters.label: Target Coarse Dimensions
parameters.description: The multigrid solver iteratively coarsens the layer to build a hierarchy of grids for rapid convergence at all scales. This parameter controls when the coarsening ceases; namely, coarsening along a dimension will stop once the number of cells falls below Target Coarse Dimensions. While larger values give a leaner hierarchy with fewer levels, they also result in larger number of variables at the coarsest level, which in turn may require more __Coarsest Smoothing Iterations__ for adequate convergence.

parameters.label: X Borders
parameters.description: State of borders on the left and right sides of the layer. __Open__ borders correspond to Dirichlet boundary conditions (prescribing value of 0). __Closed__ borders correspond to Neumann boundary conditions (enforcing normal derivative of 0). When set to __Periodic__, left and right sides of the layer are virtually connected.

parameters.label: Y Borders
parameters.description: State of borders on the bottom and top sides of the image. __Open__ borders correspond to Dirichlet boundary conditions (prescribing value of 0). __Closed__ borders correspond to Neumann boundary conditions (enforcing normal derivative of 0). When set to __Periodic__, bottom and top sides of the layer are virtually connected.

entries.title: Tone Map
entries.summary: Applies a filmic tone mapping curve to compress a high dynamic range input into a displayable range.

parameters.label: Signature
parameters.description: The layer type that the source accepts. See [Signatures|/copernicus/glossary#signatures] for more information.

parameters.label: Operator
parameters.description: The filmic tone mapping operator to use.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: The amount of the new value to mix in with the original value. Higher values mix in more of the new value. Lower values mix in less of the new value. You can also set the RGBA [channels|Wp:Channel_(digital_image)] to which you apply the effects of this node. The default value is `1`, which means this node uses only the new value. See [Mask|/copernicus/glossary#mask] for more information.

parameters.label: Treat RGBA as Premultiplied
parameters.description: Treats RGBA as premultiplied, which multiplies the red, green, and blue channels by the alpha channel.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.description: The overall brightness of the image before the node applies tone mapping. Each unit increases brightness by one stop (doubling the light) and negative values darken the image.

parameters.label: Shoulder Strength
parameters.description: The strength of the curve at the shoulder section. Lower values cause a more gradual falloff at high luminance. The curve bends downward earlier and compresses the highlights more aggressively, which mutes the highlights. Higher values make the curve compress the highlights less initially so the curve stays linear for longer and only flattens near the top, which lets bright areas stay brighter. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Linear Strength
parameters.description: The linear (straight) part of the curve between the toe (shadows) and shoulder (highlights). Higher values steepen the mid section slope, which enhances contrast and brightness. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Linear Angle
parameters.description: The angle of the linear (straight) part of the curve.

parameters.label: Toe Strength
parameters.description: The amount to lift the dark parts of the image. Higher values lift shadows, which makes them more visible but less contrasted. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Toe Length
parameters.description: How much of the dynamic range is in the toe. With a small value, the toe is short and quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of `0` means there's no toe and a value of `1` means the toe takes up half the curve. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Strength
parameters.description: The speed at which bright highlights fall off to white. Higher values create a stronger falloff and more compressed highlight. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Length
parameters.description: Adds extra stops (F-stops) beyond the point where the curve normally hits pure white if the __Shoulder Strength__ is `0`. This controls the dynamic range of the curve and stretches the highlight's range so the curve stays below white longer. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Angle
parameters.description: The angle of the curve at the shoulder section.

parameters.label: Toe Strength
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the dark color in the tonemapper. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Shoulder Strength
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the bright color in the tonemapper. This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.description: The amount to adjust the steepness of the S-curve. Higher values increase the slope's steepness (darker) and lower values decrease the slope's steepness (lighter). This value is in the `0` to `1` range.

parameters.description: If no primitive exists at the specified __Primitive Path__, and this node creates a new primitive at that location, this parameter controls the primitive type of any ancestor primitives that may have to be created prior to creating the final primitive.

parameters.label: Create Options Block
parameters.description: You usually don't need to set or change this parameter yourself. This parameter is set to on when this node is part of a "variant block" (when created by the Add Variants to Existing Primitive tool), or off when this node is stand-alone (created by the Add Variants to New Primitive tool). (As this node cooks each node connected to its multi-input, it sets a [context option|/ref/contextoptions] containing the name of the current variant being created. When this is _off_, the context option is available to all nodes in the input chain. When this is _on_, the context option is pushed on the stack, and the [Begin Context Options Block LOP|Node:lop/begincontextoptionsblock] at the start of the block will pop it off the stack, hiding it from nodes further up the chain.)

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to which this node should add its variants.

parameters.label: Variant Set Strength
parameters.description: If the __Variant Set__ is `new`, indicates the strength of this variant set relative to other variant sets on this primitive. Like references, variant sets are applied in a well defined order so that overlapping opinions in a stronger variant set will always take precedence over opinions in weaker variant sets.

parameters.label: Variant Source Primitive
parameters.description: The path to the root of the primitives that should be copied from each variant input's scene graph into the variant.

parameters.label: Variant Name Default
parameters.description: Each variant input allows you to control the name of the variant that it will create within the variant set. This variant name is set in the second column of the interface displaying the list of connected inputs. The __Variant Name Default__ parameter controls the variant name that is used if no name is explicitly set in that second column of the connected inputs interface. In the expression you can use the `@input` local variable (`$IIDX` is deprecated) as the index of the current input (numbered from left to right starting at 1 for the multi-inputs).

parameters.label: Set Variant Selection
parameters.description: When this is on, this node also _selects_ (switches the primitive to) the last variant added. When this is off, this node does not affect the currently selected variant. (You can also use the [Set Variant LOP|Node:lop/setvariant] to select a variant.)

entries.title: APEX SOP Rig Builder
entries.summary: Authors APEX rigs and binds them to USD primitives.

parameters.label: Character Primitive
parameters.description: The primitive path that represents the character (typically this is the asset's root primitive). The `HoudiniApexCharacterAPI` schema is applied to this primitive, which references the rig and binds the __Shape Primitives__ to the rig's inputs and outputs.

parameters.label: Shape Primitives
parameters.description: The pattern specifying the primitives under the __Character Primitive__ to convert to geometry and add to the [packed folder structure|/character/kinefx/packedcharacterformat] for the SOP dive target's input geometry. The packed folder paths are named based on the relative path to the __Character Primitive__. The __Character Primitive__ configures bindings for these primitives to the character's rig inputs and outputs. The default pattern includes all the geometry primitives.

parameters.label: Rig Save Path
parameters.heading: Edit Folder Paths
parameters.description: When turned on, configures the save path for the rig data. When you write out USD using a [USD Render ROP|Node:out/usd], the geometry is saved to a `.bgeo.sc` file using this file path (after [output processing|/solaris/output#processors]). When turned off, the save path is automatically determined based on the node name.

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars.

parameters.label: Enable Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Indexed Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigindexattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called `primvars:<<name>>`, and an array of indices into those values called `primvars:<<name>>:indices`). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Element Array__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus __Import as Single Value__) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Value__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigscalarconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to __Import as Single Element Array__, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, `vector3f` instead of `vector3f[]`).

parameters.label: Enable Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Boolean Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigboolattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `bool`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 32-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguintattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 64-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguint64attribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint64`.

parameters.label: Enable Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Asset Path Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigassetpathattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `asset`.

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __USD Custom Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigcustomattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).

parameters.label: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.label_norm: enable translate uv attribute to st
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Translate UV Attribute to ST__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtranslateuvtost` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.heading: Import Geometry Data
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute `uv` into a USD primvar called `primvars:st`. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of `st` is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using `uv` is the common convention.)

entries.title: Asset Reference
entries.summary: Reference, Transform, and select variants of a USD Asset.

parameters.label: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: Scene graph path where the referenced asset will be attached.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will set it to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind]. Setting this parameter to `Auto` will not author a Kind on the leaf primitive where the reference is added. Instead, it will examine the Kind of the prim after setting the reference, and automatically set the Kind of ancestor prims to ensure the leaf primitive is part of a valid model hierarchy. Note that this may result in adding a Kind to ancestor prims that were not created by this node. If the referenced prim has no kind, or is not a model kind, `Auto` mode will not author Kind on any prim.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this type.

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.description: Mark the new or modified prims as [instanceable (as in "native instancing")|/solaris/glossary#instancing]. This saves memory if you reference the same branch into multiple places, but makes the descendants of the referenced prim not editable. If this option is off, the prims are not explicitly marked as not instanceable. Instead, the current instanceable value on each prim is left unchanged.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Reference
parameters.description: The source of the asset being referenced. By default, this node will switch to the second input, when connected, and use __File__ otherwise. Users can also specify which source if they wish.

parameters.label: Reference File
parameters.heading: File Reference
parameters.description: Click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/chooser_file] __Open floating file chooser__ button to load the USD file from disk you want to add as a reference.

parameters.label: Reference Primitive Path
parameters.heading: File Reference
parameters.description: Drag a primitive from the Scene Graph Tree to this field or enter a path to the primitive you want to use as a reference.

parameters.label: Time Offset (in Frames)
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: Offsets all time samples from the file or target primitive on the first input. You can use this to re-time animations in the references file.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: Scales all time samples from the file or target primitive on the first input. You can use this to re-time animations in the references file. A value of `1` means normal speed. Values smaller than `1` make animations slower, values greater than `1` make the animation appear in slow motion.

parameters.label: Handle Missing Files
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: If the reference is to an external file, this controls what the node does if the referenced file does not exist.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Align To Up Axis
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: When enabled, the reference will be transformed so its up axis matches the current stage.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Primitives
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Primitives
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: Number of Variants
parameters.heading: Variants
parameters.description: You can perform multiple variant selections in a single Set Variant node. Set this to the number of selections you want to make, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove selections.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Variants
parameters.description: The primitive(s) you want to define as variants of a __Variant Set__. You can click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Select__ button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching.

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.heading: Variants
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to select a variant from.

parameters.label: Variant Name
parameters.heading: Variants
parameters.description: If not choosing the variant by index, this parameter is the name of the variant that should be selected within the specified variant set. If this value is an empty string, any existing variant selection specified in the active layer will be cleared. This will "reveal" any variant selection opinions authored in weaker layers. If this value is set to the special string `<block>`, an explicit empty variant selection will be made, blocking any variant selection opinions from weaker layers, leaving the chosen set without any variant selected.  If this is set to a list of variant names (space or comma- separated), then this will use the first one that matches a valid variant name in each prim's variant set.

entries.title: Assign Material
entries.summary: Assigns a material to one or more USD primitives. You can use also programmatically assign materials using VEX, programmatically override material settings for each assignment, and programmatically assign materials to geometry subsets.

parameters.label: Number of Materials
parameters.description: You can perform multiple assignments within one node. Set this to the number of assignments you want to perform, or use the plus and minus button to add or remove assignments.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) you want to assign the material to. You can click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Select__ button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching.

parameters.label: Pattern Is USD Path Expression
parameters.description: Authors the collection as a USD path expression instead of a hard coded list of includes and excludes. USD path expressions are evaluated as needed by comparing the expression to the prims on the composed stage. This approach is slower than an explicit list of includes and excludes, but allows for more dynamic collection contents. For example, the path expression `//chair` will find all prims named `chair` in the composed stage, even if the prims didn't exist when the collection was authored. There are several modes of this LOP that do not support USD path expressions. If you are doing direct bindings, or using VEXpressions or CVEX to calculate material assignments or material property overrides per-primitive, path expressions are not supported. In these cases, the path expression will be evaluated for the current stage, and replaced with a hard coded list. If this occurs, a warning will appear on this node to indicate that the path expression will not be saved to the USD stage.

parameters.label: Specify Material Using
parameters.description: How to specify the material to assign.

parameters.label: Material Path
parameters.description: When __Specify Material Using__ is __Explicit path__, the USD path to the material primitive to use for binding.

parameters.label: VEXpression
parameters.description: When __Specify Material Using__ is __VEXpression__, this [VEX snippet|/vex/snippets] is computed for each selected primitive. You can use `@primpath` (the path of the current primitive), `@elemnum` (the index of the current prim in the list of selected prims), and `@numelem` (the total number of selected prims). Must return a string containing a path to the material to assign to the current prim.

parameters.label: CVEX Node
parameters.description: When __Specify Material Using__ is __CVEX__, the path to a CVEX VOP network. See [CVEX VOP networks|#cvex] above.

parameters.label: Parameters Override
parameters.description: Whether and how to override individual material parameters for each assignment.

parameters.label: Override VEXpression
parameters.description: When __Parameter Override__ is __VEXpression__, this [VEX snippet|/vex/snippets] is run for each selected primitive. The settings under __CVEX Bindings__ control how material parameters are mapped to VEX variables. You override a material parameter by assigning to the corresponding variable. You can also use `@primpath` (the path of the current primitive), `@elemnum` (the index of the current prim in the list of selected prims), and `@numelem` (the total number of selected prims).

parameters.label: Override CVEX Node
parameters.description: When __Parameters override__ is __CVEX__, the path to a CVEX VOP network. See [CVEX VOP networks|#cvex] above.

parameters.label: VEX Bindings to Export
parameters.description: A pattern that selects VEXpression parameters that should be exported from the final VEX program.  I.e., these are the output parameters that will be used for material parameter override.

parameters.label: Materials Parent Path
parameters.description: Specifies the USD path to the parent primitive inside which the LOP should author any automatically created materials with overrides.

parameters.label: Materials Parent Type
parameters.description: Specifies the primitive type of any ancestors that needs to be authored in order to automatically create materials with overrides. ~~~~~ CVEX Bindings ~~~~

parameters.label: Create and Bind Geometry Subsets
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: When this is on, the __Primitives__ parameter should point to a geometry or geometry subset primitive, and the node runs the VEX snippet for each _geometry element_ (for example, polygon face) in the geometry, instead of for each selected primitive. In the snippet, `@elemnum` is the index of the current element, and `@numelem` is the total number of elements in the geometry. The node will automatically create geometry subsets for each set of elements with the same material path.

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: Sets the __Purpose__ method for the assignments. This controls what types of renders the assignment applies to.

parameters.label: Strength
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: Controls the strength of the assignment "opinion" relative to any conflicting assignments on descendant prims under the assigned primitives in the tree. For example, if this node assigns `/materials/zerbra` to `/a`, but `/a/b/c` already is assigned `/materials/tiger`.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: How to express the material assignment in USD.

parameters.label: Include Descendant Primitives in Collection
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: When __Method__ is __Collection Based__, turn on this option to have the collection authored for the collection-based binding be marked to expand all descendants of the target primitives. This will cause the material assignment to be applied to the entire scene graph tree branch. The equivalent of this behavior always occurs when using __Direct__ binding, which always inherits down the scene graph tree.

parameters.label: Path
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: When __Method__ is __Collection Based__, the collection-based binding will be defined on a primitive at this path. Also, if this LOP node needs to create a new collection, it will create it on a this primitive as well. If the path is empty, the LOP node tries to use the deepest ancestor common to all primitives given in the __Primitives__ parameter.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Material Binding
parameters.description: Specifies the collection-based material binding name. If empty, the name of the material will be used.

entries.title: Assign Prototypes
entries.summary: Switch point instances or USD instanceable prims to instance a different prototype.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: How you specify what to replace.

parameters.label: Instancer Path
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __PointInstancer - By Prototype__, the scene graph path to the instancer containing the prototype you want to replace. This can be a space-separated list of multiple instancer paths.

parameters.label: Prototype Index
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __PointInstancer - By Prototype__, the index of the prototype you want to replace.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[0] /geometry/instancer[1]`). To select all instances in an instancer, use `/<<path>>[*]`. To select a range, use `/geometry/instancer[4-7]` (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example `/geometry/instancer[2][7]`. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, `/geometry/instancer[{@weights>0.5}]`.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Native Instances__, a list of paths to [instanceable prims|/solaris/glossary#instancing].

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Replace With
parameters.description: How to choose the replacement prim.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Reference File
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Prototype Name
parameters.heading: Replace With

parameters.label: Frame Offset
parameters.heading: Replace With
parameters.description: If the prototype is animated, use this to get the prototype as it appears at a different point in the timeline. This lets you replace instances with a re-timed prototype, without affecting the other instances.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: Replace With
parameters.description: If the prototype is animated, use this to scale the animation on the replacement. This lets you replace instances with a re-timed prototype, without affecting the other instances.

parameters.label: Modify Source Primitive
parameters.heading: Replace With
parameters.description: When __Replace With > Type__ is __Primitives__ and __Source__ is __First input__, what to do with the primitive you based the new prototype on (from __Primitive Path__).

entries.title: Attribute VOP
entries.summary: Create/edit USD attribute values using a VOP network.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. parameters.label: Allow Instance Proxy Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When this is on, the pattern in the __Primitives__ parameter will be allowed to match instance proxy primitives (instanced ancestors of a primitive marked as instanceable). Since instance proxy primitives cannot be directly modified in USD, this mode is primarily used to allow the VEX code to pull data from the instance proxy primitives, and apply values to some non-instanced ancestor primitive.

parameters.label: Run on Elements of Array Attributes
parameters.label_norm: run on elements of array attributes
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When this is on, the node evaluates the VOP network *for each array element* of array attributes, on each prim. In this mode, the built-in `elemnum` refers to the array index, and `numelem` refers to the length of the _largest_ array. (When this is off, array attributes are available in the network as array-type variables.) If some array attributes have shorter length, their elements are padded with the last element. parameters.heading: Vex Setup
parameters.description: Where to get the VEX to run. You should usually leave this set to __Myself__ and build a VOP network inside this node, unless you have a good reason to choose one of the other options.

parameters.label: Node Path
parameters.heading: Vex Setup
parameters.description: When __Vex Source__ is __Other Node__, the node path of the node that generates the VEX code.

parameters.label: Script
parameters.heading: Vex Setup

parameters.label: Re-load VEX Functions

parameters.label: Compiler

parameters.label: Force Compile

parameters.label: Evaluation Node Path
parameters.heading: Vex Setup
parameters.description: Certain VEX functions, like `ch()`, evaluate parameters on this node. entries.title: Karma Background Plate
entries.summary: Sets up AOVs and "hold-out" or "matte" objects that leave "holes" in the scene through which the background is visible. These prims still take shadows and contribute to reflections as if they were the background.

parameters.label: Hold-Out Primitives
parameters.description: A space-separated list of prim paths for the objects you want to act as hold-outs.

parameters.label: RenderSettings Prim
parameters.description: The prim path of a USD Render Settings prim to use to set up the background and matte settings. The default is `/Render/rendersettings`, which is the default for where the Karma render node looks for render settings. If this prim doesn't already exist in the incoming stage, this node will create it.

parameters.label: Material Path Prefix
parameters.description: This is automatically prefixed to any material paths that are not absolute (do not start with a slash). This lets you specify relative paths in the multi-parm, and set their common USD parent hierarchy in this one parameter.

parameters.label: Allow Shader Parameter Animation
parameters.description: When it is turned off, all USD values are assumed non-animatable and will be authored at a default time code. And, with this option turned on, shader node parameters that are time-dependent will get translated to USD values at non-default time codes, while time-independent parameters will still author a value at a default time code. Note, checking parameter time dependency can be costly and may add up to a large portion of the shader translation time. Since the vast majority of shader nodes don't have animated parameters, this toggle is off by default to save the work involved in checking it.

parameters.label: Plate
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: The file path of the background image to use.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: Horizontal and vertical scaling factors for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered image size, so for example a horizontal scale of `1` is the width of the rendered image.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: Horizontal and vertical offsets for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered images size, so for example a horizontal offset of `0.25` moves the background image to the right 1/4 of the width of the rendered image.

parameters.label: Use Offscreen Texture
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: If the background plate does not perfectly cover the camera view, the "real" background (empty space) will show through. Use this to replace empty space with a texture. If you leave this off, the node will fill empty space with the __Offscreen Color__ instead.

parameters.label: Offscreen Texture
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: When __Use Offscreen Texture__ is on, the file path of the texture image to use to cover empty space.

parameters.label: Offscreen Color
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: When __Use Offscreen Texture__ is off, the color to use for any "empty space" if the background plate does not fully cover the camera view.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Background
parameters.description: When __Use Offscreen Texture__ is on, this sets the rotation of the offscreen texture in 3D space.

parameters.label: Shadows
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs
parameters.description: Whether to record all holdout shadows in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag.

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs
parameters.description: Generate an AOV for diffuse bounces on holdout objects.

parameters.label: Emission
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs
parameters.description: Generate an AOV for light emissions on holdout objects.

parameters.label: Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs
parameters.description: Generate an AOV for glossy reflections on holdout objects. When disabled, the background shader will become diffuse only, reflectivity and metallic shader parameters will be set to 0.

parameters.label: Reflection Occlusion
parameters.heading: Holdout AOVs
parameters.description: When __Glossy Reflection__ is enabled, whether to record all holdout reflection occlusion in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: Whether the source prims are regular __Primitives__, or a __PointInstancer__. This node does not support _nested_ point instances as sources.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Source Instances
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Target
parameters.description: Whether the blend targets are the same as the source, regular primitives, or point instances. You _can_ use a nested point instance as a _target_.

parameters.label: Target
parameters.heading: Target
parameters.description: When __Target Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Target Instance
parameters.heading: Target
parameters.description: When __Target Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Import Time
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: Specify the frame at which the source and/or target geometry are imported into the embedded SOP network to build the constraints. The default `$FF` expression forces the constraint LOP to be time dependent, which is needed when operating on a non time-dependent network that has time samples driving the source or target primitives. However, for better performance with a non time-dependent network with no time samples, it is recommended to use a static value instead.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: How to blend the transforms.

parameters.label: Rotation Blending
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: Rotation channels typically don't blend well when treated as Euler angles, and straight linear blending can result in flips and odd rotations. Instead, shortest path blending can be used to properly blend orientations represented by Euler rotation angles.

parameters.label: Blends
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: Set this to the number of blend weight you want to set for the prims selected above.

parameters.label: Blend
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: How much weight to give this transform when blending. The interpretation of this value is different when __Method__ is __Difference__.

parameters.label: Mask
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: For each blend, select which components (`TX,TY,TZ,RX,RY,RZ,SX,SY,SZ`) to blend.

entries.title: Cache
entries.summary: Caches the results of cooking the network at different times, increasing playback speed.

parameters.label: Cache Behavior
parameters.description: Specifies when and how frames are combined into the cache.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: The first frame, last frame, and increment size (in frames) between each cook request made of the input to populate the cache. The first two values control the range of frames over which the Cache should apply. The third value allows the stage to be super-sampled for improved motion blur, or sub-sampled to preserve memory (at the cost of accuracy, as USD simply uses linear interpolation between time sampled values).

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph is the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. However, if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Turn on this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives are tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types that respect the visibility attribute. This option is not available when __Cache Behavior__ is set to __Cache Cooked Frames__, as it requires all the frames to be cooked in order for the visibility authoring to behave properly.

parameters.label: Action

parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.
