parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Primitives
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Primitives
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: USD currently does not have look-at constraints. This node calculates the per-frame transform to fulfill the constraint and applies it to the object. See the [Light tool help|/nodes/lop/light#tool] for how to set up the look-at constraint interactively in the viewport.

parameters.label: Enable Look At
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Turns on the constraint that orients this object to look at a point or another object.

parameters.label: Look At Position
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: If __Enable Look At__ is on and, this is a point in space this object will look at. If __Look At Primitive__ is not blank, this is an *offset* from the centroid of the target object (in the local space of that object).

parameters.label: Look At Primitive
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: The path to a USD prim this object should look at. If this is not blank, __Look At Position__ is an *offset* from this centroid of the target object.

parameters.label: Up Vector Method
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Controls how the up vector is set.

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: When __Up Vector Method__ is __Custom__, this is the up axis to use for the look-at constraint.

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: A twist rotation (around the -Z axis, clockwise, in degrees), applied after the lookout transform.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.heading: View
parameters.description: Whether the view through this camera is perspective or orthographic.

parameters.label: Clipping Range
parameters.heading: View
parameters.description: Don't show geometry closer than the near distance or farther away than the far distance (in world units).

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.heading: View
parameters.description: Perspective focal length in millimeters. This drives an expression on a hidden parameter to generate a value in the units expected by USD, which is tenths of a world unit, as defined by the stage's meters per unit setting.

parameters.label: Control Aperture
parameters.heading: Aperture
parameters.description: Similar to the standard control menus associated with each parameter on an Edit Properties LOP, this menu controls how both the horizontal and vertical aperture attributes should be handled.

parameters.label: Horizontal Aperture
parameters.heading: Aperture
parameters.description: Horizontal aperture in millimeters. This drives an expression on a hidden parameter to generate a value in the units expected by USD, which is tenths of a world unit, as defined by the stage's meters per unit setting. <!---

parameters.label: Vertical Aperture
parameters.heading: Aperture
parameters.description: Vertical aperture in millimeters. This drives an expression on a hidden parameter to generate a value in the units expected by USD, which is tenths of a world unit, as defined by the stage's meters per unit setting. --->

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Aperture
parameters.description: When __Control Aperture__ is set to `Set Horizontal Aperture and Aspect Ratio`, this parameter specifies the desired aperture aspect ratio used to calculate the vertical aperture from the horizontal aperture. Render Settings and Render Product nodes can use the camera aperture aspect ratio to set the correct resolution automatically.

parameters.label: Horizontal Aperture Offset
parameters.heading: Offsets
parameters.description: Horizontal offset of the aperture from the center of the image defined by the view frustum expressed in millimeters. This drives an expression on a hidden parameter to generate a value in the units expected by USD, which is tenths of a world unit, as defined by the stage's meters per unit setting.

parameters.label: Vertical Aperture Offset
parameters.heading: Offsets
parameters.description: Vertical offset of the aperture from the center of the image defined by the view frustum expressed in millimeters. This drives an expression on a hidden parameter to generate a value in the units expected by USD, which is tenths of a world unit, as defined by the stage's meters per unit setting.

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.heading: Viewport Control
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the camera in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.heading: Viewport Control
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this camera from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide cameras that are used for texture projection or other utility purposes, and are not actually meant for viewing the scene.

parameters.label: Background Image
parameters.heading: Viewport Control
parameters.description: Draw a background image behind the geometry in the viewer when looking through this camera. This can be used to replace background elements in the scene with a pre-rendered image, saving memory and processing time.

parameters.label: Foreground Image
parameters.heading: Viewport Control
parameters.description: Draw a foreground image over the geometry in the viewer when looking through this camera. If the image contains a depth AOV, this is used to z-composite the image into the scene. This can be used to replace large portions of the scene with a pre-rendered image, saving memory and processing time. Houdini uses [OCIO|/solaris/ocio] to color correct images loaded from disk. OCIO is capable of guessing the image's color space based on the image filename (for example, `myimage-srgb_texture.jpg`) or format.

parameters.label: You can precisely control exposure with several parameters. Exposure is calculated as follows
parameters.label_norm: you can precisely control exposure with several parameters. exposure is calculated as follows
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: {{{ linearScale = (exposureTime * exposureIso * powf(2.0f, exposureExponent) * exposureResponsivity) / (100.0f * exposureFStop * exposureFStop) }}}

parameters.label: Shutter Open
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Shutter-open time, relative to the start of frame, in `UsdTimeCode` units. This is used to calculate motion blur. You can use a negative value to indicate that the shutter opens _before_ each frame.

parameters.label: Shutter Close
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Shutter-close time, relative to the start of frame, in `UsdTimeCode` units. If this is not greater than __Shutter Open__, the shutter will never open and the renderer will produce a black image.

parameters.label: Focus Distance
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Distance from the camera to the focal plane in world units.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Exposure adjustment, as a `log base-2` value.  The default of `0` has no effect. A value of `1` will double the image-plane intensities in a rendered image; a value of `-1` will halve them.

parameters.label: Exposure F-Stop

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives

parameters.label: Top Radius

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this `displayColor` parameter as an override.

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display __Color__. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.

parameters.label: Double Sided

parameters.label: Transform Order

entries.summary: Creates/edits collections using primitive patterns.

parameters.label: Create Primitive If Required
parameters.description: If the primitive at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, the node will create it. (The node creates a primitive with no defined Type.)

parameters.label: Default Primitive Path
parameters.description: The default primitive on which to author the collections. This parameter is referenced by default by the individual __Primitive Path__ parameters for each collection. The value of this parameter is automatically set to the value of the Collection __Primitive Path__ preference when this node is created.

parameters.label: Number of Collections
parameters.description: The number of collections to create or modify.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Turn off this option to turn off an individual collection edit without losing the parameter values that define it. ~~~

parameters.label: Collection Name
parameters.description: The name of the collection to create/edit. This parameter can be left blank, in which case no USD collection will be authored.

parameters.label: TIP
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: This tip is valid for both __Primitives__ and __Exclude Primitives__. In addition to the standard primitive patterns, you can use the special token `%self` in this parameter to specify the current members of this collection (if it already exists). Note that this does take existing exclusions into account, and is therefore slightly different from the use of `%self` in the __Primitives__ parameter. This slightly different definition makes it easy to invert a collection's membership by including `*` and excluding `%self`.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Pattern Is USD Path Expression
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: Authors the collection as a USD path expression instead of a hard coded list of includes and excludes. USD path expressions are evaluated as needed by comparing the expression to the prims on the composed stage. This approach is slower than an explicit list of includes and excludes, but allows for more dynamic collection contents. For example, the path expression `//chair` will find all prims named `chair` in the composed stage, even if the prims didn't exist when the collection was authored. When using a path expression, the __Exclude Primitives__ parameter is disabled as it has no effect. USD collection must either use the includes/excludes form, or the path expression form. The equivalent of excludes can be encoded in a path expression using the `-` operator (e.g. `//mountain - /root/mountain` will match all prims named `mountain` except `/root/mountain`).

parameters.label: Add Exclusions
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: Show another primitive pattern parameter for specifying primitives for the collection's exclusion relationship. During composition, USD removes primitives from the exclude relationship from the list of prims in the include relationship to get the final collection contents. If this option is off, the exclude relationship for the collection is unchanged by this node.

parameters.label: Exclude Primitives
parameters.heading: Options
parameters.description: Using the same format as the __Primitives__ parameter, specify a set of primitives that should be explicitly excluded from the collection.

parameters.label: Converted Attribs
parameters.heading: Attributes

parameters.label: Index Attributes
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: Converted attributes which should be index primvars.

parameters.label: Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which SOP string or integer attributes represent subsets of the geometry. The importer puts elements with the same value for this attribute into their own geometry subsets. Each attribute's subsets are added to a subset family (named from the original attribute) which indicates that the subsets are related. The subset family's type is set to `partition` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting and that every element of the primitive appears in a subset. If there are elements with empty string values (which are not added to a subset), the family type is instead set to `nonOverlapping` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting but some elements do not appear in a subset. The family's type is authored as an attribute on the parent primitive, for example `subsetFamily:shop_materialpath:familyType`. Subsets can be created from point or primitive partition attributes on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points. The importer will try to set the subset name to the attribute value, but may need to change the name to make it a legal USD primitive name. The importer stores the raw attribute value on the geometry subset prim as Custom Data with the key `partitionValue`.

parameters.label: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: When creating subsets from __Subset Attributes__, the subsets are named by combining the attribute name with the partition attribute's value (a string or integer). This avoids name collisions when multiple partition attributes contain the same values, but can be undesirable if precise control of the subset names is required. For string attributes, if this option is turned off, the attribute values are directly used as the subset names.

parameters.label: Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: Primitive groups which will be converted into GeomSubests on meshes.

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.heading: Attributes

parameters.label: Topology Attributes

parameters.label: Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: Any polygon meshes not already tagged as subdivs, set the `subdivisionScheme` to `catmullClark`.

parameters.label: Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: USD supports an `orientation` attribute on mesh primitives that indicates whether polygons have a left-handed or right-handed ordering, while SOP geometry is always left-handed ordering. When this option is on, the importer always reorders vertices (and associated primvars) to be right-handed. This is useful when round tripping right-handed oriented polygons from USD into SOPs and back into USD. The data is always converted to a left handed ordering when importing it into SOPs. If you imported the polygons back into USD without this option, they would be left-handed, unlike the original.

parameters.label: Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Attributes
parameters.description: USD has a fallback value of 1.0 for the width of curves and points, which is often far wider/thicker than desired. If the SOP geometry does not explicitly author `width`/`pscale` data, this control can be used instead to explicitly author a USD value.

entries.title: Component Output
entries.summary: Assembles the final Component prim, in a network created by the Component Builder tool.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Component Options
parameters.description: Indicates the source type connected to the node. Most of the time 'Component Geometry' is the right choice, as it expects other Component Builder nodes as inputs. __Input Primitives__ reads the input primitives as-is. __Scene Import__ will read the geometry and materials of a component from the [Scene Import LOP|Node:lop/sceneimport].

parameters.label: Root Prim
parameters.heading: Component Options
parameters.description: The root prim of the component asset, which is generally the same as the name. Used when not detected from the input nodes.

parameters.label: Kind
parameters.heading: Component Options
parameters.description: The root prim of the component asset, which is generally the same as the name.  Used when not detected from the input nodes.

parameters.label: Set Default Variants
parameters.heading: Set Default Variants
parameters.description: Sets the default geometry and material variant selections for the component.

parameters.label: Geometry
parameters.heading: Set Default Variants
parameters.description: When __Set Default Variants__ is on, the name of the default geometry variant. (The name of each geometry variant is set on the corresponding [Component Geometry LOP|Node:lop/componentgeometry] using the __Advanced > Geo Variant Name__ parameter. The default uses the name of the node as the variant name.)

parameters.label: Material
parameters.heading: Set Default Variants
parameters.description: When __Set Default Variants__ is on, the name of the default geometry variant. The name of each material variant is set on the corresponding [Component Material LOP|Node:lop/componentmaterial] using the __Variant Name__ parameter. The default is the name of the node.

parameters.label: Setup Class for Inherits
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Adds an [inherits arc from the Component prim a class prim|/solaris/component_builder#class], so this component may receive shot- and sequence-specific overrides.

parameters.label: Set Variants Inside (Extra Layer)
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Lets you override the variant selections using Lop nodes inside of this node. This lets you create variant sets that control both the `geo` and `mtl` variants. A consequence of this, is your geometry is likely to disappear from the viewport and scene graph tree, until you choose Default Variants on this node, or select variants inside of the Component Output manually. One use case for this is an "uber" variant, that controls both the `geo` and `mtl` variant selections at the same time. Such a variant cannot work if the layers already have variant selections, because the existing variant selection opinions are equally as strong.

parameters.label: Instanceable by Default
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Set Instanceable property to True on the root prim. This means that whenever a this asset is referenced into a scene, it will be implicitly instanced by USD.

parameters.label: Asset Identifier
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Optional metadata describing where this component lives on-disk.

parameters.label: Asset Name
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Optional metadata describing the name of this component lives.

parameters.label: Asset Version
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Optional version string.

parameters.label: Asset Dependencies
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Optional string listing arbitrary dependencies.

parameters.label: Houdini Icon
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Optional path to an icon file, or Houdini icon name (for example, `SHELF_tree_conifer`). If you set this, Houdini's Scene Graph Tree pane will display the component prim using this icon.

parameters.label: Custom Data
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Use this multi-parm to add custom attributes to the main __Component__ parm.

parameters.label: Load from Disk
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Once you have written the file out to USD, you can turn this on to load the component output from disk rather than cooking the input network.

parameters.label: Save to Disk
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Exports the component to disk.

parameters.label: Save to Disk in Background
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Exports the component to disk in a background thread.

parameters.label: Reload
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Reloads the component from disk.

parameters.label: Add to Asset Catalog
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Adds the exported asset from disk, into the Asset Catalog. If __Variant Layers__ is turned on, the variant layers will also be added to the Asset Catalog.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Missing

parameters.label: File Name
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Missing

parameters.label: Location
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Path to the component model's `asset.usda` on disk. By default is derived from the component's name.

parameters.label: Handle Missing Files
parameters.heading: Caching
parameters.description: Controls whether missing files are errors or warnings.

parameters.label: Payload Layer
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: The name of the file which is payloaded into the asset. It gathers the geometry, material, and extra layers. When __Source__ is set to __Input Primitives__ this node will gather everything into this layer and payload it. Location is relative to the `asset.usda` defined in the __Location__ path.

parameters.label: Geometry Layer
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Name of the file where all the component geometry and component geometry variant output is stored. Location is relative to the `asset.usda` defined in the __Location__ path.

parameters.label: Material Layer
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Name of the file where all the component materials is stored. Only applies to component materials defined below component geometry variants, if those are present to in the network. Location is relative to the `asset.usda` defined in the __Location__ path.

parameters.label: Extra Layer
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Name of the file where any opinions authored within this node's dive target are stored. Location is relative to the `asset.usda` defined in the __Location__ path.

parameters.label: Localize External Non-USD Files
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Copies any non-USD files into a subdirectory of the output location, to make portable, reusable USD models. External files are copied and localized into the specified __Sub-Directory__. The most common use case is to ensure texture maps for a model are all located within the asset's output directory.

parameters.label: Sub-Directory
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: The sub-folder of the output location, where localized files will be copied. ~~~

parameters.label: Save Source Nodes as Recipe
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Enables saving the component builder nodes to a recipe, to easily resume editing later. Only nodes connected to the component output node, or contained within the nodes connected, will be saved to the recipe.

parameters.label: Recipe File
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: The sidecar file where the source recipe is saved.

parameters.label: Recipe Name
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: The name of the recipe saved within the file. This recipe is hidden from normal recipe tools, but may appear in the recipe manager. ~~~ Which axis (Y or Z) was treated as "up" when this layer was created. This is not used to transform the layer. It serves as a hint that can help identify the cause of orientation problems when you combine USD layers.

parameters.label: Meters per Unit
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: The scale at which the scene was modeled. For example, Houdini scenes are often modeled at meter scale (`1.0`) for physical accuracy, while Maya modelers often work at centimeter scale (`0.01`). Like __Up axis__, Houdini doesn't act on this information (it can't automatically scale layers because it can't know which of all the attributes in the scene represent lengths, distances, movement vectors, and so on). It just serves as a hint to help identify the cause of scaling problems when combining USD layers. ~~~

parameters.label: Color Configuration
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Sets the default color configuration to be used to interpret the per-attribute color spaces in the composed USD stage. This is specified as an asset path which can be resolved to the color configuration file.

parameters.label: Color Management System
parameters.heading: Export Options
parameters.description: Sets the name of the color management system used to interpret the color configuration file pointed at by the active __Color Configuration__. ~~~

This option allows the metadata described by this node to be copied to the stage's root layer as well as being set on the active layer. parameters.label: Variant Layers
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: When this is on, the node generates an extra USD layer file per variant, along with a thumbnail. This can make it more convenient to work with variants as separate assets, for example in the Layout node's asset catalog, or an asset management system.

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to use when writing out separate USD files for each variant. The default variant set name for geometry variants created with the component builder network is `geo` (the default for this parameter). The default variant set name for material variants created with the component builder network is `mtl`. If you changed the default variant set name, or somehow created variants outside the component builder system, you may need to change this.

parameters.label: Directory Name
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: The name of the subdirectory (next to the main USD file) to write the variant layer files into. ~~~ This node can apply some transformations to the layer stack before writing out files. These transformations do not affect the final composed stage, only the number of layer files generated.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers authored above Layer Break nodes from being written to disk by this ROP. This allows a Layer Break node to dictate which portions of the LOP Network are to be saved. Disabling this option allows this behavior to be overridden, forcing the full stage authored by the LOP network to be written to disk. This may be used for debugging purposes, or to write a complete scene to disk for rendering.

parameters.label: Strip Post-Layers
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers added using the [Hom:hou.LopNetwork#editablePostLayer] method from being written to disk. With this option disabled, these post-layers are flattened into the layer __Output File__ layer.

parameters.label: Flush Data After Each Frame
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See [saving animation|#anim] above.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated.

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.heading: Variant Layers
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See [Filter Time Samples|#filtertimesamples]

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using __Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References)__ to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: If you use the [Load Layer LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer] to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, layers generated by importing data from SOPs with [SOP Import|Node:lop/sopimport] are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers imported from SOPs as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers.

parameters.label: Output Processors
parameters.heading: Output processing
parameters.description: Add an [output processor|/solaris/output#processors] to this node. Output processors are Python plugins that can alter the file locations and file path strings used for external files. The USD render node starts with one default output processor (called `Use Relative Paths`, see below). (See [output processors|/solaris/output#processors] for information on how to write an output processor plugin.)

parameters.label: Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: Set this to the *name* of a root primitive on the current stage to set it as the [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for the top-level file.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layer with No Default Primitive
parameters.label_norm: error saving layer with no default primitive
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: When this is on, the render node will error and stop cooking if you haven't specified a [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for all layers being written out. This is a way to force yourself to make sure layers have default prims, so you know you can reference in files without having to manually specify a top-level prim.

parameters.label: Save ROP's Time Information to Output
parameters.label_norm: save rop's time information to output
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: Write the start and end frames, as well as the current frames per second setting, to the top-level output file.

parameters.label: Clear Houdini-Specific Custom Data
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: LOP networks often attach Houdini-specific custom data to layers, prims, and properties. Houdini does not need this data to be stored on disk (usually it is related to how to write files), so by default Houdini strips out this data before saving. Normally there's no reason to turn this parameter off (it's possible it might help SideFX diagnosing a problem).

parameters.label: Ensure Basic Metrics are Set on All Layers
parameters.label_norm: ensure basic metrics are set on all layers
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: This options ensures that the `upAxis` and `metersPerUnit` metadata is set in every USD file written to disk. If a value has not been explicitly authored on a layer by the LOP Network, the default up axis and meters per unit values from the Lighting Preferences are used.

This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated.

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See [Filter Time Samples|#filtertimesamples]

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using __Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References)__ to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: If you use the [Load Layer LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer] to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, layers generated by importing data from SOPs with [SOP Import|Node:lop/sopimport] are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers imported from SOPs as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers.

parameters.label: Output Processors
parameters.heading: Output processing
parameters.description: Add an [output processor|/solaris/output#processors] to this node. Output processors are Python plugins that can alter the file locations and file path strings used for external files. The USD render node starts with one default output processor (called `Use Relative Paths`, see below). (See [output processors|/solaris/output#processors] for information on how to write an output processor plugin.)

parameters.label: Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: Set this to the *name* of a root primitive on the current stage to set it as the [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for the top-level file.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layer with No Default Primitive
parameters.label_norm: error saving layer with no default primitive
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: When this is on, the render node will error and stop cooking if you haven't specified a [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for all layers being written out. This is a way to force yourself to make sure layers have default prims, so you know you can reference in files without having to manually specify a top-level prim.

parameters.label: Save ROP's Time Information to Output
parameters.label_norm: save rop's time information to output
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: Write the start and end frames, as well as the current frames per second setting, to the top-level output file.

parameters.label: Clear Houdini-Specific Custom Data
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: LOP networks often attach Houdini-specific custom data to layers, prims, and properties. Houdini does not need this data to be stored on disk (usually it is related to how to write files), so by default Houdini strips out this data before saving. Normally there's no reason to turn this parameter off (it's possible it might help SideFX diagnosing a problem).

parameters.label: Ensure Basic Metrics are Set on All Layers
parameters.label_norm: ensure basic metrics are set on all layers

parameters.label: Report Network Use
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Print the number of bytes sent or received by the distributed simulation nodes during cooks triggered by this node. This does not track network usage from, for example, saving a file to an NFS mount. It only tracks the network communication of distributed Houdini nodes. When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See [saving animation|#anim] above.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in __Primitive Paths__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type. ~~~

parameters.label: Axis
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The axis the spine of the cone is aligned with.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The length of the spine of the cone (from the point to the base).

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The radius of the base of the cone.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this `displayColor` parameter as an override.

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display __Color__. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.

parameters.label: Double Sided
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: For renderers that distinguish between single-sided and double-sided surfaces, controls whether this prim is double-sided. Making surfaces double-sided is necessary for flat thin surfaces, or open surfaces where the camera can see both the inside and outside of the surface.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

entries.title: Configure APEX Rig
entries.summary: Configures and attaches simple APEX rigs to USD primitives.

parameters.label: Rig

parameters.label: Primitives

You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. parameters.label: Root Primitive

The `HoudiniApexCharacterAPI` schema is applied to this primitive, and this adds attributes that define how the __Primitives__ are bound to the APEX rig.

parameters.label: Rig Save Path

When you write out USD using a [USD Render ROP|Node:out/usd], the geometry is saved to a `.bgeo.sc` file using this file path (after [output processing|/solaris/output#processors]). When turned off, the save path is automatically determined based on the node name.

parameters.label: Color

parameters.label: Shape

parameters.label: Translate

parameters.label: Rotate
