entries.title: Configure Guide Deform
entries.summary: Tags groom primitives with the HairDeform procedural API, configuring how they deform at render time.

parameters.label: Groom Primitive
parameters.description: Pattern matching one or more BasisCurves primitives on the input stage. All matched prims get tagged with the hair deform procedural and configured with the same deformer relationships. Non-curve prims matching the pattern are skipped.

parameters.label: Enable Deformation
parameters.description: When off, no deformation is applied at render time — the groom curves keep their authored positions. The __Preserve Shape__ solve still runs if enabled, using the `rest` primvar as the initial shape.

parameters.label: Deform Method
parameters.description: Controls how the groom curves deform at render time. Each method needs a different combination of inputs.

parameters.label: Skin Prim
parameters.description: The skin mesh the groom is attached to. Must be a Mesh with `rest` primvar and animated `points` attribute. Surface Deform, Guide Interpolation Mesh, and Guide Weights use this to compute skin-relative transforms.

parameters.label: Guide Interpolation Mesh
parameters.description: A Mesh with per-point `guides`, `guides:lengths`, `weights`, and `weights:lengths` primvars defining which guide curves influence each region of the mesh. Groom curve roots are projected onto this mesh to look up their guide blend weights. Visible only when __Deform Method__ is Guide Interpolation Mesh.

parameters.label: Use Orient Attribute
parameters.description: When enabled, builds point-deform transforms from deformer orientation primvars (`restorient` and `orient` quaternions) instead of deriving transforms from deformer neighbourhood topology. This is required when using BasisCurves as the __Deformer / Guides Prim__ in __Point Deform__, because curve topology does not provide stable neighbourhood-based transforms. Orient primvars solve this by providing explicit frame information: the orientation change (delta rotation) between `restorient` and `orient` is extracted and applied directly to captured groom points, enabling twist-aware deformation. Also works with Mesh and TetMesh deformers for more reliable frame computation.

parameters.label: Orient Blend
parameters.description: Blends between position-only deformation (0) and full orient-augmented deformation (1) for the Guide Weights and Guide Interpolation Mesh methods. Only active when __Use Orient Attribute__ is enabled. At 0, curves are positioned by blending guide translations only. At 1, guide orientations are also blended and applied to each deformed curve. Intermediate values mix both contributions.

parameters.label: Smooth Capture / Tet Capture
parameters.description: Enable this to use connectivity-aware smooth capture instead of BVH point capture. Smooth capture is equivalent to the [Point Capture SOP|Node:sop/pointcapture], while BVH capture is equivalent to the capture built into the [Point Deform SOP|Node:sop/pointdeform]. Smooth capture prevents geometry bleed-through between neighboring features and gives smoother results, especially with small capture radii. Requires the deformer to be a Mesh or TetMesh. Only visible when __Deform Method__ is Point Deform.

parameters.label: Max Candidates
parameters.heading: Guide Shape Interpolation
parameters.description: Number of nearby guide root points to consider when assigning guides to each hair. Higher values improve assignment quality at the cost of performance.

parameters.label: Min Guides
parameters.heading: Guide Shape Interpolation
parameters.description: Minimum number of guides kept for each hair. Guides with weights below __Weight Threshold__ are normally dropped, but this many are always kept — the highest-weighted guides are retained even if they fall below the threshold. Increase this to ensure smoother blending in areas with few good guide matches.

parameters.label: Max Guides
parameters.heading: Guide Shape Interpolation
parameters.description: Maximum number of guides blended for each hair. Only the best-scoring candidates (up to this count) are considered for weighting. Higher values allow more guides to contribute but increase memory and compute cost.

parameters.label: Blur Width
parameters.heading: Guide Shape Interpolation
parameters.description: Controls the width of the Gaussian falloff applied to guide shape distances when computing blend weights. The algorithm compares each groom curve's shape to nearby guide curves via arc-length sampling, then applies a Gaussian weight function to convert those distances into influence weights. Increase this to make weighting wider so guides with slightly worse shape matches still receive significant weight, producing smoother, more diffuse blending. Decrease it to make weighting sharper so only guides with the best shape matches contribute, creating more distinct guide regions.

parameters.label: Weight Threshold
parameters.heading: Guide Shape Interpolation
parameters.description: Guides with normalized weights below this value are dropped. At least __Min Guides__ are always kept regardless of this threshold. Lower values keep more low-weight guides, producing smoother blending at the cost of more guides per hair.

parameters.label: Length Penalty Scale
parameters.heading: Guide Shape Interpolation
parameters.description: Penalizes guide curves whose total arc-length differs significantly from each groom curve's length. The penalty is the squared ratio difference: `(guideLength / groomLength - 1)²`. At 0 (default), length differences have no effect and guides are chosen by shape match and proximity alone. Increase this to prefer guides with similar total length, which reduces visible stretching or compression when guides don't closely match the groom's proportions.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Capture
parameters.description: Maximum distance (in world units) from each curve point to search for nearby deformer points. A smaller radius gives more localized deformation but may leave points uncaptured.

parameters.label: Minimum Points
parameters.heading: Capture
parameters.description: If a curve point finds fewer deformer points than this, the search radius grows until it finds at least this many. This may cause discontinuities, but is usually better than leaving points undeformed.

parameters.label: Maximum Points
parameters.heading: Capture
parameters.description: Maximum number of deformer points each curve point can be captured by. If more points fall within __Radius__, only the closest are kept. Lower values are faster and use less memory, but increase the chance of discontinuities.

parameters.label: Capture Radius
parameters.heading: Capture
parameters.description: Maximum distance (in world units) from each projected location on the capture geometry to search for connected primitives. A smaller radius reproduces local animation more accurately but may produce chunking artifacts. Decrease this if you see geometry bleed-through; increase it if you see chunking.

parameters.label: Kernel Type
parameters.heading: Capture
parameters.description: Function used to convert capture distances to capture weights. The kernel is integrated over the capture radius on the surface of the capture geometry, and the result is distributed to intersecting primitives.

parameters.label: Smoothing Method
parameters.heading: Smoothing
parameters.description: Controls how capture weights are smoothed to avoid artifacts from small capture radii.

parameters.label: Smoothing Level
parameters.heading: Smoothing
parameters.description: Amount of smoothing applied to the capture. Higher values give a smoother capture surface and smoother deformation. Increase this if the result looks too rough.

parameters.label: Tet Mesh Treatment
parameters.heading: Capture Geometry Treatment
parameters.description: Controls how tetrahedral meshes in the deformer are handled during capture.

parameters.label: Preserve Shape
parameters.heading: Preserve Shape
parameters.description: Turn this on to enable the quasi-static relaxation pass.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.heading: Preserve Shape
parameters.description: Number of solver iterations. Higher values converge more accurately but take longer.

parameters.label: Stretch Stiffness
parameters.heading: Preserve Shape
parameters.description: Resistance to stretching along the curve. Higher values preserve rest-length edge lengths more strongly.

parameters.label: Bend Stiffness
parameters.heading: Preserve Shape
parameters.description: Resistance to bending. Higher values make curves stiffer, preserving rest-pose curvature more strongly.

parameters.label: Ref Pos Strength
parameters.heading: Preserve Shape
parameters.description: How strongly points are pulled back toward their reference (rest) positions. Acts as a soft constraint that attracts points toward their original shape.

parameters.label: Lock Roots
parameters.heading: Preserve Shape
parameters.description: Keeps curve root points fixed during relaxation so they stay attached to the skin surface.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Preserve Clumps
parameters.description: Enables clump constraints for the quasi-static solve. When on, each curve is attracted toward nearby curves weighted by __Stiffness__. Neighbors are found dynamically using __Max Neighbors__ and __Max Constraints__. If `clumppts`/`clumpdists` primvars are already present on the groom, they are used as pre-computed targets instead, skipping the dynamic search.

parameters.label: Stiffness
parameters.heading: Preserve Clumps
parameters.description: How strongly each curve is pulled toward its clump neighbors.

parameters.label: Damping
parameters.heading: Preserve Clumps
parameters.description: Damping factor for the clump constraint. Higher values reduce oscillation in the clump stiffness solve.

parameters.label: Max Neighbors
parameters.heading: Preserve Clumps
parameters.description: Maximum number of nearby curves to consider as clump candidates for each curve. Higher values allow more clumping partners but increase solve cost.

parameters.label: Max Constraints
parameters.heading: Preserve Clumps
parameters.description: Maximum number of active clump constraints per curve. Only the closest candidates (up to this count) are kept. Lower values produce fewer but stronger clump pulls per curve.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

deprecation.tier: VERIFIED-DOC + VERIFIED-RUNTIME (union, sides recorded separately — never collapsed to one boolean)

entries.title: Configure Layer
entries.summary: Edits metadata on a layer.

parameters.label: Save Path
parameters.description: Where the file will be saved if and when the USD is written to disk (by a [USD Render ROP|Node:out/usd]). (This is stored in `/HoudiniLayerInfo` and is not saved to any USD output.) This path can be altered by an [output processor|/solaris/output#processors] if you have them configured on the render node. For example, it is common in Houdini to have file paths relative to `$HIP`, but in USD they should be relative to the root layer file. By default, an output processor on the USD Render ROP does this transformation automatically.

parameters.label: Default Primitive
parameters.description: Sets the [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for this layer. If another USD file references this layer, but does not explicitly name a primitive, it is given the _default primitive_. This sets the default primitive for this layer. It must be a root prim (`/prim_name`) and it must exist in this layer.

parameters.label: Comment
parameters.description: Sets a comment on this layer. This comment has no meaning to USD, but may be used to describe the purpose of the layer, or any other information you may wish to associate with the layer.

parameters.label: Start Time
parameters.description: Sets the start time of the playable range for this layer. (This is not enforced in any way, and the layer may not have any animation. This may be used by [Houdini's viewer|/solaris/view] and tools such as `usdview`.)

parameters.label: End Time
parameters.description: Sets the end time of the playable range for this layer. (This is not enforced in any way, and the layer may not have any animation. This may be used by [Houdini's viewer|/solaris/view] and tools such as `usdview`.)

parameters.label: Time Codes per Second
parameters.description: Applies a scaling factor to time samples stored in the layer. You can use this to non-destructively speed up or slow down animation in the layer.

parameters.label: Frames per Second
parameters.description: For data specified in relation to frames, how many frames fit in a second. (For example, 24 for film, or 30 for NTSC television.) ~~~

parameters.label: Up Axis
parameters.description: Which axis (Y or Z) was treated as "up" when this layer was created. This is not used to transform the layer. It serves as a hint that can help identify the cause of orientation problems when you combine USD layers.

parameters.label: Meters per Unit
parameters.description: The scale at which the scene was modeled. For example, Houdini scenes are often modeled at meter scale (`1.0`) for physical accuracy, while Maya modelers often work at centimeter scale (`0.01`). Like __Up axis__, Houdini doesn't act on this information (it can't automatically scale layers because it can't know which of all the attributes in the scene represent lengths, distances, movement vectors, and so on). It just serves as a hint to help identify the cause of scaling problems when combining USD layers. ~~~

parameters.label: Color Configuration
parameters.description: Sets the default color configuration to be used to interpret the per-attribute color spaces in the composed USD stage. This is specified as an asset path which can be resolved to the color configuration file.

parameters.label: Color Management System
parameters.description: Sets the name of the color management system used to interpret the color configuration file pointed at by the active __Color Configuration__. ~~~

parameters.label: Render Settings
parameters.description: Path to the `rendersettings` prim in the Scene Graph Tree. This prim is only available when a [Render Settings LOP|Node:lop/rendersettings] or a [Karma Render Settings LOP|Node:lop/karmarendersettings] is present in the scene. By default the path is `/Render/rendersettings`. ~~~

parameters.label: Custom Data Count
parameters.description: The metadata of every prim and property contains a dictionary for use by software packages and/or studios to store _custom data_. You can set or edit multiple custom key-value pairs here. Set the number of items to set/edit, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove items.

parameters.label: Custom Data Name
parameters.description: For each item of custom data, the name of the item.

parameters.label: Custom Data Type
parameters.description: For each item of custom data, the data type of the value.

parameters.label: Custom Data Value
parameters.description: For each item of custom data, the value to associate with the name. (Behind the scenes there are several different parameters (`customdatastrvalue<<n>>`, `customdatafloatvalue<<n>>`, `customdataintvalue<<n>>`, `customdataboolvalue<<n>>`) all labeled __Custom Data Value__, with the visible one controlled by the __Custom Data Type__ value. This may be relevant if you are using expressions or scripting these values.) ~~~

parameters.label: Stage Variable Count
parameters.description: Every USD layer can contain a dictionary of "stage variables" as metadata onthe root primitive. These stage variables can be referenced in asset path attributes, composition arcs such as references, and in variant selections.

parameters.label: Stage Variable Name
parameters.description: For each stage variable, the name of the variable.

parameters.label: Stage Variable Type
parameters.description: For each stage variable, the data type of the variable value.

parameters.label: Stage Variable Value
parameters.description: For each stage variable, the value to associate with the name. (Behind the scenes there are several different parameters (`stagevariablestrvalue<<n>>`, `stagevariablefloatvalue<<n>>`, `stagevariableintvalue<<n>>`, `stagevariableboolvalue<<n>>`) all labeled __Stage Variable Value__, with the visible one controlled by the __Stage Variable Type__ value. This may be relevant if you are using expressions or scripting these values.) ~~~

parameters.label: Also Set Metadata on Stage Root Layer
parameters.label_norm: also set metadata on stage root layer
parameters.description: USD layers each have their own metadata that is controlled through this node. But in addition, USD stage's root layer (which cannot be directly accessed in LOPs) also has metadata which may be the same as or different from any specific layer used to compose the stage. This option allows the metadata described by this node to be copied to the stage's root layer as well as being set on the active layer. It is almost always desirable to have the metadata on each component layer match the metadata of the stage's root layer, so this option is on by default.

parameters.label: Flatten Input
parameters.description: Prior to configuring the active layer, you can explicitly combine a series of layers created by earlier nodes in the chain.

parameters.label: Start New Layer
parameters.description: This node is often used to perform the final configuration of a layer's metadata before creating a new layer to be modified by following LOP nodes. Turn this on to explicitly start a new in-memory active layer that subsequent nodes will use.

parameters.label: Set Input Active Layer to Explicit
parameters.label_norm: set input active layer to explicit
parameters.description: When this node starts a new layer, the previous active layer can be marked as an explicit layer, even if a __Save Path__ has not been set. Forcing this layer to be marked explicit ensures it will be written to it's own file on disk by the USD ROP, using an automatically generated save path if necessary.

entries.title: Configure Primitives
entries.summary: Edits various metadata on one or more primitives.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Purpose
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Set the primitive's purpose. Purposes are a way to control what gets rendered. The viewer/renderer only shows primitives tagged with one of a specified set of purposes.

parameters.label: Proxy Primitive
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For a primitive with __Render__ purpose, this metadata holds the path to the primitive with __Proxy__ purpose which corresponds to this render primitive.

parameters.label: Instanceable
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: See [Instancing|/solaris/glossary#instancing] for an explanation of instanceable primitives. If a prim is marked as "instanceable", all duplicates of that prim (and its descendants) are automatically replaced with lightweight references to a single "master" instance. You can still change attributes on instanceable prim (for example, to give each instance its own transform), but you can't edit any of its descendants.

parameters.label: Activation
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If you turn this off, the primitive has no effect on the scene (for example, a light object will not cast light), it becomes invisible, and behaves as if it has no children.

parameters.label: Visibility
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For performance reasons, the options for this attribute are Inherit or Invisible (there is no explicit "visible" value). This means that when you mark a primitive is marked invisible, all its descendants are made invisible as well. It can be useful to animate this setting over time, unlike most of the parameters on this node.

parameters.label: Set Extents
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Compute any missing `extents` or `extentsHint` attributes. This information is needed to draw the cards and bounds at the correct size for those draw modes.

parameters.label: Kind
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: See [Kinds and the model hierarchy|/solaris/glossary#kind] for an explanation of kinds and how they should be used. To maintain a proper model hierarchy, you should apply a kind to any prim whose descendants contain geometry.

parameters.label: Fix Kind Hierarchy
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Set the kind of all parents of the selected prims so that the hierarchy is correct. Primarily this makes sure all parents of component or group have a kind of assembly or group.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Schema
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Schema
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Apply API Schemas
parameters.heading: Schema
parameters.description: See [schemas|/solaris/glossary#schemas] for an explanation of API schemas. Primitives automatically keep a record of which API schemas have been "applied" to them. This parameter allows to list _additional_ API schemas to apply to this primitive.

parameters.label: Apply Draw Mode On This Primitive
parameters.label_norm: apply draw mode on this primitive
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Indicates that this prim should be drawn according to the draw mode set on this prim or one of its ancestors. Component prims and prims with unloaded payloads are the normal locations where the draw mode is applied. This attribute allows any other primitive (that is part of a valid model hierarchy) to be the point in the scene graph where the chosen draw mode is applied.

parameters.label: Draw Mode
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Controls how the renderer draws geometry under this prim. These options allow you to replace extremely heavy geometry in the viewer with faster, cheaper alternatives. Descendants of this prim will inherit this setting unless they change it.

parameters.label: Draw Mode Color
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Color to draw __Origin Axis__ or __Bounding Box__, or if all the card textures are missing.

parameters.label: Card Geometry
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: If Cards Draw Mode is chosen, what kind of Cards to draw

parameters.label: +X Texture
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the +X side of the box or cross. If missing the -X texture is mirrored. If both are missing then YZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: -X Texture
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the -X side of the box or cross. If missing the +X texture is mirrored. If both are missing then YZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: +Y Texture
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the +Y side of the box or cross. If missing the -Y texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: -Y Texture
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the -Y side of the box or cross. If missing the +Y texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: +Z Texture
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the +Z side of the box or cross. If missing the -Z texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XY plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: -Z Texture
parameters.heading: Draw Mode
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the -Z side of the box or cross. If missing the +Z texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XY plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: Asset Identifier
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: Stores the file path or asset ID of the file this primitive came from. USD does not use this metadata, but it may be useful for internal tools.

parameters.label: Asset Name
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: A human readable name that may describe the asset. This may be authored by a pipeline/asset management tool. USD does not use this metadata, but it may be useful for internal tools.

parameters.label: Asset Thumbnail
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: The path to a file that should be used as the thumbnail image to represent this asset. Setting this asset info also applies the `UsdMediaAssetPreviewsAPI` schema to the prim, which defines the asset info dictionary location where the thumbnail path will be saved.

parameters.label: Asset Version
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: For version-controlled assets, the version number of the asset when the scene was authored. This may be authored by a pipeline/asset management tool. USD does not use this metadata, but it may be useful for internal tools.

parameters.label: Asset Dependencies
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: An optional list of other files that are loaded indirectly by the asset file. This may be authored by a pipeline/asset management tool. USD does not use this metadata, but it may be useful for internal tools.

parameters.label: Asset Info Count
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: Additional named values to associate with the asset info dictionary on these prims or properties. Set the number of items to set/edit, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove items.

parameters.label: Asset Info Name
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: For each item of asset info, the name of the item.

parameters.label: Asset Info Type
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: For each item of asset info, the data type of the value.

parameters.label: Asset Info Value
parameters.heading: Asset Info
parameters.description: For each item of asset info, the value to associate with the name. (Behind the scenes there are several different parameters (`assetinfostrvalue<<n>>`, `assetinfofloatvalue<<n>>`, `assetinfointvalue<<n>>`, `assetinfoboolvalue<<n>>`) all labeled __Asset Info Value__, with the visible one controlled by the __Asset Info Type__ value. This may be relevant if you are using expressions or scripting these values.)

parameters.label: Icon
parameters.heading: Interface
parameters.description: A path to an icon or image file that should be associated with the selected primitives in the Scene Graph Tree. This icon path is stored in a the primitive's custom data dictionary.

parameters.label: Catalog Parent Path
parameters.heading: Interface
parameters.description: If this prim is added to an asset or material catalog, this is the catalog folder under which this primitive's catalog entry should appear. This path is stored as custom metadata on the prim.

parameters.label: Allow LOPs to Edit This Primitive
parameters.label_norm: allow lops to edit this primitive
parameters.heading: Interface
parameters.description: Applies a Houdini-specific attribute to the primitive which controls whether Edit Properties LOP node are allowed to modify this primitive. Disallowing the editing of a particular primitive can be used to prevent accidental modifications of cameras or other critical scene elements. Note that this toggle does not affect all edits of this primitive in LOPs, only the Edit Properties type LOP nodes respect this attribute.

parameters.label: Allow Viewport Selection of This Primitive
parameters.label_norm: allow viewport selection of this primitive
parameters.heading: Interface
parameters.description: Applies a Houdini-specific attribute to the primitive which controls whether or not the primitive can be selected in the viewport. Setting this attribute on a primitive also affects all descendants of the primitive that do not specify their own explicit value for this attribute.

parameters.label: Hide Primitive In Scene Graph Trees
parameters.label_norm: hide primitive in scene graph trees
parameters.heading: Interface
parameters.description: Sets the `hidden` USD metadata to the primitive which controls whether or not this primitive (and its descendants) should be visible in the scene graph tree pane. Primitives tagged as hidden will still be visible in the viewport unless the primitive is also marked as invisible or inactive. Note that the scene graph tree pane provides an option to ignore this attribute (primarily for debugging purposes).

parameters.label: Custom Data Count
parameters.heading: Custom Data
parameters.description: The metadata of every prim and property contains a dictionary for use by software packages and/or studios to store _custom data_. You can set or edit multiple custom key-value pairs here. Set the number of items to set/edit, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove items.

parameters.heading: Custom Data
parameters.description: For each item of custom data, the name of the item.

parameters.label: Custom Data Type
parameters.heading: Custom Data
parameters.description: For each item of custom data, the data type of the value.

This may be relevant if you are using expressions or scripting these values.)

entries.summary: Configures metadata on properties (relationships and attributes).

parameters.label: Primitives

You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Properties
parameters.description: A space separated list of property names which should be affected by this node. Normal Houdini string matching rules apply (accepting wildcards and using `^` to exclude patterns). The node compares this pattern against every property name on every selected primitive. This can mean the node affects a different set of properties on each primitive.

parameters.label: Variability
parameters.description: This is a hint to the USD system indicating whether the property can vary over time, or should be uniform over all time.

parameters.label: Color Space
parameters.description: For attributes with a color data type, this metadata affects how USD interprets the color value. See the USD documentation for further information on how USD uses this color space metadata.

parameters.label: Interpolation
parameters.description: For primvar attributes, the interpolation metadata controls how the primvar is applied to the geometry.

parameters.label: Element Size
parameters.description: For a primvar attribute, this metadata controls how many elements of the array belong to each component of the geometry. This is necessary because primvar values are always flat arrays. As an example, suppose a single square exists in a `Mesh` primitive. A primvar with vertex interpolation should have four values (one for each corner). With an element size of `1`, this primvar attribute should have exactly four elements of whatever data type is set on the attribute (strings, vectors, colours, etc). With an element size of `5`, the primvar attribute value should be an array of 20 elements, of which 5 belong to each corner of the square.

parameters.label: Custom Data Count
parameters.description: The metadata of every prim and property contains a dictionary for use by software packages and/or studios to store _custom data_. You can set or edit multiple custom key-value pairs here. Set the number of items to set/edit, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove items.

entries.title: Configure Stage
entries.summary: Configures metadata for how to load layers into the stage and asset resolution.

parameters.label: Populate Primitives
parameters.description: How/whether to edit the stage population mask.

parameters.label: Populate Paths from Input
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__ or __Set primitives to populate__, this is a list of [primitive path patterns|/solaris/pattern] matching prims to include. The difference between this and __Populate paths__ is that this parameter selects from prims that exist in the input.

parameters.label: Remove Populate Paths from Input
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__, this is a list of [primitive path patterns|/solaris/pattern] matching prims to _remove_. Removing a primitive from the stage population mask means the resulting primitives will _no longer exist_ in the output stage. The difference between this and __Remove Populate Paths__ is that this parameter selects from prims that exist in the input.

parameters.label: Populate Paths
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__ or __Set primitives to populate__, this is a list of explicit paths (no patterns allowed) of prims to include. The difference between this and __Populate Paths from Input__ is that this parameter can add paths to the mask even if this node has no input, and even if the prims don't exist at the paths yet, but might be created by subsequent nodes.

parameters.label: Remove Populate Paths
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__, this is a list of explicit paths (no patterns allowed) of prims to _remove_. Removing a primitive from the stage population mask means the resulting primitives will _no longer exist_ in the output stage. The difference between this and __Remove Populate Paths from Input__ is that this parameter can remove paths from the mask even if this node has no input, and even if the prims don't exist at the paths yet, but might be created by subsequent nodes. ~~~

parameters.label: Load Primitives
parameters.description: How/whether to edit the set of primitives which should load their payloads.

parameters.label: Load Paths from Input
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__ or __Set primitives to populate__, this is a list of [primitive path patterns|/solaris/pattern] matching prims to load. The difference between this and __Load Paths__ is that this parameter selects from prims that exist in the input.

parameters.label: Remove Load Paths from Input
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__, this is a list of [primitive path patterns|/solaris/pattern] matching prims to _remove_. Removing a primitive from the set of payloads to load means the resulting primitives will no longer compose their payload arcs on the output stage. The difference between this and __Remove Load Paths__ is that this parameter selects from prims that exist in the input.

parameters.label: Load Paths
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__ or __Set primitives to populate__, this is a list of explicit paths (no patterns allowed) of prims to include. The difference between this and __Load Paths from Input__ is that this parameter can add paths to the set even if this node has no input, and even if the prims don't exist at the paths yet, but might be created by subsequent nodes.

parameters.label: Remove Load Paths
parameters.description: When __Populate Primitives__ is __Add and remove primitives to populate__, this is a list of explicit paths (no patterns allowed) of prims to _remove_. Removing a primitive from the set of payloads to load means the resulting primitives will no longer compose their payload arcs on the output stage. The difference between this and __Remove Load Paths from Input__ is that this parameter can remove paths from the set even if this node has no input, and even if the prims don't exist at the paths yet, but might be created by subsequent nodes. ~~~

parameters.label: Mute Layers
parameters.description: How/whether to edit the set of muted layers. Layers loaded from disk should be specified with their full paths. Muting layers generated by the LOP network can be done either using the anonymous identifier for the LOP-generated layer, or can be of the form returned by [Hom:hou.lop.mutingIdentifier]. This is a string like `lop:/path/to/lop/nde`. In this form, layers that will be generated by LOP nodes further down the network can be muted in advance. The muting will be applied to the USD stage seen by any node after the specified LOP node in the node graph. Note that only LOP layers that are in the root layer sublayer stack can be muted this way. LOP layers that are referenced or authored as sublayers of sublayers cannot be muted. To mute all layers above a [Layer Break LOP|Node:lop/layerbreak] (both LOP authored layers and layers loaded from disk), use this python expression in the __Set layers to mute__ parameter: {{{ lbidentifiers = pwd().input(0).layersAboveLayerBreak() return ' '.join(hou.lop.mutingIdentifier(identifier) for identifier in lbidentifiers) }}}

parameters.label: Mute Paths
parameters.description: When __Mute Layers__ is __Add and remove layers to mute__ or __Set layers to mute__, this is a list of paths to layers to mute. Even if the layers listed here do not exist on the inputs stage (if any), this set of paths will be remembered by the stage, and loading of the named layers will be prevented in subsequent nodes.

parameters.label: Unmute Paths
parameters.description: When __Mute Layers__ is __Add and remove layers to mute__, this is a list of paths to layers to unmute (if they are currently muted). ~~~

parameters.label: Resolver Context Asset Path
parameters.description: A path to a file containing configuration information for the [asset resolver|/solaris/glossary#extend]. The standard USD asset resolver and Houdini's built-in asset resolver *do not use this*, but if you use a custom asset resolver, it may read this file to change its settings when loading layers for this stage. This parameter only affects the USD stage if this node has no input connected. The contents of this file, whether it is used at all, and if it's used, how it affects the behavior of the asset resolver, is completely up to asset resolver implementation. For example, the configuration file might specify a version number, telling the resolver to prefer assets of that version when loading resources.

parameters.label: Number of Resolver Context Strings
parameters.description: The resolver context can be configured using multiple separate strings. Each string is used to configure one resolver. One string (with no URL prefix specified) is sent to the default resolver used for all asset paths that are not in URL format. Other strings can be paired with a URL prefix to configure the resolver associated with that prefix. If there is at least one non-empty resolver context string value provided, this takes precedence over any resolver context asset path, and the resolver context for the LOP stage will be created using the `ArResolver::CreateContextFromStrings` method instead of `ArResolver::CreateDefaultContextForAsset`.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: Individual resolver context configuration strings can be enabled or disabled with this toggle.

parameters.label: URL Prefix
parameters.description: This string value will be sent to the resolver responsible for the specified URL prefix. If no prefix is provided, this string value will be sent to the default resolver.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The string value sent to the resolver determined by the URL Prefix.

parameters.label: Number of Variant Selection Fallback Rules
parameters.label_norm: number of variant selection fallback rules
parameters.description: Configures what variant selection fallback values to use for specific variant sets when no explicit variant selection opinion is provided on a prim. These fallbacks are applied on top of any global variant selection fallbacks configured using the USD library plugin mechanism, and on top of any variant selection fallbacks configure on the LOP Network.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.description: A specific variant set fallback setting can be disabled with this toggle.

parameters.label: Variant Set Name
parameters.description: Name of the variant set to configure.

parameters.label: Fallback Selections
parameters.description: A space or comma separated list of variant selection values to attempt to use on this variant set when no explicit variant selection opinion is available. ~~~

parameters.label: Stage Variable Count
parameters.description: Every USD layer can contain a dictionary of "stage variables" as metadata onthe root primitive. These stage variables can be referenced in asset path attributes, composition arcs such as references, and in variant selections.

parameters.label: Stage Variable Name
parameters.description: For each stage variable, the name of the variable.

parameters.label: Stage Variable Type
parameters.description: For each stage variable, the data type of the variable value.

parameters.label: Stage Variable Value
parameters.description: For each stage variable, the value to associate with the name. (Behind the scenes there are several different parameters (`stagevariablestrvalue<<n>>`, `stagevariablefloatvalue<<n>>`, `stagevariableintvalue<<n>>`, `stagevariableboolvalue<<n>>`) all labeled __Stage Variable Value__, with the visible one controlled by the __Stage Variable Type__ value. This may be relevant if you are using expressions or scripting these values.)

entries.title: Coordinate System
entries.summary: Define named coordinate systems used in shaders.

parameters.label: Create
parameters.heading: Create
parameters.description: Create an __Xform__ or __Camera__ primitive, whose transform will be the target space of the coordsys.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Create
parameters.description: Path of the created target prim.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create
parameters.description: Prim type of any parent prims created along with the target prim.

parameters.label: Target Type
parameters.heading: Create
parameters.description: The prim target that will be created. Can be an __Xform__ or a __Camera__.

parameters.label: Ignore Parent Transforms
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Enable to cause the created Xform to ignore any ancestor primitive transforms.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.heading: Camera
parameters.description: Projection style of the camera, perspective or orthographic.

parameters.label: Z-Axis Offset
parameters.heading: Camera
parameters.description: Offset along the local Z-Axis of the created prim. Applied prior to the prim's main __Transform__.

parameters.label: Focal Length
parameters.heading: Camera
parameters.description: Perspective focal length in millimeters. This drives an expression on a hidden parameter to generate a value in the units expected by USD, which is tenths of a world unit, as defined by the stage's meters per unit setting.

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Camera
parameters.description: When __Control Aperture__ is set to `Set Horizontal Aperture and Aspect Ratio`, this parameter specifies the desired aperture aspect ratio used to calculate the vertical aperture from the horizontal aperture. Render Settings and Render Product nodes can use the camera aperture aspect ratio to set the correct resolution automatically. ~~~

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.heading: Camera
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the camera in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.heading: Camera
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this camera from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide cameras that are used for texture projection or other utility purposes, and are not actually meant for viewing the scene.

parameters.label: Number of Bindings
parameters.heading: CoordSys Bindings
parameters.description: More than one coordsys can be defined at a time. Set this to the number of coordsys bindings you want to created, or use the plus and minus buttons to add or remove bindings.

parameters.label: Primitives

You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: CoordSys Name

parameters.label: Target

entries.title: Copy to Points
entries.summary: Instances or copies primitives onto points.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: General
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to create the point instancer prim (when __Method__ is __PointInstancer__), or the parent of all created prims (when __Method__ is anything other than __PointInstancer__).

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: General
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node creates it. If it creates the prim, it sets this as the prim's [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Method
parameters.heading: General
parameters.description: See [Instancing in USD|/solaris/glossary#instancing] for more information.

parameters.label: Set Extents
parameters.heading: General
parameters.description: Compute the extents (bounding box) of the instanced geometry and store this on the instancer prim. The authored extent is static (a single default value) when both the source geometry and the prototypes are time-independent, and time-sampled otherwise -- so static scenes don't carry stray time-sampled extents.

parameters.label: Prototype Source
parameters.heading: General
parameters.description: Whether the prim(s) you want to reference/instance onto the points is/are in the first input or the second input.

parameters.label: Use Entire Stage as Prototype
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: If __Prototype Source__ is __Second Input__ and this is on, the node copies everything from the second input's scene graph tree under a new prim and uses that as the prototype. This lets you build a node chain that builds the prototype and connect it to the second input, and not have to specify which prim in the second input to use. Using this option implies that there is only one prototype, because this node has no multi-input. If you have several full stages you want to use as prototypes, combine them with a [Graft Stages LOP|Node:lop/graftstages] first, and feed the result into the second input, but with this option turned off.

parameters.label: Prototype Primitives
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: The scene graph path(s) of the primitive(s) you want to use as prototype(s). You can use [pattern syntax|/solaris/pattern] to select multiple primitives.

parameters.label: Handle Missing Prototypes
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: If a point specifies a prototype that doesn't exist, this parameter controls whether the node will present a warning, enter an error state or create the missing primitives. The default is to enter an error state, which can be useful to catch accidental use of missing prototypes. The warning mode is useful for scenarios where prototypes may be added to the instancer later in the LOP network or through USD composition.  The create mode will create placeholder prims in the scene to use as prototypes.

parameters.label: Make Prototype Source Primitives Invisible
parameters.heading: Destination
parameters.description: If __Prototype Source__ is __First Input__ and __Create Prototypes Area__ is enabled and this is on, the node sets the visibility of the prims used as primitives to "hidden" in the output. The default is on.

parameters.label: Root Prim
parameters.heading: Destination
parameters.description: The scene graph path to the root prim for the prototype area.  This prim will be created if it doesn't already exist.

parameters.label: Root Prim Kind
parameters.heading: Destination
parameters.description: When __Use Entire Stage__ is on, this sets the [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind] of the prim the node creates as a parent for root prims from the second input. The default is __None__.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Destination
parameters.description: The name for the prototype prims to be created under the prototype destination root prim.

parameters.label: Only Copy Specified Prototype Prims
parameters.heading: Destination
parameters.description: If __Prototype Source__ is __Second Input__ and __Use Entire Stage as Prototype__ is off, this controls whether to only copy the prototype primitives specified by __Prototype Primitives__, or the entire stage. The default is on. Using this option can result in a smaller stage, but requires that the prototype sources are fully self-contained (for example they cannot refer to materials that sit elsewhere in the prim hierarchy).

parameters.label: Prototype Reference Type
parameters.heading: Destination
parameters.description: If __Prototype Source__ is __First Input__ and __Create Prototypes Area__ is enabled, this parameter controls the composition type to use when creating references to the source primitives from within the `Prototypes` folder in the scene graph. This parameter can be __Reference__, __Inherit__, or __Specialize__. See [inherits and specializes|/solaris/glossary#inherits] for more information about how these choices differ from a simple reference.

parameters.label: Location Source
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: Where to get the points to copy onto.

parameters.label: Show LOP Stage in SOPs
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: Points to a LOP node whose stage will be rendered into the Scene Viewer along with the SOP geometry when diving inside this SOP Network. Any USD cameras and lights will also become available to look through in the viewport's camera menu. Specifying a LOP Network instead of a LOP Node path will fetch the stage of the LOP Node with the display flag set within the target LOP Network.

parameters.label: SOP Path
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: When __Location Source__ is __External SOP__, the node path of the SOP node that generates the target points.

parameters.label: Point Group
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: When __Location Source__ is __Internal SOP__ or __External SOP__, get the points from this named group in the SOP geometry.

parameters.label: Location Primitives
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: When __Location Source__ is __First Input's Primitives__, this is the scene graph paths of the primitives whose positions you want to use as target points. When __Location Source__ is __First Input's Points__, this is a the scene graph path(s) of one or more geometry prims containing target points (such as a polygonal mesh). In either case you can use [pattern syntax|/solaris/pattern] to select multiple primitives.

parameters.label: Prune Mode
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: You can delete or hide a certain percentage of the target points. This may be useful if the target points come from an overly dense point cloud, or to speed up display when you're first setting up the instancer. The default is __None__ to not delete or hide any points.

parameters.label: Prune Amount
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: When __Prune Mode__ is __Delete__ or __Set Visibility__, the percentage of points to delete or hide. This can be used to improve performance while setting up the operator.

parameters.label: Set Orientation
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: Rotate the instanced primitives based on standard [instancing SOP attributes|/copy/instanceattrs] on the points. These SOP attributes include `N`, `up` , and `orient`.

parameters.label: Set Scale
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: Scale the instanced primitives based on standard [instancing SOP attributes|/copy/instanceattrs] on the points. These SOP attributes include `scale` and `pscale`.

parameters.label: Make Transform Source Primitives Invisible
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: Set the visibility of the __Location Primitives__ to "hidden" in the output. The default is on.

parameters.label: Point Attributes to Copy
parameters.heading: Target Points
parameters.description: A list of attributes on the template points to copy to instances. When creating a point instancer, an array primvar will be created for each listed attribute, with an entry for each point's value. When creating reference primitives, an attribute of the same name and type will be created on each primitive.

parameters.label: Instance Base Name
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: A prefix string for the names of prims created by this node. The node appends the point index to this string to create each name. This name is then appended to the __Primitive Path__ value to create the reference prim path. This is ignored if __Use Path Attribute__ is on (below) and the path attribute exists.

parameters.label: Use Path Attribute
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: Use a string attribute on the target points to create the reference prim path.

parameters.label: Make Primitive Paths Unique
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: When __Use Path Attribute__ is on, if a path attribute is not unique append an identifier to ensure uniqueness.

parameters.label: Path Attribute
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: When __Use Path Attribute__ is on, the name of a string attribute on each point containing the path to use for the prim created at that point. The path in this attribute is appended to the __Primitive Path__ value. If this attribute doesn't exist, the node falls back to using __Instance Base Name__. If the paths in the attribute aren't unique, and __Make Primitive Paths Unique__ is off, the node will only create one reference per path. In this case the node will show a warning.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: When __Prototype Index__ is __Random__, the seed for the random number generator.

parameters.label: Index
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: When __Prototype Index__ is __Index__, the index of the prototype to use, from the list of primitives in __Prototype Primitives__. You can use an expression to choose the index based on some other factor.

parameters.label: Index Attribute
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: An integer attribute on the target points that specifies the prototype to use.

parameters.label: Name Attribute
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: A string attribute on the target points that specifies the name of the prototype to use.

parameters.label: Path Attribute
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: A string attribute on the target points that specifies the path of the prototype to use.

parameters.label: Warn on Skipped Instances
parameters.heading: Primitive Naming
parameters.description: When __Prototype Index__ is __Index Attribute__, __Name Attribute__ or __Path Attribute__, this toggle controls whether or not to emit a warning when an instance is skipped due to there being no match between the attribute data and the prototype list.

entries.title: Create LOD
entries.summary: Uses the PolyReduce SOP to automatically generate multiple levels of detail from a high-res model, and stores them as USD variants.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The path to the primitive to which the new variant information will be added. Optionally, you can specify a space separated list of explicit primpaths or a prim pattern to add the variant to.

parameters.label: Source Primitive
parameters.description: The path to the primitive that is the base definition on which the variants will be authored. This primitive will be referenced into the new primitive(s) at the primitive path(s) where the variant will be defined. This indirection ensures that opinions in the variant will be stronger than opinions that already exist on the source primitive.

parameters.label: Warn of Weak Variant Opinions
parameters.description: Adds a warning if any variant opinions are weaker than existing opinions. As each variant is added, this option examines the composed stage with that variant selected. If any opinions added by the variant are not the strongest opinion on the composed stage, add a warning. Turn off this option to avoid the performance penalty of checking for this condition.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If no primitive exists at the specified __Primitive Path__, and this node must create a new Xform primitive at the specified location, this parameter controls the kind that will be authored on this new primitive.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If no primitive exists at the specified __Primitive Path__, and this node creates a new primitive at that location, this parameter controls the primitive type of any ancestor primitives that may have to be created prior to creating the final primitive.

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.description: The name of the variant set to which this node should add its variants.

parameters.label: Variant Source Primitive
parameters.description: The path to the root of the primitives that should be copied from each variant input's scene graph into the variant.

parameters.label: Variant Name Root
parameters.description: The base name to be used for the variants being created. The node creates variant names by appending numbers to this string, starting with __ID Offset__. For example, the default `LOD_` produces variants named `LOD_0`, `LOD_1`, `LOD_2`, and so on.

parameters.label: ID Offset
parameters.description: The initial number to add to the __Variant Name Root__ for the first generated variant. For example, if you change this to `2`, this node would generate variants named `LOD_2`, `LOD_3`, `LOD_4`, and so on. This may be useful to combine the results of two different Create LOD nodes as a single variant set.

parameters.label: Display Variant
parameters.description: When this is on, the node sets the variant name in __Variant Name__ as the current variant. This is useful for visually checking what the different levels looks like.

parameters.label: Variant Name
parameters.description: When __Display Variant__ is on, the node will set the variant with this name as the current variant in the output. For example, if the node is set to produce three variants `LOD_0`, `LOD_1`, and `LOD_2`, you can turn on __Display Variant__ and set this to `LOD_1` to view the middle level of detail.

parameters.label: Number of LODs
parameters.description: The number of level of detail variants to create.

parameters.label: Keep percent
parameters.description: What percentage of the original polygons to keep. Setting this to `100` to pass through the original model. Usually you should set the __Keep Percent__ for each level to decreasing values starting with `100`.

parameters.label: Preserve Quads
parameters.description: If the input geometry has quads, the [PolyReduce SOP|Node:sop/polyreduce] will remember which polygons were quads (even though the internal algorithm works on triangles) and output corresponding quads on the reduced model. An all-quad input should produce an all-quad output.

entries.title: Xform
entries.summary: Creates or edits an Xform prim. Xform (and its sub-classes) represents a transform in the scene tree.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in __Primitive Paths__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type. ~~~

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

deprecation.tier: VERIFIED-DOC + VERIFIED-RUNTIME (union, sides recorded separately — never collapsed to one boolean)
