entries.title: Cylinder
entries.summary: Creates or edits a cylinder shape primitive.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in __Primitive Paths__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type. ~~~

parameters.label: Axis
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The axis the spine of the cylinder is aligned with.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The length of the cylinder from end to end.

parameters.label: Bottom Radius
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The radius of the bottom end cap of the cylinder.

parameters.label: Top Radius
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The radius of the top end cap of the cylinder.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this `displayColor` parameter as an override.

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display __Color__. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.

parameters.label: Double Sided
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: For renderers that distinguish between single-sided and double-sided surfaces, controls whether this prim is double-sided. Making surfaces double-sided is necessary for flat thin surfaces, or open surfaces where the camera can see both the inside and outside of the surface.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: USD currently does not have look-at constraints. This node calculates the per-frame transform to fulfill the constraint and applies it to the object. See the [Light tool help|/nodes/lop/light#tool] for how to set up the look-at constraint interactively in the viewport.

parameters.label: Enable Look At
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Turns on the constraint that orients this object to look at a point or another object.

parameters.label: Look At Position
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: If __Enable Look At__ is on and, this is a point in space this object will look at. If __Look At Primitive__ is not blank, this is an *offset* from the centroid of the target object (in the local space of that object).

parameters.label: Look At Primitive
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: The path to a USD prim this object should look at. If this is not blank, __Look At Position__ is an *offset* from this centroid of the target object.

parameters.label: Up Vector Method
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Controls how the up vector is set.

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: When __Up Vector Method__ is __Custom__, this is the up axis to use for the look-at constraint.

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: A twist rotation (around the -Z axis, clockwise, in degrees), applied after the lookout transform.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. `0` does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the __Intensity__ to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Use __Color Temperature__ to control the light color. The color calculated by __Color Temperature__ is *multiplied* by the RGB color in __Color__, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set __Color__ to `1.0, 1.0, 1.0`.

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Enable Color Temperature__ is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from `1000` to `10000`. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the `UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb()` function from the USD library.

parameters.label: Clipping Range
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Don't show geometry closer than the near distance or farther away than the far distance (in world units).

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the light in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this light from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide lights that are embedded in props, or other lights that are not meant to be modified.

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a [Light Filter Library LOP|Node:lop/lightfilterlibrary].

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Distant__, the angular size of the light in degrees. As an example, the Sun is approximately 0.53 degrees as seen from Earth. Higher values broaden the light and therefore soften shadow edges.

parameters.label: Spotlight
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Turn the light into a spotlight.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: The spread angle of the spotlight beam, in degrees.

parameters.label: Softness
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Blurs the edges of the spotlight beam, simulating light leakage and bounce.

parameters.label: Left Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the left, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Left Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.

parameters.label: Right Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the right, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Right Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.

parameters.label: Top Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the top, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Top Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.

parameters.label: Bottom Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the bottom, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Bottom Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone. ~~~~~

parameters.label: Focus
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: When turned, you can focus the beam with the numerical __Focus__ parameter.

parameters.label: Focus
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: A control to shape the spread of light. Higher focus values pull light towards the center and narrow the spread. (This is implemented as an off-axis cosine power exponent.)

parameters.label: Focus Tint
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Off-axis color tint, tints the light in the falloff region. The default is black. ~~~~~

parameters.label: IES
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Use an IES file describing angular distribution of light.

parameters.label: File
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: An IES (Illumination Engineering Society) format file to use to control angular distribution of light.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: When turned on, the IES intensities are normalized to preserve the light's energy output. Note, that IES profiles have no effect on distant lights.

parameters.label: Angle Scale
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: A global scale on angles found in the IES file.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (`0, 0, 0`) is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Falloff Start Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The near distance at which shadow falloff begins. The default value (`-1`) indicates no falloff.

parameters.label: Falloff Gamma
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: A gamma (i.e., exponential) control over shadow strength with linear distance within the falloff zone (between __Falloff__ and __Distance__).

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is `-1`, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global __Light Sampling Quality__. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree.  This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis.  If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than `0`), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than `0`). Leave it at `ß` for balanced approach.

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area.

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation.  If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the `HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE` configuration variable.

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface).  Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity.  If the radius is set to `1`, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light.  If the value is `1.4142` (`sqrt(2)`), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a [portal light|/solaris/support/portallights].

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Light

entries.title: Dome Light
entries.summary: Creates or edits a USD Dome Light prim. A dome light emits light _inward_, simulating light coming from the sky/environment surrounding the scene.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: USD currently does not have look-at constraints. This node calculates the per-frame transform to fulfill the constraint and applies it to the object. See the [Light tool help|/nodes/lop/light#tool] for how to set up the look-at constraint interactively in the viewport.

parameters.label: Enable Look At
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Turns on the constraint that orients this object to look at a point or another object.

parameters.label: Look At Position
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: If __Enable Look At__ is on and, this is a point in space this object will look at. If __Look At Primitive__ is not blank, this is an *offset* from the centroid of the target object (in the local space of that object).

parameters.label: Look At Primitive
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: The path to a USD prim this object should look at. If this is not blank, __Look At Position__ is an *offset* from this centroid of the target object.

parameters.label: Up Vector Method
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Controls how the up vector is set.

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: When __Up Vector Method__ is __Custom__, this is the up axis to use for the look-at constraint.

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: A twist rotation (around the -Z axis, clockwise, in degrees), applied after the lookout transform.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. `0` does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the __Intensity__ to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Use __Color Temperature__ to control the light color. The color calculated by __Color Temperature__ is *multiplied* by the RGB color in __Color__, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set __Color__ to `1.0, 1.0, 1.0`.

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Enable Color Temperature__ is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from `1000` to `10000`. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the `UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb()` function from the USD library.

parameters.label: Clipping Range
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Don't show geometry closer than the near distance or farther away than the far distance (in world units).

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the light in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this light from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide lights that are embedded in props, or other lights that are not meant to be modified.

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a [Light Filter Library LOP|Node:lop/lightfilterlibrary].

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: File path to the texture file to use as an environment map.

parameters.label: Format
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: How the spherical environment is encoded in the texture image. The default, __Automatic__, tries to guess.

parameters.label: Filters
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Optional light filter primitives that should be applied to this light.

parameters.label: Portals
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Optional portal geometry prim(s) to use to guide light sampling. Note that Houdini supports single-sided portal lights. Go to the __Karma_ tab's __Light__ section and turn on __Single Sided__. If you're using the [Portal Light LOP|Node:lop/portallight], add the path to the downstream portal light node(s) here. To make the portal light visible in the render, go to the __Karma__ tab. On the __Light__ section, turn on __Render Light Geometry__.

parameters.label: Pole Axis
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Indicates the starting alignment of the dome light's top pole. This alignment is for the dome itself and is not inherited by the namespace children of the dome.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (`0, 0, 0`) is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Falloff Start Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The near distance at which shadow falloff begins. The default value (`-1`) indicates no falloff.

parameters.label: Falloff Gamma
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: A gamma (i.e., exponential) control over shadow strength with linear distance within the falloff zone (between __Falloff__ and __Distance__).

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is `-1`, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global __Light Sampling Quality__. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree.  This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis.  If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than `0`), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than `0`). Leave it at `ß` for balanced approach.

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area.

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation.  If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the `HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE` configuration variable.

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface).  Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity.  If the radius is set to `1`, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light.  If the value is `1.4142` (`sqrt(2)`), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a [portal light|/solaris/support/portallights].

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe].

parameters.label: Illuminate Background Holdout
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: If a light exists to add new light source instead of trying to replicate lighting in the live action plate, enable this parameter so that its effect on background holdout geometry shows up in indirect bounces and its contribution to shadow holdout AOVs is omitted.

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.

parameters.label: Contributes to Caustics
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Default is true. Note that Karma only renders caustics if they are enabled on _both the light and the object_. This option has no effect unless you also turn on __Enable Caustics__ on the geometry object.

parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Specifies how the texture applied to a rectangle light is flipped. Default is FlipX to match the USD specification. Only supported on rectangle light type. Options are None, FlipX, FlipY, and FlipXY. <!---

parameters.label: Attenuation Type
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Controls the type of attenuation on the light source in the default light shader. This may be

parameters.label: Attenuation Start
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Minimum light distance to be used for attenuation.

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: The distance from the light at which __Half Distance Attenuation__ produces half the light intensity. --->

parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Ranges between `0` to `1` and controls beam direction along the light's normal. parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Kind
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: See [Kinds and the model hierarchy|/solaris/glossary#kind] for an explanation of kinds and how they should be used. To maintain a proper model hierarchy, you should apply a kind to any prim whose descendants contain geometry.

parameters.label: Fix Kind Hierarchy
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Set the kind of all parents of the selected prims so that the hierarchy is correct. Primarily this makes sure all parents of component or group have a kind of assembly or group.

parameters.label: Set Extents
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Compute any missing `extents` or `extentsHint` attributes. This information is needed to draw the cards and bounds at the correct size for those draw modes.

parameters.label: Apply Draw Mode On This Primitive
parameters.label_norm: apply draw mode on this primitive
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Indicates that this prim should be drawn according to the draw mode set on this prim or one of its ancestors. Component prims and prims with unloaded payloads are the normal locations where the draw mode is applied. This attribute allows any other primitive (that is part of a valid model hierarchy) to be the point in the scene graph where the chosen draw mode is applied.

parameters.label: Draw Mode
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls how the renderer draws geometry under this prim. These options allow you to replace extremely heavy geometry in the viewer with faster, cheaper alternatives. Descendants of this prim will inherit this setting unless they change it.

parameters.label: Draw Mode Color
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Color to draw __Origin Axis__, __Bounding Box__, or if all the card textures are missing

parameters.label: Card Geometry
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: If __Draw Mode__ is chosen, what kind of cards to draw.

parameters.label: +X Texture
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the +X side of the box or cross. If missing the -X texture is mirrored. If both are missing then YZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: -X Texture
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the -X side of the box or cross. If missing the +X texture is mirrored. If both are missing then YZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: +Y Texture
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the +Y side of the box or cross. If missing the -Y texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: -Y Texture
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the -Y side of the box or cross. If missing the +Y texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XZ plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: +Z Texture
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the +Z side of the box or cross. If missing the -Z texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XY plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: -Z Texture
parameters.heading: Texture Cards
parameters.description: Texture to draw on the -Z side of the box or cross. If missing the +Z texture is mirrored. If both are missing then XY plane is not drawn. This parameter can be animated.

parameters.label: Render Texture Cards
parameters.heading: Render Card Options
parameters.description: Renders the selected texture card axes.

parameters.label: Cancel
parameters.heading: Render Card Options
parameters.description: Stops any in-progress renders.

parameters.label: Reset

parameters.description: Resets the in-progress renders.

parameters.label: Renderer
parameters.heading: Render Card Options
parameters.description: List of available render delegates.

parameters.label: Maximum Image Size
parameters.heading: Render Card Options
parameters.description: Maximum width or height of the texture card images.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Dome Light
parameters.description: The intensity of the dome light.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Dome Light
parameters.description: Sets the color of the dome light.

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.heading: Dome Light
parameters.description: Optional HDR for rendering texture cards.

parameters.heading: Top Light
parameters.description: The intensity of the top light.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Top Light
parameters.description: Sets the color of the top light.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Top Light
parameters.description: Control the rotation of the top light.

parameters.label: Custom Scheduler

parameters.heading: Primitive definition

Use the default (__Reference__) unless you have a specific reason to choose [Inherits|https://graphics.pixar.com/usd/docs/USD-Glossary.html#USDGlossary-Inherits] or [Specializes|https://graphics.pixar.com/usd/docs/USD-Glossary.html#USDGlossary-Specializes]. parameters.heading: Primitive definition
parameters.description: When this is on, each of the duplicates is marked as an [instanceable prim|/solaris/glossary#instancing]. This means they will be "aliases" to an implicit shared "master" prim. The advantage is that instances take a very small amount of constant space. The disadvantage is that while you can edit attributes on each instanced prim (for example, give each instance its own transform), you can't edit any of its descendants.

parameters.label: Promote Collections
parameters.heading: Collections
parameters.description: If the source prim or any of its descendants have a collection that match this pattern (or space-separated list of patterns), the node authors a copy of the collection on the __Collection Primitive__. If the source(s) have multiple collections with the same name, the contents of the new authored collection contains the union of their contents. For example, when this is on, if you duplicate `/Geometry/orig` to `/Geometry/dupe1` and `/Geometry/dupe2`, if `orig` had a collection named `lights` containing `/Geometry/orig/lamp`, the collection will be "promoted" onto the common parent (`/Geometry`) and the contents will be rewritten to be relative to the duplicates. parameters.label: Promote Source Collections
parameters.heading: Collections

entries.title: Edit Material Properties
entries.summary: Lets you build a spare parameter interface that reflects material or shader input attributes to directly edit their values.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Reference Type
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: This node can edit properties on an existing material primitive or it can create a new on, reference it to an existing primitive, and edit properties on the newly created one.  This is useful when the original material is bound to some geometry whose appearance you don't want to change, but instead you want to base a new material on an existing one, then tweak it, and bind it to another geometry.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Class Prim Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Adds an "inherits" composition arc to the edited primitive, to listen at this location for indirect edits. The location does not have to be populated, and it does not cause any primitives to be created.

parameters.label: Create Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Creates spare parameters for editing the values of the input attributes of the material or a shader specified in the __Primitives__ parameter.

parameters.label: Create Material Outputs
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Creates spare parameters for editing the connections of the output attributes of the material or a shader specified in the __Primitives__ parameter. They enable changing the terminal shaders of the material.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Reference type__ is __Create Class__, this parameter controls where the `Class` specifier primitives end and the `Over` primitives begin. Usually the primitive being modified is a descendant of the primitive where the actual inherit composition arc lives, and all primitives below that point should use the `Over` specifier, whereas primitives above this point should use `Class`.

parameters.label: Reference Parent Material
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: If the __Primitives__ parameter specifies a shader primitive, turning this option on will ensure that the newly created primitive will reference its parent material instead of the shader itself..

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: Scene graph path where the new referencing primitive will be created.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this type.

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: If the toggle is on, the newly created referencing primitive will be instanceable.

parameters.label: Bokeh Shape
parameters.heading: Bokeh
parameters.description: A choice for what shape the bokeh should be: Circular, Polygonal (see __Number of sides__), or Texture Map (see __Bokeh texture map__).

parameters.label: Bokeh Texture Map
parameters.heading: Bokeh
parameters.description: When __Bokeh shape__ is "Texture map", this is the path to the texture to use. The texture should contain a bright bokeh shape on a black background. (The shader samples the texture based on its intensity using [Vex:importance_remap], shaping the bokeh to the bright parts of the texture).

parameters.label: Number of Sides
parameters.heading: Bokeh
parameters.description: When __Bokeh shape__ is "Polygonal", this is the number of sides the bokeh shape has. This value must be greater than 3.

parameters.label: Bokeh Rotation
parameters.heading: Bokeh
parameters.description: Rotate the bokeh shape by this number of degrees.

parameters.label: Anisotropy
parameters.heading: Bokeh
parameters.description: This is a value from `-1.0` to `1.0` which controls the aspect ratio of the bokeh shape. Set this to `0` to get square (equal height and width) shapes. Negative fractions make the bokeh shape narrower than it is tall. Positive fractions make the bokeh shape shorter than it is wide.

parameters.label: Anisotropy Texture Map
parameters.heading: Bokeh
parameters.description: A texture map to control anisotropy (see the __Anisotropy__ parameter above) for each pixel. In the texture image, black represents `-1.0` and white represents `1.0`.

parameters.label: Projection
parameters.heading: Lens Distortion
parameters.description: Change the projection type of the lense. * __Perspective__ creates a default view of the world in front of the camera. This type can capture the depth of different objects. * __Orthographic__ creates a view of the world in front of the camera. This type can't capture the depth of the different objects. * __Polar__ creates a 3-dimensional panoramic view around the camera. You can use the result in a dome-shaped world, for example a sky. * __Cylindrical__ creates a cylindrical projection where camera's horizontal __Screen Window__ maps to horizontal wrap amount (-1 to 1 maps to -180 to 180 degrees), and vertical __Screen Window__ (divided by image aspect ratio) maps to base and tip of the cylinder in world space. * __Polar Stereographic__ projection is used if preserving the shape of small object on image plane is required. * __Polar Equidistant__ projection is used if preserving angular sizes of object on image plane is required. * __Polar Equisolid__ projection is used if preserving constant ration of solid angles in object and image spaces is required. * __Polar Orthographic__ projection is used if evenness of illumination through the entire image plane is required.

parameters.label: Type of Curvature
parameters.heading: Lens Distortion
parameters.description: A type of curvature to distort the lens with: "None", "Quadratic", "Cubic", or "Texture Map".

parameters.label: Curvature Texture Map
parameters.heading: Lens Distortion
parameters.description: When __Curvature type__ is "Texture map", this is a path to the texture map. Values in the texture image represent the unit "height" of the lens (distance from flat) at a given position across the face of the lens. Black represents `-1.0` and white represents `1.0`.

parameters.label: Lens Curvature
parameters.heading: Lens Distortion
parameters.description: When __Curvature type__ is not "None", this is the amount of curvature to apply, from `-1.0` to `1.0`.

parameters.label: Chromatic Aberration
parameters.heading: Lens Distortion
parameters.description: The amount of chromatic aberration to add to the lens. This value plus one represents the index of refraction applied to blue light. The shader then linearly maps this value down to an index of refraction of 1.0 for red light. For example, a value of `0.2` means the index of refraction is 1.2 for blue light and 1.0 for red light, with a linear gradient in between. For more control over the mapping use the __Aberration ramp__. [Image:/images/nodes/vop/physicallens_chromatic_aberrations.jpg]

parameters.label: Aberration Ramp
parameters.heading: Lens Distortion
parameters.description: This ramp controls the mapping of aberrations between blue and red light. The left edge of the ramp represents blue light and the right edge represents red light. The vertical axis represents the index of refraction and goes from `1.0` at the bottom to `1.0` + the value of __Chromatic Aberration__ at the top.

parameters.label: Tint
parameters.heading: Tint and Exposure
parameters.description: Adds a color tint to the output. You can use numbers greater than `1.0` to (unrealistically) brighten the image.

parameters.label: Tint Texture Map
parameters.heading: Tint and Exposure
parameters.description: Effectively multiplies this texture map over the output image.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Tint and Exposure
parameters.description: An exponential scale for the brightness of the image.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Tint and Exposure
parameters.description: A linear scale for the brightness of the image.

parameters.label: Vignetting
parameters.heading: Tint and Exposure
parameters.description: An amount to darken the image around the edges. Because this is physically based, it is relative to the camera's field of view. Alternatively, you can use the __Tint texture map__ to get full control over darkening parts of the image.

parameters.label: Tilt X
parameters.heading: Tilt and Shift
parameters.description: The number of degrees to tilt the plane of focus by in the X direction (around the camera's Y axis).

parameters.label: Tilt Y
parameters.heading: Tilt and Shift
parameters.description: The number of degrees to tilt the plane of focus by in the Y direction (around the camera's X axis).

parameters.label: Shift X
parameters.heading: Tilt and Shift
parameters.description: The distance (in Houdini world units) to shift the lens in the X direction.

parameters.label: Shift Y
parameters.heading: Tilt and Shift
parameters.description: The distance (in Houdini world units) to shift the lens in the Y direction.

parameters.label: F-Stop Texture Map
parameters.heading: Focus Mapping
parameters.description: The path to a texture map that specifies the f-stop value at each pixel. In the texture image, black represents __F-stop near__ and white represents __F-stop far__.

parameters.label: F-Stop Near
parameters.heading: Focus Mapping
parameters.description: The lower bound of the __F-stop texture map__.

parameters.label: F-Stop Far
parameters.heading: Focus Mapping
parameters.description: The upper bound of the __F-stop texture map__.

parameters.label: Focus Texture Map
parameters.heading: Focus Mapping
parameters.description: The path to a texture map that specifies the focus distance at each pixel. In the texture image, black represents __Focus near__ and white represents __Focus far__.

parameters.label: Focus Near
parameters.heading: Focus Mapping
parameters.description: The lower bound of the __Focus Texture Map__.

parameters.label: Focus Far
parameters.heading: Focus Mapping
parameters.description: The upper bound of the __Focus Texture Map__.

parameters.label: Enable OpenCV Distortion
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: Turn this on to use the OpenCV defined intrinsic camera parameters for lens distortion. Refer to [OpenCV documentation|Link:https://docs.opencv.org/2.4/modules/calib3d/doc/camera_calibration_and_3d_reconstruction.html#camera-calibration-and-3d-reconstruction] for more details on each of the constants in the intrinsic camera parameters.

parameters.label: k1
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The k<sub>1</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion.

parameters.label: k2
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The k<sub>2</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion.

parameters.label: k3
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The k<sub>3</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Positive values will produce a barrel distortion, and negative values will produce a pincushion distortion.

parameters.label: k4
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The k<sub>4</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion.

parameters.label: k5
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The k<sub>5</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion.

parameters.label: k6
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The k<sub>6</sub> radial distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Negative values will produce a barrel distortion, and positive values will produce a pincushion distortion.

parameters.label: p1
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The p<sub>1</sub> tangential distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Positive values will give the effect that the top of the image plane is farther away than the bottom, and negative values will do the opposite.

parameters.label: p2
parameters.heading: OpenCV
parameters.description: The p<sub>2</sub> tangential distortion constant in the intrinsic camera parameters defined by OpenCV. Positive values will give the effect that the right side of the image plane is farther away than the left side, and negative values will do the opposite.

parameters.label: Rolling Shutter Direction
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: A choice for how to simulate rolling shutter: "None", "Bottom First", "Top First", "Left First", "Right First", or "Custom" (see __Time offset curve__ below).

parameters.label: Time Offset Ramp Rotation
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: When __Rolling shutter__ is "Custom", the direction of the shutter movement, in degrees. A value of `0` represents straight up (positive Y in camera space).

parameters.label: Time Offset Ramp
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: When __Rolling shutter__ is "Custom", this ramp to control the progression of the shutter across the image. See [understanding time offset and scale|#time_offset] above. The horizontal axis represents shutter time, the vertical axis represents shutter progress, where the bottom is the start position and the top is the end position. So, the default ramp (a line from bottom left to top right) represents a linear progression across the image.

parameters.label: Time Offset Texture Map
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: Path to a texture map file to control the time offset. See [understanding time offset and scale|#time_offset] above.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: A base scale on the shutter time. Basically, this affects how blurry the image is, however see [understanding time offset and scale|#time_offset] above for more information. For rolling shutter effects time scale must be quite small, otherwise the rolling shutter will not be visible.

parameters.label: Time Scale Texture Map
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: Path to a texture map file to control the time offset. See [understanding time offset and scale|#time_offset] above.

parameters.label: Use Shutter Curve
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: Turn this on to get custom control over the amount of light allowed into the camera aperture across the shutter time.

parameters.label: Shutter Curve
parameters.heading: Shutter
parameters.description: When __Use Shutter Curve__ is turned on, this ramp represents the weighting of a time sample based on its position in the shutter period. In terms of a camera, this ramp represents the amount of light that gets through to the sensor (vertical axis) at a given moment across the shutter time (horizontal axis). The default distribution is uniform. [Image:/images/nodes/vop/physicallens_blur_before.jpg] [Image:/images/nodes/vop/physicallens_blur_shutter_curve_parm.jpg] [Image:/images/nodes/vop/physicallens_blur_shutter_curve.jpg]
