entries.title: Edit Properties
entries.summary: Lets you build a spare parameter interface to directly edit attribute and relationship values.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Edit Properties
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Opens the [Edit Parameter Interface window|/network/spare] with the __From USD__ tab selected in the source pane on the left.

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in __Primitive Paths__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

entries.title: Extract Instances
entries.summary: Converts ("heroes") an instance into a "real" editable prim.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: How to select the instance(s) to extract.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[0] /geometry/instancer[1]`). To select all instances in an instancer, use `/<<path>>[*]`. To select a range, use `/geometry/instancer[4-7]` (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example `/geometry/instancer[2][7]`. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, `/geometry/instancer[{@weights>0.5}]`.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Native Instances__, a list of paths to [instanceable prims|/solaris/glossary#instancing].

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The scene graph path _under_ which to put newly extracted prims. Under this prim, for each extracted instance, the node will create an `Xform` prim with the same `name` as the instancer, and under that the extracted prim (named `instance_<<index_number>>`). For example, if you set __Primitive Path__ to `/geometry/heroes`, and extract instances `5` and `10` from `/geometry/instancer1`, the node creates the extracted prims at `/geometry/heroes/instancer1/instance_5` and `/geometry/heroes/instancer1/instance_10`.

parameters.label: Primitive Name
parameters.description: When enabled, set the extracted primitive names to be prefixed by this instead of the original primitive name.

parameters.label: Flatten Hierarchy

parameters.label: Prototype

parameters.label: Prototype Primitive

parameters.label: Modify Source Primitive

parameters.label: Make Instanceable

parameters.label: Bind Materials

parameters.label: Deactivate Entirely Extracted Instancers
parameters.description: When all instances are extracted, this option deactivates the original point instancer.

parameters.label: Scalar Primvars with Unauthored Element Size

parameters.label: Time

parameters.label: Integer Frames

entries.title: File Cache
entries.summary: Caches (writes out once and then reads from) USD layers (possibly animated) to disk.

parameters.label: Load from Disk
parameters.description: When this is on, the node reads its output from the cached disk files, rather than cooking its input. When you click __Save to Disk__ or __Save to Disk in Background__ (on the __Caching__ tab) to write out the cache files, the node automatically turns this checkbox on.

parameters.label: Reload Geometry
parameters.description: Force a reload of the file.  This will also clear any cached data for packed disk primitives (see also the [geocache|Cmd:geocache] command).

parameters.label: File Path
parameters.description: When this is __Constructed__ (the default), the node builds up the cache file path(s) from the values of various parameters, allowing features such as versioning and animation options. If you set this to __Explicit__, you need to [manually write a single expression|/render/expressions] in the __Geometry File__ parameter with all the variables you want in the path (including the frame number when __Time Dependent Cache__ is on).

parameters.label: Base Name
parameters.description: When __File Path__ is __Constructed__, this is the first part of the cache file name. The default is `$HIPNAME.$OS` (the name of the current scene file without the `.hip` extension, then a dot, then the name of this node). This is usually sufficient to prevent filename collisions between files/nodes if you give this node an meaningful, unique name (if you have two networks containing nodes both named `filecache1`, you will get a collision). The drop down menu to the right of the text field has some more possible expressions.

parameters.label: File Type
parameters.description: The default is `.bgeo.sc`, which can handle any type of Houdini geometry and uses compression, so it's always safe to use. If _all_ the primitives in the input are _always_ VDB volumes, you can switch the file type to save the files directly as `.vdb`. When you set the __File Type__ to `.vdb`, the node converts Houdini's primitive attributes to VDB grid metadata, and detail attributes to file metadata.

parameters.label: Base Folder
parameters.description: When __File Path__ is __Constructed__, this is the folder to save the cache files into. The default is `$HIP/geo` (a folder named `geo` in the same directory as the current scene file). (When __Version__ is on it adds another directory level inside the base folder.)

parameters.label: Open Directory
parameters.description: Click to show the contents of the __Base Folder__ in the file manager. This can be useful when you want to clean up old cache files.

parameters.label: Version
parameters.description: When __File Path__ is __Constructed__ and the checkbox to the left is on, the node adds a directory level (and filename part) to the cache file path(s) indicating the version. This lets you [cache multiple variations|#versioning] of the input network. == Caching == (caching)

parameters.label: Save to Disk
parameters.heading: Cache
parameters.description: Saves the geometry to disk with the last control settings.

parameters.label: Save to Disk in Background
parameters.heading: Cache
parameters.description: Use a TOP network to cook and save the cache files to disk in a separate background process. This allows you to keep working on other parts of Houdini. The cached frames will show up as they are completed by the other process.

parameters.label: Cancel Cook
parameters.heading: Cache
parameters.description: Stops all background caching processes, if any exist.

parameters.label: TIP
parameters.heading: Cache
parameters.description: You can collapse the box around these buttons as a "safety latch", to prevent yourself from clicking them and rebuilding the cache accidentally.

parameters.label: Evaluate As
parameters.heading: Cache Range
parameters.description: When this is __Frame Range__ the node writes a cache file for every frame (see Start/End/Inc below). If you don't want pre-generate all frames at once, or if you know you only need to regenerate a single changed frame, you can set this to __Single Frame__. This makes the node write out a cache file only for the current frame (or the frame you set in __Override Frame__).

parameters.label: Override Frame
parameters.heading: Cache Range
parameters.description: When __Evaluate As__ is __Single Frame__ and the checkbox to the left is on, cache this explicit frame number instead of the current frame from the timeline.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Cache Range
parameters.description: Specifies the range of frames to render (start frame, end frame, and increment). All values may be floating point values. The range is inclusive. These parameters determine the values of the local variables for the output driver.

parameters.label: Substeps
parameters.heading: Cache Range
parameters.description: When __Evaluate As__ is __Frame Range__, this is the number of fractional sub-frames to divide each frame into. Caching sub-frames increases the quality of motion blur rendering for cached animated geometry. If you set __Substeps__ greater than `1` and you've set __File Path__ to __Explicit__, make sure your explicit path expression can handle fractional frames, by using `$T` (floating point time in seconds) or `$FF` (fractional frame number) instead of `$F` (whole frame number).

parameters.label: Custom TOP Scheduler
parameters.heading: Scheduling
parameters.description: This parameter overrides the TOP scheduler for this node.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers authored above Layer Break nodes from being written to disk by this ROP. This allows a Layer Break node to dictate which portions of the LOP Network are to be saved. Disabling this option allows this behavior to be overridden, forcing the full stage authored by the LOP network to be written to disk. This may be used for debugging purposes, or to write a complete scene to disk for rendering.

parameters.label: Strip Post-Layers
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers added using the [Hom:hou.LopNetwork#editablePostLayer] method from being written to disk. With this option disabled, these post-layers are flattened into the layer __Output File__ layer.

parameters.label: Flush Data After Each Frame
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See [saving animation|#anim] above.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated.

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.heading: Layers
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See [Filter Time Samples|#filtertimesamples]

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using __Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References)__ to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: If you use the [Load Layer LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer] to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, layers generated by importing data from SOPs with [SOP Import|Node:lop/sopimport] are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers imported from SOPs as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers.

parameters.label: Output Processors
parameters.heading: Output processing
parameters.description: Add an [output processor|/solaris/output#processors] to this node. Output processors are Python plugins that can alter the file locations and file path strings used for external files. The USD render node starts with one default output processor (called `Use Relative Paths`, see below). (See [output processors|/solaris/output#processors] for information on how to write an output processor plugin.)

parameters.label: Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: Set this to the *name* of a root primitive on the current stage to set it as the [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for the top-level file.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layer with No Default Primitive
parameters.label_norm: error saving layer with no default primitive
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: When this is on, the render node will error and stop cooking if you haven't specified a [default primitive|/solaris/glossary#default_prim] for all layers being written out. This is a way to force yourself to make sure layers have default prims, so you know you can reference in files without having to manually specify a top-level prim.

parameters.label: Save ROP's Time Information to Output
parameters.label_norm: save rop's time information to output
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: Write the start and end frames, as well as the current frames per second setting, to the top-level output file.

parameters.label: Clear Houdini-Specific Custom Data
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: LOP networks often attach Houdini-specific custom data to layers, prims, and properties. Houdini does not need this data to be stored on disk (usually it is related to how to write files), so by default Houdini strips out this data before saving. Normally there's no reason to turn this parameter off (it's possible it might help SideFX diagnosing a problem).

parameters.label: Ensure Basic Metrics are Set on All Layers
parameters.label_norm: ensure basic metrics are set on all layers
parameters.heading: Layer metadata
parameters.description: This options ensures that the `upAxis` and `metersPerUnit` metadata is set in every USD file written to disk. If a value has not been explicitly authored on a layer by the LOP Network, the default up axis and meters per unit values from the Lighting Preferences are used.

parameters.label: Pre-Render Script
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Run this script before any rendering.

parameters.label: Pre-Frame Script
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Run this script before each frame.

parameters.label: Post-Frame Script
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame.

parameters.label: Post-Write Script
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame's data finishes writing to disk.

parameters.label: Post-Render Script
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Run this script after all rendering.

parameters.label: Initialize Simulation OPs
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Initialize DOP simulations before rendering.

parameters.label: Alfred Style Progress
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Print percentage complete value as files are written. This is in the style expected by Pixar's Alfred render queue.

parameters.label: Report Network Use
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Print the number of bytes sent or received by the distributed simulation nodes during cooks triggered by this node. This does not track network usage from, for example, saving a file to an NFS mount. It only tracks the network communication of distributed Houdini nodes. When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See [saving animation|#anim] above.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated.

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See [Filter Time Samples|#filtertimesamples]

parameters.heading: Extra files

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using __Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References)__ to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: If you use the [Load Layer LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer] to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, layers generated by importing data from SOPs with [SOP Import|Node:lop/sopimport] are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers imported from SOPs as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers.

This is desirable for most cases where a failure to save means an illegal path, which is not recoverable.  However, sometimes files fail to save due to network issues.  If the number of save retries is non-zero, Houdini will re-attempt to save this number of times. Each time will be accompanied with an output to the console of the failure to save and a five second wait in the hopes that the network will clear up.

parameters.label: Render with Take
parameters.heading: Save
parameters.description: Uses the settings in a particular take while rendering. Choose __Current__ to use the current take when rendering.

parameters.label: Missing Frame
parameters.heading: Load
parameters.description: This is what the node should do (in __Load from Disk__ mode) when the node can't find (or cleanly load) a cache file. __Report Error__ sets an error on the node, preventing the rest of the network from cooking. This makes it obvious when a problem happens. __No Geometry__ (the default) sets a warning on the node rather than an error, and outputs empty geometry. This can be useful if your network has a way of dealing with missing cache frames, or if they're not important.

parameters.label: Load Retries
parameters.heading: Load
parameters.description: If loading the geometry from disk fails due to a disk writing error, Houdini will usually error the output node immediately. This is desirable for most cases where a failure to load means an illegal path, which is not recoverable. However, sometimes files fail to load due to network issues. If the number of __Load Retries__ is non-zero, Houdini will re-attempt to load this number of times. Each time will be accompanied with an output to the console of the failure to load and a five second wait in the hopes that the network will clear up.

parameters.label: Pre-fetch Geometry
parameters.heading: Load
parameters.description: Attempt to predict the next frame that will be needed and load it in the background.  This lets computation be overlapped with file IO. If you are blending multiple frames, the Cache Frames needs to be large enough for only the net-new frame to be loaded each cook.  Otherwise the simple predictive model of the prefetcher will be confused and stop working.

parameters.label: Pre-Render Script
parameters.heading: Scripts
parameters.description: Run this script before any rendering.

parameters.label: Pre-Frame Script
parameters.heading: Scripts
parameters.description: Run this script before each frame.

parameters.label: Post-Frame Script
parameters.heading: Scripts
parameters.description: Run this script after each frame.

parameters.label: Post-Render Script
parameters.heading: Scripts
parameters.description: Run this script after all rendering.

parameters.label: Version String
parameters.heading: Path Construction
parameters.description: Contains an expression that generates the "version" part of the path, including a `v` prefix. *Do not edit this expression*.

parameters.label: Cache Folder
parameters.heading: Path Construction
parameters.description: Contains an expression that generates the parent directory path for cache files. *Do not edit this expression*.

parameters.label: Cache Name
parameters.heading: Path Construction
parameters.description: Contains an expression that generates the filename for cache files. *Do not edit this expression*.

parameters.label: Descriptive Label
parameters.heading: Path Construction
parameters.description: Contains an expression that generates the _descriptive text_ displayed next to this node (below the name and badges) in the network editor. This is set to output the cache filename pattern. *Do not edit this expression*.

parameters.label: Output File
parameters.heading: Path Construction
parameters.description: Contains an expression that generates the resolved, full path of the cache file for the current frame. *Do not edit this expression*.

entries.title: Follow Path Constraint
entries.summary: Constrains a prim to follow a path curve.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: Whether the source (the thing constrained to follow a path) is a regular primitive, or a point instance. You *cannot* use a nested point instance as a source.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Source Instances
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Target Source
parameters.heading: Path
parameters.description: Where to get the path curve to follow, either the first input or the second input.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Path
parameters.description: Whether the path is a regular primitive, or a point instance. (You *can* use a nested point instance as a target.)

parameters.label: Target
parameters.heading: Path
parameters.description: When __Target Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Target Instance
parameters.heading: Path
parameters.description: When __Target Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Hide Target
parameters.heading: Path
parameters.description: When __Target Source__ is __First Input__ and __Type__ is __Primitive__, whether to hide set the path's visibility to "hidden".

parameters.label: Import Time
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Specify the frame at which the source and/or target geometry are imported into the embedded SOP network to build the constraints. The default `$FF` expression forces the constraint LOP to be time dependent, which is needed when operating on a non time-dependent network that has time samples driving the source or target primitives. However, for better performance with a non time-dependent network with no time samples, it is recommended to use a static value instead.

parameters.label: Maintain Local Offset
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When this is off (the default), the source object snaps onto the path it follows. When this is on, the object maintains the same relative distance between itself and the path as it follows the shape of the path.

parameters.label: Parametrization
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: How to map the __Position__ value onto the path.

parameters.label: Distance Attribute
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When __Parameterization__ is __Distance Point Attribute__, the name of the primvar containing the distance value (not including the `primvar:` prefix). The primvar must be a `vector3`, but only the first (X) component is used.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Where to position the source object along the path. To animate the source object along the path, this should be an expression based on the current frame (`$F`) or time (`$T`). For example, if __Parameterizaiton__ is __Normalized Distance__, you might set this to `$F/100`.

parameters.label: Use Snippet
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Set the position using a VEX snippet. The snippet should write the position value to the `pos` variable. You can use the variables typically available to an [Attribute Wrangle SOP|Node:sop/attribwrangle]. `@ptnum` is the index of the current prim being constrained. You can use `npoints(0)` to get the total number of prims being constrained. You can use `@Frame` and `@Time` to make the snippet time-dependent. The initial value of `pos` (at the start of the snippet) is the evaluated value of the __Position__ parameter. So you can use an expression in that parameter to compute a "base" value, and modify it using the snippet.

parameters.label: Look At Mode
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: How to compute the direction the source object points along.

parameters.label: Look At Source
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: When __Look At Mode__ is __From Primitive__, where to get the primitive to look at (the first or second input).

parameters.label: Look At Xform
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: When __Look At Mode__ is __From Primitive__, the scene graph path of the prim to look at. (This does not support looking at a point instance.)

parameters.label: Direction Attribute
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: When __Look At Mode__ is __Direction Attribute From Path__, the name of a `vector3f` primvar (minus the `primvar:` prefix) to use as the look at direction.

parameters.label: Look Up Mode
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: How to compute the up vector.

parameters.label: Up Vector Source
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: When __Look Up Mode__ is __From Primitive__, where to get the primitive to point the up vector at (the first or second input).

parameters.label: Up Vector Xform
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: When __Look Up Mode__ is __From Primitive__, the scene graph path of the prim to point the up vector at. (This does not support point instances.)

parameters.label: Look At Axis
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: Which axis on the source object to match to the look at vector. You can use this to compensate for the orientation the source object was created in. This can't be the same as the __Look Up Axis__.

parameters.label: Look Up Axis
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: Which axis on the source object to match to the up vector. You can use this to compensate for the orientation the source object was created in.  This can't be the same as the __Look At Axis__.

parameters.label: Up Attribute
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: When __Look Up Mode__ is __Up Attribute From Path__, the name of a `vector3f` primvar (minus the `primvar:` prefix) to use as the look up vector.

parameters.label: Roll
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: Roll angle in degrees around the look at direction. You can use this, for example, to animate "banking" as the source object goes around curves.

parameters.label: Use Snippet
parameters.heading: Orientation
parameters.description: Set the roll using a VEX snippet. The snippet should write the roll degrees to the `roll` variable. You can use the variables typically available to an [Attribute Wrangle SOP|Node:sop/attribwrangle]. `@ptnum` is the index of the current prim being constrained. You can use `npoints(0)` to get the total number of prims being constrained. You can use `@Frame` and `@Time` to make the snippet time-dependent. The initial value of `roll` (at the start of the snippet) is the evaluated value of the __Roll__ parameter. So you can use an expression in that parameter to compute a "base" value, and modify it using the snippet.

entries.title: For Each
entries.summary: The end node of a For-Each loop block.

parameters.label: Iteration Method
parameters.description: How this node loops/what it loops over.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.description: When __Iteration Method__ is __For Number of Iterations__, this is the number of loops. (You can use an expression in this parameter to drive the number of loops based on something else.)

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: When __Iteration Method__ is __For Each Primitive__, __For Each Variant Set__, or __For Each Variant__, the prims to look at. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`).

parameters.label: Allow Instance Proxies in Pattern
parameters.description: When __Iteration Method__ is __For Each Primitive__, __For Each Variant Set__, or __For Each Variant__, enable this parameter to allow the __Primitives__ pattern to match instance proxy primitives. These primitives are not editable on a USD stage, but can still be used to drive the For Each loop.

parameters.label: Variant Set
parameters.description: When __Iteration Method__ is __For Each Variant__, the name of the variant set to loop over.

parameters.label: Iterate Over Strings
parameters.description: When __Iteration method__ is __For Each String in Parameter__, the list of strings to loop over. Individual strings are separated by white space. Quotes can be used around a string to incorporate white space into that value.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.description: Enable this option to remove all layers created above Layer Break LOPs on every input to this node. This is the default option since usually a layer break operation is used to separate data generated by the For Each iterations from data authored prior to the For Each Begin node, and thus prevent duplicate copies of the data outside the loop from being added to the stage. However in some cases, such as when different iterations follow different cook paths, it may be useful to preserve the layers from above layer breaks. As noted in the __Combine Iterations__ description, some values of that parameter may cause layers from above layer breaks to be stripped in spite of this option being turned off.

parameters.label: Set Last Modified Primitives from Iteration Input
parameters.label_norm: set last modified primitives from iteration input
parameters.description: Enable this option to set this node's last modified primitives to be the union of the last modified primitives from all the iterations of cooking the third input to this node. If this option is disabled, the last modified primitives set on the first input are used as the last modified primitives for this node as well.

parameters.label: Merge Load Masks From Iterations
parameters.description: Enable this option to combine the load masks (population mask, payload load mask, and layer muting) from each interation with the load masks from the first input to create the final load mask for the stage output by this node. Turn off this option to pass through the load mask from the first input unchanged, ignoring the load masks on the iteration input. ~~~

parameters.label: Iteration Option Name
parameters.description: The name of the context option variable this node will create holding the current loop number (starting from 0). You can rename this for convenience or to make nested loops use unique names.

parameters.label: Iteration Count Option Name
parameters.description: The name of the context option variable this node will create holding the total number of loops. You can rename this for convenience or to make nested loops use unique names.

parameters.label: Value Option Name
parameters.description: The name of the context option variable this node will create holding __Iteration Method__-specific information (the current iteration for __For Number of Iterations__, the current prim path for __For Each Primitive__, the variant set name for __For Each Variant Set__, or the variant name for __For Each Variant__). You can rename this for convenience or to make nested loops use unique names. ~~~

parameters.label: Iteration Range
parameters.description: This lets you optionally restrict the number of iterations the node would normally perform to start and end within a certain range. This can be useful for debugging, to observe the effect of just a "slice" of the overall result.

parameters.label: First iteration
parameters.description: When __Iteration Range__ is __Single__, only run this iteration number. When __Iteration Eange__ is __Range__, only run a subset of iterations starting at this number. The first iteration is numbered 0.

parameters.label: Last iteration
parameters.description: When __Iteration Range__ is __Range__, only run a subset of iterations including but ending at this number. The first iteration is numbered 0.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close

parameters.label: Camera Prim

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample

If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The scene graph path of the prim on which to author the value clip metadata. If the specified primitive does not exist, the node will create it with no primitive type (the primitive type will come from the clip files).

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ didn't already exist so this node has to create it, the node sets this as the new prim's [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If any parents of the path in __Primitive Path__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.

parameters.label: Get Geometry From Second Input
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Enable this option to generate clip files from the LOP node attached to this node's second input. The save path of the incoming stage will not be used to control where the clip files will be saved. The __Save Clip File Path__ parameter controls this. Turn off this option to load clip files from disk, in which case the connection to the second input is ignored.

parameters.label: Load Clip File Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Get Geometry From Second Input__ is off, this parameter specifies the path to existing clip files on disk.

parameters.label: Handle Missing Files
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If the clip files are external files on disk, this controls what the node does if some specified clip files do not exist.

parameters.label: Reload Files
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Forces Houdini to reload the USD files mentioned in the __Load Clip File Path__ parameter.

parameters.label: All Clip Files Have Matching Scene Graph Structure
parameters.label_norm: all clip files have matching scene graph structure
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Turn on this option if all clip files are known to have the same scene graph hierarchy, and the same set of time sampled attributes on those primitives. This allows the node to optimize the generation of the manifest and topology files by only looking at a single clip file instead of processing all of them. To profit from the new option, a couple of settings are mandatory * Turn off __Get Geometry From Second Input__. * Turn on __All Clip Files Have Matching Scene Graph Structure__. * In case you have an [USD ROP|Node:out/usd], set __Valid Frame Range__ to __Render Current Frame__.

parameters.label: Reference Topology File
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The generated topology file is referenced onto the primitive where the clip is authored. If disabled, the topology file is sublayered onto the active layer instead. This latter approach makes the topology layer opinions stronger than the reference approach, which involves moving some primitives on the topology layer from the clip source path to the clip destination path.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When making a value clip from these scene graphs over a frame range, the set of primitives must be fixed, because primitives not in the topology file will not appear when they show up in a clip file. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. These visibility opinions are added to the topology layer. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute. If __All Clip Files Have Matching Scene Graph Structure__ is enabled, we know that no animated visibility opinions are required  to handle changes in the scene graph structure, so this parameter is disabled.

parameters.label: Flatten Clip Files
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether the clip files are from disk or from this node's second input, it can be useful to flatten the layers of the incoming clip file. This is because clip files read in by a Value Clip in USD are not composed. Reference, sublayer, and payload arcs are not followed. Only the data stored directly in the clip file is read in by the value clip. If this option is enabled, whether the input is from the second input or files on disk, the flattened USD file will be written to disk using the path set in the __Save Clip File Path__ parameter.

parameters.label: Remove Unused Data From Flattened Clip Files
parameters.label_norm: remove unused data from flattened clip files
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If the clip files are being flattened by this node, turning on this option causes all non-animated data (which will be stored in the topology file) to be stripped out of the clip file before it is saved to disk. This is an automated process which can save considerable disk space.

parameters.label: Save Clip File Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If the clip files are being written to disk by this LOP (either because the clip data is coming from the second input, or because the option to flatten the clip files is turned on), this parameter controls the path on disk where the clip files will be written. As with all USD data authored by LOPs, these clip files will only be written to disk when the whole scene is saved out with a [USD ROP|Node:out/usd] or [USD Render ROP|Node:out/usdrender]. This parameter can be time varying, in which case a separate clip file will be written for each frame, or it can be constant, in which case the data from all frames will be written to a single clip file. Either approach is valid depending on the size of your clip data.

parameters.label: Manifest File Save Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The file path where the automatically generated manifest file will be saved. This file specifies exactly which primitives and values should be brought in from the value clip files. The contents of this file are generated automatically from the set of time sampled attributes in the clip files.

parameters.label: Topology File Save Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The file path where the automatically generated topology file will be saved. This file contains all the data from the clip files that is not animated. This topology file is referenced onto the primitive holding the clip metadata, or sublayered onto the active layer, depending on the __Reference Topology File__ setting. Value clip files are not composed by USD, and therefore will not work as expected if they contain any composition arcs. The topology file is scanned for composition arcs after it is created and warnings will be generated if any of its prims have composition arcs.

parameters.label: Clip Set
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The name of the clip set the value clip belongs to. Multiple clip sets can exist on a single prim.

parameters.label: Clip Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The path of a prim within the value clip file that should be mapped onto __Primitive Path__ when accessing values.

parameters.label: Clip Start Offset
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If individual clip files contain subframe samples, it is important that the switch from one clip file to another occur at the time of the first subsample. This offset adjusts the clip activation times to takes this into account. The __Start Frame__ should generally be adjusted by a similar amount so that the stage time of each clip file lines up with the time used within the clip file. As an example, if a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] is used to cache a rolling window of ``($F-0.2, $F-0.1, $F, $F+0.1, $F+0.2)`, this parameter should be set to -0.2, and the __Start Frame__ should be set to 0.8 so that the clip is authored with each clip file being active from `$F-0.2` to `$F+0.8`, instead of from `$F` to `$F+1`.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The first frame at which the value clip resolution should start. Prior to this frame no clip metadata is provided, which will cause USD to hold the values stored in the first clip file until the start frame is reached.

parameters.label: End Frame
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The last frame at which the value resolution will occur. This parameter has no effect if it is not enabled, in which case clip metadata is generated for every frame for which this node is cooked. Otherwise the clip metadata will simply stop at the specified frame (and the values from the last clip file will hold forever), or the earlier clip files will be reused if __Loop Frames__ is enabled.

parameters.label: Loop Frames
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: To create a repeating loop of clips, set an __End Frame__ and enable this option. For frames after the end frame, the clip files will be reused to author the clip metadata, returning to the start frame each time the end frame is reached. Clip metadata will be authored at every frame on which this node is cooked.

entries.title: Geometry Color
entries.summary: Adds display color and display opacity primvars to geometry.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Number of Assignments
parameters.heading: Color Type: Constant
parameters.description: The number of different color and opacity assignments for primitives on the stage.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Color Type: Constant
parameters.description: Primitive pattern for this specific assignment.

parameters.label: Enable Color
parameters.heading: Color Type: Constant
parameters.description: Toggle to control whether or not the display color should be assigned.

parameters.label: Display Color
parameters.heading: Color Type: Constant
parameters.description: The display color value to assign to the specified primitives.

parameters.label: Enable Opacity
parameters.heading: Color Type: Constant
parameters.description: Toggle to control whether or not the display opacity should be assigned.

parameters.label: Display Opacity
parameters.heading: Color Type: Constant
parameters.description: The opacity value to assign to the specified primitives. Can be enabled or disabled.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: Primitive pattern for randomized colors.

parameters.label: Apply to PointInstancer Elements
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: Randomize the color across each individual element of any point instancers in the pattern.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: Change the randomization seed.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: Select the style of randomization used to pick colors.

parameters.label: Hue Min Max
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __HSV__ mode, you can limit the random hue by setting minimum and maximum values.

parameters.label: Saturation Min Max
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __HSV__ mode, you can limit the random saturation by setting minimum and maximum values.

parameters.label: Value Min Max
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __HSV__ mode, you can limit the random value by setting minimum and maximum values.

parameters.label: Red Min Max
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __RGB__ mode, you can limit the random red by setting minimum and maximum values.

parameters.label: Green Min Max
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __RGB__ mode, you can limit the random green by setting minimum and maximum values.

parameters.label: Blue Min Max
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __RGB__ mode, you can limit the random blue by setting minimum and maximum values.

parameters.label: Color Ramp
parameters.heading: Color Type: Random
parameters.description: When in __Ramp__ mode, this parm sets the ranges of possible color values.

entries.title: Geometry Light
entries.summary: Adds properties to turn geometry into lights.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
