This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The parameter geometry primitives ("Gprims") you want to convert into geometry lights. Note that you can only convert primitives of type geometry, for example `mesh`, `points`, `BasisCurve` or `volume`. You can ((Ctrl))-click the __Select__ button beside the text box to select the geometry primitives from a panel. You can also use primitive patterns for advanced matching. Alternatively, you can drag geometry primitives from the Scene Graph Tree to this parameter or enter a path manually.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value.

parameters.label: API Schema
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Select which lighting schema to apply to the specified primitives.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. `0` does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the __Intensity__ to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: Use __Color Temperature__ to control the light color. The color calculated by __Color Temperature__ is *multiplied* by the RGB color in __Color__, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set __Color__ to `1.0, 1.0, 1.0`.

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: When __Enable Color Temperature__ is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from `1000` to `10000`. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the `UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb()` function from the USD library.

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.heading: Standard
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a [Light Filter Library LOP|Node:lop/lightfilterlibrary].

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (`0, 0, 0`) is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Falloff Start Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The near distance at which shadow falloff begins. The default value (`-1`) indicates no falloff.

parameters.label: Falloff Gamma
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: A gamma (i.e., exponential) control over shadow strength with linear distance within the falloff zone (between __Falloff__ and __Distance__).

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is `-1`, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global __Light Sampling Quality__. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree.  This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis.  If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than `0`), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than `0`). Leave it at `ß` for balanced approach.

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area.

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation.  If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the `HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE` configuration variable.

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface).  Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity.  If the radius is set to `1`, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light.  If the value is `1.4142` (`sqrt(2)`), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a [portal light|/solaris/support/portallights].

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe].

parameters.label: Illuminate Background Holdout
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: If a light exists to add new light source instead of trying to replicate lighting in the live action plate, enable this parameter so that its effect on background holdout geometry shows up in indirect bounces and its contribution to shadow holdout AOVs is omitted.

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.

parameters.label: Contributes to Caustics
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Default is true. Note that Karma only renders caustics if they are enabled on _both the light and the object_. This option has no effect unless you also turn on __Enable Caustics__ on the geometry object.

parameters.label: Flip Rectangle Light Texture
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Specifies how the texture applied to a rectangle light is flipped. Default is FlipX to match the USD specification. Only supported on rectangle light type. Options are None, FlipX, FlipY, and FlipXY. <!---

parameters.label: Attenuation Type
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Controls the type of attenuation on the light source in the default light shader. This may be

parameters.label: Attenuation Start
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Minimum light distance to be used for attenuation.

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: The distance from the light at which __Half Distance Attenuation__ produces half the light intensity. --->

parameters.label: Spread
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Ranges between `0` to `1` and controls beam direction along the light's normal. A value of `1` results in diffuse emission, and a value close to `0` gives parallel beams of light similar to directional light. Note that the __Spread__ option is only supported for area lights with __Type__ set to __Rectangle__ or __Disk__. In conjunction with __Disk__ lights you can, for example, create focused laser beams by leaving __Spread__ at `0`.

entries.title: Geometry Sequence
entries.summary: Imports a sequence of geometry files into LOPs as animated geometry.

parameters.label: Geometry File
parameters.description: A [filename expression|/network/expressions] matching the geometry files to load, for example `dinosaur_$F4.bgeo`.

parameters.label: Reload Geometry
parameters.description: Click this button to reload the contents of the file(s). This will also clear any cached data for packed disk primitives. See the [Cmd:geocache] command.

parameters.label: Missing Frame
parameters.description: How to deal with a missing file/number in the frame sequence. The default is for the node to error. If you choose __No Geometry__ instead, the animated geometry will be empty during the missing frames.

parameters.label: Cache Frames
parameters.description: The total number of frames to cache in memory. The cache is keyed by filename, not time, so if the __Geometry File__ expression somehow generates the same filename for multiple frames, they will overwrite each others' cached geometry. Setting this to `1` is almost the same as the default behavior of the [File SOP|Node:sop/file]. However, this node loads new geometry before flushing current geometry from the cache. This avoids possibly flushing shared agent shape caches when loading agent primitives.

parameters.label: Pre-fetch Geometry
parameters.description: Attempts to predict the next needed frame and loads it in the background. This may allow computation and file I/O to run concurrently. If you are blending multiple frames, __Cache Frames__ needs to be large enough for the total number of "needed, but currently uncached" (net-new) frames to be loaded each time the node cooks. Otherwise this node's simple predictive model will break down.

parameters.label: Save/Load Retries
parameters.description: If saving or loading the geometry from disk fails due to a disk error, Houdini will usually error the output node immediately. This is desirable for most cases where a failure to save or load means an illegal path, which is not recoverable. However, sometimes files fail to save or load due to network issues. If the number of __Save/Load Retries__ is non-zero, Houdini will re-attempt to save or load this number of times. Each time will be accompanied with an output to the console of the failure to save or load and a five second wait in the hopes that the network will clear up.

parameters.label: Load As Reference
parameters.description: When this is on, the geometry will be imported as a [payload|/solaris/glossary#payloads]. When this is off, the geometry will be imported by sublayering its hierarchy over the existing scene tree (see [sublayers and references|/solaris/glossary#sublayers]).

parameters.label: Sublayer Style
parameters.description: Only available when __Load As Reference__ is off. By default, geometry imported from SOPs is treated like geometry imported from a file on disk: you can only edit it by applying stronger [opinions|/solaris/glossary#compose] on top. Changing this parameter, allows this node to put the geometry in the _active layer_, so it can be modified by LOP nodes connected to this node's output. The node does this by copying the contents generated from the SOP geometry into an anonymous in-memory USD layer. This is slower, but provides more options for how many USD layers you need to write to disk, and what goes in each layer. This is similar to the operation of a [Load Layer for Editing LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer]. * The __Copy SOP Layer Into New Active Layer__ style creates a new active layer into which the SOP layer contents are copied. * The __Merge SOP Layer Into Existing Active Layer__ style copies the SOP layer contents into the input node's active layer, resulting in no new layers on the stage.

parameters.label: Adjust Transforms for Input Hierarchy
parameters.description: Only available when __Load As Reference__ is off. When this is on (the default), the node automatically compensates for transform problems created if you round-trip geometry from LOPs to SOPs (as packed USD primitives) and then back to LOPs again. If you know you are not round-tripping LOPs -> SOP packed USD primitives -> LOPs, you can turn this off to make importing faster. Packed Primitives in SOPs only have a single transform, representing the full local-to-world transformation of the packed geometry. If you export a USD geometry primitive to SOPs _as a packed USD primitive_, Houdini flattens the full transformation hierarchy under the USD prim into a single transformation matrix. This creates a problem if you then "round-trip" the SOP packed primitive back into LOPs, as the descendants will have their own transforms, which are _also_ now incorporated into the root prim's transform imported from SOPs. This results in an incorrect double-application of the transforms. When this parameter is on (the default), the node examines every transformation imported from SOPs, in the context of the prim's location in the scene graph hierarchy. If the prim (or its ancestors) already exist on the input stage, the node inverts the transformations of the ancestor prims, and applies them as additional local transformations on the prim. This ensures that the final world space location of the prim in LOPS will be the same as it was in SOPs. If __Copy Contents Into Editable Layer__ is on, the node applies these additional transforms directly to the imported primitives, otherwise the node creates a new active layer and puts the transforms in the new layer as overrides.

parameters.label: Reference Primitive
parameters.description: Only available when __Load As Reference__ is on. This node treats the converted geometry like an external USD geometry file. This controls which root-level prim to import from the USD prim hierarchy generated by converting the SOP geometry. You should leave this set to __Reference Automatically Chosen Primitive__.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: In create mode, this parameter specifies a single primitive path. This is the scene graph path where the referenced branch will be attached. If this prim doesn't exist, the node will create it. In edit mode, this parameter is a primitive pattern that will be matched against the existing primitives on the stage connected to this node's first input. You can use [local variables|#locals] to control the reference primitive path.

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.description: Mark the new or modified prims as [instanceable (as in "native instancing")|/solaris/glossary#instancing]. This saves memory if you reference the same branch into multiple places, but makes the descendants of the referenced prim not editable. If this option is off, the prims are not explicitly marked as not instanceable. Instead, the current instanceable value on each prim is left unchanged.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this type.

parameters.label: Enable Import Group
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import Group__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiggroup` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import Group
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: Turn this on and specify a group name (or a space-separated list of [group syntax|/model/groups]) to import. If you turn this on but leave the field blank, it imports all geometry.

parameters.label: Enable Import Group Type
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import Group Type__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiggrouptype` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import Group Type
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: Specifies whether the __Import Group__ is a point or primitive group.

parameters.label: Enable Import Path Prefix
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import Path Prefix__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpathprefix` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import Path Prefix
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: If a prim being imported has an automatically generated name (like `mesh_0`) because it had no path primitive, or if it has a path primitive but the path is relative (does not start with `/`), the node automatically prefixes the name/path fragment with this path. This is a way of keeping "un-pathed" prims organized under a single branch. (See [how to create geometry hierarchy|/solaris/sop_import].) (The default is `/$OS` which puts "un-pathed" prims under a root prim with the name of this node.)

parameters.label: Enable Layer Save Path
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Layer Save Path__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsavepath` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Layer Save Path
parameters.heading: SOP Import
parameters.description: When turned on, sets the `Save Path` metadata for the layer containing the geometry to this file path. When you write out USD using a [USD Render ROP|Node:out/usd], the geometry is saved out to a `.usd` layer file using this file path (after [output processing|/solaris/output#processors]).

parameters.label: Enable Packed USD Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Packed USD Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigusdprims` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Packed USD Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with packed USD primitives in the imported SOP geometry.

parameters.label: Enable Other Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Other Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigotherprims` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Other Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with regular non-packed primitives (points, curves, polygons, spheres, and so on).

parameters.label: Enable Define Only Leaf Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Define Only Leaf Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigdefineonlyleafprims` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Define Only Leaf Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: Author intermediate primitives (for example, any `Xform` prims created for the __Import Path Prefix__) as overrides instead of definitions. This means if they don't match up with underlying prims in lower layers, the leaf prims won't be added to the scene. This is useful if you only want to import the geometry if its ancestors already exist in the scene tree. (Note that all of the data is still imported, it just may not be visible in the scene graph tree or the viewport.)

parameters.label: Enable Packed Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Packed Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpackedprims` detail or primitive attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Packed Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with SOP-native packed primitives.

parameters.label: Enable NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __NURBS Curves__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfignurbscurves` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS curve primitives.

parameters.label: Enable NURBS Surfaces
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __NURBS Surfaces__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfignurbssurfs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: NURBS Surfaces
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS surface primitives.

parameters.label: Enable Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Kind Authoring__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigkindschema` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: How to assign [kinds|/solaris/glossary#kind] to imported prims.

parameters.label: Enable Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Path Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpathattr` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: A (comma or space-separated) list of names of SOP *primitive string attributes* to use to use as prim paths to put the SOP geometry into. The default is `path,name`. See [geometry hierarchy|#import] above. If the list has more than one attribute, the importer checks each attribute for the first non-empty value. If the string value a full path, that path is used as the USD scene graph path for that primitive. If the string is a relative path (or just a name), the string is appended to the __Import Path Prefix__ string to generate a full scene graph path. If none of the listed attributes exist on a given SOP primitive, or all values are an empty string, the importer generates a name automatically (for example, `sphere_0`).

parameters.label: Enable Import HeightFields as Mesh
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import HeightFields as Mesh__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigheightfieldconvert` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import HeightFields as Mesh
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: If the source SOP geometry contains a height field volume, it will be imported as polygonal mesh. Other layers will be imported as vertex primvar if the values are varying, or constant primvar if the values are constant.

parameters.label: Enable Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.label_norm: enable treat polygons as subdivision surfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpolygonsassubd` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: For polygon meshes that are not already tagged with a subdivision scheme, author a `subdivisionScheme` attribute set to `catmullClark`. This will convert them to subdivision surfaces.

parameters.label: Enable Subdivision Group
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subdivision Group__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsubdgroup` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subdivision Group
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: If __Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces__ is on, only convert polygons in this primitive [group|/model/groups] into subdivision surfaces.

parameters.label: Enable Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigreversepolygons` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD supports an `orientation` attribute on mesh primitives that indicates whether polygons have a left-handed or right-handed ordering, while SOP geometry is always left-handed ordering. When this option is on, the importer always reorders vertices (and associated primvars) to be right-handed. This is useful when round tripping right-handed oriented polygons from USD into SOPs and back into USD. The data is always converted to a left handed ordering when importing it into SOPs. If you imported the polygons back into USD without this option, they would be left-handed, unlike the original.

parameters.label: Enable Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Missing Widths__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsetmissingwidths` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD has a fallback value of 1.0 for the width of curves and points, which is often far wider/thicker than desired. If the SOP geometry does not explicitly author `width`/`pscale` data, this control can be used instead to explicitly author a USD value.

parameters.label: Author Time Samples
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Whether values imported from SOPs should be authored as default values for the corresponding USD attributes, or as a time sample (at the time in the timeline). (When the USD system is asked for an attribute value, it returns the default if no time samples exist on the attribute. Otherwise it returns a value interpolated from the time sample data.)

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Default Primitive__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsetdefaultprim` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Authors the [default primitive|/solaris/usd#default_prim] metadata for the layer containing the imported geometry, if there is an __Import Path Prefix__. The default primitive is set to the root of the prefix path (for example, `/a` if the prefix path is `/a/b/c`).

parameters.label: Enable Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Topology Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtopology` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Controls whether USD topology attributes should be authored as time sampled or default values.

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars.

parameters.label: Enable Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Indexed Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigindexattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called `primvars:<<name>>`, and an array of indices into those values called `primvars:<<name>>:indices`). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Element Array__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus __Import as Single Value__) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Value__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigscalarconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to __Import as Single Element Array__, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, `vector3f` instead of `vector3f[]`).

parameters.label: Enable Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Boolean Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigboolattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `bool`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 32-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguintattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 64-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguint64attribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint64`.

parameters.label: Enable Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Asset Path Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigassetpathattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `asset`.

parameters.label: Enable Relationship Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Relationship Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigrelationshipattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Relationship Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to [relationships|/solaris/glossary#relationship].

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Default Values__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigstaticattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to always author as default values for USD primvars (never time samples). This is the list of exclusions when __Author Time Samples__ is set to __If Not Specifically Excluded__.

parameters.label: Enable Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subset Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpartitionattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which SOP string or integer attributes represent subsets of the geometry. The importer puts elements with the same value for this attribute into their own geometry subsets. Each attribute's subsets are added to a subset family (named from the original attribute) which indicates that the subsets are related. The subset family's type is set to `partition` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting and that every element of the primitive appears in a subset. If there are elements with empty string values (which are not added to a subset), the family type is instead set to `nonOverlapping` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting but some elements do not appear in a subset. The family's type is authored as an attribute on the parent primitive, for example `subsetFamily:shop_materialpath:familyType`. Subsets can be created from point or primitive partition attributes on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points. The importer will try to set the subset name to the attribute value, but may need to change the name to make it a legal USD primitive name. The importer stores the raw attribute value on the geometry subset prim as Custom Data with the key `partitionValue`.

parameters.label: Enable Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.label_norm: enable prefix subsets with attribute name
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigprefixpartitionsubsets` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When creating subsets from __Subset Attributes__, the subsets are named by combining the attribute name with the partition attribute's value (a string or integer). This avoids name collisions when multiple partition attributes contain the same values, but can be undesirable if precise control of the subset names is required. For string attributes, if this option is turned off, the attribute values are directly used as the subset names.

parameters.label: Enable Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subset Groups__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsubsetgroups` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of group names/patterns specifying SOP [groups|/model/groups]. SOP elements in each group are imported as a geometry subset, named for the group. Subsets can be created from point or primitive groups on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points.

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __USD Custom Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigcustomattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).

parameters.label: Enable Capture Weights
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Capture Weights__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigcaptureweights` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Capture Weights
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Controls how capture weights (represented by the `boneCapture` SOP attribute) are translated. This does not affect agent primitives, which are always translated to UsdSkel.

parameters.label: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.label_norm: enable translate uv attribute to st
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Translate UV Attribute to ST__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtranslateuvtost` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute `uv` into a USD primvar called `primvars:st`. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of `st` is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using `uv` is the common convention.)

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

entries.title: Geometry Subset VOP
entries.summary: Creates USD geometry subsets within geometry prims (similar to groups in SOPs) based on evaluating a VEXpression or VOP network.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: How the VEX program specifies subset contents.

parameters.label: Subset Name
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is __Selection__, this is the name of the subset to create/edit. When __Mode__ is __Partition__, this string (if any) is prefixed to all subset names generated by the VEX program.

parameters.label: Family Name
parameters.description: Specifies the family name for the created geometry subset. In USD, a geometry primitive can have several related subsets. This is indicated by the subset family name. I.e., subsets with the same family name are considered related, and can be validated together for properties such as overlapping membership or coverage of the parent geometry primitive.

parameters.label: Vex Source
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: Where to get the VEX to run. You should usually leave this set to __Myself__ and build a VOP network inside this node, unless you have a good reason to choose one of the other options.

parameters.label: Node Path
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: When __Vex Source__ is __Other Node__, the node path of the node that generates the VEX code.

parameters.label: Script
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: When __Vex Source__ is __Script__, the file path to the compiled `.vex` file.

parameters.label: Vexpression
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: A bit of VEX to evaluate. The path to the current prim is available as `@primpath`. You can read current attribute values using `@<<name>>`. If this is one line, you can omit the `return` keyword and the semicolon at the end. However, if this takes more than one line or involves statements, you must use `return` and end each statement with a semicolon.

parameters.label: Vexpression Returns a String
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: Whether to interpret the result of the VEXpression as a string or integer. Turn this on when __Mode__ is __Partition__, turn it off when __Mode__ is __Selection__.

parameters.label: Re-load VEX Functions
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: When __Vex Source__ is __Script__, click this to force reload all `.vex` files on disk.

parameters.label: Compiler
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: The VEX compiler command to use to compile the VOP network inside this node. You should not change this unless you really have a good reason to do so.

parameters.label: Force Compile
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: Clear the cached VEX code generated from the children VOPs, forcing it to be generated and compiled again. Normally the node should automatically recompile whenever the network changes, but this may be useful when debugging problems.

parameters.label: Evaluation Node Path
parameters.heading: VEX Setup
parameters.description: Certain VEX functions, like `ch()`, evaluate parameters on this node. In some cases you want these functions to be relative to a different node (for example, with nodes inside a digital asset, you often want to evaluate functions relative to the parent asset). This is a relative node path to the node to use as "the current node" in the program.

parameters.label: Autobind by Name
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings
parameters.description: In a VEXpression, automatically create `@` variables corresponding to existing attributes. In a VOP network, automatically bind [Parameter|Node:vop/parameter] or [Bind|Node:vop/bind] nodes to attributes if they have the same name. (Default is on.)

parameters.label: Number of Bindings
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings
parameters.description: The number of USD attributes to bind to VEX variables.

parameters.label: Attribute Type
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings
parameters.description: The USD datatype of the attribute. You should usually leave this set to __Auto__, so the node will use the known type of an existing attribute. If you are going to create the attribute, and node doesn't translate the VEX type into the correct USD type (for example, it becomes `string` but you want a `token`), you can change this to the type you want.

parameters.label: VEX Parameter
parameters.heading: Attribute Bindings
parameters.description: The name of the VEX parameter bound to the attribute.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

entries.title: Graft Branches
entries.summary: Takes prims/branches from the second input and attaches them onto branches of the scene graph tree in the first input.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The parent scene graph path of all grafted sub-trees. The __Destination Prim Path__ of each grafted prim is appended to this path. See [Where to attach each subtree|#attach] above.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the parent prim in __Primitive Path__ does not exist, it will be created, and set to be this kind. If the prim already exists, this parameter does nothing.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If this node generates a path where intermediate prims do not exist yet, it will create them. This controls the type of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: This controls the specifier(__Define__/__Over__/__Class__) of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Make Destination Primitive Paths Unique
parameters.description: It is possible to set multiple inputs to have the same destination path. If this parameter is off, the trees are merged. If this is on, the node adds increasing numbers on to the end of each destination path until it is unique.

parameters.label: Treat Destination Paths as Parents
parameters.description: Controls whether source prims will be copied as children of the specified destination prim (on), or copied directly into the destination prim (off).

parameters.label: Frame Offset Mode
parameters.description: Controls how/whether to edit time samples on the grafted prims. (To not edit time samples, set this to __Offset__ and __Frame Offset__ to `0`.) Note that this parameter edits the time samples in terms of *frames*, not seconds.

parameters.label: Frame Offset
parameters.description: When __Frame Offset Mode__ is __Offset__ or __Match and Offset__, the number of frames (positive or negative) to offset the grafted time samples. Note that this parameter edits the time samples in terms of *frames*, not seconds.

parameters.label: Number of Source Prims
parameters.description: How many prims to graft.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Source Prim
parameters.description: Whether the node applies this graft in the output.

parameters.label: Source Prim Path
parameters.heading: Source Prim
parameters.description: The path to the prim to grab from the second input.

parameters.label: Destination Prim Path
parameters.heading: Source Prim
parameters.description: Where to put the grafted prim in the scene graph tree of the first input. This path is added on to the path in the __Primitive Path__ parameter.

parameters.label: Keep Position
parameters.heading: Source Prim
parameters.description: Keep the worldspace position of the prim(s) being grafted. This may be useful if the source and destination hierarchies have different transformation stacks.

parameters.label: Keep Material
parameters.heading: Source Prim
parameters.description: Keep the material assignment for the prim(s) being grafted. This may be useful if the source prim's material assignment comes from a parent but it is being grafted under a different parent that has a different material assignment.

entries.title: Graft Stages
entries.summary: Takes scene graph trees from other inputs and attaches them onto branches of the scene graph tree in the first input.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.description: The parent scene graph path of all grafted sub-trees. The destination path of each subtree is appended to this path. See [Where to attach each subtree|#attach] above.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.description: If the parent prim in __Primitive Path__ does not exist, it will be created, and set to be this kind. If the prim already exists, this parameter does nothing.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.description: If this node generates a path where intermediate prims do not exist yet, it will create them. This controls the type of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.description: This controls the specifier(__Define__/__Over__/__Class__) of any intermediate prims this node creates.

parameters.label: Make Destination Primitive Paths Unique
parameters.description: It is possible to set multiple inputs to have the same destination path. If this parameter is off, the trees are merged. If this is on, the node adds increasing numbers on to the end of each destination path until it is unique.

parameters.label: Destination Path Default
parameters.description: You can set the destination path (which is then appended to the __Primitive Path__) for each wire into the multi-input by clicking in the table below this node's parameters. If you don't give an input a custom destination path, the node evaluates this expression to compute destination path. The default is the name of the node connected into the multi-input. In the expression you can use the `@input` local variable (`$IIDX` is deprecated) as the index of the current input (numbered from left to right starting at 0).

entries.title: HDA Dynamic Payload
entries.summary: Cooks a OBJ or SOP asset on disk and imports the animated geometry output as a USD payload.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: In create mode, this parameter specifies a single primitive path. This is the scene graph path where the referenced branch will be attached. If this prim doesn't exist, the node will create it. In edit mode, this parameter is a primitive pattern that will be matched against the existing primitives on the stage connected to this node's first input. You can use [local variables|#locals] to control the reference primitive path.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will set it to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind]. Setting this parameter to `Auto` will not author a Kind on the leaf primitive where the reference is added. Instead, it will examine the Kind of the prim after setting the reference, and automatically set the Kind of ancestor prims to ensure the leaf primitive is part of a valid model hierarchy. Note that this may result in adding a Kind to ancestor prims that were not created by this node. If the referenced prim has no kind, or is not a model kind, `Auto` mode will not author Kind on any prim.

parameters.label: Primitive Purpose
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: Set the primitive's purpose. Purposes are a way to control what gets rendered. The viewer/renderer only shows primitives tagged with one of a specified set of purposes. If you set up purposes on your primitives, then you can control visibility of all primitives with the same purpose at render time by setting what purposes are visible in the render settings.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: If the prim at __Primitive Path__ doesn't exist, this node will create it. If it has to create the prim, it will give any intermediate prims it has to create this type.

parameters.label: Make Instanceable
parameters.heading: Destination Primitive
parameters.description: Mark the new or modified prims as [instanceable (as in "native instancing")|/solaris/glossary#instancing]. This saves memory if you reference the same branch into multiple places, but makes the descendants of the referenced prim not editable. If this option is off, the prims are not explicitly marked as not instanceable. Instead, the current instanceable value on each prim is left unchanged.

parameters.label: HDA File
parameters.heading: HDA
parameters.description: The file path of the digital asset file to load.

parameters.label: Operator Type
parameters.heading: HDA
parameters.description: If the library file in __HDA File__ contains more than one asset, this controls which asset to load and cook. If this is blank, the node just uses the first asset in the file.

parameters.label: Reload
parameters.heading: HDA
parameters.description: Click the reload the asset definition from disk. You should do this if you overwrite the `.hda` file with a new definition of the asset.

parameters.label: Other Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with regular non-packed primitives (points, curves, polygons, spheres, and so on).

parameters.label: Define Only Leaf Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: Author intermediate primitives (for example, any `Xform` prims created for the __Import Path Prefix__) as overrides instead of definitions. This means if they don't match up with underlying prims in lower layers, the leaf prims won't be added to the scene. This is useful if you only want to import the geometry if its ancestors already exist in the scene tree. (Note that all of the data is still imported, it just may not be visible in the scene graph tree or the viewport.)

parameters.label: Packed Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with SOP-native packed primitives.

parameters.label: NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS curve primitives.

parameters.label: Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: How to assign [kinds|/solaris/glossary#kind] to imported prims.

parameters.label: Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: A (comma or space-separated) list of names of SOP *primitive string attributes* to use to use as prim paths to put the SOP geometry into. The default is `path,name`. See [geometry hierarchy|#import] above. If the list has more than one attribute, the importer checks each attribute for the first non-empty value. If the string value a full path, that path is used as the USD scene graph path for that primitive. If the string is a relative path (or just a name), the string is appended to the __Import Path Prefix__ string to generate a full scene graph path. If none of the listed attributes exist on a given SOP primitive, or all values are an empty string, the importer generates a name automatically (for example, `sphere_0`).

parameters.label: Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD supports an `orientation` attribute on mesh primitives that indicates whether polygons have a left-handed or right-handed ordering, while SOP geometry is always left-handed ordering. When this option is on, the importer always reorders vertices (and associated primvars) to be right-handed. This is useful when round tripping right-handed oriented polygons from USD into SOPs and back into USD. The data is always converted to a left handed ordering when importing it into SOPs. If you imported the polygons back into USD without this option, they would be left-handed, unlike the original.

parameters.label: Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Controls whether USD topology attributes should be authored as time sampled or default values.

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars.

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called `primvars:<<name>>`, and an array of indices into those values called `primvars:<<name>>:indices`). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus __Import as Single Value__) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to __Import as Single Element Array__, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, `vector3f` instead of `vector3f[]`).

parameters.label: Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to always author as default values for USD primvars (never time samples). This is the list of exclusions when __Author Time Samples__ is set to __If Not Specifically Excluded__.

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute `uv` into a USD primvar called `primvars:st`. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of `st` is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using `uv` is the common convention.)

parameters.label: Caching Mode
parameters.heading: Time Sample Caching
parameters.description: How to cache time samples of animated geometry. Loading a time sample for the first time can be slow, but subsequent loads are faster when the time sample is cached.

parameters.label: Time Start/End/Interval
parameters.heading: Time Sample Caching
parameters.description: When __Caching Mode__ is __Range__, the start frame, end frame, and interval to cache.

parameters.label: Keep Houdini Engine Open
parameters.heading: Houdini Engine Options
parameters.description: Turn this on while you're tweaking the geometry parameters and checking the output in the viewer, for faster interaction. Once you've settled on the parameters you want to cook with, you can turn this off, so the node only runs Houdini Engine when needed.

parameters.label: Generate Parameters
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: After you choose an asset to import (__HDA File__ on the __Payload__ tab), click this button to duplicate the imported asset's parameter interface on this tab. You can then use this tab to control what parameter settings to cook the asset with.

entries.title: Hermite Curves
entries.summary: Creates or edits a hermite curves shape primitive.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in __Primitive Paths__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type. ~~~

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets a "default" color for this shape, which will be used in the viewport if the prim does not have a shader/material. You can write shaders to take this `displayColor` parameter as an override.

parameters.label: Opacity
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Sets the opacity of the display __Color__. This is a separate attribute (instead of specifying the display color as RGBA) so it can be independently overridden, and also because shaders don't usually accept RGBA parameters.

parameters.label: Double Sided
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: For renderers that distinguish between single-sided and double-sided surfaces, controls whether this prim is double-sided. Making surfaces double-sided is necessary for flat thin surfaces, or open surfaces where the camera can see both the inside and outside of the surface.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.
