entries.title: Houdini Procedural: Crowd
entries.summary: Houdini Crowd Procedural for Solaris.

parameters.label: Procedural Prim
parameters.description: The scene graph path at which to apply the `HoudiniProceduralAPI` [ApiSchema|/solaris/glossary#apischema] to define the procedural. When __Visualize Instances__ is turned on, the materials used for visualization are also authored under this path.

parameters.label: SkelRoot Primitives
parameters.description: A [primitive pattern|/solaris/pattern] specifying the `SkelRoot` instances to apply the procedural to. The default pattern selects all the visible `SkelRoot` instances.

parameters.label: LOD Camera
parameters.description: When turned on, specifies a camera to use instead of the render camera for evaluating LOD. This can be used to produce consistent results when the viewing camera is moving.

parameters.label: LOD Threshold
parameters.description: The threshold at which the LOD optimization is used. The default value of 1.0 means that the optimization is used when the tolerance between the agent poses is less than approximately 1 pixel. Lower values can eliminate deformed geometry differences that might still be noticeable, depending on the scene. However, the lower levels could make it less likely for the LOD optimization to trigger, and may also increase the render's memory footprint.

parameters.label: Optimize Identical Poses
parameters.description: When turned on, allows foreground agents with exactly the same pose as another agent to be instanced. In most scenarios, it is rare for agents to have identical poses (for example, due to randomizing clip speeds or time offsets), so this is turned off by default to avoid unnecessary computation.

parameters.label: Offscreen Quality
parameters.description: Scales the approximate size of the agent in screen space for agents that are not directly visible to the camera. Smaller values will make offscreen agents more likely to become an instance of another agent.

parameters.label: Bake Skinning for Prototype Agents
parameters.description: When turned on, deformed geometry is generated for the __SkelRoot Primitives__ that became prototypes for background agents. This geometry is instanced by the matching background agents as well as the prototype's original source agent. When turned off, the procedural only authors overrides for the `skel:animationSource` relationship to bind background agents to the same `SkelAnimation` primitive (skeleton pose) as their prototype agent. This produces the same final result, rendering background agents as instances of the prototype's deformed geometry, but is only supported in Hydra 2 and will not work if the `USDIMAGINGGL_ENGINE_ENABLE_SCENE_INDEX` environment variable is set to `0`. This method can be more efficient since the procedural authors a smaller set of changes to the stage, and the deformed point positions are generated through Hydra at render time in the usual manner.

parameters.label: Bake Skinning for All Agents
parameters.description: When turned on, deformed geometry is also generated for the remaining __SkelRoot Primitives__ that did not become an instance or prototype. This can be useful if the deformed geometry is required for subsequent procedurals. Otherwise, the deformed point positions for these agents will be generated through Hydra at render time.

parameters.label: Visualize Instances
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances
parameters.description: When turned on, applies materials to the __SkelRoot Primitives__ to visualize the changes made by the procedural.

parameters.label: Prototype Color
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances
parameters.description: When __Visualize Instances__ is turned on, this is the color of the __SkelRoot Primitives__ whose deformed geometry was used as a prototype for background primitives.

parameters.label: Instance Color
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances
parameters.description: When __Visualize Instances__ is turned on, this is the color of the background __SkelRoot Primitives__ that became an instance of another primitive's deformed geometry.

parameters.label: Default Color
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances
parameters.description: When __Visualize Instances__ is turned on, this is the color of the __SkelRoot Primitives__ that were not modified by the procedural.

parameters.label: Enable Visualization
parameters.heading: Visualize Instances
parameters.description: Controls when the visualization materials are applied to the __SkelRoot Primitives__.

entries.title: Houdini Procedural: Hair
entries.summary: Houdini Procedural: Haie for Solaris.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: Which mode of hair procedural to setup. __Generate__ will produce new curves, interpolated from existing guides. __Deform__ deforms existing render curves, using the guides.

parameters.label: Procedural Prim
parameters.description: Path of the render primitive. This prim must be directly editable on the stage.

parameters.label: Deformed Curves
parameters.description: BasisCurves primitives which are deformed by the __Guide Curves__.

parameters.label: Guide Curves
parameters.description: `BasisCurves` primitives used by the procedural to generate or deform hair.

parameters.label: Skin Prims
parameters.description: Mesh primitives used by the procedural to generate or deform hair.

parameters.label: Animated Procedural
parameters.description: Identify this procedural to be evaluated before each frame in the render, or only at the beginning of a render. If a procedural doesn't need to be re-generated on every frame of the render, you can turn this off as an optimization step. == Generation == (generation)

parameters.label: Number of Hairs
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: Total number of hairs to generate on the skin surface.

parameters.label: Scale by Density Attrib on Skin
parameters.label_norm: scale by density attrib on skin
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: If the character's skin has a `density` attribute, you can use it to drive the scale of the hair.

parameters.label: Relax Iterations
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: Number of iterations to relax the hair roots onto the skin.

parameters.label: Length Min Scale
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: Minimum scale to randomize the length interpolated from the guide curves.

parameters.label: Length Max Scale
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: Maximum scale to randomize the length interpolated from the guide curves.

parameters.label: Width Scale
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: Multiplier on the `pscale` copied from the __Guide Curves__.

parameters.label: Resample Segments
parameters.heading: Hair
parameters.description: Set the number of segments on the render curves.

parameters.label: Attributes to Copy
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: Which attributes to copy from the guide curves onto the render curves.

parameters.label: Influence Radius
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: The radius within which guides have influence over generated hair. See [Hair Generate SOP|Node:sop/hairgen#influenceradius] for more details.

parameters.label: Influence Decay
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: Controls how steeply the weight of a guide drops with distance. See [Hair Generate SOP|Node:sop/hairgen#influencedecay] for more details.

parameters.label: Max Guide Count
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: The maximum number of guides to take into account. Any exceeding guides found within the __Influence Radius__ are ignored. See [Hair Generate SOP|Node:sop/hairgen#maxguidecount] for more details.

parameters.label: Max Guide Angle
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: Ignore guides that face away from the skin normal at the hair root by more than this angle in degrees. See [Hair Generate SOP|Node:sop/hairgen#maxguideangle] for more details.

parameters.label: Clump Crossover
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: Blends the shapes of clumps of guide hair. See [Hair Generate SOP|Node:sop/hairgen#clumpcrossover] for more details.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: Seed to randomize the distribution of hair curves. == Deform == (deform)

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: This tab and its associated parameter set is only visible when you set __Mode__ to __Deform__.

parameters.label: Deform Mode
parameters.heading: Guides
parameters.description: Method used to deform the hair. * __Skin__ will deform the hair using the skin only. * __Capture and Deform__ will use the specified skin and guide curves to capture and deform the hair. * __Deform - Use Existing Weights__ deforms the hair using capture attributes authored on the render curves using the guides.

parameters.label: Split Clumps
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform
parameters.description: For curves that are influences by the guides of multiple clumps, discards any weights that are not part of the most influential clump.

parameters.label: Pick Single Best Guide
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform
parameters.description: Discards all but the single most influential guide. This can significantly speed up deformation and can be useful for outputting quick tests. Results can potentially be good enough for the final output when the guide density is very high relative to the final hair density.

parameters.label: Maximum Split Passes
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform
parameters.description: Polygons of the skin surface are split at guide locations, adding the root point into the surface topology. For polygons containing multiple guides, this is done a guide at a time, until all guides have a point on the surface or until this maximum number of passes is reached.

parameters.label: Edge Flip Passes
parameters.heading: Capture and Deform
parameters.description: Edges are flipped to create a more uniformly distributed triangle surface, which results in smoother weights. This is a maximum number of passes to perform.

parameters.label: Max Sample Count
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: Maximum number of points to interpolate from.

parameters.label: Distance Threshold
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: The maximum distance that the source guides/skin can be at to be considered.

parameters.label: Blend Width
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: Distance on top of the __Distance Threshold__, blending the velocity from guides/skin. == Primitive Prototypes == (prims)

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to  __Generate__, you can control the type of `BasisCurve`. __Linear__ is polygonal, and __Cubic__ is smoothed, depending on the selected __Basis__ method. See [BasisCurves LOP|Node:lop/basiscurves#type] for more details.

parameters.label: Basis
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Generate__, you can determine how the curve is drawn between points. See [BasisCurves LOP|Node:lop/basiscurves#basis] for more details.

parameters.label: Wrap
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: When __Mode__ is set to __Generate__, you can tell USD how to treat the ends of the curves. See [BasisCurves LOP|Node:lop/basiscurves#wrap] for more details.

parameters.label: Calculate Rest Positions for Guide Curves
parameters.label_norm: calculate rest positions for guide curves
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: Creates `primvars:rest` for the __Guide Curves__, using the current `@points` positions.

parameters.label: Calculate Rest Positions for Skin Prims
parameters.label_norm: calculate rest positions for skin prims
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: Creates `primvars:rest` for the __Skin Prims__, from the current `@points` positions.

parameters.label: Subframe Samples
parameters.heading: Velocity from Guides or Skin
parameters.description: Specifies the number of time samples to generate when executing the procedural. A value of 2 or more is required for deformation-based motion blur. Higher values will result in longer execution times for the procedural.

parameters.label: Enable Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Enables the controls for setting Karma velocity blur properties on the hair and skin.

parameters.label: Hair Velocity Blur
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Enables Karma velocity blur property on the hair curves.

parameters.label: Skin Velocity Blur
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Enables Karma velocity blur property on the skin meshes.

parameters.label: Velocity Blur Mode
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.description: Lets you choose whether to use velocity-based motion blur, or acceleration-based motion blur. Velocity blur uses the `velocities` and is always linear, but is fast. Acceleration blur uses `accelerations` and lets you get curved motion blur, but requires three or more samples for Karma to generate smooth motion.

parameters.label: Acceleration Samples
parameters.heading: Karma Velocity Blur
parameters.description: The number of interpolation copies that Karma produces internally, using the `accelerations` values, to produce the smooth motion.

parameters.label: Primitive Path

parameters.heading: Spectrum

parameters.heading: Spectrum
parameters.description: An optional animated file sequence of mask geometry that can be used to mask the ocean displacement, often created by the [Particle Fluid Mask SOP|Node:sop/particlefluidmask] SOP and set up by the [Ocean Flat Tank|/shelf/oceanflattank] or [Guided Ocean Layer|/shelf/guidedoceanlayer] shelf tools.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.heading: Spectrum
parameters.description: The time at which the ocean surface should be evaluated.

parameters.label: Reload Geometry
parameters.heading: Spectrum
parameters.description: Force a reload of the __Spectrum File__ geometry, which will refresh any previews of the ocean after a change to the spectrum file on disk,

parameters.label: Render Geometry
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: The path to the geometry that will be diced and displaced by the procedural.

parameters.label: Group
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: The primitive group on the __Render Geometry__ that should be diced and displaced.

parameters.label: Reference Render Geometry as Interior
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: Create a second USD reference to the __Render Geometry__ that will be rendered as the ocean interior, usually using a uniform volume material to give the appearance of depth falloff within the ocean volume.

parameters.label: Viewport Quality
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: The dicing resolution for the procedural when previewing the ocean in the Solaris viewport with a [Preview Houdini Procedurals LOP|Node:lop/houdinipreviewprocedurals].

parameters.label: Dicing Quality
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: The dicing resolution of the procedural. A setting of `1` generally gives full resolution, but can be increased for more detail. If you only require more detail at the horizon, consider increasing __Z Importance__ instead.

parameters.label: Geometry Z Measure
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: The space in which the diced ocean geometry's z-coordinate should be projected before measuring if it meets the __Dicing Quality__ criterion.  The X and Y coordinates are always in pixel space, but the Z coordinate along the camera direction can be in a different space.

parameters.label: Z Importance
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: A scale on the mapping specified in the __Geometry Z Measure__ parameter.  Increasing this value will increase detail at distance along the horizon, generally with lower memory usage than increasing the overall __Dicing Quality__.

parameters.label: Screen Window Size
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: The size of the screen window. Increasing this value will extend the subdivision to the offscreen area, which is especially useful if the resulting geometry might be displaced horizontally into view.

parameters.label: Downsample
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: Downsample the incoming ocean spectra before evaluating any ocean values.  This parameter specifies the number of powers of two to remove from the resolution of the incoming ocean spectrum. For example, if the spectrum was originally specified at resolution `10` to generate a 1024 x 1024 volume, downsampling by `2` will evaluate ocean volumes at resolution `8`, a 256 x 256 volume.

parameters.label: Anti-Alias Blur
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: A scale on the polygon size before measuring against wavelength for anti-aliasing.  Decrease its value to reduce the amount of downsampling done, or set to zero to disable completely.

parameters.label: Verbose
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: Output statistics to the console about ocean dicing, displacement, and foam splatting.

parameters.label: Surface Material
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: The material applied to the surface render geometry.  The default material is a MaterialX shader that will work with many renderers that support MaterialX.

parameters.label: Interior Material
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: The material applied to the interior ocean volume, usually rendered as a uniform volume to emulate depth falloff beneath the surface of the water.  The default material will work with Karma CPU and XPU.

parameters.label: Proxy Material
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: The material used for viewport display of the ocean surface, with some features like refraction disabled.

parameters.label: Point Velocity
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Generate a `velocities` primvar that can be used for shading or motion blur.

parameters.label: Cusp Min/Max
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: When enabled, the procedural will generate a `cusp` primvar that can be used for shading and/or displacement of the procedural surface.  The __Cusp Min/Max__ parameter remaps the specified cusp range to 0-1.

parameters.label: Cusp Gamma
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Applies a gamma curve to the cusp value after remapping according to __Cusp Min/Max__.

parameters.label: Cusp Intensity
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: A multiplier applied to the cusp value after remapping and gamma scaling.

parameters.label: Foam Particles
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: An optional animated file sequence of foam particles that can be used to create a `foam` primvar on the ocean for shading and/or displacement of the procedural surface.

parameters.label: Radius Scale
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern
parameters.description: A scale on the particle radius applied before looking up foam particles around a shading point. Increase this value and decrease __Alpha__ to smooth out the look of the foam.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern
parameters.description: The amount of opacity each particle will contribute. Increase this value for a thicker foam layer.

parameters.label: Filter Width
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern
parameters.description: How much to filter the streak pattern to avoid aliasing artifacts when viewed from a distance.

parameters.label: Foam Min/Max
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern
parameters.description: When enabled, the procedural will generate a `foam` primvar that can be used for shading and/or displacement of the procedural surface.  The __Foam Min/Max__ parameter remaps the specified foam range to 0-1.

parameters.label: Foam Gamma
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern
parameters.description: Applies a gamma curve to the foam value after remapping according to __Foam Min/Max__.

parameters.label: Foam Intensity
parameters.heading: Foam Pattern
parameters.description: A multiplier applied to the foam value after remapping and gamma scaling.

parameters.label: Direction
parameters.heading: Streaks
parameters.description: The direction in which to stretch the __Frequency__ to stretch out the foam in that direction. Setting this to the prevailing wind direction or wind direction plus `90` degrees can give interesting effects.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Streaks
parameters.description: The amount of __Frequency__ stretching to do along the streak __Direction__.

parameters.label: Sharpness
parameters.heading: Streaks
parameters.description: How sharp the edges of the foam are. High values will create a sharper more web-like pattern, low values will create a softer, rounder pattern.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.heading: Streaks
parameters.description: The frequency of the streak pattern.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Streaks
parameters.description: How much to offset the streak pattern.

parameters.label: Frequency
parameters.heading: Bubbles
parameters.description: The frequency of the bubble pattern.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Bubbles
parameters.description: How much to offset the bubble pattern.

parameters.label: Cusp Displacement
parameters.heading: Displacement
parameters.description: The diced ocean surface will be displaced in the normal direction by the output `cusp` primvar scaled by this amount.

parameters.label: Foam Displacement
parameters.heading: Displacement
parameters.description: The diced ocean surface will be displaced in the normal direction by the output `foam` primvar scaled by this parameter.

parameters.label: RenderProducts Primitive Path

This is necessary when rendering animation. See [expressions in file names|/render/expressions] for more information.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: Path to a USD camera (`UsdGeomCamera`) prim to render the scene from.

parameters.label: Resolution Mode
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: Use the USD Camera's aperture aspect ratio to automatically set one dimension of the resolution. The computed parm is set using an expression, but is locked to prevent accidental edits.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: The horizontal and vertical size of the output image, in pixels.

parameters.label: Engine Settings
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: Select the rendering engine.

parameters.label: Primary Samples
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: When __Engine Settings__ is __CPU Parameters__, this is the number of ray-samples sent through each pixel. More samples will result in a less noisy image. Note that __Primary Samples__ and __Pixel Samples__ are the same.

parameters.label: Path Traced Samples
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: When __Engine Settings__ is __XPU Parameters__, this is the number of ray-samples sent through each pixel when using the path-traced convergence mode. More samples will result in a less noisy image.

parameters.label: Simplified Shading
parameters.heading: Render Settings Prim
parameters.description: Disable all shading and lighting (render with one headlight on the camera). This might be useful for preview purposes if a shaded view is too slow to render. <!-- Tabs are taken from karmarendersettings -->

parameters.label: TIP
parameters.heading: Secondary
parameters.description: For an in-depth explanation of primary and secondary samples, please take a look at the [Sampling|/solaris/kug/sampling] page of the Karma User Guide.

parameters.label: Min Secondary Samples
parameters.heading: Secondary
parameters.description: Minimum number of rays to cast in per-component variance anti-aliasing. The value, given here, is multiplied with the settings of the various __Indirect Samples Quality__ parameters for diffuse, reflection, volumes, etc.

parameters.label: Max Secondary Samples
parameters.heading: Secondary
parameters.description: Maximum number of rays to cast in per-component variance anti-aliasing. The value, given here, is multiplied with the settings of the various __Indirect Samples Quality__ parameters for diffuse, reflection, volumes, etc.

parameters.label: Diffuse Quality
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on __Min Secondary Samples__ and __Max Secondary Samples__ for indirect diffuse component.

parameters.label: Reflection Quality
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on __Min Secondary Samples__ and __Max Secondary Samples__ for indirect reflect component.

parameters.label: Refraction Quality
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on __Min Secondary Samples__ and __Max Secondary Samples__ for indirect refract component.

parameters.label: Volume Quality
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on __Min Secondary Samples__ and __Max Secondary Samples__ for indirect volume component.

parameters.label: SSS Quality
parameters.heading: Indirect Samples Quality
parameters.description: This parameter acts as a multiplier on __Min Secondary Samples__ and __Max Secondary Samples__ for the SSS component.

parameters.label: Light Sampling Mode
parameters.heading: Lights Quality
parameters.description: Whether Karma should perform uniform sampling of lights or whether rendering should use the light tree. The light tree can be significantly faster for scenes that have large numbers of lights.

parameters.label: Light Sampling Quality
parameters.heading: Lights Quality
parameters.description: This is a global control to improve sampling quality for all lights. This acts as a multiplier on the individual light quality controls. Increasing the quality will improve direct light sampling as well as shadows/occlusion.

parameters.label: Screendoor Samples
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: The number of transparent samples to be shaded as a ray travels through partially opaque objects. Increasing this value will result in less noise in partially opaque objects and is generally less costly than increasing __Primary Samples__, __Volume Step Rate__, or __Min|Max Secondary Samples__, This parameter will not have any effect on noise from indirect sources however. [Image:/images/render/mug/sampling/VolumeSamplingStochastic.jpg]

parameters.label: Volume Step Rate
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: How finely or coarsely a volume is sampled as a ray travels through it. Volumetric objects are made up of 3-dimensional structures called voxels, the value of this parameter represents the number of voxels a ray will travel through before performing another sample. The default value is `0.25`, which means that every one of every four voxels will be sampled. A value of `1` means that all voxels are sampled and a value of `2` means that all voxels are sampled twice. This means that the volume step rate value behaves in a similar way to pixel samples, acting as a multiplier on the total number of samples for volumetric objects. Keep in mind that increasing the volume step rate can dramatically increase render times, so it should only be adjusted when necessary. Also, while increasing the default from `0.25` can reduce volumetric noise, increasing the value beyond `1` will rarely see similar results. [Image:/images/render/mug/sampling_tab/VolumeQuality.jpg] === Limits === (limits_tab)

parameters.label: Diffuse Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: Defines, how often diffuse rays can propagate through your scene. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/DiffuseLimit.jpg] Unlike __Reflect Limit__ and __Refract Limit__, this parameter will increase the overall amount of light in your scene and contribute to the majority of global illumination. With this parameter set to values greater than `0`, diffuse surfaces will accumulate light from other objects in addition to direct light sources. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/DiffuseLimitCompare.jpg] In this example, increasing the __Diffuse Limit__ has a dramatic effect on the appearance of the final image. To replicate realistic lighting conditions, it is often necessary to increase the __Diffuse Limit__. However, since the amount of light contribution usually decreases with each diffuse bounce, increasing the __Diffuse Limit__ beyond `4` hardly improves the visual fidelity of a scene. Additionally, increasing the __Diffuse Limit__ can dramatically increase noise levels and render times. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/DiffuseSubtleCompare.jpg]

parameters.label: Reflection Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: The number of times a ray can be reflected in your scene. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/ReflectLimit.jpg] This example shows a classic "Hall of Mirrors" scenario with the subject placed between two mirrors. This effectively creates an infinite series of reflections. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/ReflectLimitCompare.jpg] From this camera angle the reflection limits are very obvious and have a large impact on the accuracy of the final image. However, in most cases the reflection limit will be more subtle, allowing you to reduce the number of reflections in your scene and optimize the time it takes to render them. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/ReflectSubtleCompare.jpg] Remember that the first time a light source is reflected in an object, it is considered a direct reflection. Therefore, even with __Reflect Limit__ set to `0`, you will still see specular reflections of light sources.

parameters.label: Refraction Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: This parameter control the number of times a ray be refracted in your scene. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/RefractLimit.jpg] This example shows a simple scene with ten grids all in a row. By applying a refractive shader, we will be able see through the grids to an image of a sunset in the background. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/RefractLimitCompare.jpg] From this camera angle, in order for the image to be accurate, the refraction limit must match the number of grids that that are in the scene. However, most scenes will not have this number of refractive objects all in a row and so it is possible to reduce the refract limit without affecting the final image while also reducing the time it takes to render them. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/RefractSubtleCompare.jpg] Keep in mind that this __Refract Limit__ refers to the number of surfaces that the ray must travel through, not the number of objects. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/RefractLimitSurfaces.jpg] Remember that the first time a light source is refracted through a surface, it is considered a direct refraction. Therefore, even with __Refract Limit__ set to `0`, you will see refraction of light sources. However, since most objects in your scene will have at least two surfaces between it and the light source, direct refraction is often not evident in your final render.

parameters.label: Volume Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: The number of times a volumetric ray can propagate through a scene. It functions in a similar fashion to the __Diffuse Limit__ parameter. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/VolumeLimit.jpg] Increasing the __Volume Limit__ parameter will result in much more realistic volumetric effects. This is especially noticeable in situations where only part of a volume is receiving direct lighting. Also, in order for a volumetric object to receive indirect light from other objects, the __Volume Limit__ parameter must be set above `0`. [Image:/images/render/mug/limits_tab/VolumeLimitCompare.jpg] With the __Volume Limit__ set to values greater than `0`, the fog volume takes on the characteristic light scattering you would expect from light traveling through a volume. However, as with the __Diffuse Limit__, the light contribution generally decreases with each bounced ray and therefore using values above `4` does not necessarily result in a noticeably more realistic image. Also, increasing the value of this parameter can dramatically increase the amount of time spent rendering volumetric images.

parameters.label: SSS Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: The number of times a SSS ray can propagate through a scene. It functions in a similar fashion to the __Diffuse Limit__ parameter.

parameters.label: Color Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: The maximum value a shading sample is allowed to contribute to an LPE image plane to reduce appearance of "fireflies" caused by undersampling of extremely bright light sources. Note that reducing this value can result in an overall reduction in the amount of light in your scene.

parameters.label: Shared Color Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: When turned on, indirect bounces use the __Color Limit__ value and the __Indirect Color Limit__ parameter is ignored.

parameters.label: Indirect Color Limit
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: Color limit applied to indirect bounce only. Note that this parameter is ignored unless __Shared Color Limit__ is turned off.

parameters.label: Russian Roulette Cutoff Depth
parameters.heading: Volumes and Opacity
parameters.description: Depth at which indirect rays start to get stochastically pruned based on ray throughput.

parameters.label: Enable Depth of Field
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: Turn on the depth of field rendering. ~~~

parameters.label: Enable Motion Blur
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: Whether to turn on motion blur. Changing this in the display options will require a restart of the render.

parameters.label: Per-Object Motion Blur
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: Whether motion blur should be on or off for objects that don't explicitly have an opinion. If this is __On by Default__, the parameters below let you set the defaults.

parameters.label: Velocity Blur
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: This parameter lets you choose what type of _geometry velocity blur_ to do on an object, if any. Separate from _transform blur_ and _deformation blur_, you can render motion blur based on point movement, using attributes stored on the points that record change over time. You should use this type of blur if the number points in the geometry changes over time (for example, a particle simulation where points are born and die). If your geometry changes topology frame-to-frame, Karma will not be able to interpolate the geometry to correctly calculate Motion Blur. In these cases, motion blur can use a `velocities` and/or `accelerations` attribute which is consistent even while the underlying geometry is changing. The surface of a fluid simulation is a good example of this. In this case, and other types of simulation data, the solvers will automatically create the velocity attribute.

parameters.label: Motion Samples From Stage
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: For motion blur, karma gets the motion samples from the data authored on the stage.  Ideally, motion data should be authored at the shutter open and close times at a minimum.  For higher quality interpolation, additional samples can be specified between the shutter open and close times. Rather than having to specify the number of samples that karma should use, karma is able to find out how many motion samples are available and use those samples for motion blur.  If you specify the samples manually, Karma will interpolate the samples on the stage which may result in more (or sometimes less if undersampling) rendering memory, and can result in approximated motion. Please see the Karma User Guide for more detailed information.

parameters.label: Geometry Time Samples
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: The number of sub-frame samples to compute when rendering _deformation_ motion blur over the shutter open time. The default is 1 (sample only at the start of the shutter time), giving *no* deformation blur by default. If you want rapidly deforming geometry to blur properly, you must increase this value to 2 or more. Note that this value is limited by the number of sub-samples available in the USD file being rendered.  An exception to this is the `USDSkel` deformer. "Deformation" may refer to simple transformations at the geometry (SOP) level, or actual surface deformation, such as a character or object which changes shape rapidly over the course of a frame. [Image:/images/render/mug/blur/GeoTimeSamplesSimple.jpg] Objects whose deformations are quite complex within a single frame will require a higher number of Geo Time Samples.

parameters.label: Transform Time Samples
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: The number of samples to compute when rendering _transformation_ motion blur over the shutter open time.  The default is 2 samples (at the start and end of the shutter time), giving one blurred segment.

parameters.label: Motion Blur Style
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: Defines the type of motion blur. The default __Rotation Blur__ is suited for most applications, esp. spinning wheels or rotor blades, but also almost any other type of motion. __Linear Blur__ is only required in very rare cases.

parameters.label: Instance Velocity Blur
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: When defining motion blur on instances, the transform of each instance can be blurred in addition to any motion blur occurring on the prototype.  This option controls how the instance will compute the motion blur of the transform on each instance.  For example, when instancing prototypes to a particle system, you'd likely want to use velocity blur to compute motion blur (the transform on the prototype would be blurred by the velocity on the particles).

parameters.label: Instance Motion Samples
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: When motion blur on instances is computed using __Acceleration Blur__ or __Deformation Blur__, this parameter specifies the number of motion segments used for motion blur.

parameters.label: Volume Velocity Blur Scale
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: Velocity multiplier used to reduce or exaggerate amount of motion blur on volumes.

parameters.label: Instance Velocity Lattice Quality
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: Controls the resolution of the lattice super structure that is used for volume motion blur. Values closer to 1 result in a structure with velocities closer to the original velocity data but higher render time.

parameters.label: Enable Image Blur
parameters.heading: Camera Effects
parameters.description: If you turn this off, Karma still calculates velocities or motion vectors (and the velocities can be stored in an AOV), but it sends all camera rays at shutter open, so the image will not have any apparent motion blur. This may be useful if you simply don't want any motion blur to create a certain visual effect.

parameters.label: Disable Scene Materials (husk)
parameters.heading: Lighting Effects
parameters.description: When rendering in `husk`, disable scene materials.  You can also use the `husk` command line option `--disable-scene-materials`.

parameters.label: Disable Scene Lights (husk)
parameters.heading: Lighting Effects
parameters.description: When rendering in `husk`, disable all scene lights.  Emissive objects will still emit light. You can also use the `husk` command line option `--disable-scene-lights`.

parameters.label: Displacement Style
parameters.heading: Lighting Effects
parameters.description: This option sets the default displacement behavior for all objects in the scene.  It's possible that objects will override this setting.

parameters.label: Render Points as
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading
parameters.description: When rendering point clouds, they can be rendered as camera oriented discs, spheres or discs oriented to the normal attribute.

parameters.label: Render Curves as
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading
parameters.description: When rendering curves, they can be rendered as ribbons oriented to face the camera, rounded tubes or ribbons oriented to the normal attribute attached to the points. When choosing __USD Default Behaviour__, the curves will be rendered as oriented ribons if there's a normal attribute or rounded tubes if there's no attribute.

parameters.label: Override Curve Basis
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading
parameters.description: USD supports __Curve Basis__ types that may not be supported directly in Houdini.  In some cases, you may want to override the Houdini curve basis. For example, if you have linear curves in Houdini, you may want to render them with a Bezier, B-Spline or Catmull-Rom basis.  This menu will force Karma to override the basis that's tied to the USD primitives. Note that the topology of the curves must match the target basis.  For example, when selecting any cubic curve basis, every curves must have at least 4 vertices.  For the Bezier basis, curves must have `4+3*N` vertices.

parameters.label: Cull Backfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry and Shading
parameters.description: If enabled, geometry that are facing away from the camera are not rendered.

parameters.label: Enable Caustics
parameters.heading: Enable Caustics
parameters.description: Allows evaluation of glossy BSDF that's seen by indirect diffuse bounce. This is a brute-force solution which may require significant number of diffuse rays to resolve, especially if __Caustics Roughness Clamp__ parameter is set to very small value or Indirect Guiding feature is disabled.

parameters.label: Caustics Roughness Clamp
parameters.heading: Enable Caustics
parameters.description: Increasing this value can make caustics less noisy at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Ray Bias
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: The minimum distance used when testing if _secondary rays_ from a surface intersect with other objects in the scene. The distance is measure from surface along the direction of the ray. Objects within the ray bias distance are ignored.

parameters.label: Constrain by Maximum Roughness
parameters.heading: Shading
parameters.description: Roughness parameter in GGX BSDFs are clamped by the maximum roughness value propagated down the ray chain in pathtracing. Enabling this option can cut out a lot of noise in indirect specular (in particular, cases where glossy surface is reflected by a rough specular surface) at the cost of a bit of accuracy.

parameters.label: Dicing Camera
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: Specifies a camera that is used for dicing complicated surfaces.  This can provide consistent dicing of surfaces when the viewing camera is moving.

parameters.label: Offscreen Quality
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: This parameter controls the shading quality scale factor for geometry that is not directly visible to the camera. For geometry that is outside the field of view (i.e. visible only to secondary rays), Karma will smoothly reduce the shading quality based on the angle between the geometry and the edge of the viewing frustum.  Smaller values can increase performance particularly in scenes where the camera is within the displacement bound of nearby geometry, where it permits the hidden primitives to be diced more coarsely than those that are directly visible.

parameters.label: Dicing Quality Scale
parameters.heading: Dicing
parameters.description: This parameter is a global multiplier for dicing quality of all objects.

parameters.label: Enable Outlines
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Turn edge detection on or off.

parameters.label: Apply to Beauty
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Applies lines to the `beauty` pass, otherwise the result will be written to the `outline` AOV only.

parameters.label: Lines Types to AOVs
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Output __outline_contour__, __outline_crease__, __outline_depth__ lines types to separate AOVs.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Global scale for outline thickness. See [Karma:karma:object:outline_radius] for exact definition.

parameters.label: Primary
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Turn edge detection through primary rays on or off.

parameters.label: Primary Samples
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: The initial number of stencil rays to cast for primary edge detection.

parameters.label: Primary Stencils
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: When __Outline Modes__ is __Determined__, this value increases the number of stencil rays by two with each new step-value per primary ray.

parameters.label: Secondary
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Turn edge detection for reflection/refraction rays on or off.

parameters.label: Secondary Samples
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Initial number of stencil rays to cast per reflection/refraction ray.

parameters.label: Secondary Stencils
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: When __Outline Modes__ is __Determined__, this values increases the number of stencil rays by two with each new step-value per reflection/refraction ray.

parameters.label: Depth Threshold Scale
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Global scale for __Depth Threshold__.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Increasing intensity makes outlines appear more opaque.

parameters.label: Fit Min
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Remaps the outlines to fit the adjusted minimum limit.

parameters.label: Fit Max
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Remaps the outlines to fit the adjusted maximum limit.

parameters.label: Used to reduce thickness of lines on distant objects. The parameter blends between the following two modes
parameters.label_norm: used to reduce thickness of lines on distant objects. the parameter blends between the following two modes
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: * `0.0` creates uniform thickness regardless of distance. * `1.0` applies varying thickness based on distance.

parameters.label: Modes
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: You can choose from two modes. The __Random__ method is mainly here for completeness and could give slightly better results with thick lines. * __Determined__ uses a fixed stencil sample pattern that creates a less noisy result. * __Random__ uses a variable stencil sample pattern that results in more noise.

parameters.label: Default Color
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Default color applied to outlines if there is `export_outline_color` AOV provided in the shader.

parameters.label: Debug
parameters.heading: Outlines
parameters.description: Output __id__, __thickness__, __color__ outline data to `export_outline_id`, `export_outline_thickness`, `export_outline_color` AOVs.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: * When using slap comp with `husk`, output AOVs must already exist and the output types in COPs must match the AOVs. Furthermore, the output resolution must be the same as the original resolution. * Unlike in the Solaris viewport, the `depth` AOV isn’t exported by default by ROPs so you must turn it on. Add a [Karma Render Settings LOP|Node:lop/karmarendersettings] and go to __Image Output > AOVs > Utility__ to turn on __Depth (Camera Space)__.

parameters.label: Existing Render Vars
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Select existing `RenderVar` prims on the input stage and add them to the render.

parameters.label: Import Render Vars from Second Input
parameters.label_norm: import render vars from second input
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Finds `RenderVar` prims in this node's second input and adds them to this stage, so they add to the list of render vars to generate. This allows other LOP nodes (such as [Background Plate|Node:lop/backgroundplate]) to "offer" render vars related to that node to be generated.

parameters.label: Import Render Products from Second Input
parameters.label_norm: import render products from second input
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Finds RenderProduct prims in this node's second input and adds them to this stage, so they add to the list of products to generate. This allows other LOP nodes to "offer" products related to that node to be generated.

parameters.label: Pixel Filter
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Controls how individual samples are distributed over the pixel. * __Box Filter__ distributes samples uniformly over the rectangular pixel. * __Gaussian Filter__ distributes samples using a radial Guassian distribution. * __Blackman Filter__ distributes samples using a radial Blackman distribution. * __Blackman-Harris Filter__ distributes samples using a radial Blackman-Harris distribution.

parameters.label: Pixel Filter Scale
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Scales the default size of the pixel filter. Larger values like `2` blur, smaller values like `0.5` or `0.25` sharpen.

parameters.label: Global AOV Material
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Global AOV Material applies its Karma AOV nodes scene-wide, evaluating them at every hit point on every object. Note that only the Karma AOV nodes are used globally, the material's shader is ignored.

parameters.label: Split Render Product by Render Var
parameters.label_norm: split render product by render var
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: Instead of creating a single render product that contains multiple AOVs in a single image, you can create a separate render product for each render var (AOV).  Each render product filename will be suffixed with the AOV name. Note: When rendering to [MPlay|/mplay] through the [USD Render ROP|Node:out/usdrender], this option will generate multiple frames instead of a single image with multiple AOVs.

parameters.label: Camera's Far Clip as Background Value
parameters.label_norm: camera's far clip as background value
parameters.heading: AOVs (Render Vars)
parameters.description: When writing out Depth AOV (`ray:hitPz` source name), fill background value with camera's far clip distance instead of zero.

parameters.label: LPE Tag AOV Limit
parameters.heading: Component Level Output
parameters.description: When splitting AOVs per lights' LPE Tag, specify the maximum number of LPE Tag AOVs beyond which the node will emit a warning.

parameters.label: Omit LPE Tags
parameters.heading: Component Level Output
parameters.description: When splitting AOVs per lights' LPE Tag, specify a space separated list of lights' LPE Tags which will not create new AOVs.

parameters.label: Output Colorspace
parameters.heading: Component Level Output
parameters.description: Specify the [OCIO|/solaris/ocio] color output space for the component.

parameters.label: Lower Case OpenEXR Channel Names
parameters.heading: Component Level Output
parameters.description: Though the OpenEXR standard suggests using upper case names for channel components (i.e. `name.R`, `name.G`, `name.B`), some applications require channel names to be lower-case. This option will lower-case all AOVs channel components (i.e. `name.r`, `name.g`, `name.b`). ~~~

parameters.label: The following checkbox is available next to each common render var (`beauty`, `diffuse`, `reflections`, etc.)
parameters.label_norm: the following checkbox is available next to each common render var (`beauty`, `diffuse`, `reflections`, etc.)
parameters.heading: Component Level Output
parameters.description: <!-- Explain this parameter once here, and allow all the copies of it below to pick up this definition by label (DO NOT give this an ID) -->

parameters.label: Split Per LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Component Level Output
parameters.description: When this is on, the renderer creates additional AOVs specific to each tagged light. To manage LPE Tags for lights, use the [LPE Tag LOP|Node:lop/lpetag]. ~~~

parameters.label: Beauty
parameters.heading: Beauty
parameters.description: Add the beauty output as a `color4f` render var named `C`.

parameters.label: Sample Blending
parameters.heading: Beauty
parameters.description: You can use [Solaris filter syntax|/solaris/support/filters] in this parameter to blend the sample values. The default `["ubox", {}]` simply averages all the sample values within each pixel. <!-- CYCLIC-INCLUDE karmarendersettings#outputcs -->

parameters.label: Beauty Unshadowed

parameters.label: Combined Diffuse
parameters.heading: Diffuse
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `combineddiffuse`, using the LPE `C<RD>.*L`.

parameters.label: Direct Diffuse
parameters.heading: Diffuse
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `directdiffuse`, using the LPE `C<RD>L`.

parameters.label: Indirect Diffuse

parameters.label: Combined Diffuse Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Diffuse
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) unoccluded diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `combineddiffuseunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C<RD>.*[LO]`.

parameters.label: Direct Diffuse Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Diffuse
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) unoccluded diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `directdiffuseunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C<RD>L`.

parameters.label: Indirect Diffuse Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Diffuse
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) unoccluded diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectdiffuseunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C<RD>.+L`.

parameters.label: Combined Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Reflections and Refractions
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) glossy surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `combinedglossyreflection`, using the LPE `C<RG>.*[LO]`.

parameters.label: Direct Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Reflections and Refractions
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) glossy surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `directglossyreflection`, using the LPE `C<RG>L`.

parameters.label: Indirect Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Reflections and Refractions
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) glossy reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectglossyreflection`, using the LPE `C<RG>.+L`.

parameters.label: Glossy Transmission

parameters.label: BSDF Labelled `coat`

parameters.description: Add the coat component as a `color3f` render var named `coat`, using the LPE `C<...'coat'>.*[LO]`.

parameters.label: Combined Emission
parameters.heading: Lights and Emission
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) emission component as a `color3f` render var named `combinedemission`, using the LPE `C.*O`.

parameters.label: Direct Emission
parameters.heading: Lights and Emission
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) emission component as a `color3f` render var named `directemission`, using the LPE `CO`.

parameters.label: Indirect Emission
parameters.heading: Lights and Emission
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) emission component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectemission`, using the LPE `C.+O`.

parameters.label: Visible Lights
parameters.heading: Lights and Emission
parameters.description: Add the visible lights component as a `color3f` render var named `visiblelights`, using the LPE `CL`.

parameters.label: Combined Volume
parameters.heading: Volume
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) volume component as a `color3f` render var named `combinedvolume`, using the LPE `CV.*L`.

parameters.label: Direct Volume
parameters.heading: Volume
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) volume component as a `color3f` render var named `directvolume`, using the LPE `CVL`.

parameters.label: Indirect Volume
parameters.heading: Volume
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) volume component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectvolume`, using the LPE `CV.+L`.

parameters.label: BSDF Labelled `sss`
parameters.heading: SSS
parameters.description: Add the sss component as a `color3f` render var named `sss`, using the LPE `C<...'sss'>.*[LO]`.

parameters.label: Albedo

For MaterialX shaders, the preferred way to create a diffuse albedo AOV is to use the `CDA` [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe].

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
parameters.heading: Ambient Occlusion

parameters.label: P (World Space)

parameters.label: P (Camera Space)
parameters.heading: Utility
parameters.description: Add the camera space position as a `point3f` render var named `P`.

parameters.label: Depth (Camera Space)
parameters.heading: Utility
parameters.description: Add the distance from the camera origin as a `float` render var named `depth`.

parameters.label: Element (Raw ID)
parameters.heading: Utility
parameters.description: Add the element ID as a `float` render var named `element`.

parameters.label: Prim ID
parameters.heading: Utility
parameters.description: Add the primitive identifier as a `float` render var named `primid`.

parameters.label: UV

parameters.label: N (Smooth Normal)

parameters.label: N (Smooth Camera Normal)

parameters.label: N (Smooth Facing Normal)

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Normal)

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Camera Normal)
parameters.heading: Utility
parameters.description: Add the camera space primitive geometric normal as a `normal3f` render var named `Ng_camera`.

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Facing Normal)
parameters.heading: Utility
parameters.description: Add the viewer facing primitive geometric normal as a `normal3f` render var named `Ng_facing`. Backfaces also face towards the viewer.

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Facing Ratio)

parameters.label: Velocity
