parameters.label: Denoiser
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or __No Denoiser__. This utility currently supports [Intel Open Image Denoise|https://openimagedenoise.github.io] (included with Houdini) and the [NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser|https://developer.nvidia.com/optix-denoiser] (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. The NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser only works with NVIDIA cards. It is now included with the NVIDIA driver (version 435 or later). Karma uses a blue noise distribution. This noise type works better with denoisers, because it has randomization only in high frequencies, while some other noise have randomization in all frequencies. When blue noise is blurred, the high frequency noise is removed and leaves the lower frequencies of the image intact.

parameters.label: Use Albedo
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can use albedo to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise.

parameters.label: Use N Input
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can use normals to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise.

parameters.label: AOVS
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Space-separated list of AOVs to run the denoiser on.

parameters.label: Create Separate Denoised AOVs
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: When you turn on this option, Karma will create separate AOVs for the denoised versions of the source AOVs.  Each new AOV will have a `_denoise` suffix.

parameters.label: Use CPU Only
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Some denoising libraries can run on CPU or GPU.  Normally, the denoiser will use the fastest device.  This option will force the denoiser to choose the CPU device.  You can use this option to minimize GPU memory requirements, for example when denoising large images or rendering on GPU-enabled farm machines.

parameters.label: Tone Map
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: The basic idea behind tone mapping is the conversion from HDR real world luminances to LDR display values, i.e. for making images displayable on monitors. Another aspect is to simulate a particular film look. Film material is designed to have a certain "response" to light to enhance contrast and colors, represented as a characteristic curve. A filmic tone mapping curve is subdivided into toe, shoulder and linear sections for an image's dark, bright, and mid tones. Houdini provides several common operators for filmic tone mapping and each operator applies a specific S-shaped tone mapping curve. * __Reinhard__, __Ward__ and __Aces__ don't provide any further parameters to adjust the toe, shoulder and linear sections. * __Hable__, __Hable2__ and __Unreal__, however, have specific parameters for customizing the curve.

parameters.label: Tonemap Curve
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Tone map curves apply to the __Reinhard__, __Unreal__, __Aces__ and __Hable__ operators. The curve is a visual representation of the mathematical model of each operator. You can fine-tune tone mapping through the curve's control points.

parameters.label: AOVs
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Space-separated list of AOVs that will be affected by the chosen __Tone Map__ operator.

parameters.label: Toe
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable__, __Hable2__ and __Unreal__ operators and ranges between `0` and `1`. The default values for __Hable__ and __Hable2__ is `0.5`. For __Unreal__, the default value is `0.55`. The value controls the strength (curvature) of the toe segment in dark areas. Higher values create a darker image, smaller values brighten the dark tones.

parameters.label: Shoulder
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable__, __Hable2__ and __Unreal__ operators and ranges between `0`and `1`. The default values for __Hable__ and __Hable2__ is `0.5`. For __Unreal__, the default value is `0.26`. __Shoulder__ controls to curve's amount of curvature for bright tone values. The value affects where the shoulder curve starts in the graph: a value of `1` means that the shoulder starts exactly where the toe ends.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Unreal__ operator and ranges between `0` and `1`. The default value is `0.88`. Controls the tone mapping curve's steepness, where higher settings (steeper curve) make the image darker and increase contrast; smaller values brighten the image and make it pale.

parameters.label: Linear
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable__ operator and ranges between `0` and `2`. The default value is `0.3`. Tones in the linear section should not (or hardly) change during the tone mapping process and represent the image's original tones. The __Linear__ value describes the distance between toe and shoulder. Higher values mean that the tow and shoulder sections become smaller, while more tones remain unchanged: the overall curve becomes more linear.

parameters.label: Linear Angle
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable__ operator and ranges between `0` and `1`. The default value is `0.1`. Here you control the slope of the linear part of the tone mapping curve.

parameters.label: Toe Length
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable2__ operator and ranges between `0` and `1`.  The default value is `0.5`. A small value creates a short toe section that quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of `0` eliminates the toe, and value of `1` means the toe takes up half the curve. Note that there are two ways to disable the toe: you can either set __Toe Length__ or __Toe__ to `0`.

parameters.label: Shoulder Length
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable2__ operator and ranges between `0` and `1`.  The default value is `0.5`. __Shoulder Length__ describes how many F stops you want to add to the dynamic range of the curve. Here you control the transition point from the linear section to the shoulder section.

parameters.label: Shoulder Angle
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: This parameter applies to the __Hable2__ operator and ranges between `0` and `1`.  The default value is `1`. Here you control how much overshoot you want to add the curve's shoulder.

parameters.label: OCIO
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: [OCIO|/solaris/ocio] image filters can be added to various render vars/image planes.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Enables the OCIO image filter defined below.

parameters.label: Planes
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: The render var names to which the OCIO image filter will be applied.

parameters.label: Output Space
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Specify the OCIO color output space the image filter will apply.

parameters.label: Input Space
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: In most cases this should be left at `data`. There may be some strange case where the source of the AOV is already in a defined color space, in which case you can specify the source space here.

parameters.label: Looks
parameters.heading: Karma Built-in Image Filters
parameters.description: Space-separated list of looks to apply to the finished image. A "look" is a named OCIO color transform, usually intended to achieve an artistic effect. See the OCIO documentation for more information.

parameters.label: Aspect Ratio Conform Policy
parameters.heading: Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: What to do if the aspect ratio of the output image (__Resolution__ width divided by height) doesn't match the aspect ratio of the camera aperture (controlled by attributes on the camera). This allows a standard renderer to do something reasonable when you switch between cameras.

parameters.label: Data Window NDC
parameters.heading: Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: Directs the renderer to only render within this window of the entire output image. You specify the window as `minX, minY, maxX, maxY`, where each number is a normalized value from `0` to `1`. `0, 0` is the bottom left, `1, 1` is the top right, `0.5, 0.5` is the center, and so on. The default is `0, 0, 1, 1` (no cropping). Note that you can use _negative_ values. For example, `-0.1, -0.1, 1.1, 1.1` will give you 10% overscan on each side. There's also an associated dropdown menu with several preadjusted percentage values. You can use this window to temporarily _crop_ the render to a smaller region, for testing purposes. Pixels are only rendered if they are _fully_ inside the window. The normalized coordinates map to the image _after_ any adjustments by the __Aspect ratio conform policy__.

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Aspect Ratio
parameters.description: The aspect ratio (width/height) of image _pixels_ (_not_ the image itself). The default is `1.0`, indicating square pixels.

parameters.label: Custom Metadata
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: Add additional custom metadata that `husk` will save to render products.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: The type of metadata (string, integer, float, or color).

parameters.label: Key
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: The key for the metadata.  This should be a unique name used to identify the metadata.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: The value of the metadata. == Deep Output == (deep_output_tab)

parameters.label: Deep Camera Map
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: Generate a deep camera map image recording depth. Deep camera maps are rendered images, where semi-transparent areas (such as volumes) between the camera and the nearest opaque surface are stored with depth information. Each pixel in the image is represented as a curve describing how the transparency value changes across the depth of the scene. This allows you to composite rendered images and have the semi-transparent areas blend correctly according to their depth.

parameters.label: DCM Filename
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: The filename to save the deep camera map image to (this should be an `.exr` file). Include `$F` in the file name to insert the frame number. This is necessary when rendering animation. See [expressions in file names|/render/expressions] for more information.

parameters.label: DCM Render Vars
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: Space separated list of RenderVar _prim paths_ (_not_ a list of AOV names). These must be the fully qualified path to the RenderVar prim and the render var name. You can use patterns to match multiple prims. The default is `/Render/Products/Vars/*`, which matches all prims in the branch where Houdini usually creates RenderVar prims. You can also leave this field empty to omit all RenderVars and only include alpha and depth planes (like a Deep Shadow Map).

parameters.label: DCM Exclude Holdouts
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: == Advanced == (advanced_tab)

parameters.label: Set as Default Render Settings Prim
parameters.label_norm: set as default render settings prim
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: A layer in USD can define a default render settings primitive for `husk` or other tools to use when rendering. === Sampling === (advanced_sampling_tab)

parameters.label: Convergence Mode
parameters.heading: Metadata
parameters.description: When set to Path Traced, maximum of 1 indirect ray is generated per bounce. When set to __Automatic__, the number of indirect rays is calculated based on initial noise estimate, target noise threshold, and the maximum number of camera rays. Also note that under __Automatic__ mode, number ofsamples for direct lighting is adjusted based on noise estimate as well.

parameters.label: Pixel Oracle
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: When rendering, a Pixel Oracle tells karma which pixels need additional sampling and which pixels are converged. This parameter tells karma which oracle to use.

parameters.label: Minimum Samples
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: The minimum number of camera rays (primary samples) for each pixel.

parameters.label: Planes
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: Space separated list of AOVs used to measure variance (using summed pixel value of the AOVs). Typically only beauty AOV is needed, but when rendering holdout beauty or holdout shadows alongside beauty, you may want to include those AOVs to the list in order to prevent holdouts from getting undersampled.

parameters.label: Variance Threshold
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: The amount of variance that triggers more rays. <!---

parameters.label: Random Seed
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: Variance sampling involves some randomness. You can change this number to get slightly different results.--->

parameters.label: OCIO Transform
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: Whether to apply an OCIO transform to the pixels before measuring variance.

parameters.label: Display
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: When __OCIO Transform__ is __Display View__, the display to transform to before measuring variance.

parameters.label: View
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: When __OCIO Transform__ is __Display View__, the view to transform to before measuring variance.

parameters.label: Color Space
parameters.heading: Primary Samples
parameters.description: When __OCIO Transform__ is __Explicit__, the color space to transform to before measuring variance.

parameters.label: Noise Level
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Noise threshold to determine the number of indirect rays cast for indirect bounce when the __Convergence Mode__ is set to __Automatic__. Decreasing this threshold (for example, to `0.001`) will theoretically send more indirect rays and decrease noise, however the "extra" rays will likely be cancelled out by the __Max Ray Samples__ parameter. The correct way to decrease noise is to increase the __Primary Samples__ rather than changing this threshold. If you are using __Variance Pixel Oracle__, you should set the same value for both threshold parameters. Setting the oracle's threshold lower may make the indirect component reach its threshold sooner and cast fewer indirect rays, but the oracle decides to cast more expensive camera rays because the amount of final noise in the beauty pass is higher than the oracle's threshold.

parameters.label: Enable Indirect Guiding
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: When turned on, Karma does a pre-render to roughly estimate of the light in the scene, and uses that to guide indirect diffuse rays, rather than just relying on the BSDF sampling distribution. This can improve "difficult" lighting (for example, caustics, and mostly indirect lighting), but can make "easy" lighting noisier. Before using this, you can try rendering direct and indirect AOVs to see where the noise is. If the noise is mostly caused by the direct lighting, there's no point in turning on path guiding. === Checkpointing === (checkpointing_tab)

parameters.label: Output Checkpoint Files
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: When this is on, Karma will periodically write out image tile data to a checkpoint file.  If the process is terminated before completing the render, you can resume it by turning on __Resume from Checkpoint__ and restarting.

parameters.label: Checkpoint File
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: When __Output checkpoint files__ is on, the name of the checkpoint file to write to. The default (`$HIP/render/$HIPNAME.$OS.$F4.checkpoint`) puts the checkpoint file inside a `render` directory next to the current scene file, and includes the base name of the current scene file (`$HIPNAME`), this node's name (`$OS`), and the render frame (`$F`) in the filename to help avoid two processes trying to use the same checkpoint file at the same time.

parameters.label: Save Frequency
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: When __Output checkpoint files__ is on, Karma waits this number of seconds between writing out a checkpoint file. The default is `60`.

parameters.label: Resume From Checkpoint
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: If this is on and you start a render and the renderer notices there is a valid checkpoint file, it will try to resume rendering from that checkpoint. If you want to restart the render from the beginning, you can turn this off or just delete the checkpoint file(s). === Buckets and Caching === (buckets_and_caching_tab)

parameters.label: Image Mode
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Determines how the image will be rendered.

parameters.label: Progressive Passes
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: When rendering in bucket mode (see `imagemode`), this is the number of progressive passes over the image to perform before switching to bucket mode.

parameters.label: Bucket Size
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Karma breaks down an image into multiple buckets for rendering. This is the side length (in pixels) of the square bucket. The default is `32`, specifying a 32 pixel x 32 pixel bucket. Threads operate at the bucket level, so it might be useful to lower the bucket size if there are only a few buckets that are particularly expensive. That way the expensive areas can be divided across more threads. For example, if the image is mostly empty, but there's a distant object that fits within single 32 x 32 bucket, then that object will only be rendered using 1 thread. If you switch to a 16 x 16 bucket, then the object might be split across 4 buckets and have 4 threads working on it. Ideally changing the bucket size doesn't change the results, but Karma measures variance across pixels within the current bucket, so if you set it to a low value, for example `4`, Karma only has `4 x 4 = 16` pixels to look at, so Karma will tend to make very poor variance estimates. This can show up as black pixels, where pixel rendering terminated prematurely due to a bad variance estimate.

parameters.label: Cache Limit
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Whether to use a fixed size cache (`karma:global:cachesize`) or whether to use a proportion of physical memory (`karma:global:cacheratio`).

parameters.label: Cache Memory Ratio
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: The proportion of physical memory Karma will use for its unified cache. For example, with the default `vm_cacheratio` of `0.25` and 16 Gb of physical memory, Karma will use 4 Gb for its unified cache. The unified cache stores dynamic, unloadable data used by the render

parameters.label: Cancel Render if Missing Texture is Discovered
parameters.label_norm: cancel render if missing texture is discovered
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Turning on this option will cause Karma to stop the render with an error if it encounters a missing texture map

parameters.label: Cancel Render on No Working GPU Devices
parameters.label_norm: cancel render on no working gpu devices
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: Turning on this option will cause Karma to stop the render with an error if no working GPU devices are discovered. === Component Labels === (component_labels_tab)

parameters.label: Export Componetents
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: A space-separated list of shading component names that will be computed for export. If you have defined new component labels in your materials, these can be added to the list so that they are exported for per-component export planes. If you are not using some components, remove them from the list to improve render efficiency. PBR light exports assume that this list is complete - that is, all components created by shaders are listed. If there are unlisted components, light exports may be missing illumination from these components.

parameters.label: Diffuse Components
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like diffuse bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.

parameters.label: Refract Components
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like refract bounces.  This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.

parameters.label: Volume Components
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like volume bounces.  This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.

parameters.label: SSS Components
parameters.heading: Secondary Samples
parameters.description: A space-separated list of component types that will behave like subsurface scatter bounces.  This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Not categorized component types are assumed to be reflections.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

deprecation.tier: VERIFIED-DOC + VERIFIED-RUNTIME (union, sides recorded separately — never collapsed to one boolean)

entries.title: Karma Sky Atmosphere
entries.summary: Creates or edits a Karma Sky Atmosphere.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.heading: Rayleigh
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Scale__ and creates a Rayleigh scattering coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by pure air.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Rayleigh
parameters.description: Multiplier for Rayleigh __Scatter__.

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.heading: Rayleigh
parameters.description: Controls, how fast the air density falls off with increasing altitude. This parameter is measured in kilometers and multiplied by __Unit Scale__. For example, with the default of `8` km and a __Unit Scale__ of `1000`, air density is 37% at 8000 units above sea level. __Distribution__ uses Nishita's exponential decay model (referred to as "Scale Height" in literature) for calculating air density.

parameters.label: Scatter
parameters.heading: Mie
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Scale__ and creates a Mie scattering coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by aerosols.

parameters.label: Scatter Scale
parameters.heading: Mie
parameters.description: Multiplier for Mie __Scatter__.

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.heading: Mie
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Absorption Scale__ and creates a Mie absorption coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is absorbed by aerosols.

parameters.label: Absorption Scale
parameters.heading: Mie
parameters.description: Multiplier for Mie __Absorption__.

parameters.label: Distribution
parameters.heading: Mie
parameters.description: Controls, how fast the air density falls off with increasing altitude. This parameter is measured in kilometers and multiplied by __Unit Scale__. For example, with the default of `8` km and a __Unit Scale__ of `1000`, air density is 37% at 8000 units above sea level. __Distribution__ uses Nishita's exponential decay model (referred to as "Scale Height" in literature) for calculating air density.

parameters.label: Phase
parameters.heading: Mie
parameters.description: Phase ranges from `-1` to `1` and covers full back scatter to full forward scatter. Scattering represents the atmosphere's anisotropy. Aniostropy means that rays don't propagate evenly in all directions.

parameters.label: Absorption
parameters.heading: Ozone
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Scale__ and creates an ozone absorption coefficient for each color channel representing the amount of light that is scattered by the ozone layer.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Ozone
parameters.description: Multiplier for ozone __Absorption__.

parameters.label: Altitude
parameters.heading: Ozone
parameters.description: The maximum ozone density/absorption is reached at the parameter's value given in kilometers measured from the Earth's surface. The value is multiplied by __Unit Scale__. For example, at an __Altitude__ of `8` km and a __Unit Scale__ of `1000`, the final value will be `8000`.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.heading: Ozone
parameters.description: This value indicates the total height range in kilometers at which ozone absorbs (sun)light. Absorption reaches its maximum at the __Altitude__ parameter's value. Note, that __Width__ is multiplied by __Unit Scale__. For example, when __Width__ is `10` km and __Unit Scale__ is `1000`, the final value will be `10000`.

parameters.label: Ground Albedo
parameters.heading: Ground
parameters.description: The ground reflectivity that affects the sky color (when multiple scattering is turned on), as well as its appearance in primary and bounce rays.

parameters.label: Ground Visibility
parameters.heading: Ground
parameters.description: Controls visibility of the ground depending on different types of rays. For instance, you may not want the ground to be visible in the camera, but still want the sky and indirect bounce rays from underside of clouds (and other geometry) to be affected by the ground color. You can use one of the following expressions

parameters.label: Planet Center
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Unit Scale__ and represents the position where the planetary atmosphere is centered around. __Planet Center__ is measured in kilometers.

parameters.label: Sea Level
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Unit Scale__ and represents the distance from the __Planet Center__ in which the atmosphere starts. __Sea Level__ is measured in kilometers.

parameters.label: Unit Scale
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: Multiplier to every parameter in __Karma Sky Atmosphere__ that represents position or distance.

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to atmospheric volume for use with [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe].

parameters.label: Minimum Stepsize
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Unit Scale__ and represents the minimum distance between samples when marching through atmosphere. Reducing this parameter can help eliminate banding artifacts when modeling a particularly thick atmosphere, but at extra cost.

parameters.label: Maximum Stepsize
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This parameter is multiplied by __Unit Scale__ represents the maximum distance between samples when marching through atmosphere. We recommend leaving __Maximum Stepsize__ at 5 to 10 times the value of __Minimum Stepsize__.

parameters.label: Multi Scatter Limit
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Specifies, how often an atmospheric ray can propagate through the atmosphere.

parameters.label: Internal Color Space
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Scatter and absorption coefficients are interpreted in the [OpenColorIO|/solaris/ocio] color space specified by this parameter, and transformed into `scene_linear` (i.e. working space) when computing transmittance. Leave it empty to apply no transformation. This can help in preserving the look if the lookdev for the atmosphere was done in a different color space than the project's working space (however, due to the nature of RGB rendering, it can never be an exact match).

parameters.label: LUT Resolution
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: X and Y resolution for the transmittance table. The X axis corresponds to the light angle, and the Y axis corresponds to the viewer's altitude. With appropriate settings, there is no need to deviate from the default settings. An exception is if there are huge differences between the __Distribution__ or ozone __Altitude__ parameters. In this case it can help to increase the Y resolution to avoid bias.

parameters.label: Ground Offset
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Distance between ground level and sea level. Ground is modeled as a sphere with radius calculated as `Sea Level - Ground Offset`. You can set this parameter to values greater than zero to lower the ground and avoid discontinuity artifacts from objects crossing ground level. As a consequence, you'll see a vacuum between the atmosphere and the ground which may be noticeable near horizon. We recommend leaving this parameter at `0` and keeping the rest of the scene above __Sea Level__ instead.

parameters.label: Ground Receives Shadows
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Allow ground elements to receive shadows (i.e. cast shadow rays).

parameters.label: Render Backside Atmosphere
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Allows rendering of the atmosphere on the other side of the planet.

parameters.label: Solid Alpha in IPR
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Set alpha to `1` in IPR mode. Turned on by default to avoid misleading appearance due to compositing against light viewport background.

parameters.label: Ignore Camera Far Clip
parameters.heading: Advanced
parameters.description: Ignore camera's far clip distance when computing atmospheric contribution on primary rays. This allows correct appearance of the sky without having to increase camera's far clip distance to encompass the entire atmosphere.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

entries.title: Karma Sky Dome Light
entries.summary: Creates or edits a Karma Sky Dome Light.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Amount of shearing. The three values represent shearing in the X direction on the XY plane, in the X direction on the XZ plane, and in the Y direction on the YZ plane, respectively.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: Solar Altitude
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The vertical angle of the sun in the sky measured in degrees from horizon.

parameters.label: Solar Azimuth
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The horizontal angle along the horizon, where `0` corresponds to the -Z axis.

parameters.label: Turbidity
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Measure of the aerosol content of the air which defines the sky appearance. A __Turbidity__ value of `2` yields a very clear, Arctic-like sky, `3` a clear sky in a temperate climate, `6` a sky on a warm, moist day, `10` a slightly hazy day.

parameters.label: Ground Albedo
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The ground reflectivity that affects the sky color. __Ground Albedo__ does not change the ground brightness.

parameters.label: Ground Color
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The visual ground color as seen in the render.

parameters.label: Horizon Blur Falloff
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The angle in degrees below horizon where the sky and the ground color are blended to blur the horizon.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. `0` does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the __Intensity__ to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Use __Color Temperature__ to control the light color. The color calculated by __Color Temperature__ is *multiplied* by the RGB color in __Color__, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set __Color__ to `1.0, 1.0, 1.0`.

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Enable Color Temperature__ is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from `1000` to `10000`. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the `UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb()` function from the USD library.

parameters.label: Filters
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Optional light filter primitives that you want to apply to this light.

parameters.label: Portals
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Optional portal geometry prim(s) to use to guide light sampling.

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the light in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this light from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide lights that are embedded in props, or other lights that are not meant to be modified.

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a [Light Filter Library LOP|Node:lop/lightfilterlibrary].

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (`0, 0, 0`) is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is `-1`, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global __Light Sampling Quality__. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree.  This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis.  If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than `0`), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than `0`). Leave it at `ß` for balanced approach.

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area.

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation.  If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the `HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE` configuration variable.

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface).  Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity.  If the radius is set to `1`, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light.  If the value is `1.4142` (`sqrt(2)`), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a [portal light|/solaris/support/portallights].

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe].

parameters.label: Illuminate Background Holdout
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: If a light exists to add new light source instead of trying to replicate lighting in the live action plate, enable this parameter so that its effect on background holdout geometry shows up in indirect bounces and its contribution to shadow holdout AOVs is omitted.

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.

parameters.label: Contributes to Caustics
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Default is true. Note that Karma only renders caustics if they are enabled on _both the light and the object_. This option has no effect unless you also turn on __Enable Caustics__ on the geometry object.

parameters.label: Flip Rectangle Light Texture
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Specifies how the texture applied to a rectangle light is flipped. Default is FlipX to match the USD specification. Only supported on rectangle light type. Options are None, FlipX, FlipY, and FlipXY. <!---

parameters.label: Attenuation Type
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Controls the type of attenuation on the light source in the default light shader. This may be

parameters.label: Attenuation Start
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Minimum light distance to be used for attenuation.

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: The distance from the light at which __Half Distance Attenuation__ produces half the light intensity. --->

parameters.label: Spread
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Ranges between `0` to `1` and controls beam direction along the light's normal. A value of `1` results in diffuse emission, and a value close to `0` gives parallel beams of light similar to directional light. Note that the __Spread__ option is only supported for area lights with __Type__ set to __Rectangle__ or __Disk__. In conjunction with __Disk__ lights you can, for example, create focused laser beams by leaving __Spread__ at `0`.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

deprecation.tier: VERIFIED-DOC + VERIFIED-RUNTIME (union, sides recorded separately — never collapsed to one boolean)

entries.title: Karma Standard Render Vars
entries.summary: Create standard karma render vars (AOVs/Image Planes).

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Path
parameters.description: Here you can define the path where in the Scene Graph Tree your AOVs will appear.

parameters.label: LPE Tag AOV Limit
parameters.description: When splitting AOVs per lights' LPE Tag, specify the maximum number of LPE Tag AOVs beyond which the node will emit a warning.

parameters.label: Omit LPE Tags
parameters.description: When splitting AOVs per lights' LPE Tag, specify a space separated list of lights' LPE Tags which will not create new AOVs.

parameters.label: Precision
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: The color depth of the AOV image. You can choose between __16 Bit__ and __32 Bit__.

parameters.label: Output Colorspace
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: You can directly apply a [color space|/solaris/ocio] to the AOV. Choose one of the available spaces from the parameter's associated dropdown menu, e.g. __ACEScg__.

parameters.label: Split per LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Creates additional AOVs for each unique light LPE Tag. To manage LPE Tags for lights, see the [LPE Tag LOP node|Node:lop/lpetag].

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: You can use [Solaris filter syntax|/solaris/support/filters] in the following parameters to filter the sample values. The default `["ubox", {}]` simply averages all the sample values within each pixel. ~~~

parameters.label: Beauty
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the beauty output as a `color4f` render var named `C`. ~~~

parameters.label: Beauty Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the unoccluded (unshadowed) beauty output as a `color3f` render var named `beautyunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C.*[LO][LO]`. ~~~

parameters.label: Combined Diffuse
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `combineddiffuse`, using the LPE `C<RD>.*L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Direct Diffuse
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `directdiffuse`, using the LPE `C<RD>L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Indirect Diffuse
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectdiffuse`, using the LPE `C<RD>.+L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Combined Diffuse Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) unoccluded diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `combineddiffuseunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C<RD>.*[LO]`. ~~~

parameters.label: Direct Diffuse Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) unoccluded diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `directdiffuseunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C<RD>L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Indirect Diffuse Unshadowed
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) unoccluded diffuse surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectdiffuseunshadowed`, using the LPE `unoccluded;C<RD>.+L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Combined Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) glossy surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `combinedglossyreflection`, using the LPE `C<RG>.*[LO]`. ~~~

parameters.label: Direct Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) glossy surface reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `directglossyreflection`, using the LPE `C<RG>L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Indirect Glossy Reflection
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) glossy reflection component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectglossyreflection`, using the LPE `C<RG>.+L`. ~~~~

parameters.label: Glossy Transmission
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the glossy transmission component as a `color3f` render var named `glossytransmission`, using the LPE `C<TG>.*[LO]`. ~~~

parameters.label: Visible Lights
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the visible lights component as a `color3f` render var named `visiblelights`, using the LPE `CL`. ~~~

parameters.label: Combined Emission
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) emission component as a `color3f` render var named `combinedemission`, using the LPE `C.*O`. ~~~

parameters.label: Direct Emission
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) emission component as a `color3f` render var named `directemission`, using the LPE `CO`. ~~~

parameters.label: Indirect Emission
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) emission component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectemission`, using the LPE `C.+O`. ~~~

parameters.label: Combined Volume
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the combined (any number of bounces) volume component as a `color3f` render var named `combinedvolume`, using the LPE `CV.*L`. ~~~

parameters.label: Direct Volume
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the direct (no bounces) volume component as a `color3f` render var named `directvolume`, using the LPE `CVL`. ~~~

parameters.label: Indirect Volume
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the indirect (one or more bounces) volume component as a `color3f` render var named `indirectvolume`, using the LPE `CV.+L`. ~~~

parameters.label: BSDF Labelled `coat`
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the coat component as a `color3f` render var named `coat`, using the LPE `C<...'coat'>.*[LO]`. ~~~

parameters.label: BSDF Labelled `sss`
parameters.heading: Component Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the sss component as a `color3f` render var named `sss`, using the LPE `C<...'sss'>.*[LO]`.

parameters.label: P (World Space)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the world space position as a `point3f` render var named `P`. ~~~

parameters.label: P (Camera Space)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the camera space position as a `point3f` render var named `P`. ~~~

parameters.label: Depth (Camera Space)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the distance from the camera origin as a `float` render var named `depth`. ~~~

parameters.label: Element (Raw ID)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the element ID as a `float` render var named `element`. ~~~

parameters.label: Prim ID
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the primitive identifier as a `float` render var named `primid`. ~~~

parameters.label: UV
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the primitive hit UV as a `float3` render var named `UV`. ~~~

parameters.label: N (Smooth Normal)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the primitive hit normal as a `normal3f` render var named `N`. ~~~

parameters.label: N (Smooth Camera Normal)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the camera space primitive hit normal as a `normal3f` render var named `N_camera`. ~~~

parameters.label: N (Smooth Facing Normal)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the viewer-facing primitive hit normal as a `normal3f` render var named `N_facing`. Backfaces also face towards the viewer. ~~~

parameters.label: N (Facing Ratio)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the falloff (dot product) between the viewer and hit normal as a `half` render var named `N_facingratio`. ~~~

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Normal)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the primitive geometric normal as a `normal3f` render var named `Ng`. ~~~

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Camera Normal)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the camera space primitive geometric normal as a `normal3f` render var named `Ng_camera`. ~~~

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Facing Normal)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the viewer facing primitive geometric normal as a `normal3f` render var named `Ng_facing`. Backfaces also face towards the viewer. ~~~

parameters.label: Ng (Geometric Facing Ratio)
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the falloff (dot product) between the viewer and geometric normal as a `half` render var named `Ng_facingratio`. ~~~

parameters.label: Motion Vectors
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the primitive motion vector as a `vector3f` render var named `motionvector`. ~~~

parameters.label: Velocity
parameters.heading: Ray Level Outputs
parameters.description: Add the primitive velocity as a `vector3f` render var named `velocity`.

parameters.label: Albedo
parameters.heading: Raw
parameters.description: Add the albedo output as a `color3f` render var named `export_basecolor`. Only available with shaders that export this information, such as the principled shader. For MaterialX shaders, the preferred way to create a diffuse albedo AOV is to use the `CDA` [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe]. ~~~

parameters.label: Ambient Occlusion
