entries.title: Karma Texture Baker
entries.summary: Create a Render Settings primitive to create texture maps that define shading states for an object.

parameters.label: Baking Mode
parameters.description: Specifies how the shading point is determined for each point on the low-res mesh. The low_res mesh is the mesh you'll be baking. * __Trace__. This mode sends rays from the low-res/bake mesh in the direction of the surface normal to find the shading point. This method works if multiple objects are baked onto a single mesh. The other scene objects don't need UV coordinates. * __UV Match__. This method takes a single high-res mesh and determines the shading point by matching UV coordinates from the low-res mesh. __UV Match__ makes sense if the high-res mesh doesn't align very well to the low-res mesh. * __Single Mesh__. To bake a single mesh, use the same mesh for __Low Res Mesh__ and __High Res Mesh__.

parameters.label: Trace Mode
parameters.description: Determines how rays are traced from the low-resolution mesh to the high-resolution mesh during baking. There are three modes: Surface Normal (Bidirectional) traces rays in both forward and backward directions along the low-res normal to find the closest high-res surface match; Cage Mesh Topology traces a single ray from the cage mesh toward the low-res mesh using matching UV coordinates, ideal when a cage mesh with the same topology is available; Cage Offset traces a single ray by offsetting the low-res point along its normal and tracing backward, allowing cage-style baking without requiring a physical cage mesh. The Trace Bias parameter controls the offset distance used in Cage Offset mode.

parameters.label: Low Res Mesh
parameters.description: This is the mesh you're going to bake. The polygons are rasterized based on the mesh's UV coordinates.

parameters.label: Cage Mesh
parameters.description: This parameter is only available when you set __Baking Mode__ to __Trace__. Sometimes it's problematic to determine the direction to trace rays from the low-res mesh to the scene. When you specify a cage mesh, rays are sent from the position on the cage mesh through the topology matching position on the low-res mesh. This leads to finer control when determining the shading position. Note that _low-res mesh_ and _cage mesh_ must have the same topology. Furthermore, the _cage mesh_ must enclose the _high-res_ mesh completely.

parameters.label: High Res Mesh
parameters.description: When you set __Baking Mode__ to __Trace__, normally Karma will bake all visible surfaces.  This allows convenient baking of complicated terrain with instanced boulders.  However, this parameter lets you select the objects which will be baked to the low-res mesh. When you set __Baking Mode__ to __UV Mesh__, this specifies the high-res mesh that has matching UV coordinates to the low.res mesh. The position data of this mesh are used to compute the shading information. When you set __Baking Mode__ to __Single Mesh__, this specifies the high-res mesh. To bake a single mesh, use the same mesh for __Low Res Mesh__ and __High Res Mesh__.

parameters.label: Dicing Camera
parameters.description: Specifies the camera for dicing subdivision or displaced surfaces.  If no camera exists on the stage, the texture baker will create an automatic dicing camera.

parameters.label: Output Picture
parameters.description: The filename of the output image. When you bake a single image, the node uses the name exactly as entered here. However, when you render separate images for each AOV, this name will be the starting point for the individual AOV filename. The AOV name will be appended to the __Output Picture__ just before the file extension. The file extension will be changed to the format that you've chosen from the  __Image Format__ dropdown on the __Images__ tab.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: The horizontal and vertical size of the output image, in pixels.

parameters.label: UV Attribute
parameters.description: Specify the primvar name of the texture coordinate used for baking.

parameters.label: Default UDIM
parameters.description: When there are multiple UDIMs detected, the texture baker will create multiple USD `rendersettings` primitives - one for each UDIM (`karmabake_<UDIM>`). This parameter determines which of the `rendersettings` primitives will be the "default" for rendering. You can override the default primitive in the viewport display settings, or by specifying a specific `rendersettings` primitive when rendering with `husk`.

parameters.label: Create Separate Files
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: Renders either a single image with multiple AOVS, or store each AOV in a separate file.

parameters.label: Image Format
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: Specifies the format the image format of the separately rendered AOV. The file extension will change accordingly.

parameters.label: Save as Mip Mapped Texture
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: When saving separate files to .exr, .tif (.tx), or .rat files, enabling this option will ensure that the generated images have Mip Maps and are saved as tiled texture files suitable for use in rendering.

parameters.label: Name Separator
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: This character will be used to separate the file name from the __Output Picture__ parameter and the AOV channel name.  For example, when you bake `Nt` and `P` AOVs and __Output Picture__ is `render/bake.png`, the output file names will be `render/bake_Nt.png` and `render/bake_P.png`.

parameters.label: Expand UV Islands
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: Post-processes the images by smearing the boundaries of the UV islands into the empty areas of the image. This will produce better results when MIP-mapping the textures. This process can be time-consuming. For faster iterations, only turn on this feature for the final baking.

parameters.label: Denoiser
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or __No Denoiser__. This utility currently supports [Intel Open Image Denoise|https://openimagedenoise.github.io] (included with Houdini) and the [NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser|https://developer.nvidia.com/optix-denoiser] (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. The NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser only works with NVIDIA cards. It is now included with the NVIDIA driver (version 435 or later).

parameters.label: Denoise AOVs
parameters.heading: Images
parameters.description: The denoiser will be applied to the parameter's space-separated list of AOVs.

parameters.label: Normal Y Direction
parameters.heading: Alignment
parameters.description: Determines the direction of the Y value of the tangent-space normal (or rounded normal) AOVs.

parameters.label: Tangent Space Normal
parameters.heading: Tangent Space Normal
parameters.description: Creates an AOV for the tangent space normal. You can change the AOV's default `Nt` name.

parameters.label: Rounded Normal
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: Creates an AOV for the rounded normal. You can change the AOV's default `Rn` name.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Samples
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: Specify the number of directions to compute the rounded normal.  More samples will take a longer time but produce a less noisy result.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Ray Bias
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: The ray-bias for computing rounded normals to avoid self-intersection.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Radius
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: The radius for the rounded normals.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Cusp Angle
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: Polygons that have an angle less than this threshold will be assumed to be a smooth surface and not appear in the rounded normal map.

parameters.label: Rounded Edge Mode
parameters.heading: Rounded Normal
parameters.description: Whether to capture concave or convex edges in the rounded edge normal map.

parameters.label: World Space
parameters.heading: Alignment
parameters.description: Whether the world space position should be recorded in left or right handed space with Y or Z as the up axis.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: The shading position. You can change the AOV's default `P` name.

parameters.label: Shading Space
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: When you store the `P` AOV, this is how the position should be represented * __World Space__. The shading position is written directly to the AOV. * __Low Res Mesh Bounding Box__. The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the low-res mesh. * __Scene Bounding Box__. The shading position is fit to the bounding box of the whole scene. * __User Defined__. The shading position is fit to user specified values.

parameters.label: Uniform Bounding Box (Not Stretched)
parameters.heading: Position
parameters.description: When you turn on this toggle, all three axes of the bounding box will have the same length.  If unchecked, the box will fit the geometry tightly in all dimensions.

parameters.label: Normal
parameters.heading: Normal
parameters.description: The shading normal. You can change the AOV's default `N` name.

parameters.label: Geometric Normal
parameters.heading: Geometric Normal
parameters.description: The geometric shading normal (the face/non-interpolated normal). You can change the AOV's default `Ng` name.

parameters.label: Occlusion
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Ambient occlusion. You can change the AOV's default `Oc` name.

parameters.label: Occlusion Samples
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing __Occlusion__.  If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase __Occlusion Samples__ without having to increase the __Primary Samples__.

parameters.label: Occlusion Max Distance
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: The maximum distance to consider when computing __Occlusion__.  A small distance can speed up occlusion shading at the cost of accuracy.

parameters.label: Occlusion Ray Bias
parameters.heading: Occlusion
parameters.description: Controls the ray bias when computing __Occlusion__.

parameters.label: Curvature
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: The curvature at the shading position. You can change the AOV's default `Cu` name.

parameters.label: Curvature Samples
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing __Curvature__.  If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase __Curvature Samples__ without having to increase the __Primary Samples__.

parameters.label: Curvature Scale
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Controls the overall intensity or contrast of the curvature by amplifying the difference between convex and concave responses.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Smaller values (= smaller distance) emphasize the concavity. Larger values (= greater distance) reveal more curvature and improve the visibility of the convex features.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Curvature
parameters.description: Controls whether the map looks more concave or more convex. Smaller values emphasize concavity, higher values enhance convexity.

parameters.label: Cavity
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: The occlusion along the inverted normal at the shading position. This produces "relief" shading. You can change the AOV's default `Cv` name.

parameters.label: Cavity Samples
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing __Cavity__.  If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase __Cavity Samples__ without having to increase the __Primary Samples__.

parameters.label: Max Distance
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: Limits how far rays can detect nearby geometry. Smaller values (smaller distance) emphasize concavity.

parameters.label: Bias
parameters.heading: Cavity
parameters.description: Blends between full cavity contrast (`0`) and a flat result (`1`).

parameters.label: Thickness
parameters.heading: Thickness
parameters.description: The thickness at the shading position. You can change the AOV's default `Th` name.

parameters.label: Thickness Samples
parameters.heading: Thickness
parameters.description: Determines the number of indirect rays used when computing __Thickness__.  If the resulting AOV is noisy, you can increase __Thickness Samples__ without having to increase the __Primary Samples__.

parameters.label: Edge
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: Identify edges in the high res model. You can change the AOV's default `Eg` name.

parameters.label: Edge Samples
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: Specify the number of directions to compute the __Edge__. More samples will take longer processing time, but produce a less noisy result.

parameters.label: Edge Ray Bias
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: The ray-bias for computing rounded normals to avoid self-intersection.

parameters.label: Edge Radius
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: The radius of the rounded edge.

parameters.label: Edge Cusp Angle
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: Polygons with an angle below this threshold are considered smooth and won't appear in the Edge map.

parameters.label: Edge Mode
parameters.heading: Edge
parameters.description: Types of edges (concave or convex) to smooth

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Height
parameters.description: Displacement between the low-res mesh and the shading point as a scalar value. You can change the AOV's default `Ds` name.

parameters.label: Vector Displacement
parameters.heading: Vector Displacement
parameters.description: Displacement between the low-res mesh and the shading point as a vector value. You can change the AOV's default `Vd` name.

parameters.label: Tangent-Space Vector Displacement
parameters.heading: Tangent-space Vector Displacement
parameters.description: Displacement between the low-res mesh and the shading point as a tangent-space vector value. You can change the AOV's default `Vdt` name.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.heading: Alpha
parameters.description: The alpha at the shading position. You can change the AOV's default `Af` name.

parameters.label: Base Combined
parameters.heading: Base Combined
parameters.description: The MtlX Standard Surface defines the base color as `base * base_color`, where `base` is a scalar multiplier on the color given by `base_color`.  This AOV stores the multiplied result as a single channel. The __Coat Normal__, __Shading Normal__ and __Shading Tangent__ values are stored exactly as they are wired into the shader (in world position).

parameters.label: Enable Lighting
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Turns on lighting computations for baking.

parameters.label: Beauty
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Stores the beauty image as an AOV with RGBA colors through the LPE `C.*[LO]`

parameters.label: Combined Diffuse
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Stores the direct and indirect diffuse illumination through the LPE `C<RD>.*L`.

parameters.label: Direct Diffuse
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Stores the direct diffuse illumination through the LPE `C<RD>L`.

parameters.label: Indirect Diffuse
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Stores the indirect diffuse illumination through the LPE `C<RD>.+L`.

parameters.label: Facing Ratio
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Stores the facing ratio from the __Dicing Camera__.

parameters.label: Extra AOVs
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Define any custom AOVs here. In addition to lighting AOVs, you can also specify AOVs defined by primvars or other Karma-specific AOVs.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Turn the AOV on or off.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Specify the name of the AOV.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: The data type of the AOV

parameters.label: Source Name
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: The __Source Type__ dropdown menu determines the name. For example, with the default __LPE__ option, the source is a light path expression. With __Primvar__, you can enter the name of an attribute/primvar.

parameters.label: Source Type
parameters.heading: Lighting
parameters.description: Determines how the baker evaluates the __Source Name__ parameter.

parameters.label: Make Low Res Mesh Invisible
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: In most cases, the low-res mesh should be invisible to any rays. This means that the mesh won't contribute to occlusion or other ray-traced effects. However, there might be situations where the low-res mesh remains visible.

parameters.label: Primary Samples
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: Specifies the number of camera rays sent for each pixel. Higher values improve the quality of the rendering.

parameters.label: Trace Bias
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: When rays are sent from the low-res mesh to the scene, this bias is used to offset a ray's origin from the surface of the low-res mesh. You can use this parameter to arbitrarily offset the low-res mesh along its normal without having to define a cage mesh.

parameters.label: Use MikkT Tangents
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: MikkT is a common standard for tangent space used in baking tools to produce normal maps.

parameters.label: Low Res Normals
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: For texture baking to work, the __Low Res Mesh__ should have normals.  This parameter controls how the LOP will deal with low-res geometry that's missing normals.

parameters.label: Dicing Quality
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: When baking displaced meshes or subdivision surfaces, this parameter can control the level of detail of the dicing.

parameters.label: Displacement Style
parameters.heading: Baking
parameters.description: Sometimes, displacement shading inverts the surface and produces bad normals. This parameter lets you run displacement shaders as bump map shaders. Alternatively, you can disable displacement shading entirely.

parameters.label: Uncategorized Primitives
parameters.heading: Trace Set
parameters.description: Determines the behavior of primitives that don't belong to any trace set.

parameters.label: Trace Sets
parameters.heading: Trace Set
parameters.description: The number of explicit trace sets.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Trace Set
parameters.description: Turn on (or off) the creation of the trace set.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Trace Set
parameters.description: Specify a name for the trace set.

parameters.label: Visibility
parameters.heading: Trace Set
parameters.description: Specify the primitives visible to primitives in this trace set for ray tracing.  This is specified as a space- or comma-separated list of other trace set names.  Two special names are `self` (only consider primitives in this trace set) and `*` (consider all primitives). * If the visibility is `self`, only primitives in this trace set will be used for ray tracing operations. * If the visibility is `*`, all primitives in the scene will affect the visibility of these primitives. * You can also specify a pattern of trace set names which are used to determine visibility for ray-tracing operations. For example `body*`, `face body hands` or `face body* ^knapsack` to exclude `knapsack`.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Trace Set
parameters.description: The primitives that belong to this trace set.

entries.summary: Imports a character or animation from a SOP network into the USD scene graph.

parameters.label: Animated Pose

parameters.description: When turned on, shifts the animation so that it begins at the `clipinfo` attribute's source start time. This parameter is available when __Clip Range__ is set to __Use clipinfo Detail Attribute__.

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling

parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Subframe Sampling
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close

parameters.label: Camera Prim

parameters.label: Samples

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample

If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

This parameter can specify multiple paths, and use wildcards, which allows it to replace many layers with a single common replacement layer. The pattern is compared to both the original layer reference as it appears in the referencing layer, and as an absolute path (created by treating the referencing layer's path as the root location to resolve relative paths).

entries.title: Light
entries.summary: Creates or edits a USD Light prim. This node also adds some useful Karma-specific attributes.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: Transform
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: How the transform parameters below apply to the primitive. (Because each USD prim can contain multiple transforms, _and_ be affected by parent transforms, there are many different ways to apply new transforms.)

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: The order in which Houdini applies translates, rotates, and scales, and the order in which it applies rotation.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Movement amount along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Degrees rotation around XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Non-uniform scaling along XYZ axes.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.heading: Transform
parameters.description: Scales the object uniformly along all three axes.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Moves the local origin of the object.

parameters.label: Pivot Rotate
parameters.heading: Pivot Transform
parameters.description: Rotates the local origin of the object after translation.

parameters.label: NOTE
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: USD currently does not have look-at constraints. This node calculates the per-frame transform to fulfill the constraint and applies it to the object. See the [Light tool help|/nodes/lop/light#tool] for how to set up the look-at constraint interactively in the viewport.

parameters.label: Enable Look At
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Turns on the constraint that orients this object to look at a point or another object.

parameters.label: Look At Position
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: If __Enable Look At__ is on and, this is a point in space this object will look at. If __Look At Primitive__ is not blank, this is an *offset* from the centroid of the target object (in the local space of that object).

parameters.label: Look At Primitive
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: The path to a USD prim this object should look at. If this is not blank, __Look At Position__ is an *offset* from this centroid of the target object.

parameters.label: Up Vector Method
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: Controls how the up vector is set.

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: When __Up Vector Method__ is __Custom__, this is the up axis to use for the look-at constraint.

parameters.label: Twist
parameters.heading: Constraints
parameters.description: A twist rotation (around the -Z axis, clockwise, in degrees), applied after the lookout transform.

parameters.label: Intensity
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A linear scale on the power output of the light.

parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the power output exponentially as a power of 2, similar to an F-stop control. `0` does not scale intensity, negative numbers scale intensity down by the square, positive numbers scale intensity up. Often you will set the __Intensity__ to what looks like the right amount of light, and then use this parameter to "tweak" it.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: The color of the light, in energy-linear terms.

parameters.label: Enable Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Use __Color Temperature__ to control the light color. The color calculated by __Color Temperature__ is *multiplied* by the RGB color in __Color__, so if you want the "pure" temperature color, you should set __Color__ to `1.0, 1.0, 1.0`.

parameters.label: Color Temperature
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Enable Color Temperature__ is on, the temperature (in degrees Kelvin) to simulate. The valid range is from `1000` to `10000`. Lower values are warmer and higher values are cooler. The default is the common D65 white point. If necessary, you can compute the same color value using the `UsdLuxBlackbodyTemperatureAsRgb()` function from the USD library.

parameters.label: Clipping Range
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Don't show geometry closer than the near distance or farther away than the far distance (in world units).

parameters.label: Normalize Power
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Divides the set power output (intensity scaled by exposure) by the surface area or angular size of the light. This makes it easier to adjust and compare energy output without it being affected by the size of the light.

parameters.label: Diffuse Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the diffuse response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Specular Multiplier
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Scales the effect this light has on the specular response of shaders. This is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Scale Guide Geometry
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Applies a uniform scaling factor on the guide geometry that is drawn for the light in the viewport. The default value is an expression that inverts the "meters per unit" value of the USD stage to produce a consistent real-world size for the guide geometry.

parameters.label: Show in Viewport Camera Menu
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Turn off this option to prevent this light from showing up in the camera menu in the viewport. This can be useful to hide lights that are embedded in props, or other lights that are not meant to be modified.

parameters.label: Light Filters
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: A space-separated list of light filters you want to use with the light. You can create a light filter in a [Light Filter Library LOP|Node:lop/lightfilterlibrary].

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Cylinder__, __Disk__, or __Sphere__, the radius of the light.

parameters.label: Length
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Cylinder__, the length of the light from end to end.

parameters.label: Geometry
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Geometry__, the path to a geometry prim to use as the light shape.

parameters.label: Width
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Rectangle__, the width of the light area.

parameters.label: Height
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Rectangle__, the height of the light area.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Distant__, the angular size of the light in degrees. As an example, the Sun is approximately 0.53 degrees as seen from Earth. Higher values broaden the light and therefore soften shadow edges.

parameters.label: Texture
parameters.heading: Base Properties
parameters.description: Maps a texture to the area geometry of lights. This is currently only supported with rectangular lights.

parameters.label: Spotlight
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Turn the light into a spotlight.

parameters.label: Angle
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: The spread angle of the spotlight beam, in degrees.

parameters.label: Softness
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Blurs the edges of the spotlight beam, simulating light leakage and bounce.

parameters.label: Left Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the left, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Left Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.

parameters.label: Right Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the right, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Right Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.

parameters.label: Top Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the top, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Top Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone.

parameters.label: Bottom Barndoor
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Slides in a light blocker from the bottom, covering part of the spotlight cone. `1.0` reaches all the way across the cone, blocking all light.

parameters.label: Bottom Barndoor Edge
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Extends the solid light blocker above by an additional soft edge. `1.0` creates a gradient as wide as the spotlight cone. ~~~~~

parameters.label: Focus
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: When turned, you can focus the beam with the numerical __Focus__ parameter.

parameters.label: Focus
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: A control to shape the spread of light. Higher focus values pull light towards the center and narrow the spread. (This is implemented as an off-axis cosine power exponent.)

parameters.label: Focus Tint
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Off-axis color tint, tints the light in the falloff region. The default is black. ~~~~~

parameters.label: IES
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: Use an IES file describing angular distribution of light.

parameters.label: File
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: An IES (Illumination Engineering Society) format file to use to control angular distribution of light.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: When turned on, the IES intensities are normalized to preserve the light's energy output. Note, that IES profiles have no effect on distant lights.

parameters.label: Angle Scale
parameters.heading: Shaping
parameters.description: A global scale on angles found in the IES file.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: When this is on, objects hit by this light will cast shadows (subject to shadow masks).

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: Tints the color of shadows cast by this light. Changing this from black (`0, 0, 0`) is a non-physical "tweak".

parameters.label: Falloff Start Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The near distance at which shadow falloff begins. The default value (`-1`) indicates no falloff.

parameters.label: Falloff Gamma
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: A gamma (i.e., exponential) control over shadow strength with linear distance within the falloff zone (between __Falloff__ and __Distance__).

parameters.label: Distance
parameters.heading: Shadow
parameters.description: The maximum distance to check for objects shadowing this light. The default is `-1`, meaning no limit. Setting this may speed up rendering if you know all objects you want shadowed are within a certain distance.

parameters.label: MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether multiple importance sampling will sample from the BSDF, the light, or both the BSDF and light.

parameters.label: Sampling Quality
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: This is the per-light sampling quality, that acts as a multiplier on the global __Light Sampling Quality__. Increasing the quality will add additional samples for this light source, improving the sampling quality of this light relative to other light sources.

parameters.label: Sampling Mode
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: When using the light tree for rendering, Karma will try to put any light source that's compatible into the tree.  This option can force a light to be excluded from the tree and subject to uniform sampling, which can sometimes yield an improved sampling quality the light at the expense of speed.

parameters.label: Maximum HDRI Size
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: If an environment map is larger than this resolution, it will be scaled down when performing texture analysis.  If the map has some very small, very bright values, this filtering may affect how sampling of the environment map is performed.

parameters.label: Portal MIS Bias
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Controls whether the dome light is more likely to sample from the environment map or the portal geometry. For high-contrast HDRI with strong light sources, it may be beneficial to sample more from the environment map (set it less than `0`), and for low-contrast/flat HDRI, the opposite may be true (set it greater than `0`). Leave it at `ß` for balanced approach.

parameters.label: Improve Volume Sampling (Equiangular MIS)
parameters.heading: Sampling
parameters.description: Reduce noise in cases where the light is inside a volume, or in very close proximity to a volume (does not apply to directional light or dome light which do not have defined origin in world space). This feature is most effective in cases where the noise is mostly caused by sparsity of volume samples near the light source, either because the volume is too thin, or because the light has relatively small surface area.

parameters.label: Light Shader
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Defines a VEX shader to be used for light evaluation.  If the string is empty, the value will be taken from the `HOUDINI_VEX_DEFAULT_LIGHTSURFACE` configuration variable.

parameters.label: Active Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Artificially clamp the illumination distance from the light. Outside this radius, the light will have no effect.

parameters.label: Point Light Radius
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: As point lights get closer to geometry, the attenuation equation causes the intensity of lights to go to infinity (a singularity caused by the division by the distance between the light and the surface).  Increasing this value to something larger than zero creates an artificial buffer zone to prevent the light from going to infinity.  If the radius is set to `1`, the brightest value for the point light will be twice the intensity specified on the light.  If the value is `1.4142` (`sqrt(2)`), the brightest value will be the intensity specified. For distant geometry, there should be very little change in the intensity.

parameters.label: Single Sided
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Does the light emit light from a single side (ie along the normal) or from both sides? This only has effect on planar area light types.

parameters.label: Render Light Geometry
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to be visible in the render. Always turn this option on if you want to use the light as a [portal light|/solaris/support/portallights].

parameters.label: Light Geometry Casts Shadow
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Causes the light source geometry to cast shadows in the render.

parameters.label: LPE Tag
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Custom label assigned to lights or objects for use with [Light Path Expressions|/solaris/support/lpe].

parameters.label: Illuminate Background Holdout
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: If a light exists to add new light source instead of trying to replicate lighting in the live action plate, enable this parameter so that its effect on background holdout geometry shows up in indirect bounces and its contribution to shadow holdout AOVs is omitted.

parameters.label: Contributions
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Provides detailed control over which BSDF component the light affects.

parameters.label: Contributes to Caustics
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Default is true. Note that Karma only renders caustics if they are enabled on _both the light and the object_. This option has no effect unless you also turn on __Enable Caustics__ on the geometry object.

parameters.label: Flip Rectangle Light Texture
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Specifies how the texture applied to a rectangle light is flipped. Default is FlipX to match the USD specification. Only supported on rectangle light type. Options are None, FlipX, FlipY, and FlipXY. <!---

parameters.label: Attenuation Type
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Controls the type of attenuation on the light source in the default light shader. This may be

parameters.label: Attenuation Start
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Minimum light distance to be used for attenuation.

parameters.label: Attenuation
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: The distance from the light at which __Half Distance Attenuation__ produces half the light intensity. --->

parameters.label: Spread
parameters.heading: Light
parameters.description: Ranges between `0` to `1` and controls beam direction along the light's normal. A value of `1` results in diffuse emission, and a value close to `0` gives parallel beams of light similar to directional light. Note that the __Spread__ option is only supported for area lights with __Type__ set to __Rectangle__ or __Disk__. In conjunction with __Disk__ lights you can, for example, create focused laser beams by leaving __Spread__ at `0`.

parameters.heading: Parent Layer

In order for values like the frames per second or up axis settings to apply to a USD stage, they must be set directly on the root layer of the stage. This options allow for the explicit copying of layer metadata from the first layer loaded by this node on to the stage's root layer. If multiple files are specified, it it always the first file that has its values copied to the root layer. The __Auto__ option for this parameter acts like a __Yes__ (copy the sublayer's metadata to the root layer) if there is no input connected to the first input of this node. parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Set Primitive Statistics
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Adds metadata to the prim containing information about the number of primitives appearing under the payload prim.

parameters.label: Set Geometry Count Statistics
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If __Set Primitive Statistics__ is turned on, this option can also be turned on to generated more detailed statistics such as the number of faces on mesh prims. Calculating this additional information will be slower than simply collecting primitive counts. ~~~

parameters.label: Number of Colors
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Specify colors to be applied to the payload primitives which will control the appearance of the bounding box representation of the prim when the payload is unloaded.

parameters.label: Set Color
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For this multiparm instance, control whether the specified color will be applied to the prim. Expressions for this parmeter can use the `@numprim` (total number of prims being processed), `@prim` (index of the current prim being processed) and `@primpath` (scene graph path of the prim being processed) local variables to help provide variation across many primitives.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The color applied to each primitive. This parameter can also use the `@numprim`, `@prim`, and `@primpath` local variables to provide variation across prims.

entries.title: Mask from Bounds
entries.summary: Sets a primvar based on whether/by how much selected prims are inside a bounding shape.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: What type of primitives to add the primvar to.

parameters.label: Instances
parameters.description: A space-separated list of instances, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[0] /geometry/instancer[1]`). To select all instances in an instancer, use `/<<path>>[*]`. To select a range, use `/geometry/instancer[4-7]` (the range is inclusive). To select instances inside nested instancers, use multiple indexes, for example `/geometry/instancer[2][7]`. VEXpressions can be used to specify instances, for example, `/geometry/instancer[{@weights>0.5}]`.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: When __Type__ is __Primitives/Native Instances__, a space-separated list of prim paths/patterns to add the primvar to.

parameters.label: Bounding Type
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: Choose between a box, sphere, or use external geometry prims as the boundary.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: When __Bounding Type__ is __Box__ or __Sphere__, the size of the bounding volume.

parameters.label: Center
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: Moves the bounding volume.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: Rotation of the bounding volume.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: When __Bounding Type__ is __Primitives (Geometry)__, scales the bounding volume created from the external geometry.

parameters.label: Pivot Translate
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: When __Bounding Type__ is __Primitives (Geometry)__, moves the pivot for rotating ans scaling the bounding volume created from the external geometry.

parameters.label: Primitive Source
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: When __Bounding Type__ is __Primitives (Geometry)__, whether to get bounding primitives from the stage connected to this node's first input or the second input.

parameters.label: Bounding Primitives
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: When __Bounding Type__ is __Primitives (Geometry)__, a space-separated list of prim paths/patterns to use to define the bounding volume.

parameters.label: Feather
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: Creates a soft falloff between values "inside" and "outside" the bounding shape. Negative values apply the falloff inside the boundary, positive values apply falloff outside the boundary. The greater the difference from `0`, the larger the falloff radius. When this is non-zero, primvar values on points/faces (0.0 or 1.0) are multiplied by a linear gradient from 1 to 0 between the bounds and this distance.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: Shrinks (negative values) or grows (positive values) the boundary shape.

parameters.label: Invert Bounds
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: Reverses the meaning of the primvar values, so `0.0` indicates _inside_ and `1.0` indicates _outside_.

parameters.label: Ignore Primitives Outside Bounds
parameters.heading: Bounds
parameters.description: When this on, the node does not author the primvar on selected prims outside the bounding box. This is faster than authoring `0.0` values.

parameters.label: Add Primvar
parameters.heading: Primvar
parameters.description: Adds a primvar indicating how much of each prim is inside the bounding volume.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.heading: Primvar
parameters.description: The name of the primvar to create.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Primvar
parameters.description: Specify the data type for the primvar. The default is `float`. If you choose `boolean` or a number type that does not support decimals, features such as __Feather__ will have no effect. This should be `boolean`, `int`, `float`, or `double`. Most other types won't work (the values will all be zero).

parameters.label: Interpolation
parameters.heading: Primvar
parameters.description: This controls the "level" at which the node creates the primvar.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.heading: Primvar
parameters.description: When __Interpolation__ is __Constant__, this is the node combines the point values to compute an overall value for the entire mesh. The default is __Average__, which is the most useful method.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.heading: Primvar
parameters.description: The value to use for "inside". The default is `1.0`.

parameters.label: Add Weights
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: Creates a property (not a primvar) on the prims, set to the same value as would be computed for a __Constant__ primvar, using the __Method__ below.

parameters.label: Weight Name
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: The name of the weight property to create.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: See [above|#method].

parameters.label: Add Collection
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: Creates a new collection containing the prims that have a non-zero `weight` attribute. This is only available when __Add Weights__ is on.

parameters.label: Collection Name
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: The name of the collection to add the primitives to. This is always created on the `/collections` prim (this node creates `/collections` if it doesn't already exist).

parameters.label: Add Selection Rule
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: When __Type__ is Primitives/Native Instances, create a selection rule with a given name.

parameters.label: Selection Rule Name
parameters.heading: Weights, Collection and Selection Rule
parameters.description: Specify the selection rule name, which can then be used using the `%rule:selectionrulename` syntax by downstream LOP nodes.

parameters.label: Import Frame
parameters.heading: Time
parameters.description: The frame at which to cook the LOP node and sample the stage. When importing animated geometry, this could be set to `$FF`.

entries.title: Material Library
entries.summary: Authors USD material primitives from shader VOP nodes.

parameters.label: Auto-generate Preview Surface Shaders
parameters.description: When possible, the LOP will generate a [USD Preview Surface VOP|Node:vop/usdpreviewsurface] primitive. This shader type is part of the USD standard and should be implemented by all USD renderers, so this shader (which may be an approximation of the original shader) should show up in any renderer, even if the renderer doesn't understand the original shader type. Note, if textures are involved, the auto-generated preview network will wire the alpha output of a USD Texture Reader primitive to the opacity input of a USD Preview Surface shader primitive. Some renderers, like Storm, are known to mishandle the opacity, leading to artifacts in the viewport. To workaround such cases, you can turn this toggle off and then you can manually create a USD Preview network inside, feeding it to the Collect VOP along with the original surface shader.

parameters.label: Allow Shader Parameter Animation
parameters.description: When it is turned off, all USD values are assumed non-animatable and will be authored at a default time code. And, with this option turned on, shader node parameters that are time-dependent will get translated to USD values at non-default time codes, while time-independent parameters will still author a value at a default time code. Note, checking parameter time dependency can be costly and may add up to a large portion of the shader translation time. Since the vast majority of shader nodes don't have animated parameters, this toggle is off by default to save the work involved in checking it.

parameters.label: Reference Material Render Vars into Render Products
parameters.label_norm: reference material render vars into render products
parameters.description: When this checkbox is turned on, the LOP will reference the render vars parent scope primitive (if it exists) into the global render products namespace (i.e., `/Render/Products/Vars`). entries.title: Merge
entries.summary: Merges the layers from incoming stages into a unified layer stack.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.description: Enable this option to remove all layers created above Layer Break nodes on every input to this node. This option is useful when creating diamond shaped node graphs, where on one branch the top of the diamond connects to the merge at the bottom of the diamond without a Layer Break, and the other branch(es) use Layer Breaks. Without this option, in any of the Separate Layer modes, the layer stack would include two copies of every layer created above the Layer Break, which degrades performance without affecting the final composed stage. Merge styles which cause layers from inputs to be flattened always strip layers above Layer Breaks, and so will hide this parameter. This is because layers cannot be stripped after they have been flattened. The __Flatten Into First Input's Active Layer__ merge style is a special case which flattens (and therefore strip layers) from all inputs after the first input. Note that layers above Layer Breaks will not be stripped from the first input in this mode.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

entries.summary: Makes a primitive appear to inherit the transform hierarchy of another prim somewhere else in the tree.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Source Type
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: Whether the source (the thing to be transformed) is a regular primitive, or a point instance. You *cannot* use a nested point instance as a source.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Source Instances
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Target Source
parameters.heading: Parent
parameters.description: Where to get the "parent" prim, either the first input or the second input.

parameters.label: Target Type
parameters.heading: Parent
parameters.description: Whether the "parent" is a regular primitive, or a point instance.

parameters.label: Target
parameters.heading: Parent
parameters.description: When __Target Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Target Instance
parameters.heading: Parent
parameters.description: When __Target Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Hide Target
parameters.heading: Parent
parameters.description: When __Target Source__ is __First Input__ and __Type__ is __Primitive__, whether to hide set the path's visibility to "hidden".

parameters.label: Import Time
parameters.heading: Parent
parameters.description: Specify the frame at which the source and/or target geometry are imported into the embedded SOP network to build the constraints. The default `$FF` expression forces the constraint LOP to be time dependent, which is needed when operating on a non time-dependent network that has time samples driving the source or target primitives. However, for better performance with a non time-dependent network with no time samples, it is recommended to use a static value instead.

parameters.label: Position
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Inherit position (translation) from the target. If this is off, the target does not affect the source object's position.

parameters.label: Rotation
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Inherit rotation from the target. If this is off, the target does not affect the source object's orientation.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Inherit scales from the target. If this is off, the target does not affect the source object's size.

parameters.label: Shear
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Inherit shear from the target. If this is off, the target does not affect the source object's shear.

parameters.label: Relative Offset
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: Get the target's transform from a different point in the timeline. You can specify an offset in frames or seconds below.

parameters.label: Maintain Local Offset
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the object maintains the relative distance between itself and the target, even though it otherwise inherits the target's position.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When __Relative Offset__ is on, whether to calculate the offset in frames or seconds.

parameters.label: Frame
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When __Relative Offset__ is on and __Method__ is __By Frame__, the relative number of frames ahead or back to get the target's translation from.

parameters.label: Integer Frames
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When __Relative Offset__ is on and __Method__ is __By Frame__, rounds the given frame number to the nearest integer frame, avoiding fractional frame cooking.

parameters.label: Time
parameters.heading: Constraint Options
parameters.description: When __Relative Offset__ is on and __Method__ is __By Time__, the number of seconds ahead or back to get the target's translation from.
