entries.title: Scene Doctor
entries.summary: Validates primitives on a USD stage.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Kind
parameters.heading: Preset Validations
parameters.description: Choose between three levels of validations (__Message__/__Warning__/__Error__) and fixes (__Alert Only__/__Fix and Alert__/__Fix Silently__). This displays either a message, warning, or error depending on whether prims violate the model hierarchy specified by USD. For example, `component` and `subcomponent` kinds cannot have children of kind `model`. `None` kinds cannot have children that aren't also `None`. * __Alert Only__ simply displays the badge and message based on the validation level. * __Fix and Alert__ will attempt to fix the issue while retaining the badge. * __Fix Silently__ will attempt to fix the error and clear the badge.

parameters.label: Child Gprims
parameters.heading: Preset Validations
parameters.description: Choose between three levels of validations (__Message__/__Warning__/__Error__) and fixes (__Alert Only__/__Fix and Alert__/__Fix Silently__). This displays either a message, warning, or error depending on whether prims violate the model hierarchy specified by USD.For example, `mesh` types can only have child prims of type `geomsubset`, and `VolVolume` types can only have child prims of type `VolField`. This validation also checks if a Gprim is marked as `instanceable`. While Gprims may of course be instanced, the instanceable flag must always be set on an ancestor of the Gprim, rather than on the Gprim itself. Otherwise hydra will not render the prim. * __Alert Only__ simply displays the badge and message based on the validation level. * __Fix and Alert__ will attempt to fix the issue while retaining the badge. * __Fix Silently__ will attempt to fix the error and clear the badge.

parameters.label: Primvars
parameters.heading: Preset Validations
parameters.description: Choose between three levels of validations (__Message__/__Warning__/__Error__) and fixes (__Alert Only__/__Fix and Alert__/__Fix Silently__). This displays either a message, warning, or error depending on whether prims have primvars with invalid array lengths or indices. There are different rules for different prim types (`mesh`, `curve`, `point`, `pointinstancers`) and interpolation settings (`constant`, `uniform`, `varying`, `vertex`, and `face-varying`). USD specifies all of them in their documentation. * __Alert Only__ simply displays the badge and message based on the validation level. * __Fix and Alert__ will attempt to fix the issue while retaining the badge. * __Fix Silently__ will attempt to fix the error and clear the badge.

parameters.label: Value Clips
parameters.heading: Preset Validations
parameters.description: Choose between three levels of validations (__Message__/__Warning__/__Error__) and fixes (__Alert Only__/__Fix and Alert__/__Fix Silently__). This displays either a message, warning, or error depending on whether prims have value clips without an authored manifest path or if the manifest file is not found in the authored path on disk. * __Alert Only__ simply displays the badge and message based on the validation level. * __Fix and Alert__ will attempt to fix the issue while retaining the badge. * __Fix Silently__ will attempt to fix the error and clear the badge.

parameters.label: Material Binding API
parameters.heading: Preset Validations
parameters.description: Choose between three levels of validations (__Message__/__Warning__/__Error__) and fixes (__Alert Only__/__Fix and Alert__/__Fix Silently__). This displays either a message, warning, or error depending on when prims have a `material:binding` relationship but do not have the `MaterialBindingAPI` schema applied. This problem can be fixed by applying the `MaterialBindingAPI` schema to the prim. * __Alert Only__ simply displays the badge and message based on the validation level. * __Fix and Alert__ will attempt to fix the issue while retaining the badge. * __Fix Silently__ will attempt to fix the error and clear the badge.

parameters.label: Add to Collection
parameters.heading: Collections
parameters.description: If this is enabled, all prims that are reported by the validations to have errors will be added to a collection with this name, which by default is the node name.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Collections
parameters.description: The path in this stage where the collection should be authored.

parameters.label: Number of Python Rules
parameters.heading: Python
parameters.description: Press the __+__ button to add another Python code window to write your own Python validation rules. <!---

parameters.label: Validate With Python
parameters.heading: Python
parameters.description: Choose between three levels of validations (Message/Warning/Error). Display either a message, warning, or error on the Scene Doctor respectively if the Python code reports an error. --->

parameters.label: Python Code
parameters.heading: Python
parameters.description: A code editor where users can enter Python code to write their own per-prim validation rules. Return value should either be a string, or `None`. Only non-empty returned strings will be reported as errors.

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

deprecation.tier: VERIFIED-DOC + VERIFIED-RUNTIME (union, sides recorded separately — never collapsed to one boolean)

entries.title: Scene Import
entries.summary: Imports models, materials, and lights from the Object level into the LOP network.

parameters.label: Import Objects
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Whether to import object nodes (models, cameras, and lights) into USD, mapping as many parameter values as possible to standard USD attributes.

parameters.label: Destination Path
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Prefix the node path of each imported object with this path to create its scene graph path. The default is `/`, which imports objects at the root level.

parameters.label: Root Object
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Only look at object nodes inside this node network path. The default is `/obj`, which means the node will try to import all object nodes.

parameters.label: Objects
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: A list of node paths to import. If this is blank (the default), the node imports _nothing_. Set this to `*` to try to import all object nodes.

parameters.label: Include Invisible Geometry
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Control whether to import geometry that has its object-level display flag turned off. If disabled, the geometry will not be imported at all. If enabled, the geometry will still be imported, but the USD prim will be marked as invisible.

parameters.label: Force Objects
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: A list of object name patterns to match for object-level nodes that should always be imported and marked as visible, regardless what their object-level status is.

parameters.label: Exclude Objects
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: A list of object name patterns to match for object-level nodes that should never be imported, even if they also appear in __Objects__ or __Force Objects__.

parameters.label: Filter
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Choose whether to import all object node types, or only cameras, only lights, or only geometry objects.

parameters.label: Make Conflicting Paths Unique
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: When this is on, the node will add numbers to names to ensure prims at the same level have unique names. When this is off, conflicting names will make the node stop cooking and show an error. Name conflicts most often occur when __Flatten Hierarchy__ is enabled, but can also happen because by default the scene graph path is built from both _containment_ and _wiring_ relationships at the object level.

parameters.label: Flatten Hierarchy
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Imports every object directly under the __Destination Path__, ignoring containment and wiring. Since this discards any intermediate subnets or input objects from the name space, this makes name conflicts more likely. You can __Make Conflicting Paths Unique__ to fix these.

parameters.label: Ignore Inputs
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Don't use the parent-child wiring relationships between object nodes to create prim hierarchy.

parameters.label: Import Bundles As Collections
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Convert object-level bundles to USD collections.

parameters.label: Collection Prim
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: When __Import Bundles As Collections__ is on, the USD prim to use for the collections.

parameters.label: Import SOP Geometry
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: Import the geometry generated by SOP nodes inside geometry objects as USD geometry. Turning this off might be useful if you only want to import the transform hierarchy from the objects, and want to treat actual geometry separately.

parameters.label: As Reference
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: When importing SOP geometry, this controls whether to create references on the current layer, or new sublayers (one per geometry). In both cases, __Destination Path__ is used to create a consistent hierarchy.

parameters.label: SOP Import Mode
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: When importing SOP geometry, this controls whether the node with the __Display/Render__ flag is used. Choosing __Default__ will make the choice on a per-node-type basis, and will generally use the node with the __Render__ flag (an exception is for the `hairgen-` node where it will use the node with the __Display__ flag).

parameters.label: Set Subdivision Scheme to Match Object Parameters
parameters.label_norm: set subdivision scheme to match object parameters
parameters.heading: Objects
parameters.description: When __Import SOP geometry__ is on, check for rendering properties that control subdivision on the object, and set the USD Subdivision Scheme to match.

parameters.label: Enable Packed USD Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Packed USD Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigusdprims` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Packed USD Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with packed USD primitives in the imported SOP geometry.

parameters.label: Enable Other Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Other Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigotherprims` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Other Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with regular non-packed primitives (points, curves, polygons, spheres, and so on).

parameters.label: Enable Define Only Leaf Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Define Only Leaf Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigdefineonlyleafprims` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Define Only Leaf Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: Author intermediate primitives (for example, any `Xform` prims created for the __Import Path Prefix__) as overrides instead of definitions. This means if they don't match up with underlying prims in lower layers, the leaf prims won't be added to the scene. This is useful if you only want to import the geometry if its ancestors already exist in the scene tree. (Note that all of the data is still imported, it just may not be visible in the scene graph tree or the viewport.)

parameters.label: Enable Packed Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Packed Primitives__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpackedprims` detail or primitive attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Packed Primitives
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with SOP-native packed primitives.

parameters.label: Enable Agents
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Agents__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigagents` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Agents
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with [agent primitives|/crowds/agents]. In all modes, a prim is created from the agent primitive's transform and attributes, and the agent's geometry and animation are imported underneath.

parameters.label: Enable NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __NURBS Curves__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfignurbscurves` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS curve primitives.

parameters.label: Enable NURBS Surfaces
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __NURBS Surfaces__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfignurbssurfs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: NURBS Surfaces
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS surface primitives.

parameters.label: Enable Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Kind Authoring__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigkindschema` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: How to assign [kinds|/solaris/glossary#kind] to imported prims.

parameters.label: Enable Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Path Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpathattr` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: A (comma or space-separated) list of names of SOP *primitive string attributes* to use to use as prim paths to put the SOP geometry into. The default is `path,name`. See [geometry hierarchy|#import] above. If the list has more than one attribute, the importer checks each attribute for the first non-empty value. If the string value a full path, that path is used as the USD scene graph path for that primitive. If the string is a relative path (or just a name), the string is appended to the __Import Path Prefix__ string to generate a full scene graph path. If none of the listed attributes exist on a given SOP primitive, or all values are an empty string, the importer generates a name automatically (for example, `sphere_0`).

parameters.label: Enable Prefix Absolute Paths
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Prefix Absolute Paths__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigprefixabsolutepaths` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Prefix Absolute Paths
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: Whether absolute path values from __Path Attributes__ should be prefixed/parented or not. By default this is off and only relative path values are prefixed.

parameters.label: Enable Import HeightFields as Mesh
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import HeightFields as Mesh__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigheightfieldconvert` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import HeightFields as Mesh
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: If the source SOP geometry contains a height field volume, it will be imported as polygonal mesh. Other layers will be imported as vertex primvar if the values are varying, or constant primvar if the values are constant.

parameters.label: Enable Use XformCommonAPI for Transforms
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Use XformCommonAPI for Transforms__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigusexformcommonapi` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Use XformCommonAPI for Transforms
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: Turn on this option to have the SOP Import operation author transforms on prims that match the requirements of the UsdGeomXformCommonAPI standard. This authors separate xform operations for translate, rotate, scale, and for storing the pivot. The alternative is to author the transform as a single 4x4 matrix.

parameters.label: Enable Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.label_norm: enable treat polygons as subdivision surfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpolygonsassubd` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: For polygon meshes that are not already tagged with a subdivision scheme, author a `subdivisionScheme` attribute set to `catmullClark`. This will convert them to subdivision surfaces.

parameters.label: Enable Subdivision Group
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subdivision Group__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsubdgroup` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subdivision Group
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: If __Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces__ is on, only convert polygons in this primitive [group|/model/groups] into subdivision surfaces.

parameters.label: Enable Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigreversepolygons` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD supports an `orientation` attribute on mesh primitives that indicates whether polygons have a left-handed or right-handed ordering, while SOP geometry is always left-handed ordering. When this option is on, the importer always reorders vertices (and associated primvars) to be right-handed. This is useful when round tripping right-handed oriented polygons from USD into SOPs and back into USD. The data is always converted to a left handed ordering when importing it into SOPs. If you imported the polygons back into USD without this option, they would be left-handed, unlike the original.

parameters.label: Enable Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Missing Widths__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsetmissingwidths` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD has a fallback value of 1.0 for the width of curves and points, which is often far wider/thicker than desired. If the SOP geometry does not explicitly author `width`/`pscale` data, this control can be used instead to explicitly author a USD value.

parameters.label: Author Time Samples
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Whether values imported from SOPs should be authored as default values for the corresponding USD attributes, or as a time sample (at the time in the timeline). (When the USD system is asked for an attribute value, it returns the default if no time samples exist on the attribute. Otherwise it returns a value interpolated from the time sample data.)

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Default Primitive__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsetdefaultprim` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Authors the [default primitive|/solaris/usd#default_prim] metadata for the layer containing the imported geometry, if there is an __Import Path Prefix__. The default primitive is set to the root of the prefix path (for example, `/a` if the prefix path is `/a/b/c`).

parameters.label: Enable Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Topology Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtopology` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Controls whether USD topology attributes should be authored as time sampled or default values.

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars.

parameters.label: Enable Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Indexed Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigindexattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called `primvars:<<name>>`, and an array of indices into those values called `primvars:<<name>>:indices`). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Element Array__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus __Import as Single Value__) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Value__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigscalarconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to __Import as Single Element Array__, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, `vector3f` instead of `vector3f[]`).

parameters.label: Enable Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Boolean Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigboolattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `bool`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 32-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguintattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 64-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguint64attribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint64`.

parameters.label: Enable Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Asset Path Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigassetpathattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `asset`.

parameters.label: Enable Relationship Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Relationship Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigrelationshipattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Relationship Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to [relationships|/solaris/glossary#relationship].

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Default Values__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigstaticattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to always author as default values for USD primvars (never time samples). This is the list of exclusions when __Author Time Samples__ is set to __If Not Specifically Excluded__.

parameters.label: Enable Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subset Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpartitionattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which SOP string or integer attributes represent subsets of the geometry. The importer puts elements with the same value for this attribute into their own geometry subsets. Each attribute's subsets are added to a subset family (named from the original attribute) which indicates that the subsets are related. The subset family's type is set to `partition` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting and that every element of the primitive appears in a subset. If there are elements with empty string values (which are not added to a subset), the family type is instead set to `nonOverlapping` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting but some elements do not appear in a subset. The family's type is authored as an attribute on the parent primitive, for example `subsetFamily:shop_materialpath:familyType`. Subsets can be created from point or primitive partition attributes on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points. The importer will try to set the subset name to the attribute value, but may need to change the name to make it a legal USD primitive name. The importer stores the raw attribute value on the geometry subset prim as Custom Data with the key `partitionValue`.

parameters.label: Enable Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.label_norm: enable prefix subsets with attribute name
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigprefixpartitionsubsets` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When creating subsets from __Subset Attributes__, the subsets are named by combining the attribute name with the partition attribute's value (a string or integer). This avoids name collisions when multiple partition attributes contain the same values, but can be undesirable if precise control of the subset names is required. For string attributes, if this option is turned off, the attribute values are directly used as the subset names.

parameters.label: Enable Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subset Groups__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsubsetgroups` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of group names/patterns specifying SOP [groups|/model/groups]. SOP elements in each group are imported as a geometry subset, named for the group. Subsets can be created from point or primitive groups on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points.

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data

Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtranslateuvtost` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST

parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute `uv` into a USD primvar called `primvars:st`. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. entries.title: Scope
entries.summary: Creates a "scope" primitive. Scope is the simplest form of grouping, and does not have a transform. Scopes can be useful for organizing the scene tree.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Action
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Whether this node should create new prims, or edit existing prims. In addition, the `Force Edit` option can be chosen to cause this node to ignore the `houdini:editable` attribute on prims, and always edit the specified attributes. This is in contrast to the `Edit` mode which will trigger a warning and not set attributes on prims with the `houdini:editable` attribute set to `false`.

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Create__ mode, this lets you control where in the scene graph to create the prim(s). The default is usually `/$OS`. This creates a primitive at the root level with the same name as the node (for example, `/tube1`). This is a useful default for preventing naming conflicts, but terrible for organization. You should try to remember to change the __Primitive Path__ to a better value when you create prims. For example, instead of naming models after the node that created them, you might want to name them after the geometry inside, and organize them under a `/Models` branch. The __Create Primitives__ section contains basic controls for how to create the new prim(s).

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, the node has a __Primitive Pattern__ parameter. This lets you specify the prim(s) the node should operate on. You can click the select button beside the text box to select the primitives from the scene graph tree. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection.

parameters.label: Allowed Primitive Types
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: In __Edit__ mode, only prims that match one of the specified primitive types (or API schemas) can be modified by this node. Leave this parameter empty to permit editing any primitive type.

parameters.label: Initialize Parameters
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Changes the state of all control menu parameters to __Do Nothing__, so that this node will not apply any changes. Also grabs the current values of each property from the first __Primitives__ match, and sets the values of the corresponding parameters to match. This means that changing any parameter's control menu to __Set or Create__ mode will set the property to its current value, making it easier to apply changes to an existing value rather than setting a brand new value. With __Rebuild Render-Specific Parameters__ you reset all parameters from render-specific tabs to their default values for the specific node. If you want to reset the parameters for the entire scene, you can also open the top-level __Render__ menu and choose __Rebuild All Render-Specific LOP Parameters__.

parameters.label: For example
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: * If you want to create a new cube primitive at `/world/objects/cube1` on an empty stage: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Define__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __Xform__. * If you want to override the radius of a sphere at `/world/objects/sphere1`: Set __Primitive Specifier__ to __Over__, and the __Parent Primitive Type__ to __None__. This makes sure the primitive types of any existing ancestor prims are not be modified by this node.

parameters.label: Primitive Count
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The number of primitives to create.

parameters.label: Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: Set all created prims to have this [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind].

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: The USD operator to use when creating the new prims.

parameters.label: Class Ancestor
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If __Primitive Specifier__ is __Define__ or __Over__, this parameter will cause some ancestor primitives to be authored with a specifier of __Class__. This makes it easy to create an __Over__ or __Define__ within a __Class__ without having to use two separate nodes. When __Primitive Specifier__ is __Class__, this parameter is disabled because the entire primitive hierarchy is already authored as __Class__ primitives.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Create Primitives
parameters.description: If any parents of a path in __Primitive Paths__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.

If you are doing something like choosing a variant set using a random number generator, it's easier to deal with variant sets by their index rather than their name.

parameters.label: Variant Set Index
parameters.description: When __Choose Variant Set by Index__ is on, the index of the variant set (in an alphabetically sorted list of variant sets on the primitive).

parameters.label: Choose Variant Name by Index
parameters.description: When this is on, you specify the variant using a number representing the index of a variant in the alphabetically sorted list of variants, rather than a name. If you are doing something like choosing a variant using a random number generator, it's easier to deal with variant sets by their index rather than their name.

parameters.label: Variant Name
parameters.description: If not choosing the variant by index, this parameter is the name of the variant that should be selected within the specified variant set. If this value is an empty string, any existing variant selection specified in the active layer will be cleared. This will "reveal" any variant selection opinions authored in weaker layers. If this value is set to the special string `<block>`, an explicit empty variant selection will be made, blocking any variant selection opinions from weaker layers, leaving the chosen set without any variant selected.  If this is set to a list of variant names (space or comma- separated), then this will use the first one that matches a valid variant name in each prim's variant set.

parameters.label: Variant Name Index

entries.summary: Part of the [Shot Builder Toolset|/solaris/shotbuilder], outputs USD data and /or rendered images to your project.

parameters.label: Save to Disk
parameters.description: With __Multi-Shot__ on, this executes the internal TOP Network to output all requested shots. Otherwise, this will output the current __Shot Context__

parameters.label: Cancel
parameters.description: With __Multi-Shot__ on, this cancels any currently running __Shot Output__ TOP Network.

parameters.label: Valid Frame Range
parameters.description: See [saving animation|#anim] above for more information.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.description: When __Valid Frame Range__ is __Render Frame Range__ or __Render Frame Range (strict)__, the start and end frames (inclusive) and interval.

parameters.label: Preroll/Postroll/Inc
parameters.description: When __Valid Frame Range__ is __Render Frame Range From Stage__, the number of frames before and after the stage's official start and end frame to save, and the interval between time samples.

parameters.label: Render with Take
parameters.description: Render with the parameter values stored in this [take|/basics/takes].

parameters.label: LOP Path
parameters.description: Node path to the LOP node whose output this node will render. If this node is in a LOP network and you connect its input, the node disables and ignores this parameter, and renders the data from the input instead.

parameters.label: Output File
parameters.description: The "top-level" USD file to write the root layer to. Other layers that have file path metadata set will be written to their own USD files. A default output processor (see below) translates external file references in nodes to be relative to this file's directory, as is recommended.

parameters.label: Save Style
parameters.description: This node can apply some transformations to the layer stack before writing out files. These transformations do not affect the final composed stage, only the number of layer files generated.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers authored above Layer Break nodes from being written to disk by this ROP. This allows a Layer Break node to dictate which portions of the LOP Network are to be saved. Disabling this option allows this behavior to be overridden, forcing the full stage authored by the LOP network to be written to disk. This may be used for debugging purposes, or to write a complete scene to disk for rendering.

parameters.label: Strip Post-Layers
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers added using the [Hom:hou.LopNetwork#editablePostLayer] method from being written to disk. With this option disabled, these post-layers are flattened into the layer __Output File__ layer.

parameters.label: Flush Data After Each Frame
parameters.description: When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See [saving animation|#anim] above.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated.

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See [Filter Time Samples|#filtertimesamples]

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using __Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References)__ to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: If you use the [Load Layer LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer] to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. Turn this on to flatten layers from disk as if they were anonymous layers. This can be useful for generating more portable USD layers that rely on a minimal number of external layers. It can also be used to "harden" the sublayered files on disk in their current state if they may be changing, but you are generating a USD file for archiving purposes and do not want it to reflect any upcoming changes to the external files.

parameters.label: Flatten SOP Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapse Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, layers generated by importing data from SOPs with [SOP Import|Node:lop/sopimport] are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. parameters.label: Save Style
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: This node can apply some transformations to the layer stack before writing out files. These transformations do not affect the final composed stage, only the number of layer files generated.

parameters.label: Strip Layers Above Layer Breaks
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers authored above Layer Break nodes from being written to disk by this ROP. This allows a Layer Break node to dictate which portions of the LOP Network are to be saved. Disabling this option allows this behavior to be overridden, forcing the full stage authored by the LOP network to be written to disk. This may be used for debugging purposes, or to write a complete scene to disk for rendering.

parameters.label: Strip Post-Layers
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Enable this option to prevent layers added using the [Hom:hou.LopNetwork#editablePostLayer] method from being written to disk. With this option disabled, these post-layers are flattened into the layer __Output File__ layer.

parameters.label: Flush Data After Each Frame
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: When this is on, the node writes out each frame's data to disk before cooking the LOP Network to generate the next frame of data. When this is off (the default), the node cooks the data for all frames into memory and writes out the animated files all at once. Turning on this option ensures that only a single frame worth of data is in RAM at any one time, allowing arbitrarily large USD files to be created. But saving each frame can be slightly slower, and the generated files may be larger because of the way USD files append new data to an existing file. See [saving animation|#anim] above.

parameters.label: Track Primitive Existence to Set Visibility
parameters.label_norm: track primitive existence to set visibility
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: LOP networks may generate vastly different scene graphs from one frame to the next. When combining these scene graphs over a frame range into a single animated scene graph, the set of primitives in the combined scene graph will be the union of the primitives in each frame's hierarchy. But if a mesh appears at frame 50, this generally means that it is desired for this mesh to not be visible prior to frame 50. Enable this option to cause this node to track a list of all primitives at each frame, and automatically author animated visibility attributes for any primitives that are added to or removed from the scene graph over time. This gives the appearance of primitives being added and removed over time. Only subclasses of `UsdGeomImageable` primitives will be tracked this way, since these are the only USD primitive types which respect the visibility attribute.

parameters.label: Use Network Drive Safe Save (Windows Only)
parameters.label_norm: use network drive safe save (windows only)
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: When running on Windows, the USD library often has issues saving layers to network mounted drives when those layers are currently loaded into a USD stage. This can make it impossible to overwrite a USD layer that is in use, even by the current Houdini session. This option works around this issue by having the USD ROP mute each layer right before ti is saved to disk (but only when running under Windows - on Linux and MacOS this parameter has no effect). Once the layer is saved, it is un-muted. This approach incurs a performance penalty as any stages using this layer will be recomposed twice instead of once. But in some settings this can make the save process much more robust.

parameters.label: Filter Time Samples
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: When to remove time samples that lie outside the frame(s) of the USD being exported, potentially reducing the size of the data generated.

parameters.label: Extra Frames
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: How much to expand the window of time samples to keep during filtering. Note that, in addition to any extra frames specified, there is always one additional extra sample included both before and after the window, to better support motion blur. Generally this value can safely be left at 0 (the default) and typically only needs changing when using multi-segment motion blur. See [Filter Time Samples|#filtertimesamples]

parameters.label: Files to Save
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: A list of patterns matching which files the node is _allowed_ to save. If this is blank (the default), the node saves all files. You can use this, for example, to avoid rewriting layer files that you know will never change.

parameters.label: Error Saving Layers with Implicit Paths
parameters.label_norm: error saving layers with implicit paths
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the node errors if it would otherwise write an anonymous in-memory layer (that is, a layer with no file path metadata) to disk. You will usually only turn this off if you are using __Save Style > Separate Layers (Preserve All Sublayers and References)__ to write out every layer separate for debugging purposes.

parameters.label: Save Updates to Modified Files From Disk
parameters.label_norm: save updates to modified files from disk
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: If you use the [Load Layer LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer] to bring a layer onto the stage, this "editable" version of the layer on disk has metadata marking it as originally coming from disk, rather than being created from scratch by LOPs. When this is on, layers created this way are saved to disk just like any other layer with file path metadata. Turning this off prevents saving these layers to disk. This can be useful if you never want these "edited from disk" layers to overwrite the original files, or at least prevent overwriting them until you are certain the output of the LOP network is correct, when you can allow the edited layers to be written to disk.

parameters.label: Flatten File Layers
parameters.heading: Extra files
parameters.description: When __Save Style__ is __Flatten Implicit Layers (Collapes Implicit Sublayers, Preserve References)__, files loaded from disk with a Sublayer LOP are not considered anonymous layers, and so are not composed down. parameters.label: Render All Frames with a Single Process
parameters.label_norm: render all frames with a single process
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Render all frames with a single process. Default is off, which causes a new render process to be invoked to render each frame. To render multiple frames with a single process, the render process renders an image, then advances the time on the scene and renders the next image (just like how the Solaris viewport plays back animation). If there is a lot of data shared between frames, this can render significantly faster compared to rendering a single frame per process. If the invocation of a render process is disabled, this setting still affects the behavior of the USD save process. If each frame's USD is being authored to a separate file or directory, this setting has no effect. But if every frame is configured to author the USD files to the same location, leaving this option off will overwrite the USD data with each frame, leaving only the final frame's data in the USD files on disk. Enable this option to have each frame's data merged with all the previous frames' data, resulting in a USD file that contains data for all the frames.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Choose the __Output Mode__. # __Publish__ mode, only updates to the USD data in your project will be output.  Any layers that have not changed since their last output will be by-passed, only new data is written out. # __Render__ mode, only the images will be written out.  No USD data will be written back to your project.  Instead, it is written to a temporary location for use in the render. # __Render and Publish__ mode, first the USD data is written out to your project, then that data is used to render out the images.

parameters.label: Multi-Shot
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Toggle __Multi-Shot__ mode on/off. With __Multi-Shot__ mode __on__, all shots that match the pattern provided in __Shots__ will be output via the internal TOP Network. With __Multi-Shot__ mode __off__, the current shot context will be used for output.

parameters.label: Enable GPU Delegates
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: `husk` normally doesn't support delegates which require a GPU rendering context for rendering.  This allows `husk` to run on headless machines.  Enabling this option will cause `husk` to try to create a GPU rendering context so that delegates like `HdStormRendererPlugin` can be used as delegates. A GPU rendering context allows a device or software to send commands to the GPU and control the state of a GPU. A context requires a GPU and the appropriate drivers and libraries installed. However, machines on render farms often don't have a GPU rendering context.

parameters.label: Render Settings
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Scene graph pattern specifying the `RenderSettings` prims to render with. Husk supports running multiple renders with different render settings prims from one process. When evaluating this pattern with __Render existing file__ enabled, the specified file is opened as a USD stage with a population mask limiting the stage to the `/Render` branch, and the pattern is evaluated on that stage. If this is blank, the node looks for default render settings on the root prim. If the root prim has no render settings, the node will use default settings.

parameters.label: Render Passes
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: With __Multi-Shot__ mode __on__, each available render pass for each requested shot that matche this pattern will be output.  This will create a PDG work item per shot per matching renderpass.  See Render Pass for how each matched render pass is used.

parameters.label: Render Pass
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Scene graph pattern to the `RenderPass` prims to use for specifying object visibility etc. Husk supports running multiple renders with different render passes (each specifying their own render settings prim) from one process. If this is blank, the default setting, the render will continue with no pass (i.e., all contents will be rendered).

parameters.label: Override Output Image
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: If this is not blank, render to this file path instead of the output specified in the `RenderSettings` prim. When starting a new render process for each frame, this parameter can use standard Houdini variables such as `$F4` to specify unique per-frame image files. When `Render All Frames with a Single Process` is enabled, this parameter must pass an un-expanded frame specifier (such as `$F4` or `<FF>`) to `husk`. This may require the use of a backslash to prevent variable expansion when evaluating the parameter.

parameters.label: Override Resolution
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Override the resolution by either scaling the USD resolution by a percentage or by specifying a specific resolution.

parameters.label: Resolution Scale
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Specify a scale (as a percentage) for the output resolution.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.heading: Context options
parameters.description: Specify a resolution explicitly. See the [USD Render render node|Node:out/usdrender].

floor.definition: summary AND >=1 documented parameter with a non-empty description  (I0-FLOOR, adopted verbatim)

deprecation.tier: VERIFIED-DOC + VERIFIED-RUNTIME (union, sides recorded separately — never collapsed to one boolean)

entries.title: Shot Split
entries.summary: Passes through the input node's stage, but may alter the shot context option depending on which output branch is being cooked.

parameters.label: Create New Layer
parameters.description: Turning on this option causes this node to create a new sublayer on an existing __Parent layer__, rather than directly editing a specific __Target layer__ in the local layer stack. Adjusts the node interface to reveal parameters specific to creating a new layer, rather than editing an existing layer.

parameters.label: Target Layer
parameters.description: Like the [Edit Layer Begin|Node:lop/editlayerbegin] node, this parameter specifies which layer within the sublayer stack of the input stage should be affected by nodes following this one. Only visible if __Create new layer__ is turned off.

parameters.label: Clear Source Layer
parameters.description: Turning on this option causes the __Target layer__ to be cleared before passing the stage to the nodes connected the outputs of this node. Only visible if __Create new layer__ is turned off.

parameters.label: Parent Layer
parameters.description: The layer to which a new sublayer will be added. This will be a layer in the stage's current layer stack. Only visible if __Create new layer__ is turned on.

parameters.label: New Layer Index
parameters.description: The position of the new layer in the __Parent layer's__ sublayer list. Only visible if __Create new layer__ is turned on.

parameters.label: New Layer
parameters.description: The path to which this new sublayer will be saved by a [ROP USD Output LOP|Node:lop/rop_usd]. Only visible if __Create new layer__ is turned on.

parameters.label: Outputs
parameters.description: Specifies the number of output connections this node should have. Each output corresponds to a different set of shots.

parameters.description: Provides a way to override the automatic input selection based on the current shot context option.

entries.title: Simulation Proxy
entries.summary: Generates low-poly collison geometry suitable for physical simulation and creates a proxy relationship to the original model.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: The primitive(s) the node should operate on. You can drag primitives from the scene graph tree pane into this textbox to add their paths, or click the [Smallicon:BUTTONS/reselect] __Reselect__ button beside the text box to select the primitives in the viewer, or ((Ctrl))-click the __Reselect__ button to choose prims from a pop-up tree window. You can also use [primitive patterns|/solaris/pattern] for advanced matching, including matching all prims in a collection (using `/path/to/prim.collection:<<name>>`). You can drag and drop a specific (or multiple specific) USD prim(s) from the Scene Graph Tree into the window to run validation on only these USD primitives.

parameters.label: Traversal
parameters.description: Specifies how to find the USD prims to extract.

parameters.label: Exclude Primitives with Existing Proxy
parameters.description: If a prim selected in __Primitives__ already has proxy geometry, ignore it.

parameters.label: Display Proxy
parameters.description: Display the generated proxy geometry in the viewport. See [Tips|#tips] above.

parameters.label: Load from Disk
parameters.heading: File Cache
parameters.description: Load the proxy geometry from the file specified below.

parameters.label: Geometry File
parameters.heading: File Cache
parameters.description: File path to save the generated geometry to. Use `.bgeo.sc` as the file extension.

parameters.label: Save to Disk
parameters.heading: File Cache
parameters.description: Click to regenerate the proxy geometry and save it to the file path above.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Polygon Reduction
parameters.description: Uses [PolyReduce|Node:sop/polyreduce] to produce a proxy with fewer polygons while keeping the same general shape.

parameters.label: Percent to Keep
parameters.heading: Polygon Reduction
parameters.description: The percentage of polygons to keep. For example, if the original model has 1000 polygons, setting this to `10` will generate a proxy with 100 polygons.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: VDB Resurface
parameters.description: Converts geometry to a VDB surface volume and then back to polygons. This is a good method for getting clean/simple surfaces out of very complex/bumpy geometries like woven fabrics or baskets (it essentially "blurs" out small details).

parameters.label: Voxel Size
parameters.heading: VDB Resurface
parameters.description: The voxel size of the VDB surface, in world units. The larger the voxel size, the chunkier the proxy will be.

parameters.label: Dilation
parameters.heading: VDB Resurface
parameters.description: The distance in voxels to dilate & erode the VDB surface by. You can use this to close any gaps and small holes in the geometry for a cleaner, smoother surface.

parameters.label: Post Percent to Keep
parameters.heading: VDB Resurface
parameters.description: This node automatically uses [PolyReduce SOP|Node:sop/polyreduce] on the surface generated from the VDB volume, since it tends to have many polygons, even though the overall shape is simpler. This is the percentage of polygons to keep. For example, if the surface has 10000 polygons, setting this to `5` will generate a proxy with 500 polygons.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Convex Hull
parameters.description: Turn meshes into convex hulls, which are ideally suited for physics simulation.

parameters.label: Granularity
parameters.heading: Convex Hull
parameters.description: The Bullet RBB solver is much more efficient with purely convex collision geometry than with complex/concave geometry. If the model can be well represented by a "skin" stretched around its outside, choose __Convex Hull Per Primitive__. If the original model has space between disconnected pieces, choose __Convex Hull per Connected Piece__. If your model is concave, you can try using __Decompose Each Connected Piece__ to see if the computer can approximate the original shape using multiple convex shapes (this can benefit from using a [VDB Resample SOP|Node:sop/vdbresample] to blur out details first).

parameters.label: Max Concavity
parameters.heading: Convex Hull
parameters.description: When __Granularity__ is __Decompose Each Connected Piece__, the maximum distance from a point on the geometry to its closest convex hull edge (in world units). Lowering this may give you a better approximation of a concave original, but increases complexity of the proxy.

parameters.label: Enable
parameters.heading: Final Polygon Reduction
parameters.description: Uses a [PolyReduce SOP|Node:sop/polyreduce] on the results any enabled steps above. This can be useful for a final cleanup for __Convex Hull__, which can sometimes leave behind useless co-planar polygons.

parameters.label: Post Percent to Keep
parameters.heading: Final Polygon Reduction
parameters.description: The percentage of polygons to keep.
