entries.title: Split Primitive
entries.summary: Splits USD geometry prims into child primitives based on geometry subsets or primvar values.

parameters.label: Primitives
parameters.description: A USD path or space-separated list of paths of prims to split.

parameters.label: Subset Attribute Name
parameters.description: When __Split Mode__ is __Geometry Subset__, the name of the geometry subset attribute by which to split the primitives.

parameters.label: Primvar Name
parameters.description: When __Split Mode__ is __Primvar__, the name of the primvar by which to split the primitives.

parameters.label: Import Frame
parameters.description: This is the frame at which to cook the LOP node and sample the stage. When importing animated geometry, this could be set to `$FF`.

parameters.label: Sublayer Style
parameters.description: Only available when __Load As Reference__ is off. By default, geometry imported from SOPs is treated like geometry imported from a file on disk: you can only edit it by applying stronger [opinions|/solaris/glossary#compose] on top. Changing this parameter, allows this node to put the geometry in the _active layer_, so it can be modified by LOP nodes connected to this node's output. The node does this by copying the contents generated from the SOP geometry into an anonymous in-memory USD layer. This is slower, but provides more options for how many USD layers you need to write to disk, and what goes in each layer. This is similar to the operation of a [Load Layer for Editing LOP|Node:lop/loadlayer]. * The __Copy SOP Layer Into New Active Layer__ style creates a new active layer into which the SOP layer contents are copied. * The __Merge SOP Layer Into Existing Active Layer__ style copies the SOP layer contents into the input node's active layer, resulting in no new layers on the stage.

parameters.label: Enable NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __NURBS Curves__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfignurbscurves` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: NURBS Curves
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS curve primitives.

parameters.label: Enable NURBS Surfaces
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __NURBS Surfaces__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfignurbssurfs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: NURBS Surfaces
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: What to do with NURBS surface primitives.

parameters.label: Enable Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Kind Authoring__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigkindschema` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Kind Authoring
parameters.heading: Primitive Definition
parameters.description: How to assign [kinds|/solaris/glossary#kind] to imported prims.

parameters.label: Enable Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.label_norm: enable treat polygons as subdivision surfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpolygonsassubd` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: For polygon meshes that are not already tagged with a subdivision scheme, author a `subdivisionScheme` attribute set to `catmullClark`. This will convert them to subdivision surfaces.

parameters.label: Enable Subdivision Group
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subdivision Group__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsubdgroup` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subdivision Group
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: If __Treat Polygons as Subdivision Surfaces__ is on, only convert polygons in this primitive [group|/model/groups] into subdivision surfaces.

parameters.label: Enable Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigreversepolygons` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Reverse Polygon Vertex Ordering
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD supports an `orientation` attribute on mesh primitives that indicates whether polygons have a left-handed or right-handed ordering, while SOP geometry is always left-handed ordering. When this option is on, the importer always reorders vertices (and associated primvars) to be right-handed. This is useful when round tripping right-handed oriented polygons from USD into SOPs and back into USD. The data is always converted to a left handed ordering when importing it into SOPs. If you imported the polygons back into USD without this option, they would be left-handed, unlike the original.

parameters.label: Enable Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Missing Widths__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsetmissingwidths` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Missing Widths
parameters.heading: Geometry Handling
parameters.description: USD has a fallback value of 1.0 for the width of curves and points, which is often far wider/thicker than desired. If the SOP geometry does not explicitly author `width`/`pscale` data, this control can be used instead to explicitly author a USD value.

parameters.label: Author Time Samples
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Whether values imported from SOPs should be authored as default values for the corresponding USD attributes, or as a time sample (at the time in the timeline). (When the USD system is asked for an attribute value, it returns the default if no time samples exist on the attribute. Otherwise it returns a value interpolated from the time sample data.)

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Default Primitive__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsetdefaultprim` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Default Primitive
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Authors the [default primitive|/solaris/usd#default_prim] metadata for the layer containing the imported geometry, if there is an __Import Path Prefix__. The default primitive is set to the root of the prefix path (for example, `/a` if the prefix path is `/a/b/c`).

parameters.label: Enable Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Topology Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtopology` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Topology Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Controls whether USD topology attributes should be authored as time sampled or default values.

parameters.label: Enable Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars.

parameters.label: Enable Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Indexed Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigindexattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Indexed Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as indexed primvars. If a SOP attribute matches this pattern, the importer authors the primvar as an indexed array of values (that is, an array of values called `primvars:<<name>>`, and an array of indices into those values called `primvars:<<name>>:indices`). Preparing an indexed primvar can be expensive for attributes that are not integers or strings. You should only use indexed primvars where it is likely to result in significant savings in storage size due to a small number of unique values being used across a large number of components.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Element Array
parameters.label_norm: enable import as single element array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Element Array__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Element Array
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation (an array with a single value for the whole primitive), regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. Importing as a single element array (versus __Import as Single Value__) can be useful since it allows the primvar's interpolation to be overridden without changing the primvar's type.

parameters.label: Enable Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Import as Single Value__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigscalarconstantattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Import as Single Value
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as primvars with `Constant` interpolation and a single value for the whole primitive, regardless of whether the SOP geometry attribute is a point, primitive, or vertex attribute. If multiple values could be chosen for a particular USD primitive, the importer chooses the first value it encounters. This is the default behavior for how detail attributes are imported. This is similar to __Import as Single Element Array__, but the primvar's type is a scalar value instead of an array with a single element (for example, `vector3f` instead of `vector3f[]`).

parameters.label: Enable Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Boolean Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigboolattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Boolean Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `bool`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 32-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguintattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 32-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint`.

parameters.label: Enable Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Unsigned 64-bit Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfiguint64attribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Unsigned 64-bit Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which integer SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `uint64`.

parameters.label: Enable Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Asset Path Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigassetpathattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Asset Path Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to primvars of type `asset`.

parameters.label: Enable Relationship Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When enabled, the __Relationship Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigrelationshipattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure])

parameters.label: Relationship Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which string SOP attributes should be converted to [relationships|/solaris/glossary#relationship].

parameters.label: Enable Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Set Default Values__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigstaticattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Set Default Values
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to always author as default values for USD primvars (never time samples). This is the list of exclusions when __Author Time Samples__ is set to __If Not Specifically Excluded__.

parameters.label: Enable Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subset Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigpartitionattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subset Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying which SOP string or integer attributes represent subsets of the geometry. The importer puts elements with the same value for this attribute into their own geometry subsets. Each attribute's subsets are added to a subset family (named from the original attribute) which indicates that the subsets are related. The subset family's type is set to `partition` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting and that every element of the primitive appears in a subset. If there are elements with empty string values (which are not added to a subset), the family type is instead set to `nonOverlapping` to indicate that the subsets are non-intersecting but some elements do not appear in a subset. The family's type is authored as an attribute on the parent primitive, for example `subsetFamily:shop_materialpath:familyType`. Subsets can be created from point or primitive partition attributes on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points. The importer will try to set the subset name to the attribute value, but may need to change the name to make it a legal USD primitive name. The importer stores the raw attribute value on the geometry subset prim as Custom Data with the key `partitionValue`.

parameters.label: Enable Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.label_norm: enable prefix subsets with attribute name
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigprefixpartitionsubsets` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Prefix Subsets with Attribute Name
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When creating subsets from __Subset Attributes__, the subsets are named by combining the attribute name with the partition attribute's value (a string or integer). This avoids name collisions when multiple partition attributes contain the same values, but can be undesirable if precise control of the subset names is required. For string attributes, if this option is turned off, the attribute values are directly used as the subset names.

parameters.label: Enable Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Subset Groups__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigsubsetgroups` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Subset Groups
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of group names/patterns specifying SOP [groups|/model/groups]. SOP elements in each group are imported as a geometry subset, named for the group. Subsets can be created from point or primitive groups on SOP meshes, curves, tetrahedra, and points.

parameters.label: Enable USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __USD Custom Attributes__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigcustomattribs` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: USD Custom Attributes
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: A space-separated list of attribute names/patterns specifying the SOP attributes to import into USD as attributes (rather than primvars).

parameters.label: Enable Capture Weights
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Capture Weights__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigcaptureweights` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Capture Weights
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: Controls how capture weights (represented by the `boneCapture` SOP attribute) are translated. This does not affect agent primitives, which are always translated to UsdSkel.

parameters.label: Enable Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.label_norm: enable translate uv attribute to st
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, the __Translate UV Attribute to ST__ setting is used when translating the SOP geometry to USD. Otherwise, the parameter's default value is used unless a `usdconfigtranslateuvtost` detail attribute exists on the SOP geometry (for example, from the [USD Configure SOP|Node:sop/usdconfigure]).

parameters.label: Translate UV Attribute to ST
parameters.heading: Import Data
parameters.description: When turned on, converts the SOP vertex attribute `uv` into a USD primvar called `primvars:st`. Whether you need to turn this on depends on the renderer you are using and how your shaders are authored. If you are rendering with Karma, leave this off. (As of this writing there is no strict standard for texture coordinate naming in USD, but the use of `st` is a common convention, whereas in SOP geometry, using `uv` is the common convention.)

entries.title: Sublayer
entries.summary: Imports from USD files or other LOP node chains into as sublayers, or removes/replaces/reorders existing sublayers.

parameters.label: Load Payloads
parameters.heading: Parent Layer
parameters.description: When this option is on (the default), the payload loading configuration of the input stage is not changed. When this option is off, the stage's load mask will be modified to turn off all payload loading. Note that this will affect the loading of payloads anywhere in the stage, not just payloads loaded by the sublayers added by this node. Use the [Configure Stage LOP|Node:lop/configurestage] to have more control over which payloads are loaded on the stage.

parameters.label: Copy Layer Metadata to Stage Root Layer
parameters.label_norm: copy layer metadata to stage root layer
parameters.heading: Parent Layer
parameters.description: Layer metadata is not composed by USD following the normal rules. In order for values like the frames per second or up axis settings to apply to a USD stage, they must be set directly on the root layer of the stage. This means any layer metadata authored on a file being loaded by this node will not affect the stage level metadata. This options allow for the explicit copying of layer metadata from the first layer loaded by this node on to the stage's root layer. If multiple files are specified, it it always the first file that has its values copied to the root layer. The __Auto__ option for this parameter acts like a __Yes__ (copy the sublayer's metadata to the root layer) if there is no input connected to the first input of this node. Otherwise it behaves as a __No__ (does not affect the stage's root layer metadata).

parameters.label: Edit Root Layer
parameters.heading: Parent Layer
parameters.description: When this is on (the default), the new sublayers are added to the layer stack. This is usually what you want. When this is off, the content of the imported layers become sublayers of the active layer. Turning this on or off usually does not make a visible difference, but affects the priority given to opinions on the layers, and what content is in what layers when you [write USD to disk|/solaris/output].

parameters.label: Find Sublayers
parameters.heading: Parent Layer
parameters.description: A space-separated list of patterns that match layers by their "source file" metadata. This selects the layers for removal or reordering when you use the __Remove Found Sublayers__ or __Sublayer Position__ parameters below.

parameters.label: Remove Found Sublayers
parameters.heading: Parent Layer
parameters.description: Turn this on to remove any layers that match the patterns the __Find Sublayers__. This is useful if you want to _replace_ layers rather than just add them. For example, you may be editing a layer that has sublayers for animation, effects, and lighting. If your LOP network generates a new version of the effects layer, you would want to remove the existing effects layer and replace it with the new one.

parameters.label: Handle Missing Files

parameters.label: Sublayer Position

parameters.label: Position Index

entries.title: Surface Constraint
entries.summary: Constrain a prim to stick to a surface.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: Whether the source (the thing constrained to the surface) is a regular primitive, or a point instance. You *cannot* use a nested point instance as a source.

parameters.label: Source
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __Primitive__, the scene graph path to the prim to use.

parameters.label: Source Instances
parameters.heading: Source
parameters.description: When __Source Type__ is __PointInstancer__, the point instance to use, using `/<<path>>[<<instance_index>>]` syntax (for example, `/geometry/instancer[1]`).

parameters.label: Target Source
parameters.heading: Surface
parameters.description: Where to get the surface to stick to, either the node's __First Input__ or the __Second Input__.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.heading: Surface

parameters.description: The file path to an optional manifest file that specifies exactly which primitives and values should be brought in from the value clip files. Providing this file helps the USD framework optimize value clip resolution. See the USD documentation for more information about the manifest file.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.description: The frame on the current stage at which the value clip resolution should start.

parameters.label: First Clip Start Frame
parameters.description: When this is turned on, it sets a different start time within the value clip files. When this is turned off, the nodes uses the __Start Frame__ parameter as the clip start time.

parameters.label: Clip Time Scale
parameters.description: A scale factor applied to the time samples read in from the clip files.

parameters.label: Loop Until Frame
parameters.description: To create a repeating loop of the specified clip files, turn on this parameter and set it to the end frame of the loop. (USD does not natively support looping of animation or value clips, so this node explicitly authors all provided clips repeatedly until the requested loop end time is reached.)

parameters.label: Loop First and Last Frames Match
parameters.label_norm: loop first and last frames match
parameters.description: When looping an animation and using deformation or transform motion blur, it is important that the first and last frames of the looping animation are identical. In this case, enable this parameter so that the Value Clip LOP will author a "discontinuity" in the clip frames when looping from the end of the animation back to the start. This discontinuity prevents doubling up the display of the shared first and last frame, while also avoiding unexpected motion blur effects. With this option turned off, the `clip times` metadata for a looping 100 frame clip would be `(1, 1), (100, 100), (101, 1), (200, 100)`. In this data, the first number in each pair is the global stage frame number, and the second number is the frame within the clip that should be displayed for that global frame. So stage frame 1 is clip frame 1. Stage frame 100 is clip frame 100. Then stage frame 101 is back to clip frame 1. There are two problems here. First, if the clip's first and last frames are equal, frame 100 and frame 101 will be identical. But even worse, when rendering with motion blur (using a shutter open/close of +/- 0.5), rendering frame 101 will show data interpolated at frames 100.5 and 101.5. But USD does this by interpolating the _clip metadata_, not the data stored within the clips. So the frame 101.5 data will be as expected (showing data from clip frame 1.5). But the frame 100.5 data will be generated by grabbing the clip data at a frame half way between 100 and 1, which is frame 50.5. This is obviously very unexpected. With this option turned on, the same setup would author clip times of `(1, 1), (100, 100), (100, 1), (199, 100)`. Note that there are two different clip times authored for the single stage time of 100. This is the "discontinuity". But it eliminates both problems mentioned above. Stage frame 100 is clip frame 100, but stage frame 101 is now clip frame 2, eliminating the duplicated data. And for motion blur rendering frame 101, frame 100.5 will use the clip data at frame 0.5 and 1.5, exactly as expected. Note that, if the first and last frames of the clip are not equal, there is no way to get perfect looping, unless you use velocity motion blur which does not require grabbing interpolated data between frames. The first problem mentioned above (the duplicated frame at the end of the loop) will be avoided, but the clip metadata interpolation approach used by USD means sampling frame 100.5 will return data from the middle of the clip, resulting in incorrect motion blurring. ~~~

parameters.label: Number of Clips
parameters.description: You can add references to multiple clip files in one node. Set this to the number of clips to reference, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove clips.

parameters.label: Clip File or Sequence
parameters.description: The file path to this value clip file. This path can include number-sign (`#`) characters to perform numeric substitutions in a loop. For example, on disk there may be multiple files named `sim_0001.usd`, `sim_0002.usd` and so on, each containing one frame of animation. In this case you could use `sim_####.usd`. Numeric substitution only happens if __File Sequence count__ is turned on. See __File Sequence Count__, __File Index Start__, and __File Index Step__ below. For example, if you turn on __File Sequence Count__ and set * __Clip File or Sequence__ to `sim_####.usd`, * __File Index Start__ to `10`, * __File Index Step__ to `2`, and * __File Sequence Count__ to `3`, the node will try to load `sim_0010.usd`, `sim_0012.usd`, and `sim_0014.usd`. If you use numeric substitution, each file must have the same number of frames of animation (__File Duration__).

parameters.label: File Duration
parameters.description: The number of frames for which this clip file is active. If the __Clip File or Sequence__ path matched multiple files through numeric substitution, each clip file will get this same duration.

parameters.label: File Sequence Count
parameters.description: If you turn this on, the node evaluates the __Clip File or Sequence__ filename with numeric substitution this many times, starting the number at __File Index Start__ and increasing the number each time by __File Index Step__.

parameters.label: File Index Start
parameters.description: When __File Sequence Count__ is turned on, the node evaluates the __Clip File or Sequence__ multiple times with numeric substitution, starting at this number.

parameters.label: File Index Step
parameters.description: When __File Sequence Count__ is turned on, the node evaluates the __Clip File or Sequence__ multiple times with numeric substitution, incrementing the number by this many each time.

entries.title: Volume
entries.summary: References volume data on disk into a volume prim containing field prims.

parameters.label: Sampling Behavior
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Cooking this node can generate many USD time samples, rather than just a single time sample at the current time. This can be equivalent to having a [Cache LOP|Node:lop/cache] following this node, but it will evaluate much faster, and does not cache data from any other nodes. This allows animated data to be authored to USD without introducing a node time dependency which would then cause all following nodes to also be time dependent. This can vastly improve playback performance of some LOP Networks. In all sampling modes, if a parameter on this node does not vary with time, and does not rely on other time sampled data from the stage, only a single default value will be generated in USD for the corresponding attribute. USD time samples are only generated for parameters that may vary over time.

parameters.label: Start/End/Inc
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When the __Sampling behavior__ is __Sample Frame Range__, this parameter controls the number and spacing of base time samples to be generated by this node. The default values of this parameter are `@fstart`, `@fend`, and `@finc`. These values correspond to the start, end, and step size of the global Houdini animation settings when interacting with Houdini. When using a ROP node to generate a range of frames, these values correspond to the start, end, and increment values specified on the ROP node being executed. This default ensures that a USD file written to disk will contain time samples for exactly the frame range requested by the ROP (regardless of the Houdini animation settings).

parameters.label: Subframe Sampling
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: For each primary sample generated by this node, these parameters can cause additional samples to be generated around that primary sample time. This is most often used to ensure that accurate data exists at exactly the camera shutter open and close times, as well as at the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Shutter
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Controls the method used to specify the shutter open and close times relative to the primary sample times.

parameters.label: Shutter Open/Close
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Specify Manually__, these two offset values are added to the primary sample time to indicate the shutter open and close times. The open time should be less than or equal to zero, and the close time should be greater than or equal to zero.

parameters.label: Camera Prim
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When __Shutter__ is set to __Use Camera Prim__, this is the scene graph path of a camera prim on the input node's stage. The shutter open and close attribute values are read from this primitive.

parameters.label: Samples
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The number of subframe samples to create for each primary sample. These samples are evenly distributed between the shutter open and close times. Note that such an even distribution may or may not create a sample at exactly the primary sample time.

parameters.label: Always Include Frame Sample
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: When turned on, forces a sample to be created at exactly the primary sample time. If the __Samples__ value, together with the shutter open and close times, already place a sample at the primary sample time, turning on this option has no effect. Otherwise, this option causes an addition sample to be added. This means that the actual number of samples per primary sample may in fact be one more than the number specified in the __Samples__ parameter. ~~~

parameters.label: Primitive Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Create the main volume primitive at this scene graph path.

parameters.label: Primitive Kind
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Set this as the new volume prim's [kind|/solaris/glossary#kind]. The default is None.

parameters.label: Parent Primitive Type
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If any parents of the path in __Primitive Path__ do not exist, this node will automatically create them. In this case, it will create parent nodes of this type.

parameters.label: Primitive Specifier
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: Determines the USD [specifier|/solaris/glossary#specifiers] set on the volume primitive and any ancestor primitives created by this LOP.

parameters.label: Generate Errors For Missing Files
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: If any volume files cannot be found or cannot be loaded, this node will generate an error, causing all downstream nodes to also error. Turn off this option to generate warnings instead. This is only recommended in the early stages of a project where the integrity of the output does not need to be validated. ~~~

parameters.label: Files
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: This node can reference multiple files as fields of a single volume. Set this to the number of fields to read, or click the plus and minus buttons to add or remove field file references.

parameters.label: File Path
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: The location of the volume file on disk. USD is not capable of representing volumes currently. It can only point to volumes stored as separate files on disk. These files can be `BGEO` _or_ `VDB` when working _within_ Houdini and using a Houdini render delegate. If you want to use the volume data with non-Houdini processes, then you'll need to save the volume data as `VDB` files.

parameters.label: Fields
parameters.heading: Frame Range/Subframes
parameters.description: A space separated list of field names (as they appear in the file) to read. You can use patterns to match multiple names. ~~~

parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: When a third input is not attached, a global blend is applied between the 2 inputs.

parameters.label: Blend Factor
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: Globally blends between input one (0) and two (1).

parameters.label: Input 1 Weight
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: If using blend weights, this specifies the factor to multiply input 1 by.

parameters.label: Input 2 Weight
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: This specifies the factor to multiply input 2 by.

parameters.label: Normalize Weights
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: If on, the weights will always be scaled to sum up to 1.

parameters.label: Blend Mask
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: If a third input is used to control the blending, this menu selects the plane or component to use as the blend mask. Black is input 1, white is input 2.

parameters.label: Invert Blend Mask
parameters.heading: Blend
parameters.description: If on, black is input 2, while white is input 1.

parameters.label: Overview
parameters.heading: Merge
parameters.description: These parameters specify how to build the output sequence when there are differences between the input sequences.

parameters.label: Plane Merge
parameters.heading: Merge
parameters.description: If the planes in the inputs differ, this specifies what the output planes should be.

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.heading: Merge
parameters.description: If the raster depth for a given plane differs between inputs, this specifies what the output raster depth for the plane should be.

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.heading: Merge
parameters.description: If the frame ranges of the inputs differ, this determines what the output range should be.

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.heading: Merge
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines what the output frame rate should be.

parameters.label: Frame Match
parameters.heading: Merge
parameters.description: If the frame rates of the inputs differ, this determines which input frame to pick when the cook time doesn't reside on a frame boundary.

entries.title: Blur
entries.summary: Blurs an image.

parameters.label: X/Y Filter
parameters.heading: Blur
parameters.description: Defines the blur kernel function.

parameters.label: Size
parameters.heading: Blur
parameters.description: Defines the diameter of the blur for both X and Y.

parameters.label: Y Size
parameters.heading: Blur
parameters.description: Turn on to adjust the diameter of the blur for Y independently of X ('Size' now controls X Size).

parameters.label: Units
parameters.heading: Blur
parameters.description: Defines the units that the diameter of the blur is expressed in.

parameters.label: Per-Pixel Blur
parameters.heading: Blur
parameters.description: If on, the mask affects the diameter of the blur at each pixel, rather than just blending the input with the output. This produces much more realistic blur transitions for grayscale masks, at a significant performance expense. The float value specifies the kernel size tolerance. By default this is set to 0.1, so only kernels evenly divisible by 0.1 will be used. Higher values blur faster, but tend to introduce ringing artifacts. Set to zero for completely accurate blurs (very slow for floating point masks).

parameters.label: Fast Blur
parameters.heading: Blur
parameters.description: If on, the blur is done using a faster approximation technique. This option is only supported for Box, Bartlett (Cone) and Gaussian filters. The error is generally less than 1%, though for small filter widths (<10) it can be more significant (5-7%). Images with extremely high dynamic ranges may have higher error. For large filter sizes (1000's), this technique is orders of magnitude faster than the mathematically accurate blurs.

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.heading: Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces.

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified).

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input.

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.

entries.title: Color
entries.summary: Creates a constant color image.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The color of the plane. The 4th component is interpreted as alpha and will affect the alpha plane.

parameters.label: Component 4
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The value of the 4th component, in the case where the plane is a 4 element vector.

parameters.label: Scalar
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The value of Luminance, Depth and Single channel Mask planes. The mask parameters control the mask applied when a node is connected to the mask input. The Effect Amount parameter is always available, whether a mask is connected or not.

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask. Parameters relating to the structure of the image generated, including Resolution, Pixel Aspect Ratio and Raster Depth.

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane.

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory.

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even)

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.heading: Color
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.heading: Color

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Color Wheel
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).

parameters.label: Frame Scope

parameters.label: Frame Range

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff

parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect

parameters.label: Point Distance
parameters.heading: CornerRamp

parameters.heading: CornerRamp

parameters.label: Point `[num]`
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The (u,v) location of this ramp point.

parameters.label: Color
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The color of this ramp point.

parameters.label: Weight
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The weight of a point determines how much it contributes to the ramp. The point weight is relative to all other points' weights (so if all the weights are 2, the ramp would appear the same as if they were all 1). Increasing a point's weight makes a larger area of effect in the ramp. Setting the weight to zero removes the point from the ramp altogether. The mask parameters control the mask applied when a node is connected to the mask input. The Effect Amount parameter is always available, whether a mask is connected or not.

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this multiplies the output by a constant amount (0 = black, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.

parameters.label: Mask Plane
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask. Parameters relating to the structure of the image generated, including Resolution, Pixel Aspect Ratio and Raster Depth.

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. Many effect filters that have parameters that represent width and height will have the width scaled appropriately (such as Blur, Defocus, Expand).

parameters.label: Image Planes
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: Specifies the plane(s) to generate. Color and Alpha will always be present, but the generator does not always have to write to them. The list of planes is all the ones Houdini recognizes as special. Other planes can be added with the 'Custom Planes' parameter. C, A (C:rgb A): Color and Alpha C, A (C:rgb A:rgb): Color and 3-channel Alpha

parameters.label: Add Plane
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: When a generator is connected to an input, it generates a Mask plane by default. This parameter determines which planes are generated in this case. The list of planes to generate are the same as 'Image Planes'. In addition, if the plane already exists in the input sequence, one of the following operations will be performed to combine the new plane.

parameters.label: Custom Planes
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane

parameters.label: Raster Depth
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The byte format of the image. Higher bit depths provide better color resolution and range at the expense of memory.

parameters.label: Black/White Points
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The integer formats (8, 16 and 32 bit) can specify the raw values that the black and white points occur at. The white point must always be higher than the black point. The minimum and maximum values for the black and white points

parameters.label: Interlacing
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: Controls the ability to generate images that are compatible with interlaced images. If you are manipulating the generated output with a filter that uses neighboring pixels (like Blur or Expand), it is recommended that you do not use Black Interlaced, as the filter will use the black scanlines as well. The second menu determines which scanlines are in which fields (odd,even)

parameters.label: Override Global Range
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: If off, the global animation range is used as the frame range. If on, the frame range of the sequence can be specified in the following parameters.

parameters.label: Still Image
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: A still image is time-invariant. It exists at every frame. If off, the Start Frame and Length are used to determine the frame range.

parameters.label: Start Frame
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Length

parameters.description: The length of the sequence (number of frames in the sequence).

parameters.label: Frame Rate
parameters.heading: Ramp Points

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames before the start frame.

parameters.label: Pre Hold
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the first frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: For sequences with a frame range, this determines how to show frames after the last frame.

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.heading: Ramp Points
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if 'Hold N Frames' is selected.

entries.summary: Defocuses an image similar to a real camera defocus.

parameters.label: Defocus
parameters.description: The amount of defocusing to apply (in pixels). This is the diameter of the defocus circle (or poly).

parameters.label: Defocus Y
parameters.description: If you would like to specify a different defocus size for the vertical direction, toggle on this parameter (useful for getting a motion blur defocus effect).

parameters.label: Defocus Shape
parameters.description: The shape of the lens's circle of confusion.

parameters.label: Polygon Edges
parameters.description: If the defocus shape is a polygon, this is the number of edges that the regular polygon has.

parameters.label: Lens Rotation
parameters.description: If the defocus shape is a polygon, you can rotate the polygon shape to any orientation.

parameters.label: Per Pixel Defocus
parameters.description: This option is enabled when a mask is used (Mask tab). It allows you to vary the amount of defocus applied based on the mask brightness. There is also a tolerance value which quantizes the defocus sizes. This can speed up the per-pixel defocus, especially when the mask is at a high bit depth (like floating point). It is expressed in defocus size; so a tolerance of 0.01 would have 500 distinct defocus levels between 0 and a defocus size of 5 (0, 0.01, 0.02, ... 4.99, 5). Higher tolerances produce faster composites, at the expense of image quality. Artifacts generally become noticeable around 0.1.

parameters.label: Add Edge Ring
parameters.description: Adds a brighter ring area around the defocused area, to mimic a real lens.

parameters.label: Ring Size
parameters.description: The portion of the defocused area that will be visible as a bright ring (its proportional thickness). 0 is none, 1 is the entire area. Normally the ring is only a small portion of the defocused area (around 5%, or 0.05).

parameters.label: Ring Intensity
parameters.description: The extra brightness of the ring (0 is none).

parameters.label: Ring Offset
parameters.description: The ring can be biased more to one side of the bloom; a negative value shifts the bloom ring left or down, while a positive value shift the bloom ring right or up.

parameters.label: Boost Intensity of Bright Spots

parameters.label: Boost Threshold
parameters.description: All luminances above this value will be boosted.

parameters.label: Boost Factor
parameters.description: Multiplies the luminance above the threshold to produce the boost. Produces a more gradual boost.

parameters.label: Boost Level
parameters.description: Boosts the luminance above the threshold amount by this value (by adding it to the luminance). Produces more abrupt changes in color, making the defocus shape stand out more from the image.

entries.title: Denoise
entries.summary: Removes white noise from an image.

parameters.label: Iterations
parameters.heading: Denoise
parameters.description: Governs the number of rounds of denoising that will be performed on the image. Running time is proportional to the number of rounds. Additional iterations will increase the removal of noise at the expense of losing more fine detail.

parameters.label: Diffuse
parameters.heading: Denoise
parameters.description: A scale factor for the amount of diffusion to apply in each round of iteration. The total amount of diffusion will thus be this times the Iterations. However, if this is made too large, the process can become unstable and not converge to a good result.

parameters.label: Full Sequence
parameters.heading: Denoise
parameters.description: Instead of operating on a single frame, perform the denoise calculation across the entire sequence. This requires the entire sequence be loaded into memory and processed at once, so may be infeasible for large images or long sequences. This will result in greater frame-to-frame coherency of the resulting denoising. An internal cache is generated for each image plane (such as C or A) denoised. To save out the result in a file ROP it is recommended to only save one plane at a time so the cache can be used.

parameters.label: Pixel Size
parameters.heading: Denoise
parameters.description: Acts as the conversion factor from pixel space into the three dimensional coordinates in which the denoising will occur. The relative magnitude of the pixel size is important, not the absolute values. This is primarily used for the Full Sequence mode to determine how far in Z one frame should be. Making the Z steps smaller or larger will affect the relative importance of temporal coherence versus spatial coherence.

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input.

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a Scale COP down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an Invert COP after the node with the mask.

parameters.label: Plane Scope
parameters.heading: Scope
parameters.description: Specifies the scope for both the RGB components of Color, Alpha, and other planes. The (C)RGBA mask only affects Color components and Alpha. 'C' will toggle all the RGB components. For planes other than Color and Alpha, the plane name (plus component, if applicable) should be specified in the string field. The pulldown menu can be used to select planes or components present in this node. A plane is specified by its name. A component is specified by both its plane and component name. The '*' wildcard may be used to scope all extra planes. Any number of planes or components can be specified, separated by spaces.

parameters.label: Frame Scope
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: Allows scoping of specific frames in the frame range. This is in addition to the plane scope (so a plane at a certain frame must be both plane scoped and frame scoped to be modified).

parameters.label: Frame Range
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside range, this parameter specifies the subrange of the sequence to scope (or unscope). This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).

parameters.label: Frame Dropoff
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: For Inside/Outside Range, this parameter specifies certain number of frames before and after to slowly ramp up to scoped. The operation will be blended with its input to 'ease in' or 'ease out' the scoping effect over a number of frames. This can be edited in Timeline viewer mode (((Ctrl + 2)) in viewer).

parameters.label: Non-scoped Effect
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: For unscoped frames, this sets the blend factor between the input and modified images. Normally this is zero (use the input image). By setting this to a non-zero value, you can make unscoped frames be 'slightly' unscoped. The value can vary between 0 (unscoped) and 1 (scoped).

parameters.label: Frame List
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: The frame list for 'Specific Frames'. Frame numbers should be separated by spaces.

parameters.label: Automatically Adjust for Length Changes
parameters.heading: Frame Scope
parameters.description: If the sequence range changes, enabling this parameter will adjust the subrange and frame dropoff lengths to fit the new range.

entries.title: Depth Darken
entries.summary: Darkens depth boundaries in an image.

parameters.label: Depth Scale
parameters.description: Differences in depth have to be converted into differences in intensity. As the size of scenes can vary, the correct ratio will vary depending on the size of the scene. The Depth Scale allows one to compensate for the ratio of the scene.

parameters.label: Radius
parameters.description: The diameter of the depth darkening effect. Pixels up to this radius from the depth boundary can be affected.

parameters.label: Maximum Darken
parameters.description: The final darkening effect is clamped against the maximum darken value. A solid black halo can be too aggressive, so smaller values are useful to modulate the extent of the effect.

parameters.label: Use Logarithmic
parameters.description: Unlike traditional color values which have a fixed range, z-depth values can vary considerably over the image. Working with linear z-values may cause far away depth discontinuities to be exaggerated because their absolute difference is large, despite their relative difference being the same. By working in logarithmic space, a depth boundary that doubles the distance to the camera will have a fixed level of effect.

parameters.heading: Frame Scope

parameters.description: When enabled, planes with non-linear colorspaces will be converted to linear colorspace. parameters.label: Image Color Space
parameters.heading: File
parameters.description: When __Linearize__ is enabled, the image color space is determined by looking at the image file itself. In some cases, the file may contain an image in a colorspace that is different that the one the format specifies (ie, an sRGB image in an OpenEXR file, which the format dictates should be linear). This parameter allows you to explicitly state the color space of the loaded image, which may affect if the image is linearized (sRGB) or not (Linear). parameters.label: Enable Proxy Files
parameters.heading: Proxy
parameters.description: Enables the use of proxies, which are smaller versions of the full sized images. A proxy sequence should be identical to the original sequence, except for the resolution. parameters.label: 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 Res Proxy

parameters.description: Specifies the proxy sequence to use for 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 of the full resolution.

parameters.label: Custom Proxy
parameters.heading: Proxy
parameters.description: Allows you to specify other proxy resolutions and their proxy sequences.

parameters.label: Effect Amount
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: If no mask is present, this blends the output with the input by a constant amount (0 = all input, 1 = all output). If a mask is present, this amount multiplies the mask.

parameters.label: Operation Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Selects the mask plane to use as a mask from the mask input. A mask can be a component of a plane or an entire plane. If a vector plane is supplied as a mask, its components are multiplied by the images' components. *Scalar Mask ('A', 'C.r')* {{{ C.r = I.r * M C.g = I.g * M C.b = I.b * M }}} *Vector Mask ('C')* {{{ C.r = I.r * M.r C.g = I.g * M.g C.b = I.b * M.b }}}

parameters.label: Resize Mask to Fit Image
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: If the mask image is a different resolution than the output image, turning on this parameter will scale the mask to the output image's resolution. If this node is changing constantly, and the mask is not, it is somewhat faster to put a [Scale COP|Node:cop2/scale] down to do the resize for the mask image. Otherwise, the scale will occur every time this node cooks.

parameters.label: Invert Mask
parameters.heading: Mask
parameters.description: Inverts the mask so that all fully 'masked' portions become unmasked. This saves you from inserting an [Invert COP|Node:cop2/invert] after the node with the mask.

parameters.label: Pre Extend
parameters.heading: Sequence

parameters.label: Pre Hold

parameters.label: Post Extend
parameters.heading: Sequence

parameters.label: Post Hold
parameters.heading: Sequence
parameters.description: The number of frames to hold the last frame for, if __Hold N Frames__ is selected.

entries.summary:
Adds a variety of atmospheric effects to an image, including fog,
haze and heat waves.

parameters.label: Fog Type
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: The atmospheric effect to be applied.

parameters.label: Fog Density
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: The density of the atmospheric effect. For each depth unit, this amount is applied.

parameters.label: Fog Color
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: The color of the fog for fog effects (Normal and Additive fog only).

parameters.label: Distance Offset
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: A constant value added to the per-pixel distance.

parameters.label: Fog Direction
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: The direction the distance is computed in, either X,Y,Z or camera depth.

parameters.label: Smooth Edges
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: Enabling this option attempts to blend the fog on edges with sharp changes in depth. Because only 1 depth value is stored per-pixel, and they aren't normally blended, some edges can have sections look fogged and some that aren't at all, depending on the sampling. This option detects edges and corrects these artifacts.

parameters.label: Smooth Edge Threshold
parameters.heading: Fog
parameters.description: Edges are blended if the edge transition is greater than this threshold, from the current edge pixel to a neighboring pixel. If all the neighboring pixels are within this distance of the current pixel, it is not considered an edge and smoothing is not applied.

parameters.label: Smoothness
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):
parameters.description: The number of samples taken from the image. '1' produces a grainy effect, while higher values produce a blurry effect.

parameters.label: Horizontal Scale
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):
parameters.description: How much horizontal deviation the heat waves cause.

parameters.label: Vertical Scale
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):
parameters.description: How much vertical deviation the heat waves cause.

parameters.label: Time Scale
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):
parameters.description: How quickly the heat waves change.

parameters.label: Noise Offset
parameters.heading: Heat (only applicable for Heat Waves):
parameters.description: The 3D noise offset for the heat waves. Animate the 'Y' parameter with $F to see rising heat waves.

parameters.label: Layered
parameters.heading: Layer
parameters.description: Turns layered fog on, with the fog appearing in the specified area. The most common type of layered fog is 'Y Layered Below' (for ground hugging fog) and 'Y Layered Above' (for clouds).

parameters.label: Layer Edge
parameters.heading: Layer
parameters.description: Where the fog begins to falloff to zero. If Layered is set to 'Y Layered Below', all values with a Y value lower than the layer edge value will be fogged.

parameters.label: Layer Falloff
parameters.heading: Layer
parameters.description: The size of the falloff region, which produces a gradual decrease in the fog once the Layer Edge has been reached.

parameters.label: Falloff Function
parameters.heading: Layer
parameters.description: The shape of the falloff region.

parameters.label: Use Fog Noise
parameters.heading: Noise
parameters.description: If on, the fog is not uniform and has 3D noise variations in it.

parameters.label: Noise Amplitude
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Frequency
parameters.heading: Noise

parameters.label: Noise Offset

parameters.label: Turbulence

parameters.label: Override Size
parameters.heading: Layout
parameters.description: If off, the resolution of the image is defined by the resolution in the Composite Project settings. If on, any resolution can be specified.

parameters.label: Pixel Aspect Ratio
parameters.heading: Layout
parameters.description: If off, the pixel aspect ratio of the image is defined by the pixel aspect ratio in the Composite Project settings. If on, any pixel aspect ratio can be specified. The pixel aspect ratio determines the shape of the pixel; it represents the width of the pixel compared to the height. A pixel with an aspect ratio of '2' is twice as wide as it is high (2:1). Pixel aspect ratios less than 1 are taller than they are wide. The image viewer attempts to show the image as it would appear by horizontally scaling the image by the pixel aspect ratio. This can result in slight artifacts for non-integer ratios (ie, 0.9:1, 1.442:1). Turn off 'Fast Pixel Aspect' in the Display Options to suppress these artifacts. parameters.description: This string parameter allows you to create your own plane

entries.summary: Renders geometry from a SOP as a single color image.

parameters.label: SOP
parameters.heading: Geometry
parameters.description: The path of the SOP containing the geometry.
